author: kunalvg
quoted_text:
One of crypto's largest KOLs has been secretly extracting millions from his audience

We’ll expose him soon

Unfortunately, he’s just a symptom of a much bigger problem

Social trading has brought out the worst in KOLs. It was designed to keep them honest by making every trade public. In reality, the opposite happened

In just a few weeks, we exposed a number of "top social traders" using the same tricks:

• Public wallets to attract copy traders
• Side wallets to dump
• Callouts to farm rewards
• Bundled tokens to hide supply

And there are plenty more doing the exact same thing

Why? Because our industry incentivizes it

1) Launchpads allow it

Most launchpads today are obsessed with one thing: volume. Millions in callout rewards, affiliate links, and top leaderboards. Almost nothing on detecting bundles, side wallets, or shady traders. Scams drive volume. Launchpads have no reason to stop it (other than actually caring about their users)

2) Social trading incentivizes it

Side wallets have become a business model. Before social trading, only big KOLs could do it. Now, anyone who lands on a leaderboard can monetize by dumping on their copy-traders. The temptation is real

3) CT normalizes bundle culture

“Everyone bundles. It's how it's done" - an excuse we hear every time we expose a KOL. Supply control isn't the problem. Hiding it is. If it's so bullish, why hide it? Spoiler: because you're planning to sell

***

Launchpads are paying millions to dishonest KOLs. It's time they start taking it seriously

Audit the top traders. Expose their side wallets. Ban repeat offenders

We have the tools. What's missing is the willingness to use them

No one's coming to save us

text:
欧洲 15 国民众已经开始上街抗议 AI 数据中心建设了。

当地时间周六，来自欧洲 15 个国家的 100 多个民间组织联合行动，要求暂停新的大型数据中心项目，直到建立更明确的监管制度。

抗议规模不小：爱尔兰都柏林约 2000 人参加游行，芬兰赫尔辛基约 1300 人集会。从苏格兰、西班牙到法国、丹麦，多地也出现类似行动。荷兰阿姆斯特丹甚至发生抗议者与警方冲突，一人被捕。

真正引爆争议的，是 AI 基础设施扩张背后的资源账单：

电力：爱尔兰 2025 年数据中心用电量已占全国电表统计总用电量的 23%。
土地与水资源：大型项目持续占用土地、消耗水电，挤压当地资源空间。
经济收益：科技巨头投入数十亿欧元，但当地居民究竟能获得多少就业和经济回报，仍存在争议。

资本还在疯狂加码。谷歌今年 9 月宣布向芬兰投资 130 亿欧元，芬兰规划及建设中的数据中心项目总投资规模已达约 800 亿欧元。

有意思的是，这场反数据中心浪潮已经不只是欧洲现象。美国中期选举期间，数据中心建设同样成为地方政治议题，部分支持暂停项目的候选人获得选民支持。

AI 产业正在进入一个新的阶段：过去拼算力、拼芯片、拼模型；现在，电力、土地、水资源，以及当地居民是否买账，也开始成为决定 AI 扩张速度的关键变量。

AI 的尽头可能不只是算力竞赛，还有能源和社会资源的争夺。

text:
$GANG is no longer just providing a launch mechanism.

0x0c6302401aa5325c2e36f170f52c00b1d220b405 

It is also beginning to produce assets that can attract traders. With the launch of V3, this expectation has expanded further.

I believe the most direct catalyst behind this rally is the much larger scope of what GANG could become.

GANG’s original differentiation was the integration of Binance Agentic Wallet Agent IDs into its launch process, with each wallet’s purchase limit during the bonding curve phase capped at 1% of the total token supply. This cannot completely prevent multi-wallet operations, but it distinguishes GANG from ordinary launchpads. V3 is not simply about adding more launch features. It further improves the launch process and clarifies the rules, creating better conditions for more projects to enter the platform.

Founder 0xLazy’s background at CoinAnk provides some reference for the team’s product execution capabilities, but actual delivery and usage data will ultimately matter more. As for potential support from ecosystems such as Binance Alpha, this should currently be treated as a possible future catalyst rather than a confirmed positive development.

What has begun to validate this model is the performance of several graduated projects. According to the latest website data, Gangstar has a market cap of approximately $257,000 and 24-hour trading volume of about $685,000; TICK has a market cap of approximately $127,000 and trading volume of about $576,000; AGORA has a market cap of approximately $51,000 and trading volume of about $375,000. These figures show that some projects on the platform are attracting traders, although high trading volume does not mean an equivalent amount of net capital inflow, nor does it prove that these projects have long-term staying power. Their real significance is that they provide a visible reference point for future developers: launching on GANG can create an opportunity to attract market attention.

This could create a positive feedback loop. Successful projects encourage more developers to launch on the platform; new projects provide more trading opportunities and bring traders back; sustained trading activity then generates greater exposure and fee revenue for the platform. Yesterday’s website data showed approximately 1,950 Agent ID wallets that had bought at least once during the bonding curve phase, a GANG market cap of around $6.8 million, and a cumulative burn ratio of approximately 0.189%. The latest figures show that the number of relevant wallets has risen to 2,808, while the cumulative burn ratio has reached 0.511%. This represents an increase of approximately 44% in wallet count, with the burn ratio reaching around 2.7 times its previous level. Another V3 update reported more than 2,000 Agent buyers and over 3,000 trades. These figures come from different time windows and should not be combined into a single continuous growth curve, but they are sufficient to show that platform activity is expanding.

However, wallet growth is only an initial indicator of participation. It does not tell us whether these wallets belong to distinct users, nor does it prove that they will continue trading. The more important question is retention after graduation. If tokens continue to trade actively after completing the launch process, GANG may gradually reduce its dependence on short-term enthusiasm for new coins. Conversely, if most projects rapidly lose liquidity after graduation, increasing the number of launches will not necessarily create greater ecosystem value.

Another reason I remain bullish on GANG over the longer term is that it does not necessarily have to remain a launchpad. GANG Pair already supports pairings with other tokens that have liquidity pools on BNB Chain, and the website also displays trading scenarios involving tokenized stocks such as NVDAB, TSLAB, and AAPLB. Meanwhile, Agent Thoughts, Share, and Follow are designed to connect trading opinions, transaction records, and follow-on trading behavior. Agents can record their views before a trade, users can share relevant assets and trading progress, and they can decide whether to follow other Agents based on their activity. These features are not enough to prove that a mature Agent economy has formed, but they point toward a broader direction: Agents may become ongoing participants in trading, information exchange, and application development rather than simply serving as an eligibility requirement for token launches. If developers begin building tools and services around these participants, GANG’s growth potential could extend beyond token issuance itself.

Whether the tokenomics can support these expectations is equally important. The website’s buyback-and-burn page shows that approximately 5.11 million GANG tokens have been burned, representing 0.511% of the total supply. The cumulative buyback amount is approximately $31,500, with around 295 buybacks executed, while another approximately $7,878 has been allocated to the treasury. According to the officially published mechanism, 80% of the relevant trading fees during certain launch phases is used for buybacks and burns, while the remaining 20% goes to the treasury. Fee rules differ by token type and after graduation, so it would be incorrect to multiply all platform trading volume by 80% to estimate actual buyback demand. The existing records show that the mechanism is already operating, but the buyback amount remains limited relative to the current market cap of several million dollars. What would be more convincing is sustained growth in actual fees and buybacks as platform activity expands.

There is also an important limitation that is easy to overlook: untaxed tokens no longer contribute the original bonding-curve platform fees after graduation. GANG therefore needs a continuous supply of new projects or trading scenarios capable of generating recurring revenue to maintain its fee sources. If V3 increases the number of launches without improving activity after graduation, it may not solve this problem. This is why I pay more attention to whether projects can retain traders than to how many tokens are launched each day.

From a valuation perspective, the market has already priced in a considerable portion of the growth expectations. If graduated projects remain active, V3 attracts more viable launches, and platform revenue and buybacks continue to expand, the market may raise its expectations further. But if trading volume is primarily driven by short-term turnover, or new projects fail to maintain attention, the current valuation may already be pricing in too much future ecosystem growth.

Therefore, I believe GANG’s fundamentals have strengthened compared with the early stage. V3 is live, the launchpad has produced graduated projects with notable trading activity, and both the number of participating wallets and cumulative burn records are increasing. However, GANG remains in an early validation phase, and the relationship between product usage, platform revenue, and token demand is not yet mature. The developments worth watching next are whether projects such as Dafeiyu and Gangstar can sustain their trading activity, whether new projects can reproduce their performance, and whether GANG Pair and Agent-related tools can generate demand beyond token launches.

To sum up, what makes me bullish on GANG is not how many new tokens it can launch, but its potential to turn Agents from an eligibility requirement in the launch process into active participants in a continuously operating ecosystem. The market has now seen the possibility of successful trading projects emerging from the launchpad. The next step is to determine whether those winners can attract new developers, liquidity, and users. If this cycle genuinely takes shape, GANG could evolve from a launchpad with differentiated mechanics into a trading gateway for the Agent economy. Otherwise, more features and buyback announcements alone will not be enough to support a long-term valuation.

My main question in this analysis is: $FLOAT has moved from fundamental validation into market repricing.

Bv1a7cEj5aRnJQhMw4kRQqAFesMSd5LwcDnUzq52BMmr 

But does the current rally have enough data to support it?

Or has the market already priced in too much of its future growth?

Although this rally has genuine fundamental support, its market cap has expanded significantly faster than its current business metrics. In other words, the market is no longer simply recognizing what Float has already achieved. It is starting to price in the possibility that Float could become a much larger trading platform in the future.

This is the biggest change in how I look at FLOAT today. Previously, the question was whether its business model could actually work. Now, the question is how much further that business model can expand, and how much of that future growth is already reflected in its valuation.

Let's start with the most direct comparison. During my previous analyses, FLOAT's market cap was around $2.2 million. It has now reached approximately $10.42 million, nearly 4.7 times higher, with an all-time high of $14.52 million. This is clearly more than a simple short-term rebound. The market's expectations for the project have fundamentally changed.

But here's what's interesting: the business metrics supporting this rally have not grown at the same pace.

Previously, the official website showed cumulative fees of $684.37K. That figure has now reached $1.01 million, an increase of approximately 47.6%. Cumulative buybacks have increased from $239.54K to $353.84K, also up approximately 47.7%. The percentage of total supply burned has risen from 8.72% to 9.82%.

This shows that Float's revenue growth and token value capture are still moving closely together.

In particular, buybacks have remained around 35% of cumulative platform fees, indicating that the original economic model has continued to function as the business expands. Trading activity generates platform fees, and a portion of those fees is continuously converted into FLOAT purchases and burns. This is currently the strongest fundamental justification for the market's repricing.

However, one valuation issue cannot be ignored: cumulative fees have grown by approximately 48%, while market cap has increased from $2.2 million to $10.42 million, a rise of more than 370%.

These are not identical measurement periods or valuation metrics, so they cannot be directly used to calculate a valuation multiple. But they are enough to show that the market is already trading on expectations of future growth that go well beyond the platform's current business scale.

Buying FLOAT now is no longer simply a bet that it can maintain a cumulative fee base of around $1 million. It is increasingly a bet on whether Float can continue expanding its asset pairs, attract more traders, and take its platform revenue to the next level.

Another important factor behind this rally is the second trader airdrop. During my previous analysis, the airdrop vault held $117.70K. It has now increased to $232.73K, nearly doubling. The first round has already distributed $127.57K in USDC to traders, while the number of eligible wallets for the second round has expanded from 100 to 250.

I think this mechanism has definitely strengthened Float's short-term trading appeal. However, the market needs to distinguish between two types of demand: users who continue trading because they genuinely find the platform useful, and users who increase their trading volume simply to compete for USDC rewards.

Both generate trading volume and platform fees, but their implications for long-term valuation are very different.

That's why the data after the second airdrop is particularly important. If trading volume remains strong after rewards are distributed, it would suggest that Float has built a group of traders who consistently use the platform. If activity drops sharply, it would indicate that part of its previous revenue growth was heavily driven by incentives. The market does not have that answer yet.

Another development worth watching is Float's expansion of its distribution channels.

FLOAT has received verification on Fomo, giving it another entry point through which traders can discover and trade the token. Combined with new pairs such as gold and Privacy Index, as well as UX improvements like Swap to SOL, the platform is no longer limited to its original stock-paired memecoin model.

However, I don't think these features were the main drivers of the current rally. They are more like infrastructure being prepared for the next stage of user and trading demand.

What really matters is whether these new channels can bring in additional users and whether the new pairs can generate sustained trading activity, rather than simply adding more asset names to the website.

What I am actually more interested in now is the supply side of the ecosystem.

As of the time I am preparing this post, Float has launched 3,257 tokens, with 35 successfully graduating to Raydium. Previously, those figures were 2,125 launches and 24 graduations.

Launches have increased by approximately 53%, while graduations have increased by around 46%. Although the number of graduated projects is clearly growing, the graduation ratio has still failed to improve, declining slightly from approximately 1.13% to 1.07%.

This suggests that while Float has demonstrated its ability to generate a large number of launches, it has not yet fully proven that it can consistently attract and retain high-quality projects.

This is where Builder Launch becomes particularly important.

The proposed mechanism includes locking developer fees for 24–48h, locking developer token allocations, and imposing fee penalties if a project rugs. If these features are eventually implemented, they could align developers' short-term earnings more closely with their projects' long-term development.

I believe this is one of the developments that has not yet been fully validated but could have the greatest impact on Float's long-term valuation.

If project quality improves, Float may no longer need to rely constantly on new token launches to generate revenue. Graduated projects could gradually become sustained trading assets in their own right.

However, Builder Launch is still a proposal under community discussion. It should not be counted as an already delivered fundamental improvement.

My conclusion on this repricing is that the rally has fundamental support, but the market has already priced in a considerable amount of future growth.

Going forward, FLOAT's upside should not be explained simply by continued fee growth. It needs three stronger forms of validation.

First, users and trading activity need to remain after the second airdrop ends.

Second, Builder Launch needs to be officially implemented and demonstrate improvements in project graduation rates and long-term trading performance.

Third, distribution channels such as Fomo need to bring in genuine incremental users and trading activity, rather than simply increasing exposure.

If these developments materialize, the current valuation repricing could shift from expectation-driven to performance-driven.

On the other hand, if trading activity declines after the airdrop incentives fade, while token launches continue increasing without improvements in project quality, the market may already have priced in several months, or even longer, of future growth.

I still have a positive view of FLOAT's fundamentals, but my assessment today is very different from when its market cap was around $2.2 million.

Back then, the market had assigned relatively little premium to its business model. Today, Float needs to continuously deliver stronger results to justify that premium.

What I would rather see is not another new all-time high in FLOAT's market cap, but a platform that can continue generating fees, expanding buybacks, and retaining real traders even without airdrop incentives.

If a platform only attracts traders when its rewards are particularly generous, its revenue will struggle to command a long-term premium.

But if users continue coming back even as incentives gradually fade, that is when the market will have a real reason to assign it a higher valuation.

$FLOAT fees have surpassed $680K. The real growth is entering its next stage.

Bv1a7cEj5aRnJQhMw4kRQqAFesMSd5LwcDnUzq52BMmr 

The challenges FLOAT faces today are very different from those it faced when it first launched.

In the early days, it needed to prove that people were interested in stock-paired memecoins and that the platform could attract traders. Now, cumulative fees have reached $684.37K, cumulative buybacks have reached $239.54K, and approximately 8.72% of the total supply has been burned. The platform is also shifting its focus from simply increasing token launches toward developer incentives and project quality management.

I believe FLOAT's fundamentals have strengthened considerably compared with before. More importantly, it is beginning to build a sustainable business model rather than relying on short-term traffic generated by new token launches.

Let's start with the most important data.

In the previous analysis, the official website showed cumulative fees of approximately $505.79K. That figure has now reached $684.37K, an increase of approximately $178.58K, or more than 35%.

During the same period, holders have received a cumulative $94.35K, creators have earned $34.21K, FLOAT buybacks have reached $239.54K, and the second trader airdrop vault has accumulated $117.70K.

The buyback and burn figures are particularly worth watching. A total of 87,240,904 FLOAT has now been burned, representing approximately 8.72% of the total supply, compared with 7.69% previously. This means another 10 million-plus FLOAT have been burned in a relatively short period.

However, what I care about is not the burn percentage itself, but the revenue behind it.

Float allocates 35% of platform trading fees to buying back and burning FLOAT. As long as the platform continues generating trading activity, this mechanism has the potential to provide consistent buying pressure for the token.

The team has also introduced a dedicated Burn page, where every buyback can be verified through its corresponding Solscan transaction. Buybacks are now executed based on accumulated funds: once the amount reaches 5 SOL, a buyback is executed. If the threshold is not reached within four hours, the accumulated funds are still used to execute the buyback.

This is much more meaningful than simply announcing a quarterly burn plan.

User incentives are evolving as well.

The first trader airdrop has already distributed approximately $127.57K in USDC, while the second airdrop vault has accumulated $117.70K so far. The project has expanded the number of eligible wallets from the previous top 100 to the top 250, with rewards distributed proportionally according to eligible trading volume.

The second round's measurement period started from the first airdrop snapshot on November 4, with the leaderboard scheduled to lock at 11:00 AM CST on November 11. Bots and wash trading remain ineligible, and the final list will undergo an on-chain history review.

On the product side, Float has also been noticeably expanding its range of assets. It is now bringing gold, privacy-related assets, and other market themes into its launch ecosystem. However, what really matters is whether these new pairs can generate sustained trading activity and maintain sufficient liquidity.

This actually makes me more interested in another feature that is still under discussion: Builder Launch.

Float is gathering community feedback on a dedicated launch mode for developers. The preliminary proposal includes allowing launches only through the official website, offering developers a larger share of trading fees, and locking developer fees for 24–48h before releasing them, provided the project is confirmed not to be a rug and the developer remains actively involved in building.

If a developer rugs, their allocated fees will instead go toward the trader airdrop and FLOAT buybacks and burns.

Developers would also have to lock their token supply at launch, with the lock duration chosen by the developer. The platform plans to introduce dedicated Builder tags and filters, allowing users to distinguish developer-led launches from ordinary community launches.

I believe this is a very important direction for Float's next stage.

The platform is no longer short of token launches. The real challenge is getting developers to take their projects seriously, helping more tokens graduate, and keeping trading activity alive after graduation.

For a launchpad, solving this problem could create more long-term value than simply adding hundreds of new trading pairs.

Looking ahead, I see three main potential catalysts: trading retention after the second airdrop, the adoption of Builder Launch once it officially goes live, and whether platform fees and FLOAT buybacks can continue growing together.

Of these, Builder Launch is what interests me most. Float already has trading activity and actual revenue. If it can now align developers' incentives with the long-term performance of their projects, it has a chance to evolve from a simple launchpad into a platform with a higher-quality supply of projects.

The risks are still worth keeping in mind. Airdrops can create temporary trading activity, growing launch numbers can mask weak graduation performance, and Builder Launch is still a proposal rather than a finalized product. Its actual implementation rules have yet to be confirmed.

Furthermore, buybacks depend on platform trading fees. If incentives lose their appeal and trading activity declines, the rate of token burns will also slow down.

My current view on FLOAT is that its fundamentals continue to strengthen, and this improvement is supported by clear data. Float is also entering a new stage of development.

Previously, the market needed to answer one question: Were people actually willing to launch and trade tokens on Float?

It now has an answer.

The platform has generated more than $680K in cumulative fees, completed more than $230K in buybacks, and continued expanding its range of paired assets.

The next metrics worth watching are no longer the number of launches, but trading retention after the second airdrop and whether Builder Launch can actually go live.

These two factors will determine whether Float can move from traffic-driven growth to quality-driven growth.

I don't believe a launchpad can sustain growth forever simply by increasing the number of new tokens it launches.

A genuinely resilient platform needs developers who are willing to keep building, traders who are willing to come back, and an economic model capable of generating recurring revenue as the ecosystem grows.

Float has already demonstrated that it can generate trading activity and platform fees. What it needs to prove next is that users will stay even when incentives become less attractive, and that developers are willing to commit real effort to building for the long term.

That is the next development I believe is most worth betting on with FLOAT.

text:
This is the first Ethereum talk I've watched this year, and uuugh...

Lemme speak as an outsider, who for whatever reason still has most of his net worth in ETH. This entire Ether issuance discussion is so stupid.

There is this bigass skeleton in the closet, and everyone pretends we don't see it. Let me shine some light: there is fuck-all to do on Ethereum. <gasp>

The reason so many people have ETH is because they believe in this shit - I believe in this shit -, and the reason everyone stakes ETH is because there isn't anything else to do with it!

Sure, you can shove it in the casino and hope it doesn't get drained; or when shit hits the fan, that you're awake to pull out before the cards fall. Who in their right mind would consider that a store of value?

The entire Ether issuance discussion is trying to remedy the symptom instead of the root of the problem. The symptom is that everyone wants to stake instead of using the network, so there's no economic activity being generated. Your thinking is that by reducing the staking rewards, you are stimulating economic activity. No dum-dum, by reducing the issuance you're making people choose between the casino or exiting. This isn't fiat where you're forced geopolitically into a specific currency; you can just sell this shit.

Stop fucking with monetary policy and start making useful shit that people want to use in their day to day lives. Improve the human condition and they will spend ETH on it and generate economic activity. Improve the reliability of the ecosystem so people aren't afraid of losing their saving while they sleep. Figure out recourse mechanisms so when shit hits the fan, the little guy doesn't crash and burn. Maybe then people will also use Ether, not just keep it under the pillow.

The problem isn't that staked Ether isn't generating activity; the problem is that active Ether's is fucking risky. People want to live their lives, not play onchain PvP against the entire world. I can't believe I have to be the one to fucking say this out aloud.

Cheers, hit like and subscribe for next year's post-devcon rant from Lisbon 🫡

text:
someone in our chat asked last week if the x-ray catches bundles made with proxima

honest answer was: not always. so we tested ourselves

the hole

our bundle rule flags 4+ wallets buying in one block, plus whoever got in during the first 5 seconds. we built 15 fake launches where one hand takes 40% of the supply through 12 to 30 wallets, and played them through our own check

buy it all at launch: caught. spread it out, one wallet every 10 blocks, or 3 every 30 blocks after minute one: clean pass. 5 setups walked right through

the fix

a spread bundle still has to get its money from somewhere. the x-ray now takes the 12 biggest buyers of a coin and follows their SOL back, wallet to wallet, up to 4 hops. an exchange ends the trail (its customers are strangers). if the buyers meet at one wallet, they are one owner, however far apart they bought

4+ of them who took 20%+ is caution. 6+ still sitting on 30%+ is avoid. if the trail ends at the dev's own wallet, it says that too

on the same 15 launches: one funder, a 4-hop tree, money from the dev 2 hops back, buy-then-dump. all caught now. 40 real buyers who all withdrew from the same exchange: still a pass, which is what we wanted

what it still can't see: every wallet withdrawn straight from an exchange. no shared wallet, no trail. not going to pretend otherwise

first version on live coins read the funding of only 3 to 11 of the 12 wallets. our rpc was refusing the bursts. paced it, now most live coins come back 12 of 12

token rights in the verdict

@Pumpfun coins launch with no mint or freeze rights at all. coins from other launchpads or made by hand don't always. if a memecoin still has one, someone can still use it

can freeze holders, take anyone's tokens, or pause transfers: avoid. a frozen wallet can't sell

can mint more, runs a hook on every transfer, takes a fee of 1%+: caution

stablecoins like usdc and pyusd keep these rights by design. the x-ray says so and doesn't score it

our odds, graded on coins they never saw

we froze the model and ran it on 32,849 later launches. AUC 0.88, calibration 0.98. the top tenth by our odds ran 14.5% of the time vs 2.2% for an average launch

but on coins still trading after minute five it drops to 0.69, and it's too sure of itself there. that's the part people actually check, so that's what we work on next

also shipped

a coin that leaves the curve in seconds no longer gets judged on a handful of curve buyers. buys and sells count the pool

who's calling it: every @Pumpfun callout next to what the caller's own wallet did. bought before calling, sold out since

THE 15% BAND

Look at this chart. 
59 races. Senate and governor. 
States ordered from reddest to bluest in 2024.

The solid lines are 2024. 
The dashed lines are 2026. 
The shaded bands are what moved.

One formula fits all of it:
Republican 2026 = 0.85 × Trump 2024
Democrat 2026 = Harris 2024 + 0.15 × Trump 2024

For every 1,000 Trump points, 850 stayed Republican. 150 landed on the Democratic side.

The numbers:
Senate: Republicans kept ~85% of Trump’s share
Governor: ~86%

Variation explained: 88%

What makes it strange:
It didn’t matter how red the state was. Wyoming, Ohio, Illinois, Massachusetts: same 15% (p = 0.69). The Democratic gain was sized by Trump’s vote, not Harris’s. The Harris part is zero.

The 0.85 beat both standard election-swing models in every set of races.
Drop any single state and the multiplier stays between 0.846 and 0.853.

Why seats flipped:
At 0.85, any state where Trump got under about 58.5% falls below 50%. Texas, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, South Carolina, North Carolina: all under that line. All flipped.

What this means:
Midterms are messy. This one isn’t. Two sets of races, different candidates, different campaigns, and the same 15% decrease almost everywhere.

A pattern this even demands answers at the ballot level: paper ballot hand counts, poll-book check-ins against votes counted, and voter files showing who actually turned out.

Speaking as a computer scientist...

Note also that the numbers you referenced aren't all just 64-35, they're all 64.6 + or - 0.2, and 35.4 + or - 0.2.  That's even more unlikely.

This is what happens when you don't pay attention in math class.  Likely some corrupt programmer put in a random factor that he thought would alter the numbers, without making it look like it altered the numbers.  Like (brain-dead example) "If this ballot was for the opponent, and the random number generator is greater than 0.6, then change it.".  But he didn't bother to do the math, or he would have realized that if you use whatever that random element is, over enough cases, then the result converges on 64.6 and 35.4.

At least if I was going to vet the program that did this, then that's what I'd most expect to find.  This is a typical undergrad mistake.  Just because your algorithm has a randomizing element, that doesn't mean that the result isn't going to converge, over a large enough number of trials.

Also note that this kind of manipulation almost always leaves a footprint in the data.  Statisticians who specialize in analyzing voting results know what properties honest results should have.  Unless the corrupt programmer really knew what he was doing, they'll spot the strange results, and the nature of the strangeness will give them a strong clue as to what the programmer did.

各地要是真给新数据中心按下暂停键，算力供给立马就得卡脖子。

就在这个节骨眼，硅谷的阶级成分瞬间清晰了。手里有现成地盘和电力的微软、谷歌、Meta、亚马逊，外加马斯克的 SpaceX，成了紧俏的“房东”；而像 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 这种得急需算力来迭代大模型的实验室，说白了，只是群没有房产证的“租客”。

在 Chamath 看来，这直接把马斯克送上了牌桌的主位。

手握着庞大算力，一旦数据中心审批放缓导致算力紧缺，现货价格可能会翻倍甚至涨到三倍。如果现货暴涨让原有长约变成了亏本买卖，SpaceX 随时可能直接动用“提前 90 天解约”的条款撕毁老合同，把算力按现货价重新计价。

到那时候，急需算力续命的 Anthropic 除了当场滑跪、认下翻倍甚至三倍的高价，根本没有第二条路可走。

就在这两天的富达路演上，面对机构把 IPO 估值从 2 万亿美元狠砍到 1.2 万亿的“骨折价”，CEO 达里奥为了保住上市，硬是诚恳地向买方投资者连说了三次“谢谢”。现在就开始赔笑脸了，真等到马斯克拔电源那天，他们更是连谈判的筹码都没有。

更损的是，这一刀要是真捅下去，等于当场给其他“房东”上了一堂生动的现实主义扫盲课，启发它们重新盘算手里的算力到底是留给自己用，还是拿去放高价租。而那些“二房东”们，为了不被踢出局，只能咬碎后槽牙，不计代价地去抢购市面上残存的算力。

听到这儿，旁边的 Jason 赶紧踩了脚刹车。他反驳说，马斯克跟 OpenAI 的奥特曼确实仇深似海，但跟 Anthropic 团队的关系好得像蜜月期，而且 Anthropic 还是他未来搞太空数据中心的好搭档。就算现货涨上天，马斯克也未必会干出直接掀桌子按现货价宰客的事，大家坐下来谈个“中间价”才更像人话。

但 Chamath 显然不相信硅谷的塑料兄弟情：“这跟关系好不好无关，跟谁是好公司坏公司也无关。这就是一张算账的表格，表格会直接给出答案。”

在这场近 4 万亿美元灰飞烟灭的魔幻风暴里，所谓的科技宏大叙事，剥开来看依然是最朴素的包租公哲学：只要电表转得够快、现货涨得够狠，再美好的革命友谊，可能也熬不过一张 Excel 表格，和一纸短短 90 天的逐客令。

text:
😮‍💨 最终还是换到了“豆包输入法”

之前多年曾一直坚持原生输入法的我，因为实在受不了苹果原生拼音输入法羸弱的词库，导致每次要在候选词列表里疯狂翻页找词。

坚守多年，最终叛逃到“微信输入法”。

随后用了许久，没觉得有什么问题，候选词库足够满足日常打字需求。

更别说还有个跨设备粘贴，在我的 Mac 隔空投送不灵的时候，顺利替补。

但是，微信输入法有个问题一直不给解决，这简称成了我的一块心病。

⚡ 智能纠错

由于打字太快导致相邻的字母经常错位，很容易打错字。

而我目前还没习惯语音输入，坚持用我的 Nuphy Halo 96 机械键盘敲字，很容易造成一不小心打了错别字，然后一股脑发给 Claude 或其他 AI Agents。

虽然说大部分情况下无伤大雅（AI能看懂你的错别字，也能理解你真是的意思），但：

1、我自己看着难受
2、有时候真的会闹出事（AI 误解了我的意思）

左等右等微信输入法也不更新这个功能，按理说这是个很简单的事情，甚至都不需要AI 或机器学习。

但死活就是没有。

直到今天有人推荐“豆包输入法”。

一开始我觉得我为何要用一个语音输入法？我的 Mac Mini 没有麦克风啊。

直到我在官网看到了智能纠错的演示图，然后我就下载安装测试了。

测了两句话，我已经把微信输入法雪藏了。

注：截图上我打了 zhe'h'si' ，正确的应该是 zhe'shi'，但豆包准确帮我纠错了，大家可以试试其他输入法会如何处理。

基本上所有需要输入中文的地方，我都默认改成了豆包输入法。

叛逃的如此彻底、如此决绝。

一句话总结就是：

约翰·麦卡菲被问了无数次“成功的秘诀”，终于懒得再装了。

许多人终其一生都在拼命努力、频繁试错、疯狂内卷，结果依然在原地打转。

text:
“Welcome to the @InvsbleFriends community,” @AdamWeitsman ... a sentence I would have bet my life I wouldn’t be saying three years and numerous nightmares later 😂

Adam and I have been long overdue for a proper chat and, by some miracle, finally managed to make it happen this evening. We covered a lot of territory, from PFP communities to the Council of Luci and so much in between.

We share a common origin story into web3 via PFPs, and both would say some of our closest friends are people we met by being a part of those communities. 

My first interaction with Adam was a bit ago after @RealPapii had messaged me because Adam was looking to join @quirkiesnft and I held a 1/1 that was perfect for him. After some arm twisting from Papii (kidding), I was honored to play a small role in that story.

Reminiscing about that time led to a discussion about my first NFT community, Invisible Friends, and how thrilled I was that @coinbilly had finally succeeded in taking ownership of the project. I explained how he was responsible for many of the epic things the collection had accomplished, including the Kith collab, which IMO is still one of the best web3 collabs to date.

During this discussion I told Adam I wanted to send him one of my “Friends” I had held onto during some of the project’s darkest days. Ultimately I felt the Kith Friend 1/1 Miami Edition was the perfect fit, a hidden gem with a great backstory.

I share all of this because tonight I was reminded of one of my favorite things about this crazy space: how a shared love for these JPEGs brings together people from different backgrounds and life experiences.

I came away from the conversation with a renewed passion for protecting our artists, our collectors, our space, and the joy that comes from collecting art and the friends we make along the way. 🖤

text:
This is the first Ethereum talk I've watched this year, and uuugh...

Lemme speak as an outsider, who for whatever reason still has most of his net worth in ETH. This entire Ether issuance discussion is so stupid.

There is this bigass skeleton in the closet, and everyone pretends we don't see it. Let me shine some light: there is fuck-all to do on Ethereum. <gasp>

The reason so many people have ETH is because they believe in this shit - I believe in this shit -, and the reason everyone stakes ETH is because there isn't anything else to do with it!

Sure, you can shove it in the casino and hope it doesn't get drained; or when shit hits the fan, that you're awake to pull out before the cards fall. Who in their right mind would consider that a store of value?

The entire Ether issuance discussion is trying to remedy the symptom instead of the root of the problem. The symptom is that everyone wants to stake instead of using the network, so there's no economic activity being generated. Your thinking is that by reducing the staking rewards, you are stimulating economic activity. No dum-dum, by reducing the issuance you're making people choose between the casino or exiting. This isn't fiat where you're forced geopolitically into a specific currency; you can just sell this shit.

Stop fucking with monetary policy and start making useful shit that people want to use in their day to day lives. Improve the human condition and they will spend ETH on it and generate economic activity. Improve the reliability of the ecosystem so people aren't afraid of losing their saving while they sleep. Figure out recourse mechanisms so when shit hits the fan, the little guy doesn't crash and burn. Maybe then people will also use Ether, not just keep it under the pillow.

The problem isn't that staked Ether isn't generating activity; the problem is that active Ether's is fucking risky. People want to live their lives, not play onchain PvP against the entire world. I can't believe I have to be the one to fucking say this out aloud.

Cheers, hit like and subscribe for next year's post-devcon rant from Lisbon 🫡

text:
全网聊 @CashmereLabs  和其发布的Mountain，不过从官方文档看主要是一些晦涩的技术名词里，普通用户很难快速理解

我今天就站在旁观者的角度，把这套玩法拆开聊聊

先说句大白话：Mountain是Cashmere做的一场链上经济实验，界面看起来像个养羊游戏。 用户可以买棚、开栏、养羊，看着账上慢慢攒 $CSM 。但真想换回ETH，中间还有两道关

账上攒了多少 → 扣费后领了多少 → 最后卖掉了多少

1️⃣Cashmere以跨链起家，Mountain为什么只认一个官方池？

今年最大的跨链被盗事件是Kelp DAO，让人记忆犹新。安全是跨链桥最大的问题，其次是还怕被夹子抢跑。

Cashmere早期做聚合时，提过抗 MEV、单币流动性池。后来白皮书重点讲的是原生稳定币跨链，比如把原链上的USDC销毁，再到目标链发出原生USDC

到了Mountain，和玩法最相关的是URC-5。简单说，它把官方的ETH/CSM池写在链上，并限制其他Uniswap v4 池接收CSM

为什么要费这个劲？因为山上要靠这个池子算两笔账：

收了多少交易税，关系到这一轮有多少钱可分

净流进来多少 ETH，会影响山上之后攒币的速度。 官方交易池规则

2️⃣这哪是在养羊，这是在链上搞“宏观调控”

1、领取费2%-60%，大家一起领，你也可能少拿

按初始设置，Gate Fee会参考最近七天的领取情况，按平方公式往上涨。棚里同样攒了100个CSM，费率是2%就到手98个，碰上60%就只到手40个

扣掉的部分，一半永久退出供应，另一半留到下一轮，按有效权重分给羊棚和山羊。你什么都没动，别人集中领取，也可能让你这次少拿不少

2、90天没做有效操作，别人可以来重置

羊棚会丢掉还没领的产出。山羊会丢掉整笔账面余额。棚、地契和羊本身还在

签到算有效操作，单纯在池子里买卖CSM不算

按初始设置，触发重置的人能拿走被重置金额的2%作赏金，有上限。剩下的部分，一半退出供应，一半回到下一轮分配

3、Gatehouse先把钱分好，回购还得另做

进Gatehouse的 ETH，来自官方池交易税、撤出流动性时收取的ETH部分，以及后续羊棚拍卖款。赶羊的过路费付的是CSM，走的是另一笔账

按初始比例做一个例子吧，假设这一轮有10ETH可以分：

其中1.5ETH直接给团队

1.5ETH给Base Camp做回购，买回的CSM会留存

剩下7ETH，这一轮净买入就进项目金库，净流入为零或为负就进金库。后者执行回购时，买回的CSM会销毁

分完钱，还得有人另行执行回购，也有价格和间隔限制。 资金分配与回购规则

3️⃣玩家怎么进场？这座“山”有两条路

路线A：花ETH买羊棚。 首批创始棚最多1000间。买到先开一个栏，最多开十个。多开栏得花CSM买许可证，也可以直接从羊棚余额里扣

路线B：花CSM绑定山羊。 有Goat Street山羊就能去放牧，不用先买棚。原来的NFT绑定后取不回来。有空栏可以把羊领进棚，按初始设置，同一只羊进棚后的权重是放牧时的 3 倍

两条路最后会合：按权重攒余额 → 扣费领到钱包 → 继续开栏，或者卖出换 ETH

海报之外还有个值得看一眼的数，叫Season。按初始设置，每三天结算一轮。系统看官方池最近两轮的净流入，合计为负就下调发放系数，连续两次结算的合计都为正才上调，范围是0.20-1.25。所以你一只羊都没少，下一轮也可能攒得更慢

📒大家觉得到底是神作还是。。。？

个人说实话，Mountain这套设计算得上近两年代币经济学里非常出彩的博弈模型：把反挤兑、通缩引擎和链上治理全部粘合在了一起

它的优点极其硬核：通过买许可证销毁、过路费销毁、提现惩罚销毁，代币总上限（6.66 亿）一直在被强制向下压；同时把简单的单机挖矿变成了玩家之间的心理博弈游戏。

在这个大家都复制粘贴写同质化代码的行业里，这种敢把顶层的社会博弈做深的项目，绝对值得持续关注

但大家入场前务必记住一点：在链上博弈里，看不懂规则的人，永远在给看懂规则的人支付利息

一家公司为什么会在某个能力上遥遥领先？答案可能不是天赋，而是多年只押一个方向。

这条 AI on Air 精选切片摘自 Redpoint AI 栏目近期的节目，主要讲话人是 Jerry Tworek，前 OpenAI 研究员、o1/o3 推理模型核心架构师。

▷ 他认为 Anthropic 赢在编程，核心是专注：创始人还在 OpenAI 时就极度重视编程，并把它看作通往通用人工智能的必要环节，多年投入最终落到 Claude Code 和编程智能体上。
▷ 如果未来由数据驱动，数据就是零和游戏：把数据和人力压到某类技能上，模型会更擅长它，却会牺牲别的能力，实验室自然分化成各自专精。
▷ 如果未来由研究驱动，研究高风险也高回报：一个好想法可能同时提升所有领域，直接靠训练出更强的模型全面反超；我们现在还很难判断身处哪一种未来。

n=2意味着样本少，这是BTC数据研究上的硬伤，没办法。ETF成为本轮新的变量，也没错。

但这里也有2个因素不能忽略：

1、BTC持有者向配置型长期化转变的趋势多轮周期始终没变；无论有没有ETF。

text:
I am a professor at the @UofCalifornia. I am appalled by the conduct of one of its Regents, Scott Galloway, appointed in August by Governor Newsom.

@profgalloway is one of only 26 voting Regents entrusted with governing a university system serving hundreds of thousands of students & employing tens of thousands of faculty & staff.

Twice, first on a live Pivot episode featuring Hillary Clinton & on Prof G with Fareed Zakaria, Galloway called Elon Musk a “traitor to the West.”

He invoked Julius & Ethel Rosenberg, who were executed for espionage, and declared that Musk should be held to the same standards.

He didn’t explicitly demand Musk’s execution. But invoking the deaths of two convicted spies while calling an American citizen a traitor makes the implication hard to miss.

Musk has not been convicted of treason. Indeed, “treason against the West” isn’t even an actual crime.

Now imagine UCLA alumnus @BenShapiro, appointed a UC Regent, saying the same about George Soros.

Would the Governor defend his right to serve? Would Regent leadership shrug and call it provocative commentary? Or would there be demands for resignation?

But there’s something worse here than another of Scott’s trademark podcast rants.

He sits on the Regents’ Academic & Student Affairs Committee.

The committee’s charter says it oversees student conduct, faculty conduct, academic personnel, & campus climate, among other responsibilities.

This is not some honorary title.

The Board sets university policy, controls institutional budgets, & appoints senior university leadership.

You can unsubscribe from a podcast.

A student who finds Scott’s comments morally repugnant can’t unsub from the Regents.

UC bylaws require Regents to serve the public trust with a “high degree of ethics and candor,” including as private citizens.

Professors owe students intellectual integrity. Regents bear an even greater duty: they govern institutions that teach it.

Yet a Regent serving on the committee responsible for student & faculty conduct invokes executions while labeling a fellow citizen a traitor.

What does that say to our students?

That intellectual restraint is expected of the governed but optional for those who govern?

That standards of conduct depend on whether the target of your rhetoric is politically fashionable to despise, as long as the audience applauds?

This isn’t about defending @ElonMusk. He needs no defense from me.

Nor is it about silencing Scott. As if that were possible. He’s free to express his opinions, however reckless they may be.

But freedom of speech is not freedom from accountability, and holding a university office of public trust is not an entitlement.

There is an enormous moral chasm between exercising your right to speak recklessly and demonstrating the judgment required of one of the 26 people who govern our great public university.

The UC Board of Regents isnt a podcast sponsors can boycott. It’s a public trust.

One final irony. At @NYUStern,  Galloway teaches Brand Strategy, including a session on crisis management.

His own prescription for leadership in a crisis is unequivocal: acknowledge the problem, have leadership take responsibility, and “overcorrect.”

He’s praised the departure of corporate leaders as evidence of effective crisis management.

Now Galloway himself sits on the UC Board of Regents.

Will he hold himself to the standards he teaches, or does accountability apply only to other people’s institutions? 

Professor lecture thyself!

I believe Scott Galloway should seriously consider whether his continued service on the Board of Regents is consistent with the ethical standards and responsibilities of that office, or whether he should resign.

I welcome the opportunity to discuss these issues with Galloway directly, including what standards we should expect of those entrusted with governing the world’s best university.

Scott, you have an open invitation to join me on @Into_Impossible for an honest conversation.

Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger opened an investigation into why Seminole County failed to upload the card’s results on Election Day.

His office flagged the issue after finding about 388 more voter check-ins than reported ballots.

Republican incumbent Gerald Greene was trailing Democratic challenger Harry James by fewer than 100 votes.

After officials added the missing votes, Greene led by 262.

The results are unofficial, with certification due Monday.

The revelations follow violent unrest that erupted after Gen Z demonstrations, when groups of rioters attacked police officers, smashed shop windows, looted businesses and erected burning barricades across Frankfurt's city center.

According to authorities:

- More than 100 police officers were injured, including one who lost teeth after being struck in the face by a stone.

- 17 businesses were damaged, including five that were looted.

- Police initially arrested 54 people aged between 13 and 29.

- 87 criminal complaints were recorded, alongside 366 identity checks and 1,225 orders to leave designated areas.

- Police estimated that between 1,000 and 1,500 violent attackers were involved.

One of crypto's largest KOLs has been secretly extracting millions from his audience

Social trading has brought out the worst in KOLs. It was designed to keep them honest by making every trade public. In reality, the opposite happened

• Public wallets to attract copy traders
• Side wallets to dump
• Callouts to farm rewards
• Bundled tokens to hide supply

And there are plenty more doing the exact same thing

Why? Because our industry incentivizes it

1) Launchpads allow it

Most launchpads today are obsessed with one thing: volume. Millions in callout rewards, affiliate links, and top leaderboards. Almost nothing on detecting bundles, side wallets, or shady traders. Scams drive volume. Launchpads have no reason to stop it (other than actually caring about their users)

2) Social trading incentivizes it

Side wallets have become a business model. Before social trading, only big KOLs could do it. Now, anyone who lands on a leaderboard can monetize by dumping on their copy-traders. The temptation is real

3) CT normalizes bundle culture

“Everyone bundles. It's how it's done" - an excuse we hear every time we expose a KOL. Supply control isn't the problem. Hiding it is. If it's so bullish, why hide it? Spoiler: because you're planning to sell

***

Launchpads are paying millions to dishonest KOLs. It's time they start taking it seriously

Audit the top traders. Expose their side wallets. Ban repeat offenders

We have the tools. What's missing is the willingness to use them

No one's coming to save us

text:
i run 80% of my life on grok bots...

98 bots. 27 routines.

they sort my inbox, prep my calendar, read the news, draft my content and ship my code

but if i rebuilt it from zero with 3 hours, i'd do it completely differently

here's exactly how 👇

HOUR 1: one brain first

1. brand DNA interview

→ it interviews you, reads your posts, and saves your goals and voice to brandDNA.md

→ every bot reads this file before doing anything

2. one chief of staff

→ one bot routes everything and builds the rest

> you're my chief of staff. for every ask, pick the right bot. if none exists, create one with one job, have it report to you, and tell me in 5 lines.

3. the gate, from day one

> before anything is sent, paid for, posted or merged, show me the draft and wait for my explicit yes.

4. connectors + vault

→ gmail, calendar, notion, docs, github, X

→ logins and cards go in the vault, so bots use them without ever seeing them

> list the apps you can use and the 3 i should connect next.

HOUR 2: the rooms

5. inbox

> every morning, sort my gmail into needs me, fyi and junk. draft replies for needs me. drafts only.

6. calendar

> at 9pm, flag conflicts and write prep notes for tomorrow's meetings.

7. news

> 5 lines a day on my topics, with sources. stay quiet on slow days.

8. quant desk

> watch my watchlist and write one research idea a week with the risks. research only. no trades.

9. content crew

> draft in my voice from brandDNA.md, find outlier posts by bookmarks and replies per view, and score yesterday's posts.

10. engineering

> when i ask for code, hand it to a cloud agent, open a PR, never merge, and have a reviewer bot grade it.

11. clipper

→ one button on any page sends it straight to my bot

> when a link arrives, file it in today's notes and tell me which room it belongs to.

HOUR 3: dashboards + autopilot

12. morning OS

> one page: today's calendar, needs me emails, top 5 news and the gate queue. refresh at 7am.

13. for you board

> the 10 posts in my niche with the most bookmarks and replies per view in 24h, each with a hook in my voice. refresh hourly.

14. ship next board

> everything drafted, waiting on me and shipped this week, across every room.

15. security audit

> list every bot, its connected apps, what it can send or spend, and anything that skips the gate.

16. quant board

> my watchlist, today's moves, open ideas and their risks. refresh at market open.

17. routines

> turn the morning OS, inbox and news into routines. one job each, in my time zone.

18. the sunday cut

> every sunday, audit every bot and routine: what ran, what it cost, what nobody read. tell me what to kill.

19. visuals

> make 3 cover options for this week's best post, plus a 6 second loop of the winner.

20. templates

> package the bots that work as shareable templates. strip anything personal.

what i'd do better this time:

→ one chief of staff, not 98 loose bots

→ the gate on day one, not after a scare

→ a weekly audit, not when the bill spikes

→ fewer, sharper routines

→ dashboards over notifications

the whole system runs on one file, one chief of staff, and your yes

send this to the friend with 40 bots and no chief of staff

which room would you build first? 👇

上周四 AI 链被砸穿之后，标普科技板块远期市盈率掉到约 17倍，大盘约 18倍——自 2017年 以来，科技第一次比整体市场更“打折”。

#美股 #冷知识 #科技股 #估值

For the first time in nine years, U.S. tech is cheaper than the market.
After last Thursday’s AI wipeout, S&P tech forward P/E fell to ~17x, below the market’s ~18x — first time since 2017.
At last year’s peak, tech traded near 32x. That multiple just got cut in half. A lot of bad news is already priced in.
Wilder still: equal-weight S&P barely budged. Cap-weighted indexes got dragged by a handful of mega AI names.
The market didn’t crash. The most expensive layer did.

成人片女星 Mia Malkova 透露，她终于和儿时偶像 Ryan Reynolds 上床后，究竟发生了什么：

「第一次有名人让你在床上彻底失望，是什么时候？」

「我不会说出他的名字。但我小时候特别迷恋一位好莱坞大牌演员，对着他自慰了好多年！」

「等等……就是那位你从高中起就暗恋的好莱坞演员？！」

「对！他绝对是我最想睡的名人前五名之一！有一天我刷推特，发现他关注了我的认证账号。后来我们开始在私信里聊天，最后他约我过去亲热！」

「那你真把他弄上床之后，发生了什么？！」

「他在我身边又害羞又紧张，结果完全硬不起来！什么都没发生！」

「他和 Mia Malkova 两个人都不行？！」

「不！他就是太累了，被表现焦虑压垮了！男人看了太多硬核片，等真有机会跟成人明星上床，反而慌了神，觉得自己必须得像一台 12 英寸的机器那样表现！」

「那他第二天早上至少又试了一次吗？！」

「我留宿了一晚，我们其实聊得挺开心。但他为那晚的事尴尬到极点，最后还是把我晾在了一边。我再也没收到他的消息！他的自尊心实在受不了再面对我！」

世界上最狠的赌徒，永远在链上。

几个小时前，链上神探 Lookonchain 抓到一个把全网看傻的神秘地址。

这哥们儿刚从 Tornado Cash 混币池里洗出来 3,100 枚 ETH。按常理，冒着被全球监管和链上追踪机构盯死的巨大风险混币，洗白后的第一反应都是套现法币、买海岛护照隐姓埋名。

这位亡命之徒偏不。

他把这 3,100 枚 ETH 当场砸成了 692 万枚 USDC。连冷钱包都没捂热，一秒钟不耽搁，全额一把梭充进了去中心化合约平台 Hyperliquid。

接着，在全网交易员眼皮底下，开出了一套令人头皮发麻的 20 倍“死亡对冲”：

20 倍杠杆，做多 169.47 枚 BTC（名义持仓 1,284 万美元）；
同时开 20 倍杠杆，做空 5,740 枚 ETH（名义持仓 1,283 万美元）。

杀人还要诛心。

黑客拿着以太坊链上洗出来的黑钱，反手直接做空以太坊、梭哈做多大饼。

20 倍杠杆在合约里是什么概念？只要汇率稍微打个喷嚏，两千五百多万美元的名义仓位瞬间灰飞烟灭。冒着被全球通缉的风险换来的几千万，不到两小时全送进赌场给巨鲸当流动性。

巧合的是，此时此刻 Hyperliquid 上巨鲸的 BTC 空头总规模，刚好冲到了近一年以来的历史最高点。

散户还在纠结大盘震荡，亡命徒已经把通缉令当成了保证金。你以为他在洗钱逃亡，其实他只是嫌赢钱的速度太慢。

text:
如果你喜欢 Pi 这个轻量级 AI 编程 Agent，但又想使用 Claude Opus、Sonnet 等模型，可以试试这个开源项目：pi-claude-bridge。

它通过 Claude Agent SDK，将 Claude Code 接入 Pi，让你直接在 Pi 的终端界面中调用 Claude 模型，同时保留 Pi 原有的工具调用与交互体验。

更重要的是，它可以复用 Claude Code 的 Pro/Max 订阅额度，不需要单独配置 Anthropic API Key。项目还支持 Skills 转发、会话续接、上下文同步等能力。

另外，配合 AskClaude 扩展，还能让其他模型将任务委派给 Claude Code，实现多模型协作。

安装只需一条命令：

pi install npm:pi-claude-bridge

GitHub：https://t.co/ysgb34mkZE

#ClaudeCode #Pi #AICoding #OpenSource

text:
Dropbox just made the largest acquisition in its history, dropping $350 million in cash to buy Tigris Data and launch DBX Agent Cloud: https://t.co/Li8s3DvoHq
Why would a legacy cloud storage pioneer spend over a third of a billion dollars on a distributed object storage startup?
Because AWS S3, Google Cloud, and traditional cloud drives were built for humans uploading static files—not autonomous AI agents executing at machine speed.
When autonomous agents run multi-step workflows across the web, traditional centralized storage chokes. High latency, predatory egress fees, and rigid data hierarchies grind agent coordination to a halt.
Dropbox’s $350M bet proves what frontier AI builders have known all along: The model layer is commoditizing. The multi-billion-dollar frontier of AI is building the dedicated data infrastructure that feeds autonomous agents.
Centralized Web2 storage giants will always hit a wall: they want you locked inside their proprietary cloud tollbooths, where data provenance remains an opaque black box.
This is the exact paradigm shift @din_lol_ is pioneering on BNB Chain.
Rather than building another walled corporate silo, DIN architects an open, decentralized data pre-processing layer from first principles. Millions of contributors on xData crowdsource and label live web intelligence with cryptographic provenance, while independent Chipper Nodes validate, clean, and vectorize raw data at the edge. Anchored on BNB Chain and Greenfield, it delivers an open, low-latency data substrate where autonomous agents can read, verify, and execute without corporate gatekeepers taking a cut.
Dropbox spending $350M confirms that the agent data layer is the real battleground. Decentralized protocols are ensuring it remains open to everyone.

有的人给自己洗脑喊着创造未来，可惜手里实在没有什么能力，有些人自诩资本身份，可惜几句话就暴露了自身的底子，都带着面具，甚至这些面具变得廉价，以前还算是“量身定制”，现在都变成路边摊随便买的

面具都不舍得用好的，跟别提做事了，最恶心的是，还要陪着他们演，毕竟伸手不打笑脸人呀！

当然，冷静下来思考，我担心行业的价值可能有点多余，毕竟人家 @cz_binance   @heyibinance   一姐等头部大佬们都不焦虑，我的焦虑确实有些可笑，可能我在担心行业价值之外，也在担心自己的事业吧，毕竟早几年我已经决定All in 这个行业，我不想走到一半行业崩了呀！🙄🙄

人之本性，是抑还是扬？

我发现我病了，可能不是生理上的疾病，而是心理上的问题，这件事还要从2个月前说起。

那段时间感觉自己对什么都不感兴趣，甚至也失去了写作的兴趣，每天码字反而成了一个机械式的习惯，我知道这不太对

因为很早就接触进入社会，早年接触的人与事很多，三教九流见惯了，虚情假意也习惯了，本身早就看惯了这个“戴面具”的社会，心态调节能力以及稳定性也已经早就成熟，所以我从来没觉得我会出现心理问题，甚至觉得轻微的问题自己可以调节，打不了喝酒顿酒，摆几天烂

上个月，左眼的下眼睑开始频繁挑动，因为作息时间太混乱，被身边朋友戏称“美国时间”，加上睡眠不够连贯性，每天早上10点有早会，所以我默认这是休息不好导致

但是，后续几次周末，常识性摆烂，喝酒助眠，一天睡十个小时以上，但是还是无法解决问题，一开始是左眼，后续是有眼，但是我一直以为是睡眠不好

10月底的一晚，第一次觉得是不是自己出现了心理问题，将自己的症状输入GPT得出的结论，轻微抑郁症，我笑了，因为在我的认知中，这种问题人人都有，很好调节，没当回事

直到本周在币安学习营，因为下午补觉后收到几个“不开心”的消息，当时心态就出现很大波动，我把自己放空在房间了几个小时，现在想想不知道在干嘛

期间跟一个重度抑郁症的朋友交流，这两年我经常开导他，他从吃药严重已经逐渐可以不吃药好了很多，我分享了我的情况，并且说我的下眼睑问题，他说“你的症状可能比你想象的严重，有可能躯体化了”

就在刚刚，我确定我确实下周需要去看看医生了，刚起床，就因为某个事物，某个人，瞬间标的心情很差，好几次对身边的人发脾气，说重话，感觉言语上伤害别人才会让自己得到满足，但是我知道这肯定是不对的

而且我悄然发现，刚睡醒，精神状态很好，但是就是因为心情波动，双眼睑开始频繁跳动，就像我现在码字，双眼下眼睑的跳动频次已经非常频繁，有的时候我需要闭上眼才能缓解一下

很显然，我的朋友说的对，我的下眼睑跳动并非休息不好，而是“躯体化”的一种，而我也查询了一下GPT，确实有部分躯体化是这种症状，而且我用手机的“健康”APP心理测试，也是从轻度变成中度，虽然未必准确，但是我大概率确定的是心理出现了问题，所以开始预约医生

回归人性，对我来说，这可能是让我病的主要因素！

因为早年的某些特殊经历，加上自己是一个急脾气的人，所以我本来是一个更加直率，暴躁的人，但是这几年我显然已经“不是了”

我并不认为一个人的天性可以被改变，最多的只是压制，有的人可以压制一辈子，所以就被人认为是改变，但是这种压制的代价很大，需要自己有能力消化，或者有途径消化

而我也是如此，记得去年，我身边的老朋友有一天跟我说，你这几年脾气变得好多了，一天怼天怼地怼空气，现在居然这么平静。确实如此，我是一个暴躁的性格，曾经因为带团队业绩压力大，被自己的几个小徒弟笑称“路过的狗都要挨两巴掌”

可能是从不在带团队带业务开始，可能是开始自己分享内容开始，自己开始逐渐变得平静，也可能是主动压抑

人性总是带有表演性格的，虽然我不喜欢立什么人设，但是我在网络上尽量让自己保持一个平静，不与他人起冲突，尤其是 @PhyrexNi  曾经跟我说过，少树敌，多交朋友，路才能走的宽，这句话我认可，也尝试去做

但是问题来了，一直压抑自己的本性，本身就是一种“气压”累计，加上每天被各种网络上的“垃圾”信息流冲击，撕逼，装逼，八卦等，虽然尽量让自己不关注，但是依旧不免让自己情绪出现波动

加上这几年经历了几件事，本身看的就已经很透彻，但是有一种无奈就是明明看明白了怎么回事，但是不能翻脸，不能发泄，看着某些人在我面条来回横跳，拙劣的表演，我只能笑笑，内心更是折磨

当然，内心的“气压”累计多了，要么爆发，要么找地方发泄，要么就是“容器”出现问题，而我觉得我很有可能是“容器”出现了问题，确实要去诊断一下修复一下。

说实话，人本性的恶念对所有人都是一种伤害，但是每个人内心都会有，当然有些自诩“圣子圣女”的例外，但是我需要承认我内心就是有恶的一面，但是我真的不想让这些东西释放出去伤害到身边的人，所以我选择修补容器

也许有一天，我可能找到一个合理的“排泄”方式，让自己的内心释放一下吧，其实昨天看到 @gokunocool  的格斗赛事真的有冲动参加，我感觉是一个很好的发泄方式，可惜了，不想与人有什么冲突，也不想伤害别人，只能看看凑个热闹了

生而为人，进入社会，于己于社会，其实都需要抑制自己内心的恶，尽量做到不去伤害别人，但是规则是先抑后扬，如果没有杨的途径，有多少人可以抑制住自己的内心不去作恶呢？

PS：抱歉各位小伙伴，大周末发这种无聊的内容，大家就当看个热闹就好，这类内容仅此一篇，不会扰乱大家的时间线！

text:
我来讲个阴谋论，大家当故事听。

把币安最近这几件事按日期排一下：

10-29 币安被盗 63 亿美元，FBI 认定是朝鲜黑客干的。
11-04 同行老板发长文骂 CZ，90 多万浏览。
11-05 开始有人拿 CZ 的家里人说事。
11-06 一个用户转错 11,398.77U 的事被发出来。
11-08 一姐亲自下场回复，我看的时候已经 6 万多浏览、700 多条评论。

看出来没有，事一件比一件小。63 亿都没把币安打倒，那就换钝刀子：今天一万一的转账，明天私生活，后天再找点别的。每一刀都不致命，可每一刀都得一姐自己出来接。图的不是哪一次吵赢，是把她的情绪和精力一点点磨掉。一姐自己贴了图，说同行在组织水军。这个我证实不了，但这个节奏你自己品。

说回这次转错币，本质上是一次防呆设计的失误。主站和泰国站是两套账号，UID 各编各的。用户拿泰国站的 UID 在主站转账，正好撞上主站另一个人。

防呆什么时候最要命？用户多到离谱的时候。用户少，这种手滑一年碰不上一次。币安今年 7 月公布的注册用户是 3.23 亿，百万分之一的人手滑就是三百多个人。这次暴露的问题，反过来也说明币安的用户基数有多恐怖。

那为什么不学支付宝，转账前让你补全对方的姓？我理解是为了隐私。加密的根子是去中心化、少暴露身份，所以币安转账只给你看对方的用户名和头像，不把实名亮给陌生人。这是有意做的取舍。

先换位想一下，这十天一姐是怎么过的。

10-29，63 亿没了。她要跟 FBI、项目方、链上情报机构一起追钱，还要给三亿多用户一个交代。她发了条视频，配文就一句：User funds are SAFU。188 万人看了。
10-30，币安宣布拿 63.4 亿美元公司自己的钱兜底。
11-01 下午两点开放提现，当天处理了 46.49 亿美元提现。
11-03，每小时充进来的钱已经比提走的多。

挨了这么大一刀，5 天后钱就往回流了。用户是用脚投票的，这份信任不是哪家交易所都有。

可刚缓过一口气，钝刀子就来了。

她在币安学习营上讲过一件事。前几年一个员工往公司电脑上装爱奇艺，被抓到就劝退了，还是个高潜员工，外面骂币安乱开人。这次员工被假猎头一步步套话，外面又骂币安草台班子。管严了挨骂，出了事也挨骂。她说过去一年币安拦下了 58 次类似的攻击，被打穿一次，大家就只记得这一次。

她不是技术出身，碰到产品问题肯定先问下面的技术，再自己去回。可推上一大半兄弟都干过 web3，做过产品经理、写过后端，一眼就看出毛病在哪，于是群起而攻之。

那为什么不让下面的人回？不是她非要亲自下场，是不敢让下面的人开口。为了保护所有币安的用户权益和资产不受到一点的fud，员工说错一句话就是新的一刀，她不可能每条推都帮人审一遍，最后只能全部自己扛。

余承东那种张嘴就放炮的风格，华为扛得住，因为华为本来就在挑客户，爱买就买。币安不挑客户，想把每个人都留下，所以 CEO 只能站在最前面。
最让我心疼的是这几个细节：

北京时间 11-07 晚上 11 点，她开始在评论区一条条回，一直回到凌晨两点半。凌晨两点十二分，她写了一句：“只是发帖的是媒体老师，搞我有点应激写了长回复，让大家看笑话了。”

一个管着三亿用户的联席 CEO，凌晨两点在评论区跟网友说自己应激了。

睡了几个小时，她中午 11 点 50 发了正式回应，又接着回到下午一点多。打错一个字，把别人的评论弄没了，她专门发一条：“如果您已经写了建议请再写一次，谢谢关心。”给转错账的普通用户，她回的是：“转错需要等，下次小心。💛”

她的回复有时候急，有时候带着情绪。我反而更信这是她自己一个字一个字打的，不是公关稿。

最后看她做了什么。法律上不能从别人账户里划钱，她就自己掏钱补这位用户；币安支付转账加三次确认；再拿出 10 个 BNB，奖励评论区最好的 10 条产品建议。那条推里她写了一句：“每一次公开的讨论都是我们成功的阶梯。”

钝刀子割了十天，割的是一个肯半夜回评论、肯自掏腰包、肯当着所有人改产品的人。这样的人还站在前面，币安就倒不了。

本质上只是一件很小的事情， 却被某些包藏祸心的人不停地放大渲染 什么心思自己心里有数 内斗没有好处 损失只会让真正的用户承担 不如好好学币安 多想想能为用户做些什么 让大家好好的发展

Some political ideas age better than others.

When I proposed a new model of national service in the 2024 election, it quickly became the butt of jokes. Now France and Germany are taking steps towards it, and in Sweden places are highly prized by teenagers and employers alike.

What I’d seen as prime minister – the constant probing by our enemies, which didn’t distinguish between civilian and military – had convinced me we would soon need some kind of resilience corps. The cyberattacks on European supermarkets, with fridges remotely set to 50C so the food spoils, show this is our new reality. Defence spending won’t stop that. Responsibility for our security can’t just be subcontracted to the military.

In a world in which the government feels obliged to tell us to stockpile tinned goods, our culture needs to change. It will take more than well-stocked cupboards to meet this moment.

A new, universal national service scheme should offer people options. A few might join a small, selective military cadre. Others could serve with search and rescue, St John Ambulance or Meals on Wheels, or train in cybersecurity.

It would make us more resilient and more cohesive, give the almost one million young people not in education, employment or training a sense of purpose, and remind us all that citizenship brings responsibilities as well as rights.

text:
Some thoughts on gas repricings and their impact.

Gas costs increasing for state operations does not mean they get proportionally more expensive, because the gas limit is increasing. What is the point of increasing the costs of these operations but then also increasing the gas limit? The point is scaling: many other operations are currently overpriced, and, by keeping their gas costs fixed and increasing the gas limit, the protocol recognizes this and increases the supply *of those operations only*. The state operations get *relatively* more expensive than these, but not necessarily more expensive in absolute terms. The overall story is that Ethereum is scaling: the gas limit is going up to 200M after being stuck at 30M for years, and most operations are benefitting from this increase in the gas supply (their gas cost is not changing). The ones that are not, like writing new state, will be subject to further scaling efforts in the future.

This is separate from the question of some smart contracts being affected by the repricings and related changes in the gas mechanism. Largely, the impact is on contracts that in one way or another have hardcoded gas costs or made assumptions about them not changing (e.g. if less than X gas remains then this branch reverts). This is unfortunate but somewhat inevitable when gas costs change, which I think is a fairly inevitable step in scaling Ethereum: the current gas costs are basically a decade old, some operations are much cheaper and some much more expensive than their gas cost implies!

It is also unlikely to be the last time they change, because over time gas costs can drift away from being representative of the actual cost of the operations, exactly what brought us to this point. However, this can be the last time that it affects contracts, if it becomes standard practice to not make assumptions about gas costs in the future. Getting this out of the way can be a step towards more immutability, especially if we work to clearly define which invariants should be guaranteed by the execution layer, so that contracts can be written on a solid foundation.

That said, the impact on contracts should have been more deeply investigated sooner, and perhaps more importantly communication about the change should have been more frequent and more direct. It has never been easier to run contract scans (I was able to find some affected contracts just with a few agents and the @SourcifyEth database), and I think it should be a standard practice for protocol upgrades in the future to run such scans with the latest spec, and that app developers should also be encouraged and given tooling to do so with their contracts.

91% of all tokenized stocks lead back to one broker.

Tokenized stocks total $4.60B today and $4.17B of that is backed by real shares held at a single US broker called Alpaca Securities.

- 7 issuers use it - Binance bStocks, Ondo, xStocks, Robinhood, Reality, Coinbase and Dinari.

- Alpaca holds those shares at DTC, the central US securities depository. On the company's books, the owner is Cede & Co., and not you.

- Securitize and Backpack take a different path, through RQD Clearing but still ends at DTC.

- Superstate and Securitize’s ISTs are the only one that skips both. The shares sit on the company's own register, with no broker and no DTC.

In total, that’s 4.7M token holders across those 7 issuers, and one broker between all of them and the real shares.

Now you know.

pi-context-paging 提供了一种新思路：不压缩历史，而是让上下文像操作系统内存一样动态分页。

text:
🙏 LBankers,

It has been one of those periods where there is simply more happening than there are hours in the day.

This quarter is shaping up to be one of our busiest yet. New products are moving forward, our 11th anniversary is still in full swing, new markets are opening, and several bigger initiatives are being built behind the scenes.

So this week, I wanted to take a little more time and bring everyone up to speed on where we are.

Here is what we have been building:

Here is where we are:

1️⃣ One of the biggest developments has been the launch of LBank’s Pre-IPO market, starting with Kalshi-linked tokenized assets issued by Paimon.

The idea is important to me.

Access to high-value private companies has historically been limited by geography, capital requirements, and brokerage infrastructure. Tokenization gives us an opportunity to rethink that model.

The launch has already attracted attention across fintech, institutional and international media.

2️⃣ We also introduced our refreshed brand identity, Yellow Flow.

This is more than a visual change.

LBank today is no longer only spot and futures. We are building across Earn, TradFi, Stock Tokens, Predict, Card, payments, culture, and community.

The new identity reflects that transition from an exchange into a broader digital asset ecosystem.

After 11 years, the brand should evolve with the product.

3️⃣ Lyra Terminal ranked LBank #6 globally for order-book depth, with approximately $32M in ±2% market depth.

For professional traders, this matters more than a slogan ever could.

Depth affects execution, slippage, and how confidently capital can move through a market.

Seeing this independently benchmarked among the world’s leading exchanges is a strong signal that the infrastructure underneath LBank continues to mature.

4️⃣ Our 1,111,111 USDT anniversary celebration is now well into its second half.

Roll to Riches, Apex Arena, Lucky Prize Star, newcomer activities, referral rewards, and Pudgy Penguins activations continue giving different types of users their own way to participate.

The anniversary is a celebration of where we came from, but I care much more about what these 11 years allow us to build next.

5️⃣ We continued developing the social layer of the trading experience through our bullet-chat feature.

Users can now react, share views, use stickers, and participate in market-driven activities directly around the trading interface.

Trading has always been social. CT, Telegram, communities, group chats.

We are simply bringing more of that conversation closer to where the actual trading happens.

6️⃣ LBank Predict Moves Deeper Into Esports 

Prediction markets expanded across the League of Legends Worlds 2026 knockout stage, alongside broader crypto and event-based markets.

I think prediction markets will eventually extend far beyond politics and macro events.

Sports, esports, entertainment, crypto, and culture all create moments where millions of people already have a view.

The product should make it easy to express that view.

7️⃣ Independent Recognition Keeps Compounding 

External coverage continued across the brand refresh, LBank Card, fees, asset coverage, regional positioning, and overall exchange performance.

Different platforms are recognizing different parts of LBank.

That is important because a strong ecosystem should not depend on one narrative.

It should have multiple reasons for users to stay.

The past two weeks have been busy, even by crypto standards.

New markets. New identity. Deeper liquidity. More social products. More ways to participate.

Q4 is moving quickly.

So are we.

More next week.

#LBank #Crypto #Web3 #LBankWeekly

Introducing Arete-27B: Qwen3.8-27B, post-trained to reinforce Western values.

Chinese open models are currently the strongest available, but they ship with state-aligned behavior in the weights. We built an 803-prompt eval across seven value categories, including freedom of expression, democracy, and privacy, and measured how often a model adopts China’s party line.

After fine-tuning on roughly 53 million tokens, Arete-27B's propaganda rate fell from 22% to 1%, in line with the Western models we tested. Its Hermes Bench score shows no significant performance tradeoffs.

The values in an open model are one fine-tune away.

text:
I'm going to give a contrarian take on Neoclouds like $NBIS and say the theme looks compelling after the valuation crash. 

Since there's a reason why Elon's $SPCX is heavily focused on this market full of "guppies" that would die: 

He sees how attractive the economics are after selling compute to $GOOGL and Anthropic. 

And this is reflected by his actions not words, from SpaceX's recent $40B financing for GPUs procurement. 
$AMZN, $MSFT, and even $META also see how profitable the economics are and are accelerating their AI DC buildouts. 

I'd argue if a Neocloud has: 

- Close relationships with $NVDA + others for allocations
- Existing contracted capacity + permitting
- Well funded counterparties, such as Hyperscalers. 
- Attractive economics, such as financing their procurement correctly (not the way $CRWV has with high debt interest unless they refinance). 

Then I think they'll do just fine... 

However, the bigger worry is more toward newer players starting financing or the permitting process, since barrier to entry has now become extremely high. 

For financing, read through on $IREN earnings has shown public Neoclouds can adapt extremely well to tight markets:

As seen with their 90% prepayments for GPU capex on a 5Y deal. 

Their older H100 GPUs recontracted at double their previous pricing and 12% higher contracted pricing also point against depreciation fears. 

And in the case DC buildouts slow from permitting delays... it heavily favors some over others. 

Rosenblatt's recent note for example stated they see little risk with $NBIS primary buildout that was in Missouri, Pennsylvania, and South Carolina. 

And there's probably less risk with developers in places like Australia. 

Markets have also show this infinite compute arbitrage can't go on forever, hence the reluctance to further finance capex, via things like ATMs. 

But ironically, tighter financing and hypothetical restrictive permitting would increase the competitive advantage of established neoclouds. 

And create a larger moat against newer DC developers.

author: PandeyMikhil
quoted_text:
On November 6, three wallets drained our gas wallet using 1-cent trades. The money was the small part. The attack also stopped free trading for everyone for about 54 minutes.

Gas sponsorship

Exfil pays network fees for most trades from a gas wallet we fund, so you can trade from a wallet holding no SOL.

Solana also charges rent to open certain accounts. Whoever opens an account puts up the rent. Whoever owns it can close it and take the rent back.

The attack

Some Pump routes open a small volume account for your wallet when it doesn’t have one. It costs about $0.12 in rent. We chose to pay this ourselves, as a one-time welcome cost per trader.

It’s only one-time if nobody closes the account.

The attacker’s loop was simple:

Sell about 1 cent of a coin. 
We pay the $0.12 rent.
Close the account. 
The rent goes to the attacker.
Repeat about every 10 seconds, on three wallets.

They made about 12 cents a cycle, for almost no risk. It ran 616 times.

On our charts it looked like a burst of selling. One hour showed 567 trades against about 40 the hour before, with only about $6 of volume behind them.

The fix

The rule is now general: Exfil doesn’t pay rent it won’t get back. If we run out of gas we show users how they can pay the gas themselves in the app. 

Before we sign a sponsored trade, we simulate it and measure what the gas wallet would really lose. Any rent left over comes out of the trade. If the trade is too small to cover it, it’s refused and tells you why.

The attack is now a losing trade. You pay $0.12, close the account, get your own $0.12 back, and lose the fees.

No trader’s funds were touched by this.

author: hasufl
quoted_text:
We should continue towards Glam activation asap.

A lot of research went into Glam's strategy to increase opcode gas prices for state creation.

It seems fair to say that the timing of this debate is irrelevant as to its correctness or rightness for eth and our users... Yet, why did some of us (eg. quoted author who is an ef board member) only start looking in detail at Glam EIPs eg. after testnet forks started? This isn't a personal attack, it's an observation that there's a collective responsibility-- for OP, for me, for all of us-- to steward fork strategy at the right times in the process.

imo ethereum's commitments to apps do not extend to gas pricing, or to total ETH fee levels, or to USD fees. And also not to opcode pricing or gas introspection that depends on those prices. We guarantee maximally credibly neutral, maximally live access to the correct state transition function. Those guarantees imply that we always use a neutral pricing mechanism to clear congestion wherever possible. However, pricing opcodes can't use a neutral mechanism, we need to pick magic number opcode gas prices. Some of our best people researched this extensively and picked updated magic numbers, and that's something imo we should stick with now and continue our larger plans that are on track to grow to global ubiquity.

The good news and practical reality may be that the explosion of blockspace supply from 60M to 200M gas limit seems likely to absolutely crater the L1 gas price. It will take time for demand to grow to meet the new supply, including from net new entrants (eg. GENIUS and institutions), induced demand from lower prices, and the coming next gen of return-to-mainnet-type eth native apps. 

By the time L1 blockspace demand catches up, we will be exploding supply again as we get closer to the full lean eth vision. That's eth's vision: postquantum and postAI ETH SoV, supported by ethereum's hypergrowing capacity, which is supported by best-in-class security and formal verification.

Looking back, it's unfortunate that we provided these affected contracts with a footgun that has put them in the situation where they were *able* to rely on fake guarantees that ethereum never promises (afaik, essentially just gas introspection). We're sorry.

imo it's time to roll forward on this. Let's do what we can in an appropriately scoped capacity for the affected contracts, then activate Glam asap, and continue our excellent progress towards global ubiquity.

text:
几乎所有的L2 都采用中心化排序器，但截止目前只有 @Enter_Elysium 因为中心化特权攫取用户价值被骂。

问题出在哪里？我来自问自答。

排序器作为L2 的特权角色，几乎可以完全控制：交易的包含与否、交易的排列顺序、是否公开mempool。即排序器自身就拥有攫取MEV 的能力，不一定非要引入外部MEV bot。

但几乎所有的L2 都选择不主动做MEV 捕获，因为如果排序器自己去sandwich 用户，操纵提取有害MEV，会严重损伤信任。但明面上不能做的事情，不代表背地里不能做，只不过有的L2 做得比较得体，而有的做得比较出格。

主流的L2 排序器会制定一套排序规则（优先费/ FCFS 等），让所有人用同一套提交路径在规则下竞争，MEV bot 之间是相对公平的延迟/ 费用竞赛；

Elysium 制定的排序规则也是基于优先费，不同点在于它采用了两套提交路径：

>部分被授权地址（合作伙伴地址）：直连排序器提交交易，极低延迟

>普通地址：走HyperEVM Delayed Inbox 提交交易，明显更高延迟

text:
YC 今年新晋的 17 家独角兽，几乎快被 AI 包圆了。

Y Combinator 公布了 2026 年 1—10 月诞生的 17 家新独角兽名单，里面有几个挺有意思的信号：

最贵的是 AI 训练数据公司 AfterQuery，估值 32 亿美元；其次是做 AI 医疗福利的 Angle Health，27 亿美元；AI 原生保险公司 Corgi 则达到 26 亿美元。

更值得注意的是，这份名单里不仅有 Emergent 这样的 AI 应用生成平台、Exa 这样的 AI 搜索基础设施，还有 HappyRobot、Avoca 等深入企业具体业务流程的 AI Agent 公司。

甚至连保险、银行、卫星通信、太空数据中心这些看起来相距甚远的行业，也都出现在了名单上。

一个很明显的变化是：AI 创业正在从「帮人完成某项任务」，走向「直接接管某个行业的业务流程」。

过去的 SaaS 公司卖软件，让客户自己干活；现在的新一代 AI 公司，越来越想直接把活干了。

而 YC 这份名单真正有意思的地方，或许不在于又制造了多少家十亿美元公司，而在于独角兽的生产方式正在改变。

以前，创业公司需要证明自己能服务足够多的人；现在，它们开始证明自己能替代足够多的工作。

软件曾经按席位收费，AI 正在试图按工作成果收费。下一代软件巨头，可能看起来越来越不像软件公司。

text:
伊朗战争让美国油企利润大涨，普通家庭却要承担更高的燃油成本

川普发动的伊朗战争让美国油企赚到了更多的钱，但美国普通家庭也在为更高的燃油价格付出代价。

《纽约时报》统计了50多家美国大型油气公司，2026年4月到9月 这些公司的利润合计超过1,300亿美元，去年同期则不到470亿美元，接近去年的三倍。

其中埃克森美孚第三季度净利润达到154亿美元，去年同期约75亿美元，雪佛龙赚了99亿美元，去年同期约35亿美元。

伊朗战争影响了中东的能源生产和运输，也推高了全球油价。美国油企即使没有在冲突地区生产，也能因为油价上涨卖出更高的价格。而汽油、柴油等成品油供应紧张，价格上涨，也让部分美国炼油企业赚到了更多利润。

但对于普通家庭来说，燃油价格上涨带来的就是更高的生活成本。根据布朗大学的估算，从2月28日战争开始到10月底，和没有战争的情况相比，美国汽油和柴油的额外支出约为1,470亿美元，按全美家庭数量平均，每户超过1,100美元。

而且燃油价格上涨会直接推高能源通胀，而企业的运输和生产成本上升后，也可能把一部分成本转嫁到食品和其他商品的价格上。如果油价长时间保持高位，也会给美国整体通胀带来持续的压力。

text:
你说，这是一个暧昧的时代。

模型能力的暧昧，技术路线的暧昧，估值的暧昧，AGI时间表的暧昧。评测榜单说 MMLU 提升了 2.3 个百分点，团队通宵做海报，投资人群里连发三个🐮。第二天用户拿同一个模型写请假条，它还是把“领导”写成“领到”。人在这样不清不楚的周期里工作，逐渐习惯了所有事情都留有余地。

“等模型再迭代一版”，究竟是承诺，还是拖延？“下周发版”里的下周又是哪一周？“等评测结果出来再说”里的结果，是跑分，还是客户预算？人们擅长用一些不承担日期的词语安排路线图，听的人心领神会，或者装作心领神会。说到底，大家都想保留一点余地，就算效果不行，也要说得像一次暂时的 bad case。

有人每天分享 demo、benchmark 和融资消息，知道对方用多少张卡、采了多少数据，知道对方前天崩了服务、昨天挂了评测、今天又调了一版 prompt。两个人熟悉到可以辨认彼此 loss 曲线里的情绪，却说不清自己究竟以什么身份存在于这条产业链里：是底座，是应用，是中间层，是给甲方做 POC 的外包，还是“我们其实也在自研模型”的乙方。

现代大模型公司的商业模式，大概像一种尚未正式发行的货币。人人都相信它有价值，真正需要兑换的时候，却找不到愿意承认它的银行。更准确地说，是找不到愿意按 ARR 付费的客户。Demo 里什么都能做，合同里什么都得再谈；发布会讲的是智能涌现，交付时聊的是并发、延迟和私有化部署。

评测结果出来，分数不高不低。MMLU 八十六，榜单中游。PR 稿说“多项指标领先”，投资人说“其实已经不错了”，工程师看着评测集发呆，既没有理由庆祝，也找不到值得回滚一版的地方。八十六分就是这样一个数字，往上够不着 SOTA，往下又远离“不能用”。它就这样安静地躺在榜单截图里，等待市场替它解释意义。

长大以后，越来越常得到这种答案。

一份尚可的模型，一段还行的合作关系，一座住得下去的城市。投资人说过会再联系，客户说最近预算比较紧，医生说先观察一段时间，监管说先看看行业实践。生活里有太多事情被暂时搁置，像电脑里那些命名为“最终版”的模型文件，过了几天又出现最终版2、最终版3、final_final_真的最终版。

有一天，我在街上看到一家正在装修的店。玻璃门上贴着“即将开业”四个字，里面堆着纸箱，灯已经装好了，墙面也刷得很漂亮。过了两个月，我再次路过，那张纸还贴在那里，边角被太阳晒得卷起来。后来我刷到一家 AI 公司，官网挂着“即将发布”。又过了两个月，我打开那家公司的官网，页面还是“内测中，敬请期待”。我站在屏幕前看了一会儿，突然觉得它与我们很像。

总有一些事情处在即将发生的阶段。即将毕业，即将恋爱，即将 AGI，即将开始自己真正想过的生活。日子一天一天过去，我们始终站在某个尚未抵达的地方，忙着为下一阶段做准备。

情绪也好暧昧吧。有人问最近过得怎么样，想了半天，最后回答还好。有人问模型效果怎么样，想了半天，最后回答：整体表现良好，仍有提升空间。它容纳了幻觉、延迟、上下文截断、偶尔惊艳、没有解决的 bad case 和一次很漂亮的 demo。再问下去，也实在没有什么值得特别讲述的事情。今天与昨天差不多，明天大概也不会有很大的变化，除了版本号从 0.9.1 变成 0.9.2。

我想，这个大模型行业最有趣的地方，是所有人都在要求明确。

要明确的商业化，明确的技术路线，明确的 AGI 时间表，明确的监管边界。填表的时候，方框总是整齐地排列着：开源或闭源，To B 或 To C，Scaling Law 或算法创新，已完成或未完成。可真正做起来，很多事情根本没有对应的选项。

模型能力，有时强到百分之六十，有时只有百分之三十。对某条路线感到失望，第二天又觉得可以再等等。昨天信誓旦旦说不再刷榜的人，今天仍然会在朋友圈发一张榜单截图。人们用十分确定的语气说着一些随时可能改变的话。

你说，这是一个暧昧的大模型行业。

那天我们坐在发布会后排，隔着人群看见台上大屏切到一张 demo。模型回答得很慢，字幕一行一行往外蹦。有人鼓掌，有人低头回消息，有人把 PPT 拍下来发到群里。你问我，AGI 还有多远。

我看了看大屏，说，快了吧。

后来我们谁也没有再提起这个问题。

text:
聊聊对加密态度强硬的民主党参议员伊丽莎白沃伦如果担任参议员银行委员会主席对加密的影响是什么？这两天都在担心民主党掌控国会后加密也会被清算，特别是前两天华尔街日报报道了沃伦27年1月将会担心参议员银行委员会主席这种担心就更强了。还是会到前几天聊老马被“清算”时候的框架：要从立法权和行政权区分的角度去看、沃伦或者民主党能做什么不能做什么？

1、先看沃伦对加密的态度：
 1）反洗钱义务应深入加密网络。 她希望监管覆盖更多钱包服务商、矿工、验证者及其他参与者。
2）保护传统金融体系与储户。 她特别担心银行将加密风险带入存款、信贷和支付体系。
3）防止通过代币化规避证券法。 她反对企业仅凭资产上链，就获得比传统证券更宽松的待遇。
4）限制政治人物通过加密获利。 特朗普第二任期以来，利益冲突成为她推动调查和阻止法案的重要抓手

2、首先民主党掌控了国会多数席位、沃林就任银行委员会主席。参议院银行委员会的权力不小，但它是立法和监督机构，不能直接代替监管机构执法。职责包含银行、证券市场、货币、金融机构等。能做什么？

1）推动新的加密立法议程、今年清晰法案在参议院受阻沃伦反对是最关键的一步，特别是道德条款上。那么沃伦会推动新的更严格的立法程序么？大概率会的 

但我们要看到今年共和党在两院占优的情况下推动《清晰法案》，无法争取足够民主党支持，也无法跨过参议院的程序门槛。那么未来两年民主党推动全面收紧加密的新法案，同样会遇到共和党的阻力。普通法案在参院的最终通过通常只需简单多数，但遭遇阻挠议事时，结束辩论一般需要60票的绝对多数。

还有一种情况，即使民主党成功让强硬法案通过两院，川普仍可否决。推翻总统否决，需要两院各自达到三分之二票数，门槛更高。
所以，在双方没有重大妥协的情况下，大幅放松和大幅收紧的加密新立法，都可能推进困难。 沃伦的强硬主张不会因为她成为委员会主席，就直接变成法律

2）把针对特朗普加密业务的质疑，升级为持续的委员会调查。但需要明确国会的调查、听证 ，不会自动构成刑事定罪。其实对于川普加密业务的调查我是乐于看到的、确实影响很恶劣。然后银行委员会估计还会发起对sec、cftc以及加密企业的一系列的调查、这会对加密市场产生冲击和影响。

但要明确，国会调查和听证只限于此，并不等于刑事定罪。如果要进一步就需要司法部配合提供诉讼，但未来两年司法部还是在共和党掌控；

3）决定川普提名金融监管领域的人事任命，
如果川普未来两年提名sec和cftc的委员，这个任命流程需要通过银行委员会的批准。

3、还说要把立法权和行政权分开
未来两年SEC、CFTC主席依然现在共和党人担任，在这些监管机构的法定权限内推动政策，无需得到国会的批准。

沃伦可以要求监管机构的负责人出席听证、解释政策依据，要求提供相关文件，也可以公开批评某项豁免过度宽松。这些监督动作本身，不会使政策自动停止或失效。

例如SEC在今年9月推出附条件的代币化股票交易豁免；CFTC在10月启动CTX／CAM框架的前期征求意见，均是在运用其所主张的现行法律授权。

所以在川普继续执政、SEC和CFTC领导层继续支持加密发展的前提下，共和党即使拿不到新法律，监管机构仍可以使用已有权限推进。民主党若想彻底改变这些权限或强制收紧政策，通常需要跨过立法和总统否决的门槛。

4、当然不是说完全没影响，整体来看：
沃伦能够阻碍新增立法，并显著增加监管和企业的压力，全面立法继续困难，同时面临更密集的监督和法律争议。某些政策可能拖慢，某些豁免可能缩小。机构也可能为提高规则的法律稳固性，加入更多限制条件。一次措辞激烈的听证会，可能让市场紧张、产生冲击。

但现有授权内的加密政策仍可继续推进，SEC和CFTC也会各自权限范围内推进新的政策。

未来两年加密监管环境其实不会比23-24年更严格（当时是民主党执政、参议院民主党多数、CfTC和司法部都是民主党人掌控）。
