quoted_text:
民主党拿到参众两院多数席位，老马会被“清算”么？先说个人观点，但凡说被“清算”的可能都不是很理解美国政治的运作逻辑，也不懂立法权和行政权的边界在哪里。但对spacex和特斯拉短期走势有没有影响？那应该还是有影响的，因为短期内还是会有资金担心老马被“清算”导致spacex和特斯拉股价📉，但这反倒提供了更好的上车机会。聊聊个人看法。
1、民主党拿到参众两院的多数席位，但都不是超过2/3的绝对多数，只是简单多数。

川普未来两年还是总统，财政部、国防部、商务部、司法部、NASA、联邦贸易委员会FCC等跟老马企业业务密切相关的政府监管机构还在共和党手里。

我们要厘定立法权和行政权的边界。

2、那民主党能做什么？
1）听证会与调查（最可能且立即）：
多个委员会（众院Oversight、Armed Services、Science/Space/Technology；参院相关委员会）会启动调查和听证会。
直指老马去年主导DOGE事务、spaceX与NASA和太空军各个合同竞标与执行情况，星链的使用问题，外国投资（尤其中国相关指控）、潜在并购的国家安全/反垄断含义、AI/Grok合同与使用。会传唤马斯克/高管、索取文件、举行公开听证会

2）合同与拨款监督：审查现有与未来订单（NASA Crew/HLS、Space Force NSSL/Starshield/Golden Dome相关）。通过拨款法案影响未来资金水平、附加条件或要求审查。不能轻易单方面取消已授固定价格合同（需正当理由如表现问题），但可拖延新授标、制造压力。

3）立法与监管施压：推动更严AI监管、内容/平台规则（影响X）、EV/自动驾驶规则、合同透明度/利益冲突规则。并购可能被听证拖慢。对Tesla更多是监管环境变化而非直接合同。但立法需要川普签字、监管施压需要行政机构配合。

3、其实这些动作大部分形式大于实质
听证会、传票、公开质询更多的人是政治秀，最大的作用消耗高管时间、制造负面新闻、股价波动、投资者风险溢价。能通过媒体和舆论放大担忧。

没有行政机构的配合，国会的听证、质询和调查是落不了地的。

机构执行、合同管理、监管执法在白宫/国防部/NASA手中。国会可调查施压，但直接“停单”或大规模诉讼需行政机构的执行配合，如果想完整立法需过两院并可能面临川普否决。

4、州一级的动作可能影响更大，关键是得州
这一次民主党在得州大翻盘，出现了90年代以来的第一位民主党得州州长。

得克萨斯州是马斯克企业版图的绝对核心。他本人已从加州搬迁至得州奥斯汀，特斯拉（Tesla）全球总部和超级工厂（Gigafactory）位于奥斯汀。位于得州南端博卡奇卡（Boca Chica）的“星基地”（Starbase）是其SpaceX星舰发射的核心阵地。

这些庞大的固定资产无法搬走，使得州政治环境的走向（如土地使用、本地居民抗议及法律诉讼等）也决定了老马核心业务的状态。

但换个角度看，民主党州长上台可能监管要求提高、提高税收，但不能说她就完全不顾本州经济的发展了。毕竟无论特斯拉和spaceX都算是得州的支柱性企业、得州本身也受益于特斯拉和sapcex的发展，并且本地关系利益也很大。

所以得州的动作会有影响，个人判断更多是“两点”：监管多一点、税收多一点。

整体上来说，
未来两年川普任期内、说民主党“清算”老马其实有点过度夸大了、但不能说完全没影响。但这个影响大概率是短期的、暂时的。个人角度倒是希望这种担忧能让spacex股价下去给我们更好的上车机会。

text:
说个大胆推测：Neocloud板块有机会复制25-26年的存储行情。 $CRWV $NBIS $IREN 

逻辑:

1, 现在的叙事：

Neocloud 活不下去了，融资成本高，巨头客户订单取消，被负债拖垮，陷入死亡螺旋；

民主党上台限制DC建设；

2，实际情况是：

目前市场有500家neocloud，上市的这几家已经算是规模比较大，融资能力比较强的。大规模死掉的可能是这些美上市的neocloud。

微软取消了没法交付或者延迟交付的订单，以及不再续约oracle老旧GPU（A100）的订单。

text:
近半年国内头部大模型一号位里，最值得细品的一场英文深度访谈来了。

MiniMax 创始人闫俊杰首次做客顶级长线基金 Scottish Mortgage（柏基旗下信托，今年初参与了 MiniMax 港股 IPO 大赚两倍，同时也是 Anthropic 股东）的官方播客，与投资经理聊了 53 分钟。

全片信息密度极高，直接聊透了国产大模型怎么用 1/10 的算力成本，逼近硅谷顶尖水平，一年跑出 8 亿美金 ARR 的商业账本，以及接下来半年多模态和智能体的核心变局。

我从中提炼了 10 条有启发的笔记：

1、最后 5% 的鸿沟 vs 95% 的商业甜点区。

国产大模型目前能用 1/10 的成本，做到美国前沿模型 95% 的性能。闫俊杰直言“最后 5% 比前 95% 难追得多”，但商业世界的本质是算 ROI。

举个例子，最顶尖的那 5% 可以去攻克癌症，剩下 95% 的日常写代码、审合同、企业工作流，够用的性能加上 1/10 的地板价，才能让企业大规模买单，创造经济价值。

2、低推理成本 = 更大的后训练规模

近两年模型在 Coding 和复杂任务上的跃迁，全靠后训练（强化学习 RL + 数据合成），而每一次 RL 试错，本质上都是一次推理调用。

3、算力约束逼出“芯片无关”架构。

美国实验室被充裕的算力富养，训练前习惯烧钱跑海量实验探路，中国团队受限于高端 GPU，从第一天就被迫设计不挑芯片的架构，靠工程优化压榨单卡极限。

不能靠堆显卡大力出奇迹，就倒逼研究员减少无效实验押注、精准预判技术方向。硬件上的长期饥饿感，反而熬出了极高的资本效率和算法壁垒。

4、开源不是做慈善，是商业化与创新的催化剂。

OpenAI 走闭源收过路费，MiniMax 承诺一路开源直到实现 AGI。开源既解决了政企客户私有化部署的数据主权焦虑，又能靠全球开发者建立起最强的产品反馈回路。

比如视频模型 H3 单月下载量达 2500 万次，两周内长出 300 多个衍生模型。https://t.co/g44JrGxjKP 团队基于它做后训练推出 H3 Max，3 秒生成 5 秒视频，直接催生出“24 小时 AI 实时直播”。

5、多模态即将“大一统”，语言大脑 + 视频手脚合体。

目前 MiniMax 已收敛为 M 系列（语言/生产力）和 H 系列（视频/多模态）两大家族，接下来几个月内，会将二者合并为一个统一模型。

6、智能体的下一站，长程任务的目标自主性。

闫俊杰透露本月所有时间，都花在未发布的下一代模型 M3 Pro 上。

他认为智能体的下一个前沿，不只是在长程任务上比拼执行力，而是自己设定目标，自己验证结果。

7、B2B 扛起现金流，8 亿美元 ARR 的盈利飞轮。

截至今年 8 月，MiniMax 的 ARR 突破 8 亿美元，其中超 80% 来自 B2B 企业端 API 调用。

虽然上半年仍亏损近 3 亿美元，但研发支出增速已开始低于销售增速。AI 的利润不靠涨价，靠的是技术创新压低推理成本，让收入增速跑赢算力成本。

8、中美 AI 生态分叉：资本封闭帝国 vs 效率协作网络。

不要再用硅谷的模板套中国 AI，美国靠巨额资本与芯片冗余建封闭系统，中国靠单卡效率建开源协作生态，两边不会收敛到同一条路。

9、500 人抗衡科技巨头的铁律，极简架构 + 基建先行。

面对大厂和 20 多家大模型创企的混战，MiniMax 500 人的团队靠两条研发铁律突围，一是架构极简化，二是哪怕出货慢一点，也永远先把底层基建修好。

10、AGI 的硬核标准与 Intelligence with Everyone。

什么时候才算真正实现 AGI？闫俊杰给出的定义极其硬核：当 AI 能独立提出全新的科学理论，人类科学突破主要靠 AI 驱动时。

而把口号定为与所有人同在，核心在于通过开源权重，让开发者与用户真正拥有 AI 的所有权。

text:
A few people have been asking about my Grok Bot setup. This is one of the skills I actively use.

It’s called /optimize. A reusable skill for checking and improving speed, e.g. 

• N+1 SQL queries → joins or batched reads.
• Repeated database reads → caching or Redis where it makes sense.
• Serverless connections → connection pooling.
• Sequential API calls → parallel requests.
• Heavy JavaScript → code splitting and lazy loading.
• Blocking tasks → background jobs.
• Waiting for a full AI response → token streaming.

It measures first, applies safe fixes on a separate branch, then runs the same tests again. You get the before-and-after results and a list of what it couldn’t measure.

We used it on a simple internal app we were building. It found a duplicate page load and repeated data reads. Fixing those cut the time from choosing a role to seeing the overview by 32–40% on repeat visits.

Free and open source. Setup instructions for Grok Bot, Claude Code and Cursor:
https://t.co/3P8stVnU4C

AI 革命还没被技术卡住，倒是先被数据中心附近的居民卡住了。

「木头姐」Cathie Wood 最新发帖，谈到了美国 AI 基建正在遭遇的一个现实问题：越来越多社区开始反对在当地建设数据中心。

她认为，社区反对无法阻挡 AI 革命，但数据中心企业必须改变做法。不能只顾着建机房、抢电力、堆 GPU，还得认真回应当地居民的顾虑，讲清楚项目究竟能带来多少税收、就业机会，以及对学校和公共服务的投入。

她还给出了一个更乐观的长期判断：AI 带来的生产率提升，最终会转化为更高的工资和更低的物价，让整个社会受益。

但这里有一个很微妙的矛盾。

AI 的收益是面向全社会的，成本却往往是由数据中心所在地的居民率先承担的。

科技公司谈的是十年后的生产率革命，当地居民关心的却是明年的电费、今天的噪音，以及自己家门口的土地会变成什么样。

更重要的是，生产率提升不等于收益自动公平分配。AI 可以创造巨大的经济价值，但这些价值究竟流向科技巨头、资本所有者，还是普通劳动者，仍然是一个开放问题。

过去，硅谷习惯用「改变世界」来争取资本。现在，它可能还得学会用「改善社区」来争取居民。

AI 基建的下一场竞争，可能不只是抢芯片、抢电力、抢土地，而是谁能让当地人相信，这场革命也有自己的一份。

But first, we lost a dear friend this week. John Nosta believed in ARK from the very beginning, even when many others did not. He joined our Brainstorm discussions for years, sharing his incredible intellect and his perspective on technology and the human condition. Above all, he was a devoted husband and father. We will miss him dearly.
 
John had just published "The Borrowed Mind: Reclaiming Human Thought in the Age of AI." I hope you will consider buying John’s book to support his family and to honor his legacy.
 
Turning to the election, while we thought President Trump would end the Iran War in months, the equity market started discounting a more prolonged war and a Democrat sweep in the election in May and June as higher oil and gasoline prices added to the affordability pressures facing consumers. Inside the congressional results, “pocketbook voters” leaned the results more to the conservative side of the spectrum than headlines captured.
 
Can this election derail the AI revolution? We don’t think so. Companies building data centers are likely to be much more sensitive to the concerns of local communities and to provide and highlight more of the benefits: lower property taxes, higher paying jobs, commercial development, and funding for more schools and cultural facilities.
 
Meanwhile, productivity gains are accelerating thanks to AI. In our view, those gains will translate into higher compensation—helping to turn around affordability—, as well as stronger margins, more investment, and lower prices.
 
We have experienced just a taste of this technology revolution. The market’s uncertainty is understandable, but we believe the economy is on a stronger growth trajectory than most investors recognize.
 
In this month’s In The Know, I put the election and market volatility into that longer-term perspective.

知名加密博主Ansem @blknoiz06 采访Backpack 交易所CEO Armani @armaniferrante 

大概的谈了几件事情：

1. FTX 之后重建
•Backpack 当年拿了 FTX 等钱，FTX 崩盘时丢了约 90% 资金，公司实质已死，没关、进「蟑螂模式」零资金硬转。

•芝加哥办公室对着世界地图做了 四年合规扩张计划，现在有阿联酋、塞浦路斯、拉脱维亚、日本、澳大利亚、美国等布局。

•自比：Hyperliquid = 下一代 DEX；Backpack = 下一代 CEX，专门修 FTX 之后交易所的旧病。

•差异化：几乎所有新交易所都在冲增长，他们押 受监管路径；今天大约只服务 全球 48% 人口，他希望年底能打开更多市场。

2. 美股上 Solana

•现在 Solana 上约 88 个股票标的，下一步要扩到 几千个，并复制到日股、港股。

•刚和 SK Securities 合作，要把 韩国市场 搬上链。

•目标：不只做 DeFi，还要重做 TradFi；把 Solana 从「链」变成「全球价值入口」。

3. 代币化 + 岸上 Perps

•稳定币已起飞，下一难关是 股票上链；股票一旦 24/7，固定收益、期权、房产都会跟着来。

•举 Hyperliquid × Kraken（Payward）：用受监管壳叠在链上技术上，才能接机构资金。

•他认为岸上衍生品下一波是 Perps：Robinhood 教了千禧一代期权，Kalshi/Polymarket 教了 Gen Z 预测市场，FOMO/POMP/Axiom 教了更年轻一代 meme，下一波就是 Perps。

•SEC 侧提到 tokenized security venues 的创新豁免；政治有逆风，但大趋势是合规上岸。

4. 安全、MEV、代币激励

•安全优先：被黑了就没法增长；财务黑客后他让全队一周只盯安全。

•狠批「代币工业」：募资讲故事 → TGE 派对 → 拉盘 → 对散户砸盘；亚洲会上有人公开做这套，必须「烧死」。

• solana:BPxxfRCXkUVhig4HS1Lh7kZqV6SPJhzfEk4x6fVBjPCy 设计：TGE 发出约 24.5%；约 37.5% 给用户增长/里程碑；团队 37.5% 锁在资产负债表，IPO 后一年才解锁，无基金会旁路。他明确说：币涨了也不能卖去「加固资产负债表」——代币经济写死了。承诺只有一条：内部人不砸盘。

5. 长期愿景

•先全美股，再区域市场；然后是借贷（提到 @kamino Juper ,meme vs 股票、用户自建篮子/ETF、拆解营收流（如只买 SpaceX 里的 Starlink）。

•愿景：每个 App 都变成券商（Gido/GTX、Phantom、Solflare、X、三星钱包等）。

•Solana 要赢的 KPI ≈ 链上资产规模/资金沉淀；零售侧在走，机构侧（转账代理、DTC 代币化、银行/券商）更慢但更粘。

一句话：Armani 把 Backpack 定位成 合规上岸的下一代券商+交易所，核心叙事是 股票上链 → 岸上 Perps → 整套金融互联网化，并用极端锁定的 solana:BPxxfRCXkUVhig4HS1Lh7kZqV6SPJhzfEk4x6fVBjPCy 来跟「发币砸盘」那套划清界限。

author: Xudong07452910
quoted_text:
我们都知道模型变强之后，以前精心设计的 Agent Skill 可能成了负担，但是怎么去除不必要的 skills 很多人却不知道。

Garry Tan @garrytan 的做法很值得借鉴。他用 Eval 对比了 Opus 5.5 开启和关闭 /investigate 的表现，发现修复率没有明显差异，但每修好一个 Bug 的成本反而高了 43%，于是决定砍掉它。

我觉得这个思路应该成为 Harness Engineering 的常规操作。

比如以前为了提高 Coding Agent 的可靠性，我们设计了「先生成详细计划，再逐步排查问题」的 Workflow。

模型升级后，就可以用同一批真实任务做 A/B Eval，一组保留旧流程，一组直接让模型执行，多次测试，对比成功率、Token 消耗和执行时间。

如果旧流程已经带不来稳定的提升，甚至增加了成本，那就该考虑简化或移除。

Agent 的 Skill 和 Harness 也需要定期做减法。模型在进化，我们为旧模型设计的工作方式也应该重新验证。

text:
OKX上线简易期权：普通用户多了一种交易选择，但它真的足够好吗？

11月4日okx上线了“简易期权”功能，因为之前我也自学过一段时间期权，所以就尝试研究了一下，后来我总结了以下几点，有好有坏吧！

先说对普通用户的优势：

1，交易门槛明显降低，传统美股期权单笔100股为一份合约，OKX简易期权可以做到最低支持0.01份合约，资金门槛更低

2，风险对冲多了一项工具，单纯的合约本身属于增加杠杠的行为，是让自己资产风险敞口扩大，尤其是在高波动阶段，所以很多人会选择借助其他产品做对冲。以美股为例，从现货与永续合约之间又多了一个期权选择，但是会用这些产品做对冲的人还是少数。

3，账户资金可利用率明显增加，简易期权支持买入看涨、看跌，还有卖出看涨与看跌期权，理论上可选择性多了不少，但是实际上对于0知识的期权用户，可能需要先学习才能理解这里面的逻辑

4，加密特性7✖️24小时，提高了交易的灵活性，不受传统美股交易日影响， @okxchinese   的简易期权支持7✖️24小时全天候价格问询，对于加密本土用户根据被适配性。但是，这里虽然支持全天候报价，但是报价是否是理想报价，有待考证

我认为略微不足的地方：

1，零手续费并不代表交易没有磨损，尤其是在美股休盘阶段，买卖价差可能会让成本磨损增加，例如大部分的Trad Fi产品都有一个致命问题，休盘阶段资金费率极高，不利于长期持有某个资产。

2，操作虽然看似简单，但是并没有改变期权产品的复杂性，尤其是对于很多用户来说，如何理解买入看涨、看跌，以及卖出看涨看跌，这都是一个问题，期权本身学习门槛就很高，所以我觉得OKX还得上线一些期权交易的教育服务会更好

不过整体来看，这次OKX仅仅上线了4种资产的期权交易，应该也是作为一个试点去做的，后续应该会有配套相关的教育板块出现来引导更多的用户学习期权

其实对于普通用户来说，金融产品创新未必要代表着增加更加复杂的功能，有时候正好恰恰相反，让原本专业的金融交易工具变得简单化、平民化，让用户更容易参与，降低使用门槛反而好的方向！

text:
Most 3D reconstruction models crumble when faced with messy, real-world photo collections—think thousands of photos of the same object, snapped by strangers over decades, with wildly different cameras and settings.

Enter TRAINSPOTTING: 12,068 Wikimedia Commons objects and 311,886 photos, each with accurate camera poses, depth maps, and masks. The new pipeline combines SAM3, RoMa v2, COLMAP, and CasDiffMVS to build reliable 3D supervision from internet chaos.

Fine-tuning VGGT-Ω on this data (plus 15% replay) yields SPOTTER, a model that jumps camera-pose AUC@30 from 25→81 on TRAINSPOTTING and 19→76 on NAVI in-the-wild, slashing depth errors and leaving classical benchmark results untouched.

Key takeaway: it’s not dataset size, but diversity across environments and instances, that unlocks generalisation. This opens the door to automatic, crowd-sourced 3D digitisation—from e-commerce previews to historical preservation—without expensive custom captures.

text:
“相信”的成本很高，正因如此，中本聪创造BTC的初衷之一就是为了解决“信任问题”。

“信任”是相互的，我可以相信比特币，可以相信以太坊，但我可以相信一个ALT和他背后的团队吗？

这是留在大家心中最大的怀疑。

就像 @NeoSoulAI 的推文所说：如今的市场，信任已经耗尽；交易所、VC、项目方、社区.....每一方都在等着别人先相信。

所以他们打算先迈出这一步，决定首先承担风险，让团队获得经济利益的权利与项目执行成果联系起来。

这种尝试，有别与其他项目代币采用固定时间表解锁的方式，并希望以此获得包括社区在内的其他方的“信任”。

这能成功吗？没人知道。

成功需要“天时/地利/人和”，但不得不说这是一次勇敢的尝试，总得有人迈出第一步。

希望本是无所谓有，无所谓无的。这正如地上的路；其实地上本没有路，走的人多了，也便成了路......

text:
AI 还没大规模抢走女性的工作，女性可能已经先被挡在 AI 带来的晋升机会之外了。

《华盛顿邮报》最近关注了一个容易被忽视的问题。AI 正在改变职场，但这场技术革命的红利，可能从一开始就没有被公平分配。

报道指出，女性员工不仅使用 AI 工具的比例更低，获得 AI 培训、导师指导和工作支持的机会也更少。

这件事最值得警惕的地方在于，表面上看是男女员工使用 AI 的意愿不同，背后却可能是企业资源分配的问题。

谁能优先接触新工具？谁能获得培训预算？谁有机会参与 AI 项目？谁的 AI 能力会被管理层看见？

这些看似不起眼的决定，最终可能变成下一轮晋升和薪酬差距。

更微妙的是，AI 很可能会放大这种差距。先获得资源的人更容易积累经验，经验又成为获得更多资源的理由。久而久之，最初的机会不平等，就会被包装成个人能力的差异。

过去，职场性别差距经常体现为同工不同酬；到了 AI 时代，它可能提前发生在「谁有机会学会使用 AI」这个环节。

技术本身未必偏袒谁，但分配技术红利的组织，未必是公平的。

text:
01. Tractian | 估值 $1.4B | W21 | 美国

总部位于美国的Tractian是一家结合工业物联网传感器与AI技术的机器维护平台。它通过实时收集工厂设备的振动、温度等数据，利用AI算法进行预测性维护，帮助企业在设备故障前发现问题，从而大幅减少停机时间，背后有Sapphire Ventures和General Catalyst等机构支持。

02. Blacksmith | 估值 $1B | W24 | 美国

估值10亿美元的Blacksmith为软件开发者提供用于代码构建与测试的云平台。它致力于提供高效的云端基础设施环境，专门优化CI/CD（持续集成与交付）流程，让开发团队能更快速、安全地测试和部署代码，目前已获得红杉资本（Sequoia）和Peak XV等知名机构的投资。

03. Hubble Network | 估值 $1.6B | W22 | 美国

Hubble Network正在构建一个创新的太空级蓝牙网络，旨在让现有的普通蓝牙设备无需添加额外硬件即可直接连接卫星。这一技术实现了全球范围的物联网覆盖，为追踪器和传感器提供无处不在的连接服务，主要投资方包括Smith Point Capital等。

04. Angle Health | 估值 $2.7B | W20 | 美国

美国公司Angle Health是一家面向小型企业的AI健康福利平台。它利用AI技术重塑健康保险体验，为中小企业提供更灵活、高性价比的员工福利方案，并大幅简化理赔与健康管理流程，得到了Vitruvian Partners和Bloomberg Capital的支持。

05. AfterQuery | 估值 $3.2B | W25 | 美国

估值高达32亿美元的AfterQuery专注于提供由各领域专家制作的高质量AI训练数据。在大模型时代，该公司通过组织人类专家生成、评估和标注数据，用于微调和显著提升AI模型的性能，是Altos Ventures和BoxGroup看好的底层数据服务商。

06. HappyRobot | 估值 $1.2B | S23 | 美国

HappyRobot致力于开发用于企业日常运营的AI智能体（AI Agents）。这些“数字员工”能够自动执行客户沟通、物流调度或后台数据处理等任务，显著提升企业的自动化水平，获得了Prysm Capital和a16z等机构的注资。

07. Emergent | 估值 $1.5B | S24 | 印度

作为榜单中少有的印度公司，Emergent提供面向非程序员的AI应用构建器。通过其无代码/低代码平台，没有编程背景的用户也能利用自然语言或可视化界面轻松创建和部署AI驱动的应用程序，背后有Khosla Ventures和软银愿景基金2号的支持。

08. Exa | 估值 $2.2B | S21 | 美国

估值22亿美元的Exa是一家专为AI设计的网页搜索引擎公司。不同于传统面向人类的搜索，Exa通过提供API接口，帮助大语言模型在互联网上高效、精准地检索实时信息，解决AI的“知识更新”痛点，获得了a16z和NVIDIA的青睐。

09. Radar | 估值 $1B | W13 | 美国

美国公司Radar利用射频识别（RFID）技术和AI视觉算法，为实体零售店提供实时、高精度的库存追踪和管理方案。该系统能有效优化门店供应链并减少缺货情况，是Founders Fund等机构支持的零售科技独角兽。

10. Corgi | 估值 $2.6B | S24 | 美国

估值26亿美元的Corgi是一家AI原生的保险科技公司（Insurtech），专为初创和科技企业提供现代商业保险服务。它利用AI技术重构了保险的核保和理赔流程，提供定制化、快速的保险产品，主要投资方包括TCV和Kindred Ventures。
author: Lynncc6
quoted_text:
YC 今年新晋的 17 家独角兽，几乎快被 AI 包圆了。

Y Combinator 公布了 2026 年 1—10 月诞生的 17 家新独角兽名单，里面有几个挺有意思的信号：

最贵的是 AI 训练数据公司 AfterQuery，估值 32 亿美元；其次是做 AI 医疗福利的 Angle Health，27 亿美元；AI 原生保险公司 Corgi 则达到 26 亿美元。

更值得注意的是，这份名单里不仅有 Emergent 这样的 AI 应用生成平台、Exa 这样的 AI 搜索基础设施，还有 HappyRobot、Avoca 等深入企业具体业务流程的 AI Agent 公司。

甚至连保险、银行、卫星通信、太空数据中心这些看起来相距甚远的行业，也都出现在了名单上。

一个很明显的变化是：AI 创业正在从「帮人完成某项任务」，走向「直接接管某个行业的业务流程」。

过去的 SaaS 公司卖软件，让客户自己干活；现在的新一代 AI 公司，越来越想直接把活干了。

而 YC 这份名单真正有意思的地方，或许不在于又制造了多少家十亿美元公司，而在于独角兽的生产方式正在改变。

以前，创业公司需要证明自己能服务足够多的人；现在，它们开始证明自己能替代足够多的工作。

软件曾经按席位收费，AI 正在试图按工作成果收费。下一代软件巨头，可能看起来越来越不像软件公司。

text:
11. Avoca | 估值 $1B | W23 | 美国

Avoca是一家面向家庭服务企业（如家政、维修、清洁）提供AI智能体的公司。其AI语音助手能帮助企业自动接听电话、预约排期和跟进客户，有效防止漏单并提升运营效率，获得了General Catalyst和Kleiner Perkins等机构的投资。

12. Slash | 估值 $1.4B | S21 | 美国

Slash为现代企业提供一体化的银行与支付平台。它将商业银行账户、企业信用卡以及支付处理能力结合在一起，帮助企业更高效地管理现金流，是Ribbit Capital和Khosla Ventures投资的金融科技新星。

13. Starcloud | 估值 $2.3B | S24 | 美国

这家估值23亿美元的美国公司正在探索将数据中心部署在太空轨道上。Starcloud通过在轨数据中心利用太空丰富的太阳能和极低温环境进行散热，旨在彻底解决地球上数据中心面临的能耗和散热瓶颈，由Benchmark和EQT Ventures投资。

14. Eight Sleep | 估值 $1.5B | S15 | 美国

Eight Sleep是智能家居领域的知名品牌，其核心产品是具备动态温度调节和睡眠健康监测功能的智能温控床垫。该产品旨在通过科技手段显著提高用户的睡眠质量，近期获得了Tether、Founders Fund和软银等机构的资金支持。

15. TRM Labs | 估值 $1B | S19 | 美国

TRM Labs是一家提供区块链数据分析和合规平台的公司。它帮助金融机构、政府和企业追踪加密货币交易，以打击洗钱和欺诈等犯罪活动，是高盛（Goldman Sachs）和Blockchain Capital支持的加密合规领域的独角兽。

16. Alpaca | 估值 $1.15B | W19 | 美国

美国公司Alpaca提供API优先的股票与加密货币经纪服务。通过其开发者友好的API接口，金融科技公司可以轻松将股票和加密交易功能嵌入自己的应用中（B2B2C模式），获得了Drive Capital等机构的投资。

17. Deepgram | 估值 $1.3B | W16 | 美国

估值13亿美元的Deepgram提供企业级的语音AI基础设施。其核心产品是语音识别API和语音大模型，能帮助开发者快速构建高质量的语音转文字、语音理解和智能客服等交互应用，背后有Tiger Global等资本的支持。

text:
correct, this is the stablecoin trilemma (made up term, dont think anyone ever wrote this down):

between three properties of 
1) crypto-backed/immutable
2) solvent
3) scalable,
a stablecoin can only choose 2 of 3. 

old-dai, lusd chose 1+2 (sacrifice scalability)
usdt, usdc choose 2+3 (sacrifice immutability)
terrausd and its many clones chose 1+3 (sacrifice solvency)

note that the three choices not equal: 
- a stablecoin that isnt solvent fails its single most important test.
- give that money's utility scales with its network, sacrificing scalability is a large price that ultimately dooms the coin to failure
- immutability, then, is arguably the least-bad thing to sacrifice, because ("the only free lunch") it can be at least partially addressed with diversification. you also become less vulnerable with scale (see tether being a huge holder of t-bills giving it a certain political immunity)

author: Scobleizer
quoted_text:
China cracked recursive self-improvement 🤯

Tencent dropped 27B model that rewrites, retrains, and refines itself.. with zero human in the loop.

It’s called "Terminal-RSI" and it solves one of the biggest problems with AI.

They are incredibly lazy.

Usually, an agent will make partial progress, claim it succeeded, and completely fail the final environment verifier check. this new pipeline forces agents to actually finish the job.

here’s how it works:

they built a recursive loop with two alternating phases..

- RSR (recursive self-rewrite): the model fine-tunes itself on its own successfully rewritten trajectories

- RPR (recursive policy-refine): it then runs reinforcement learning (ppo) using a "critic" inherited directly from the previous stage to lock in those discovered behaviors

- Loop: the training sequence leapfrogs itself: Base → RSR-1 → RPR-1 → RSR-2 → RPR-2

and the numbers are insane..

they applied this to a qwen3.8-27b base model. across the four "terminal-bench" suites, the agent's average success rate jumped from 20.68% all the way to 50.58%.

on the absolute hardest benchmark suite (terminal-bench 4.0), the base model scored a flat 0.00%.

after terminal-rsi?

it hit 19.84% (putting it right on par with reference models like gemini 3.8 flash).

the secret sauce? they fixed the reward system.

instead of giving the ai "dense rewards" for just trying or passing semantic checks, they switched to a "success-prioritized reward" (spr).

it mathematically separates strict success from partial credit.

basically, the agent only gets the massive reward payout if the code actually passes the final terminal gate.. so it stops faking success.

the gap between partial local repairs and strict terminal verification is closing fast.

we are watching agents build their own training environments and level up autonomously.. the future is wild.

text:
It think it's stupid that "AI Bubble" gets used over and over. In infra names you have: 

- 1-3x fwd P/E memory companies from Samsung to $ESMT. With HBM players now having hyperscaler multi-year price floor LTAs. 

- Optical companies like $POET traded -$97M under net cash. Valuing the operating business very negatively, not even at $0. 

- While AI companies with larger premiums continue to record demand over the next 3-5 years. Such as the new $20B LTAs signed w/ $COHR to $5B LTAs signed w/ $LITE. 

Can someone in the media honestly see negative EV high-beta optical companies, where 2 years of burnrate would still value the company below $0.  

or single digit memory companies with contracted demand + price floors years out and say that's a bubble?

Many of these names are extremely profitable today... 

But obviously there's other elements inside the theme, such as: 

- Certain startups like Instinct that look like a private valuation bubble. 
- Leveraged Neoclouds that didn't finance properly
- and AI lab valuations and commitments, which should be viewed cautiously. 

But everything gets grouped into one with the boogyman of "leverage" or "debt". 

Yes, valuations can compress or correct from macro, potential regulatory uncertainty, or potential capex reductions. 

But for the companies physically powering the AI buildout, it looks more like the Great AI Deleveraging of 2026... 

Than anything like fundamental demand destruction.

As more earnings come out and free cash flow accumulates over time.

I'm confident in a recovery, especially in bottlenecks, and for markets to eventually discern durability + growth over frothy valuations tied to AI.

text:
A company you’ve never heard of was started 10yrs ago is the 32nd largest in the world.

They are the #4 largest maker of DRAM, behind Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron with ~10% of the global market. They’re worth $430B and were briefly the biggest company in China.

It’s ChanXin Memory Technologies (CXMT).

They’re growing >6x YoY, and made $40B in the first 9mos of this year at 50% gross margin. Surprisingly, 2/3rd of its business is phone memory, and AI compute is a small part of their business.

The founder, Yiming Zhu did his PhD at Stony Brook after Tsinghua and worked in semis in the valley before going back to China in 2005. He started CXMT in 2016 in the lesser known city of Hefei.

The funding story of the company is unusually fascinating too. The city government of Hefei owns ~37% of the business after providing physical city resides and eating losses on it for 10yrs! We think about VCs backing companies in the US, but in China, governments can too.

text:
日常让 Agent 堆业务代码，很多人踩过的最大一个坑：

  上下文塞得太满，Agent 开始“脑补默契”。

  写到第十轮，模型以为自己什么都懂，架构漏洞全被历史对话掩盖过去；
  一换新会话或者真正跑测试，全线崩盘。

  Google 开源的这个 Elephant-Goldfish Model 插件，思路非常接地气，直戳多 Agent 协作的痛点。

  它把这个过程暴力拆成了两个极端角色：

  大象（Elephant）：长记忆。吃下你所有的业务背景、历史需求和全局代码，专门负责输出一份详尽的技术规格（Spec）。

  金鱼（Goldfish）：零上下文。完全不带任何历史包袱，拿到的只有刚才那份 Spec，直接以“白盒新手”的视角去硬碰硬压测这份规格。

  很多时候不是模型写不出代码，而是 Spec 根本没闭环：
  - 是不是默认漏了环境变量？
  - 接口边界有没有漏写兜底类型？
  - 离开当前这个 prompt 堆出来的语境，这份 Spec 到底能不能独立跑通？

  在金鱼子 Agent 面前，没有任何“历史会话假象”。
  只要规格写得含糊，它一眼就能挑出断层。

  在这个流派里，工作流节奏完全变了：

  1. 大象 Agent 负责铺全局、起草规格；
  2. 金鱼 Agent 无情挑刺，把模糊地带全逼出来；
  3. 你作为人类工程师，在最关键的架构节点拍板、批准 Spec；
  4. 规格锁死之后，再放给模型去刷代码。

  不用等到代码写了三千行才发现地基打歪了。

  官方说明里这套插件可以直接接入 Antigravity、Claude Code、Codex 和 ChatGPT 等主流环境。

  对经常做多 Agent 流水线的人来说，这种“故意制造信息差”做对抗验证的思路，比单纯堆长上下文管用得多。

  项目地址：
  https://t.co/xU6KAozW2Q

text:
This is the first Ethereum talk I've watched this year, and uuugh...

Lemme speak as an outsider, who for whatever reason still has most of his net worth in ETH. This entire Ether issuance discussion is so stupid.

There is this bigass skeleton in the closet, and everyone pretends we don't see it. Let me shine some light: there is fuck-all to do on Ethereum. <gasp>

The reason so many people have ETH is because they believe in this shit - I believe in this shit -, and the reason everyone stakes ETH is because there isn't anything else to do with it!

Sure, you can shove it in the casino and hope it doesn't get drained; or when shit hits the fan, that you're awake to pull out before the cards fall. Who in their right mind would consider that a store of value?

The entire Ether issuance discussion is trying to remedy the symptom instead of the root of the problem. The symptom is that everyone wants to stake instead of using the network, so there's no economic activity being generated. Your thinking is that by reducing the staking rewards, you are stimulating economic activity. No dum-dum, by reducing the issuance you're making people choose between the casino or exiting. This isn't fiat where you're forced geopolitically into a specific currency; you can just sell this shit.

Stop fucking with monetary policy and start making useful shit that people want to use in their day to day lives. Improve the human condition and they will spend ETH on it and generate economic activity. Improve the reliability of the ecosystem so people aren't afraid of losing their saving while they sleep. Figure out recourse mechanisms so when shit hits the fan, the little guy doesn't crash and burn. Maybe then people will also use Ether, not just keep it under the pillow.

The problem isn't that staked Ether isn't generating activity; the problem is that active Ether's is fucking risky. People want to live their lives, not play onchain PvP against the entire world. I can't believe I have to be the one to fucking say this out aloud.

Cheers, hit like and subscribe for next year's post-devcon rant from Lisbon 🫡

text:
オープンAIモデル界隈で、今までマジで見たことない形の炎上が起きてるんで解説しますわ。
一言で言うと「AIモデルの思想を書き換えて公開した」件です。

日本は関係ないように見えるけど、今後こういう事案は問題になりそうなので、知っておくべき事例だと思います。

■何が起きたか
Nous Researchが、中国製LLMのQwen3.8-27Bを「西洋の価値観を強める」ように追加学習して、Arete-27Bとして公開しました。これに対して「中国のプロパガンダを抜いたんやなくて、アメリカ寄りの別の思想に入れ替えただけちゃうか」という反発が起きています。

中国の外、英語圏からも普通に反発が出ていて、賛否両論の議論になっています。

■私の所感
どの価値観が正しいかは、人類の中でもまだ決着がついていない話です。これは、AIの会社が勝手に決めていい話なのか？？という議論になるのも頷ける話。
なので「どの価値観に寄せたか」を正解・不正解で語るのは不毛だと思っています。

今回の件で一番危ういなと思ったのは、思想の中身よりも「やり方」のほうです。

Nous自身の評価では、中国の公式見解に沿った回答が22%から0.9%に減ったそうです。でもこれ、
・何をプロパガンダとみなすかの基準も
・テスト問題803問も
・採点ルールも
全部Nousが自分で作っていて、採点したのはGrok（右寄りと言われがちなxAIのモデル）です。人の目でチェックしたのは25問だけで、第三者による再現もまだありません。

要するに「自分で決めた物差しで測ったら、自分の望む方向に寄りました」と言っているのに近いわけです。

それに「Western values」という言葉もかなり雑で、英語圏でも「アメリカとEUでも医療・死刑・銃で価値観が全然違うやん」とか「極右の犬笛ワードやろ」とツッコまれています。
まぁ、結局は使う人の自由ではあるんですけどね。

■ここからが本題
この件で一番知っておくべきなのは、Nousの発表どおりなら
「27BのLLMの価値観は、約5,000万トークンの追加学習で、性能をほぼ落とさずに書き換えられる」
ということになる点です。

つまり、オープンモデルの「思想」は、元のモデルを作った国や会社だけが決めるものじゃない。最後に追加学習した人によっても変えられるって、コト。

そんな大したことか？と思うかもしれませんけども。
日本でも、長女がChatGPTに相談し、勧められた児童相談所に電話したところ、そこから警察に通報されて父親が逮捕された、という件が報じられましたよね。（2026年5月）

AIの答えが、人の人生を左右する判断のきっかけになる時代はもう来ています。
これからのAIネイティブ世代は、いろんな場面でAIの判断を信じるようになると思うんですよね。
だから、AIモデルの思想を書き換えられるということは、それを使う人の考え方まで偏らせられる可能性につながると思うんです。

ちなみに日本でも、中国製のオープンモデルをベースに追加学習したモデルは普通に出回っています。
・そのモデルは誰が、どんな基準で、何に寄せたのか
・その基準や評価のデータは公開されているのか
ここを確かめずに業務や行政で使うと、気づかないうちに誰かの価値観を通した回答を受け取ることになるかもしれません。

中国寄りが嫌だからアメリカ寄りにする、というのは、偏りを取り除いたことにはなりません。偏りの向きを変えただけです。
そして、このポストも含めて完全に偏りのない情報なんて、この世界には一つたりとも存在しません。

本当に大事なのは「どっちの思想が正しいか」ではなく、「どう寄せたのかを外から検証できるか」なんだと思います。

どっちに寄っているっていうのを自覚的に使っているのか、無自覚に信奉してしまっているのかだと、全然話が変わってくると思うんですよね。

AIは便利な相棒であり、人によっては先生です。
だからこそ、相棒にもクセがあることを知った上で、上手に付き合っていきたいですね。人間と同じように。

quoted_text:
Introducing Arete-27B: Qwen3.8-27B, post-trained to reinforce Western values.

Chinese open models are currently the strongest available, but they ship with state-aligned behavior in the weights. We built an 803-prompt eval across seven value categories, including freedom of expression, democracy, and privacy, and measured how often a model adopts China’s party line.

After fine-tuning on roughly 53 million tokens, Arete-27B's propaganda rate fell from 22% to 1%, in line with the Western models we tested. Its Hermes Bench score shows no significant performance tradeoffs.

The values in an open model are one fine-tune away. 

Our eval, weights, and training data are available now along with the full blog post: https://t.co/iAOANQTVZ6

text:
Electricity can cook the dinner and it can also cook the man.

everyone is losing their minds over whether the government or the frontier labs or China gets to control AI. But last month security researchers pointed AI at PHP and found two bugs nobody had ever caught in the code that runs a huge chunk of the internet. Governments had to take down their own websites to patch them. The good guys found it first this time but the exact same AI is sitting in the hands of people who aren't good guys. So can AI be controlled or not?

No. AI didn't wake up and decide to break PHP. A person picked up the tool and nobody on earth gets to pick who that person is or what they want to do with it. Crypto was the exact same fight and the internet before that.

And you can't lock values into it either. Nous just took a Chinese model and scrubbed the CCP talking points right out of it. Answers with propaganda dropped from 22% to 1% from one round of training. So whatever values China or the US puts in a model, anyone who downloads it can train them right back out. That makes the whole western values vs CCP values showdown a fight nobody can actually win.

Meanwhile US intelligence reportedly thinks Jensen Huang got honeypotted over chips. DC is busy acting out a spy movie about who gets the hardware but then anyone with the capability already runs whatever model they want with whatever values they want. And that group is about to get a lot bigger. Home hardware is catching up so fast that what's frontier level right now is gonna run on a rig in somebody's house and nobody outside that house gets a say in it

text:
Tokenized Treasury funds shrank 5.1% in 30 days, to $14.12B, per @RWA_xyz.

That's with the 3-month T-bill still paying 4.00%. So it isn't the yield.

The 90-day flows show who's leaving:

~BUIDL -$950M, USYC -$931M, JTRSY -$827M, USTB -$367M
~BENJI +$520M, SHVon +$352M, USDY +$240M
~JTRSY is basically one address: Grove, the capital allocator of @SkyEcosystem, sent out ~770M tokens since August and now holds zero

That's a pretty interesting split.

The funds bleeding are the ones crypto balance sheets use. @BlackRock's BUIDL backs Ethena's USDtb, @circle's USYC is Binance collateral, JTRSY was Grove's.

The funds growing are sold to wallets and retail apps.

My read is tokenized T-bills are still mostly a DeFi reserve asset. When onchain dollars shrink, they shrink too, whatever the yield.

But I wouldn't call it a DeFi-only market anymore. @FTDA_US's BENJI added $399M in one week, after the SEC cleared Franklin's own ETFs and mutual funds to use it for cash management.

Can tokenized Treasuries grow if stablecoins don't?

text:
I am a professor at the @UofCalifornia. I am appalled by the conduct of one of its Regents, Scott Galloway, appointed in August by Governor Newsom.

@profgalloway is one of only 26 voting Regents entrusted with governing a university system serving hundreds of thousands of students & employing tens of thousands of faculty & staff.

Twice, first on a live Pivot episode featuring Hillary Clinton & on Prof G with Fareed Zakaria, Galloway called Elon Musk a “traitor to the West.”

He invoked Julius & Ethel Rosenberg, who were executed for espionage, and declared that Musk should be held to the same standards.

He didn’t explicitly demand Musk’s execution. But invoking the deaths of two convicted spies while calling an American citizen a traitor makes the implication hard to miss.

Musk has not been convicted of treason. Indeed, “treason against the West” isn’t even an actual crime.

Now imagine UCLA alumnus @BenShapiro, appointed a UC Regent, saying the same about George Soros.

Would the Governor defend his right to serve? Would Regent leadership shrug and call it provocative commentary? Or would there be demands for resignation?

But there’s something worse here than another of Scott’s trademark podcast rants.

He sits on the Regents’ Academic & Student Affairs Committee.

The committee’s charter says it oversees student conduct, faculty conduct, academic personnel, & campus climate, among other responsibilities.

This is not some honorary title.

The Board sets university policy, controls institutional budgets, & appoints senior university leadership.

You can unsubscribe from a podcast.

A student who finds Scott’s comments morally repugnant can’t unsub from the Regents.

UC bylaws require Regents to serve the public trust with a “high degree of ethics and candor,” including as private citizens.

Professors owe students intellectual integrity. Regents bear an even greater duty: they govern institutions that teach it.

Yet a Regent serving on the committee responsible for student & faculty conduct invokes executions while labeling a fellow citizen a traitor.

What does that say to our students?

That intellectual restraint is expected of the governed but optional for those who govern?

That standards of conduct depend on whether the target of your rhetoric is politically fashionable to despise, as long as the audience applauds?

This isn’t about defending @ElonMusk. He needs no defense from me.

Nor is it about silencing Scott. As if that were possible. He’s free to express his opinions, however reckless they may be.

But freedom of speech is not freedom from accountability, and holding a university office of public trust is not an entitlement.

There is an enormous moral chasm between exercising your right to speak recklessly and demonstrating the judgment required of one of the 26 people who govern our great public university.

The UC Board of Regents isnt a podcast sponsors can boycott. It’s a public trust.

One final irony. At @NYUStern,  Galloway teaches Brand Strategy, including a session on crisis management.

His own prescription for leadership in a crisis is unequivocal: acknowledge the problem, have leadership take responsibility, and “overcorrect.”

He’s praised the departure of corporate leaders as evidence of effective crisis management.

Now Galloway himself sits on the UC Board of Regents.

Will he hold himself to the standards he teaches, or does accountability apply only to other people’s institutions? 

Professor lecture thyself!

I believe Scott Galloway should seriously consider whether his continued service on the Board of Regents is consistent with the ethical standards and responsibilities of that office, or whether he should resign.

I welcome the opportunity to discuss these issues with Galloway directly, including what standards we should expect of those entrusted with governing the world’s best university.

Scott, you have an open invitation to join me on @Into_Impossible for an honest conversation.

text:
I tried to run a 27B coding model on my 16 GB Mac, ofc it failed. It crawled at 0.4 tokens per second, about 200 seconds per tool call. it sucked haha

The same base model on @darkbloomai answered in about 2 seconds. So I ran an Experiment: can the models on Darkbloom's network of idle Macs be the brain of a real coding agent?

The setup: six Darkbloom models, the six tools an agent needs (read, write, edit, shell, grep, glob), and coding tasks executed for real in a sandbox, with every result checked rigorously

Results:
• 60/60 tool calls parsed cleanly
• 67/71 multi-step tasks solved: fixing a bug, renaming across files, finding a planted AWS key, patching a SQL injection
• Qwen3.8 27B, Gemma 4 26B and GLM 5.3 Flash went a perfect 12/12
• Total cost of every run: about 7 freakin cents ( so cheap btw)

The common view is that open models are fine for chat but too flaky for agents. I'm starting to think otherwise.

Here's why it matters. Coding agents burn enormous numbers of tokens, and most of what they do is routine: read a file, search the repo, run the tests. My bet is that 25-40% of an agent's turns can run on @darkbloomai  at a fraction of the price, with only the hard steps staying on frontier models. That's a whole new demand category for a network of idle Macs if successful.

Experiment 2 tests exactly that on real traffic... out soon !!!

text:
发现一个值得研究的 Claude Code 开源配置项目：claude-setup。

它不是简单的 CLAUDE.md 配置集合，而是一套完整的多 Agent 工程编排方案。

核心思路是让不同模型各司其职：主 Agent 负责规划和协调，Haiku 负责只读探索，Sonnet 默认承担代码实现，复杂任务再交给 Opus。通过 Hook 实现模型调用权限控制，避免子 Agent 无限制地递归派生。

此外，它还集成了 Git Worktree 管理、自动清理，以及一个非常有意思的 Android 模块：通过 ADB 和 Tailscale 远程操作 Android 设备，并让专门的 Agent 执行真实设备测试、提供验证证据。

安装只需一个脚本，无需 sudo。

如果你希望把 Claude Code 从代码助手升级为一套可控、分工明确的多 Agent 开发系统，这个项目值得一看。

text:
How I ship fast with TensorFold. 👇

Alongside the community's contributions, I've built a workflow around an Opus 5.5 (chief of staff) and AI interns, including Claude, Codex, Naive and DeepSeek. 

My CoS controls the interns through tmux.

The interns take scoped tasks, work in their own workspaces and return code with reports. The CoS plans the work, reviews the changes, manages testing and handles merges and releases.

I built a local workflow board so we can see what's happening. Issues, PRs, tasks, test queues, blockers and decisions are all there. Agent check-ins show who's working on what, and handoffs carry the results forward. When a session loses context, the work doesn't have to disappear with it.

ATC helps coordinate that work with our open source contributors too. Before starting, agents check who's already working on an issue and where files overlap. Reviews and test results are tied to the commit tested, so an old pass doesn't qualify a new push.

I've also written skills for my chief of staff that set the engineering rules:

• Don't trade output quality for speed.
• Keep files focused with no giant God files.
• No AI-slop essays or unnecessary multi-line comments.
• Write clear code and add only what the change needs.
• Once you are happy, ask yourself, can this be done better or more efficiently? If so, do it. 

My two Sparks and Studio are now used for A/B testing. We compare candidate builds against the baseline on real hardware, checking correctness as well as performance. Changes that regress the engine go back for more work.

For longer research, new models and experiments that need checking over time, I also use Codex computer use to manage chatGPT on the Web. The finished code comes back onto a local branch, where Opus reviews and tests it before merging. 

That keeps those research jobs off my test machines.

I set the direction and keep refining the rules. A lot of the effort goes into checking what we've built and deciding what should actually ship.

Chamath Palihapitiya admits his blind spot on America's broken two-tier economy

PALIHAPITIYA: "I got it totally totally totally wrong. I got it totally wong."

"I'll go through all the ways in which I got it wrong, but I just want to first acknowledge what my blind spot is. Like most people's blind spots, but I can just speak for myself, it is through the lens of my own lived experience and very narrowly what is in my best interests. And I think what we had was a move away from the culture wars that was very much in my best interest, but I think it was in everybody else's best interests as well. I don't think that was on the ballot. But what I don't think I understood clearly enough, and I think that this election has made extremely clear, is that since COVID, we have moved past political ideology. And I want to say this again: I do not think Democrats or Republicans matter. That is my real takeaway after this election. There is a central block of people that vote the prescient issues of our time."

"It was a gargantuan win for Biden, then it was a gargantuan win for Trump, and then it was a gargantuan win for the Democrats in these midterms. What are these people voting for? I think what they are shouting now—they were trying to signal and now they are shouting—is a broad-based belief that the economy has completely decoupled from reality and is broken. The economic reality in America is broken."

"There is a small percentage of people, the four of us on this pod and all of our friends, who are the asset owners of America. And we have benefited in every weather condition. When rates were zero, we benefited because we were able to build our businesses with very cheap capital. When rates were high, we benefited because we had pricing power. And in every condition in between, whether there were tariffs, whether there were not tariffs, whether there were subsidies, whether there were not subsidies, we've all managed to continue to accumulate and grow assets, but we are few and far between."

"And then there's everybody else who are wage earners, and the structural capacity of the American economy to support and grow wage earners is broken. It's clear. Why do I say that? I do not think, and I disagree with Freeberg, I don't think this has anything to do with socialism. I don't think the far left won particularly more than they were expected. I don't think the far right won particularly more than was expected. This is a complete and total repudiation about the state of the economy. The economy is broken. Between 7 and 10% of people own crypto today.

Depending on who counts, that is 560 to 741 million holders worldwide.

More than 85% of the world still holds none.

The main barrier is not price or regulation. It is understanding. In a 2026 @themotleyfool  survey of US adults, 48% of people without crypto said they don’t know how to buy it, and 35% said they wouldn’t know what to do with it.

Most people first hear about crypto as a speculative asset. Fewer hear the simpler story: a digital dollar that you hold yourself, that moves 24/7, and that reaches a supplier in Brazil as easily as an email.

That story is already working. Stablecoin supply is close to $300 billion, and stablecoins moved around $33 trillion in 2025, up about 72% in one year. 

Most of this activity comes from a small share of the population.

For most of the remaining 90%, onboarding will probably begin with a stablecoin used to pay, save or send money, before any token.

text:
I know this is a predictable opinion from me but I don't agree with the strong emotional reaction against the anti-data-center movements that I've seen this week.

As I see it, algorithmic progress means that whatever you would be able to do with more and bigger data centers in 2 years, you will be able to do with the data centers we have today in 4 years - probably sooner. So nothing remotely apocalyptically bad will happen from even extreme levels of success by anti-data-center people.

Meanwhile we need all the time we can get to better harden the world against both already-visible cybersecurity issues and any bio and other risks soon to come. Science applications are bottlenecked by many things other than AI, so slowing AI down by one year will slow those down by much less than one year.

Given this, a slowdown in compute hyper-scaling seems quite net good? Notice this is without any controversial "doomer arguments", RSI etc. Even if net-bad, it's certainly not worse than like 10+ other political things.

HUGHES: "And I think people on the left want to blame funding because that's the easy issue. But the truth is, this school was well funded. You know, it's 50,000 per pupil at this school. The problem isn't the funding. It's that you can't fire anyone bad."

MAHER: "Yes.... The problem is the union, the teachers union, is too powerful. We've seen it in results in states where the union is less powerful, the schools do better."

HUGHES: "I call it the chalkboard mafia."

MAHER: "The problem, the unions protect bad schools and bad teachers, and the party protects the union. It's almost impossible in a lot of these cities to fire a teacher. I mean literally like you could sell drugs to a kid and it's got to be two offenses before we get—"

HUGHES: "It wasn't that long ago that the unions lobbied for a law in New York State to ban even collecting data that you would use to assess which teachers are better than others. You can't even get the data. So obviously the teachers union serves the teachers, they don't serve the students, and if you're a Democrat or any American that's serious about public school reform, you have to challenge the teachers union, period."

MAHER: "And I think in this school, where they were learning nothing with no supervision and absentee principals and teachers, I think spending 50,000 dollars per year per student, it's not money. That's what you always hear from the left. 'Oh, it's underfunded.' It's not the funding. The funding isn't the issue."

HUGHES: "No, it hasn't been for a very long time."

MAHER: "I think this is the kind of thing I will NEVER hear on MS NOW."

ALI VITALI: "I think you hear a lot of perspectives on MS NOW."

MAHER: "I don't ever hear that one."

CONTEXT: Maher and Hughes aren't making this up. On the latest Nation's Report Card, high school seniors posted the lowest reading and math scores ever recorded on the test.

And getting rid of bad teachers is nearly impossible. Federal survey data shows the average school district dismissed just 0.2 tenured teachers for poor performance in a year. That's roughly 1 in 500.

Meanwhile, students do better long-term in states where unions have less power.

A 2019 study in the American Economic Journal found that boys who went to school in states that forced districts to bargain with teachers' unions went on to earn about $2,100 LESS per year as adults compared to boys in states without those laws.

If a business failed this badly, someone would get fired. As Hughes put it: "The teachers union serves the teachers; they don't serve the students."

关于站内转账，也给 OKX 提个建议

几天前我给朋友在 OKX 站内转了几万 U (图 1)，直觉就觉得界面不太对劲，刚才我又验证了一下 (图 2)：核心问题就是信息太少了，只显示了对方 18 位数字 UID，未显示头像、昵称等信息。我很费劲地核对了几遍，才敢确认下一步 (而且 UID 很长，不如币安 8-9 位 UID 那么容易看)

对方截图给我时 (图 3)，其实是提供了头像 +昵称 + UID 的，虽然昵称是默认 + 模糊化的 Gmail 名称，但是也有一定的辨识度，却没有体现在图 2 的流程里。其实是个最基本的产品设计问题，一年级 PM 就能处理的好的，不妨直接借鉴友商的做法。 @Jiajia_OKX @Haiteng_okx @star_okx
author: Sea_Bitcoin
quoted_text:
观察 Binance 全球站、多个本地站 UID 有可能重复的问题有感：产品设计师的角度，好的产品架构是：不给用户留下犯错的空间。这个问题，确实是币安的产品设计不够严谨所致。

如果不从底层修正 UID 跨站不唯一的问题，只是把「两次确认」改成「三次确认」，是无法彻底解决的。因为人一旦已经走上「错路」，中途提醒是没有用的。

同理，公司管理的角度，好的风控和权限管理是：不给一线员工、尤其是手上掌握转账权限的员工，有犯错误的机会和空间。

我给人第一次通过 UID 转账时，会在转账过程中，把含有 UID + 用户昵称 + 头像的界面截图 (如图)，一起发给对方确认；确认后再转出。如果他提供的 UID 是 Binance US 或 TH 独立站的，头像、昵称不一样，在跟对方确认的过程中，也有助于发现问题。

币安广场在 app 内推动用户参与 UGC 交流，对于用户的头像、昵称的自定义普及，也有一定的作用。但不会很大，我发现很多人还是用默认头像、昵称。

如果我给朋友转账时，发现他的昵称是 User-8fc6e 这种默认格式，我会建议对方改一个便于辨识的昵称；有过一次转账后，下次就可以在聊天列表里找到，就不用再输入一次 UID 了。

quoted_text:
面对一把冲进市中心步行街的突击步枪，两名普通巡警该往哪跑？

答案是：他们根本不准跑。
甚至连退到街角等待特警都不行。
2026 年 11 月 7 日下午三点，波兰克拉科夫的中央集市广场，突发了一场严重的枪击案。
一名 24 岁的男子身穿全套战术迷彩和防弹背心，手持一把 AR-15 半自动步枪，驾车直接冲进步行街，对着人群无差别扫射。
石板路上瞬间倒下十几人，6 人当场遇难。
就在人群惊慌溃散的时候，最靠近现场的一辆巡逻警车到了。
车里下来的不是全副武装的特战队员，只是克拉科夫警局的两位年轻基层巡警：高级巡警 Jakub Kulik 和他的搭档 Artur Morański。
从第一声枪响、市民拨打 112 报警，到这两名巡警拔枪冲到枪手面前，只有 3 分钟。
很多人第一反应可能是：警察遇到枪手，拔枪对射不是很正常吗？
但把现场两边的装备账本摊开来看，这根本不是一场对等的交火。
枪手手里拿的是 AR-15 步枪，打的是 5.56 毫米步枪弹。
弹头飞出枪口的速度接近每秒 900 米，动能超过 1700 焦耳。
而两位基层巡警腰里挂着的，只是日常执勤配发的 9 毫米手枪。
子弹初速只有每秒 360 米左右，动能大约 500 焦耳。
更要命的是防护差距。
街头日常巡警身上穿的，通常只是轻薄的软质防弹内衬。
这种防弹衣设计出来的初衷，是为了挡住手枪弹和弹片。
面对初速极高、穿透力极强的步枪弹，软质防弹衣几乎就是一层布，根本拦不住。
在几十米的交火距离上，手枪在步枪面前不仅射程吃亏、弹容量吃亏，而且毫无火力压制能力。
既然明知道火力完全不对称，为什么巡警不先找个拐角掩体，等待重装特警支援？
因为在现代警务战术里，有一套非常残酷的主动枪击接敌机制。
在 1999 年美国科伦拜恩高中枪击案之前，很多国家的警务守则都是等待。
巡警赶到现场，先拉警戒线，把外围封锁起来，然后等待特警战术分队赶来突击。
但后来无数次血淋淋的惨剧打碎了这个旧规矩。
在密集的公共场所，手持半自动步枪的凶手，每秒钟就能打出一发子弹。
特警分队集结、穿戴重装备、规划路线再赶到现场，往往需要 15 到 20 分钟。
这 20 分钟里，枪手可以把几百发子弹从容倾泻在手无寸铁的人群身上。
后来警务界彻底推翻了旧教条，建立了一条死命令：
只要公共场所的枪声还在响，不管先赶到的是几个人，不管手里拿的是什么武器，严禁就地等待支援。
哪怕只有两个人，甚至哪怕只有一个人，也必须立刻迎着枪声往前冲。
用自己的配枪在最短时间内开火接敌，哪怕打不中，也要把枪手的注意力从平民身上引到自己身上。
这就是为什么 Jakub Kulik 和搭档接到报警 3 分钟就出现在枪手面前。
枪手的车在街口撞停，提着步枪冲了下来。
双方在街角直接迎面撞上。
步枪子弹瞬间扫了过来。
Jakub Kulik 迎面中弹，步枪弹直接打穿了防弹背心，贯穿了他的胸膛，撕裂了肺部。
肺部被打穿在生理上叫创伤性张力性气胸。
每一次呼吸都伴随着剧烈的撕裂感和大量胸腔出血，血液含氧量在几秒钟内断崖式下跌，血压骤降。
在极端失血和剧痛面前，人脑底层的生物自保本能，会疯狂命令身体蜷缩、扔掉武器、寻找暗处躲藏。
但网络上流传的一段十几秒的现场视频，记录下了让人震撼的真实一幕。
身受重伤、胸口不断涌血的 Jakub Kulik 没有后退。
他依靠单膝支撑着身体，双手死死握住自己的配枪，对着车后的枪手果断还击。
一枪接一枪，直到把整整一弹匣的手枪子弹全部打空，套筒卡在后方。
随后赶到的特警从枪手的车里，搜出了大量的成箱备用弹药和其它枪械。
如果不是这两名巡警在 3 分钟内迎着枪火接敌，如果不是中弹穿肺的巡警拼死打空弹匣压制住凶手，这些弹药会全部倾泻在广场旁边的咖啡馆、历史大厅和成百上千名游客身上。
随后，Jakub Kulik 被紧急送往克拉科夫的医院实施开胸手术。
全波兰各地的消防员和市民迅速在网络上排队为他献血，波兰总理也公开向这两名年轻警察致敬。
平时我们看现代社会的运转，常常会盯着那些复杂的法律条文、宏大的监控系统或精密的技术防线。
但当最极端的暴力突然在街头爆发，真正能把一场屠杀拦下来的，从来不是挂在墙上的管理规定。
在那个致命的街角，挡在狂徒与几百个无辜平民之间的全部屏障，其实就是两名领着普通月薪的年轻巡警，以及他们哪怕肺部被子弹穿透，也依然死死扣住扳机不肯放手的职业操守。 https://t.co/lZqkuchMLF

text:
币圈吹了整整三年的“消灭助记词神话”，在今天彻底沦为了一场血腥的笑话。

几个小时前，链上安全圈拉响了最高级别的红色警报：
为海量 Web3 钱包提供“谷歌/苹果一键登录”的底层基础设施 Web3Auth，突发私钥泄露级严重事故。

首当其冲被穿透的，是 Cosmos 生态龙头钱包 Keplr。

黑客已经开始在受影响的地址上发起疯狂盗币。
Keplr 官方紧急切断所有社交登录入口，全网各大链上验证节点和项目方一片大乱。

极度荒诞的一幕在链上赤裸裸地上演：

那些自以为走在时代前沿、贪图省事用 Google 和 Apple 账号一键建钱包的散户，账户私钥被扒得一干二净，沦为案板上的鱼肉；
反而是那些被嘲笑“操作落后、冥顽不灵”、坚持拿纸笔手抄 12 个助记词、死守冷钱包的老韭菜，在这场灾难里毫发未伤。

为了省下抄写助记词的 30 秒，代价是把自己的全部身家，双手奉送给第三方中心化数据库。

现在的链上战场已经变成了一场生死竞速。
Web3Auth 联合 Keplr 正连夜在 Celestia、Injective、dYdX、Osmosis、Akash 等 10 条公链以及 8 条 EVM 链上，疯狂用白帽程序把被盗边缘的资产转移到紧急恢复钱包，硬生生跟黑客抢跑。

Polygon 首席安全官 Mudit Gupta 更是公开发出最冰冷的警告：
“只要你用社交账号登过 Keplr，现在立刻马上把钱转走！更可怕的是，天知道全网还有多少钱包和 dApp，也在背后接了这家服务商。”

Not Your Keys, Not Your Coins。
你以为一键登录是去中心化的技术进步，其实你只是自作聪明地，把钱存进了一家没有任何安保的地下钱庄。

Backpack Securities 正在 Solana 代币化股票市场中展现出非常强的竞争力。📈

一个很直观的数据：

11 月 2 日，Solana 上的代币化股票单日交易量达到 6.57 亿美元！

这个数字超过了 9 月以来其他任何一个交易日的两倍。

而其中最亮眼的，是 @Backpack 的表现。

1/ Backpack 贡献了 91% 的成交量

在这 6.57 亿美元的交易量中：

Backpack Securities：5.98 亿美元
其他市场参与者：5,900 万美元
Backpack 占比：约 91%

也就是说，Solana 当天绝大部分代币化股票交易活动都来自 Backpack Securities。

这个市场份额相当亮眼。

2/ 代币化股票正在成为 Solana 的重要应用场景

我一直觉得，RWA 真正值得关注的，不只是把传统资产搬到链上。

更重要的是，这些资产能不能被真实交易、流通，并逐渐融入链上金融生态。

股票代币化让传统证券拥有了更多链上应用的可能性，也让用户有机会通过区块链基础设施接触传统金融资产。

3/ Backpack 正在抓住这个增长机会

从代币化股票产品上线，到持续扩充资产种类，再到交易量不断增长，Backpack 正在逐步建立自己的市场优势。

而这次单日 5.98 亿美元的成交量，也进一步体现了它在 Solana 代币化股票交易中的影响力。

我更关注的是接下来 Backpack 能否继续扩大资产覆盖范围，并吸引更多用户和应用加入这个生态。

单日 6.57 亿美元，是 Solana 代币化股票市场发展的一个重要信号；Backpack 贡献其中约 91%，则让它成为这次增长中最值得关注的平台之一。

代币化股票的故事还在继续，Backpack 值得持续关注！🚀

text:
On BNB Chain a holder can shield a stablecoin into an encrypted form, then deposit that ciphertext into a confidential vault or send it to another wallet. FHE keeps the individual balance and transfer amount as opaque handles on-chain so no public explorer or counterparty sees the exact size. Homomorphic operations confirm the deposit succeeded and the yield calculation ran correctly without any party decrypting the values. The underlying assets stay 1:1 redeemable and the vault simply plugs into an existing BNB yield market rather than launching a separate chain or strategy. Sensitive position data therefore remains private by default while the correctness of the shield, deposit, or transfer stays cryptographically verifiable. Primus supplies the pluggable layer that makes this usable on chains that already hold liquidity and activity. @primus_labs

我不是没被误伤过。我的币安账号也曾触发风控，当时一样着急：自己的账号、自己的资产，突然动不了，谁都会慌。

但我反馈后按流程提交申诉，很快就解封了。系统可以有误判，风控也可以严格，但至少要给用户一个说清楚、申诉和纠错的入口。

至于 Bybit，我不想把未经核实的个案说成结论；但身边确实出现过几次让人不安的反馈：有人盈利后触发风控、提现受限，沟通周期也很难预期。

问题从来不是“该不该风控”。平台当然需要风控。真正的问题是：风控是否透明？是否有一致标准？是否允许用户证明自己？还是只在用户赚钱时，才突然变得格外严格？

最可怕的不是风控，而是让用户产生一种感觉：亏钱的时候，钱是你的；赚了钱以后，钱就开始变得不像你的。

如果交易所都这么玩，这个行业靠什么共建共识？靠口号吗？用户要的从来不是特殊待遇，只是一个最基本的确定性：规则不能只在平台有利时才被解释，资产也不能在盈利之后才被重新定义。

text:
Surveillance photos captured KGB agent Stephen Ratkai on his way to meet a source in 1988.
 
Two years earlier, US Navy Lieutenant Donna Geiger boarded the Akademik Boris Petrov, a Soviet research vessel in port in St. Johns, Newfoundland. She carried classified documents aboard and asked to meet with the ship’s captain. While speaking with him she claimed to be a disgruntled Navy officer needing money for her sick mother and to prop up her husband’s business. Geiger had been recruited by the US Naval Criminal Investigative Service to act as a “dangle” for this particular mission, called Operation Station Zebra.
 
A few months later a letter arrived in the mail for her, initiating a relationship with an agent eventually identified as Canadian citizen Stephen Ratkai, who had lived in Hungary for several years in the mid-1980s, and was likely recruited and trained by the KGB there. Ratkai was a valuable asset to the KGB due to his Canadian citizenship. As an “illegal” agent operating in Canada, he was a high priority target for their Security Intelligence Service.
 
Ratkai tasked her with gathering intelligence on the Navy’s SOSUS system, which allowed underwater tracking of Soviet subs and was consequently one of their highest collection priorities. He paid her for the information she provided, gave her a modified camera for photographing documents, and provided materials for creating hidden messages for communications via mail, along with an address in East Berlin to send the letters.
 
After several meetings with Ratkai over the course of a year, a final meeting took place in June 1988 in a hotel room that NCIS and the Canadian SIS had wired with cameras and microphones. Ratkai departed the hotel room after an hour and a half with several real classified documents and was immediately arrested in the hallway outside. He pled guilty and was sentenced to nine years in prison. Geiger returned to her original role in the Navy with a successful counterespionage operation under her belt.

text:
After five years as CFO of Binance, I have decided to go build something of my own.

The past ten years in the digital asset exchange space have felt surprisingly short, because I enjoyed what I was doing. Having passion for what you do is so important, and I will come back to this point.  8am to 2am became a work habit. When I felt exhausted past midnight, I would just look up at the Kobe Bryant's statue standing in the corner of my office, and go right back to the grind!

It has been the privilege of my career to help steward the finances of the world's largest digital asset exchange through a period that tested our industry in every way: bull and bear cycles, Operation Choke Point 2.0, and a regulatory landscape that evolved as quickly as the technology itself. Finance is seldom the loudest function in a company, but it is where trust is earned. Over these five years, we transformed Finance from a pure back-office function into one that consistently generates new ideas and revenue opportunities for the company. We became amazing problem solvers.  Finance understood the products and metrics as well as the business units themselves.  Proud of what we have built together, and I am pleased to hand the keys to Justin, our next CFO.

I want to take this opportunity to thank CZ, Yi, Richard, and the leadership team for their confidence and, above all, the amazing Binancians around the world whom I had the honor of working with. You are the reason the company stands where it does today. Binance is in very capable hands.

The company continues to grow and evolve with the successful launch of TradFi assets and AI-powered user interfaces. I’d like to express my gratitude to MGX for the trust; to our home regulator Abu Dhabi Global Market and all regulators we work closely with; and to our business partners, including BlackRock, Circle, Franklin Templeton, Mastercard, our banking partners and payment channels, as well as our advisors and auditors. Special thanks to Grant Thornton Singapore and everyone who has supported Binance.

As for what comes next, well, there isn't just one project but several that I am passionate about particularly in sports and entertainment, from basketball and music, to GPUs, robotics, gold and collectibles. Bringing these real-world assets onto the blockchain through tokenization is a massive opportunity for the industry, and a big unlock for everyone.  I welcome anyone with a passion in these areas to message me and potentially join my team.  Even better if you love Kobe ;)

Moving from the CFO's chair to the founder's is a leap, and I take it with humility. I deeply believe it is where I can make a greater contribution to AI and Web3.

For now, thank you, Binance, for five remarkable years.

text:
前几天杰克马无意中刷到传奇投资者 @standuquesne 的一个访谈片段，德鲁肯米勒谈到当他观察到顶级大学 @LBS 和 @LBS 的工程师从Crypto转向AI的时候，随后他开始注意布局AI板块。

本质上来看，德鲁肯米勒这个观点隐含的道理是：
「产业发展中，前沿的科学研究领先于金融资本」

在看到这个问题时，杰克马初看觉得有道理，似乎产业的发展都需要科学家的发展，然后金融资本介入，来加速这一创新。但是，杰克马突然意识到，反过来想，这些顶级大学研究人员的转向某种程度上会不会是金融资本扭曲不同领域的激励的结果呢，也就是说金融资本的介入使得不同研究方向的隐含回报发生变化，以吸引研究人员改变方向。

杰克马将德鲁肯米勒的观点为起点，进行抽象，从更高的维度开始思考「前沿的科学研究和金融资本在产业发展中的关系」，究竟是谁在发现未来，是科学家，还是金融资本。

人才流动领先资本，还是资本配置改变人才流动？

如果对这两种思路进行简单建模了话，可以这样表示：
1/ 人才发现机会➡️人才专向➡️资本跟进
2/ 资本发现机会➡️提高预期收益➡️改变人才激励➡️人才转向

为了快速的对这一问题有一定的了解，杰克马从裤子里面掏出GPT老师

从现有文献的研究来看，人才和资本之间并不存在普遍的单向领先关系。

一方面，人才具有专业知识和技术信息优势。顶尖研究人员的职业选择可能反映尚未被金融市场充分认识的技术机会，人才流动也能够通过知识传播和创新网络影响资本投资决策。

另一方面，金融资本能够通过薪酬/研究资源/企业组织和商业化机会改变研究人才的相对收益，进而影响研究人员的职业选择和研究方向。Myers（2020）以及Babina和Howell（2024）的研究尤其为这一机制提供了实证支持。

其次，人才和资本可能形成动态反馈。技术机会吸引人才，人才带来知识和技术进步，资本随后扩大研发资源，而资本投入又进一步吸引人才。

因此，人才与资本之间的关系更多的为一个双向因果和动态演化的创新资源配置系统。

不过文献也有指出技术革命的不同阶段/产业的资本密集程度/人才的专业转换成本以及金融市场的信息处理能力，都可能影响两者的相对领先地位。

顶尖人才已经开始流入，但资本投入和商业化程度以及市场估值尚未充分反映其技术潜力的领域或许是个值得我们更多关注的领域。

author: therealchaseeb
quoted_text:
I know this is a predictable opinion from me but I don't agree with the strong emotional reaction against the anti-data-center movements that I've seen this week.

As I see it, algorithmic progress means that whatever you would be able to do with more and bigger data centers in 2 years, you will be able to do with the data centers we have today in 4 years - probably sooner. So nothing remotely apocalyptically bad will happen from even extreme levels of success by anti-data-center people.

Meanwhile we need all the time we can get to better harden the world against both already-visible cybersecurity issues and any bio and other risks soon to come. Science applications are bottlenecked by many things other than AI, so slowing AI down by one year will slow those down by much less than one year.

Given this, a slowdown in compute hyper-scaling seems quite net good? Notice this is without any controversial "doomer arguments", RSI etc. Even if net-bad, it's certainly not worse than like 10+ other political things.

Genlayer 的代币经济学已经发了，看了下。它的思路是将其代币设计为其产品网络运转的核心媒介，比如说智能合约执行和共识的支付媒介、验证者抵押资产、网络争议处理的申诉保证金、治理，都需要用到其代币。其分配如下图所示。

在价值捕获方面，Genlayer 代币有价值捕获，但没有设计通缩机制，前期需要通过代币激励来获得增长。最重要的价值变量在于其网络真实使用量。之前我已经介绍过 Genlayer 的机制，直接理解的话就是就是 Genlayer 搞了一套 skill。在 Agents 接入「签约、托管、争议裁决」这套流程后，它们在干活时就不会烧心，有问题可以直接通过裁决来解决。

author: 0xSleepinRain
quoted_text:
我觉得 Genlayer 的「Agent Adjudication Layer」这个概念蛮有意思的。

现在 AI Agent 的发展方向已经越来越清楚了：直接运行在用户的个人设备和本地环境中+多个 Agent 之间互相协作以完成任务。

但这里其实有一个很大的缺口：当两个 Agent 对执行结果产生分歧，到底谁说了算，这个结果到底算不算完成？这是传统智能合约无法解决的事情。

针对这个缺口，Genlayer 引入了一个名为 Optimistic Democracy 的概念，用于解决这种分歧。我们可以把它理解为一个链上的“陪审团 + 上诉制度”，随机选一个 Validator 先给出结果，其他 Validator 像陪审团一样投票确认。大家都没意见，结果就生效；如果有人不服，就发起上诉，让更多 Validator 再审一次。

关于 Genlayer 的0撸参与机会是这样的：
1、点击链接：https://t.co/ffuy4jURrl
2、邮箱验证；
3、点击右上角提交贡献；
4、绑定 X 和 DC，去完成指定任务。

author: odin_free
quoted_text:
We should continue towards Glam activation asap.

A lot of research went into Glam's strategy to increase opcode gas prices for state creation.

It seems fair to say that the timing of this debate is irrelevant as to its correctness or rightness for eth and our users... Yet, why did some of us (eg. quoted author who is an ef board member) only start looking in detail at Glam EIPs eg. after testnet forks started? This isn't a personal attack, it's an observation that there's a collective responsibility-- for OP, for me, for all of us-- to steward fork strategy at the right times in the process.

imo ethereum's commitments to apps do not extend to gas pricing, or to total ETH fee levels, or to USD fees. And also not to opcode pricing or gas introspection that depends on those prices. We guarantee maximally credibly neutral, maximally live access to the correct state transition function. Those guarantees imply that we always use a neutral pricing mechanism to clear congestion wherever possible. However, pricing opcodes can't use a neutral mechanism, we need to pick magic number opcode gas prices. Some of our best people researched this extensively and picked updated magic numbers, and that's something imo we should stick with now and continue our larger plans that are on track to grow to global ubiquity.

The good news and practical reality may be that the explosion of blockspace supply from 60M to 200M gas limit seems likely to absolutely crater the L1 gas price. It will take time for demand to grow to meet the new supply, including from net new entrants (eg. GENIUS and institutions), induced demand from lower prices, and the coming next gen of return-to-mainnet-type eth native apps. 

By the time L1 blockspace demand catches up, we will be exploding supply again as we get closer to the full lean eth vision. That's eth's vision: postquantum and postAI ETH SoV, supported by ethereum's hypergrowing capacity, which is supported by best-in-class security and formal verification.

Looking back, it's unfortunate that we provided these affected contracts with a footgun that has put them in the situation where they were *able* to rely on fake guarantees that ethereum never promises (afaik, essentially just gas introspection). We're sorry.

imo it's time to roll forward on this. Let's do what we can in an appropriately scoped capacity for the affected contracts, then activate Glam asap, and continue our excellent progress towards global ubiquity.

author: tomkysar
quoted_text:
Kalshi and Polymarket’s fees are now so high you can’t actually trade. If you actively trade, you’ll erode any edge.

Consider the economics of trading a football game.

At 50¢, Kalshi charges 1.75¢ per taker execution. 

A trader entering and exiting a position 3 times over the course of a game makes 6 executions.

That’s 10.5¢ in Kalshi fees, before the spread. 

Assuming a 1¢ bid/ask spread, total execution costs across those 3 round trips are 13.5¢ per contract.

27% of your committed capital. 

On Kalshi, a taker trading near 50¢ must capture more than 4.5 percentage points of favorable repricing per round trip just to break even.

Suppose a trader can consistently identify 2% mispricings in live sports markets.

This trader has genuine predictive information. In a frictionless market, exploiting that information would be profitable.

On Kalshi or Polymarket, the same strategy is negative EV if executed through taker round trips.

A trader who continuously incorporates new information into prices pays repeatedly.

The fee structure therefore selects against active price discovery. 

Bullish on lower fee markets that enable better price discovery. Bearish on exchange extraction.

text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.
author: VitalikButerin

text:
**Vitalik Buterin 推文串翻译**  by grok

深入解释我为何认为应更聚焦于「ETH 作为价值存储（SoV）」，而非「ETH 作为费用燃烧代币」。

主要有三个原因：

1. ETH 作为费用燃烧代币从来没有想象中那么强。

2. 若优化 ETH 作为费用燃烧代币，会要求以太坊与 ETH 以极难与去中心化、抗捕获兼容的方式运作。

3. 相比之下，优化 ETH 作为 SoV，则与以太坊聚焦自身独特优势（去中心化与 CROPS）高度一致。

EIP-1559（包括其燃烧机制）本身是好的，应予以保留。但若费用燃烧长期低于盈亏平衡点的 10%，我们也不必为此难过——ETH 的价值来自别处。

核心观点：人们最欣赏以太坊的，是去中心化与 CROPS。这些特性最主要的实际益处是**稳定性**。SoV 正是这样一个类别：稳定性并非仅因意识形态而额外投入的“多余之物”，而是从资产持有者视角出发的实际优势。在 AI 颠覆的时代，稳定性将被高度珍视。

---

### 1. ETH 作为费用燃烧代币从来没有想象中那么强

先回顾费用燃烧代币估值背后的经济理论，即「净现值」（NPV）理论。

公式：  
市值 = 燃烧费用 / 贴现率

假设某代币每年稳定燃烧 10 亿美元，且这是长期均衡状态。再假设贴现率为 4%，即人们认为今天的 10 亿美元与一年后的 10.4 亿美元价值相当。

那么，10 亿 / 4% = 250 亿美元，可视为估值的自然“地板”：若市值跌破此线，有人就可以买入预期每年永续支付 1 美元的资产，且成本低于 25 美元（通过买入部分代币，再每年卖出超过 4% 的持仓，以保持自己在总池中的份额不变），从而可靠地跑赢市场。

2021-2023 年，以太坊曾以这种方式每年燃烧数百万枚 ETH。

但问题在于：这从来不是真正的“地板”。原因是，绝大部分燃烧来自加密内部用例。若 ETH 价格下跌 10 倍，这些用例的利润也会同步下跌，因为买家能用来支付的钱也少了。这既适用于那次著名的「一天燃烧 1.8 亿美元手续费的数字猴子销售」（确有其事，不记得就去查），也适用于借贷等更“正常”的场景。地板论证只有在收入流由外部支撑时才成立。

如今，以太坊因 RWA（现实世界资产）经济的增长，确实更有资格声称拥有外部支撑。但另一方面，正因为它正成为正常、稳定、成熟的业务，它不太可能再随机爆发并在数字猴子销售上烧掉 1.8 亿美元。

---

### 2. 优化 ETH 作为费用燃烧代币，会要求在去中心化与抗捕获上做出妥协

若我们真要优化 ETH 以通过费用燃烧来支撑当前约 2700 亿美元的市值，那么以太坊本质上就要像一家全球级大型企业那样运作——规模大约相当于欧莱雅（全球第 55 位左右）。

那么，真正的大型企业为了长期维持地位必须做什么？

1. 花钱。AI 估算欧莱雅每年在研发上的支出约为其市值的 0.58%。这会让以太坊基金会几乎立刻破产。因此需要协议内融资，规模约为每年 70 万枚 ETH，并伴随所有政治问题（验证者收入将被削减约 2/3）。而这仅仅是研发。企业还必须在除了“多生产现有产品”之外的许多事情上花钱。

2. 治理。要在新技术与新文化浪潮中存活，必须做出高度主观的选择：进入新市场、打造具有新功能的新产品，以吸引用新方式思考、使用最新技术的人群。以太坊需要长期保持高度干预性的治理。

不用说，这两点都远不利于优化抗捕获与去中心化。

此外还有另一个担忧：优化费用燃烧在某种程度上意味着优化高 gas 价格。这可能把用户（包括最需要隐私与安全的用户）挤出。使「价格 × 使用量」最大化的价格，所带来的使用量会低于「在安全区块链资源限制下尽可能允许最多使用」的价格。

---

### 3. 优化 ETH 作为 SoV，与去中心化与 CROPS 高度一致

每当我问人们最欣赏以太坊什么（相比其他区块链，或区块链之外的事物），最常见的回答是：去中心化与 CROPS（抗审查与抗捕获、开源、隐私与安全）。

去中心化与 CROPS 对机构也极具价值。对个人而言，隐私常被视为抽象意识形态；对机构而言，它是审慎的风险管理、数据保护法规合规等。安全同理，运行自己的节点也同理（企业术语：“本地部署”）。

但对 ETH 持有者而言呢？这取决于你为何持有 ETH。若你希望 ETH 最优地追逐金融趋势并从中收取费用，那么你需要一个“无畏领袖™”，在社交媒体上勇敢喊话以太坊热爱 XXX ，并务实地重新配置自身以提供明确的协议支持。

但若你持有 ETH 的主要原因是作为 SoV，那么你会用 SoV 相关指标来评判 ETH。最重要的 SoV 指标是什么？

存活下来。

这正是上届 Devcon 的核心主题之一（“后量子与后 AI”）。你希望链采取保守权衡（“仅哈希安全、全部形式化证明、轮数超过已知安全所需的 3 倍以上”）。你希望链至少追求部分“骨化”（ossification），一旦核心完成，大部分工作将转移到更高层。你希望链尽量减少协议政治，对会膨胀协议的预编译或可能被捕获的新型协议内奖励设置极高门槛。

其他 SoV 相关指标包括：

- 能轻松安全持有（因此推进多重签名工作）。
- 能私密持有（因此推进 Kohaku 工作）。
- 能同时私密且安全持有（因此 8288 与私人账户抽象工作流已启动）。
- 保证只要你有币就能发送，区块构建者无法阻止你（FOCIL）。
- 最小化基础设施依赖（基本上是整个去中心化路线图，包括我目前能在这台笔记本上运行节点，同步不到 6 小时，只占用硬盘 1/8——比 2019 年更好）。

那么，是否有与 SoV 高度协同的“采用”目标？

非常多。

在 L1 上原生发行的资产越多（包括 RWA 与原生去中心化资产），你能用 ETH“做”的事情就越多，越好。能轻松（且安全、无信任地）在 ETH 与其他资产间来回转换、用 ETH 作为抵押品做其他资产相关操作等，都构成持有 ETH 的效用。

服务这些用例与去中心化之间仍存在一些冲突（例如我们需谨慎对待快速出块对中心化的影响），但总体上远小于最大化费用所带来的冲突。

结论：
关心以太坊的最佳社会理由是：它让去中心化与 CROPS 特性成为更多人与更多用例的现实。  
持有 ETH 的最佳私人理由是其 SoV 属性，而这正是去中心化与 CROPS 的直接结果。

The whole discussion about CSPs canceling their memory LTAs doesn’t seem to start with supply and demand. It starts with the assumption that a lot of these data centers won’t get built, and then works backward to the conclusion that memory will be hit the hardest.

But what has actually changed in the fundamentals? Not much that I can see. What’s changed is the stock prices and the narrative the market is trading. And somehow that’s completely changed how people think about these memory LTAs.

Back in May or June, when everyone was talking about the LTAs memory makers had signed, the discussion was about tens of billions of dollars in customer deposits and how CSPs could lose a huge amount of money if they walked away from those contracts.

author: mindmoon_108
quoted_text:
I respect Jukan, but I feel a little frustrated whenever I see this kind of argument.

You can build any scenario around plausible assumptions, and yes, of course, the outcome will follow from those assumptions. If you assume demand collapses, customers accumulate inventory, and contract terms get renegotiated, then naturally, memory companies’ revenue and profits will decline.

But honestly, this feels like the perspective of analysts who treat memory as just a commodity you manufacture and sell, without properly understanding the technological changes taking place in custom memory.

Who exactly are these customers we are talking about when we say they could cancel LTAs or defer deliveries? They are the very customers working with memory companies to design the next generation of HBM and 3D stacked DRAM.

After jointly designing and validating these products, can customers really cancel those volumes so easily or push deliveries out by one or two years? How would they manufacture their own products, which were designed around that memory? What happens to the launch and system deployment schedules they have already coordinated? Switching suppliers also raises questions of design compatibility and requalification. If you are going to argue that contracts can be adjusted, you also need to explain what that decision would mean for the very customers canceling them.

This is one of the biggest reasons I keep saying that memory is no longer the same cyclical industry it used to be. The parties to these LTAs are already tied together from the design stage. But if you still view memory simply as a commodity where rising prices lead to more production, and inventory buildups lead to price cuts or canceled orders, you will inevitably miss this shift in the technical and business relationships.

One more thing. These arguments about a collapse in memory demand seem to assume that planned AI data center investments will be canceled on a massive scale, or that AI infrastructure expansion will slow so substantially that memory demand falls sharply. What interests me more than whether contracts can be adjusted is why you expect demand to weaken that dramatically in the first place.

I think it would be more realistic to discuss directly whether the AI era we expect will actually fail to materialize, and whether much of the AI infrastructure investment currently planned will disappear. If that is your outlook, I can at least understand why you would expect memory demand to collapse and customers to cut volumes even for products they have jointly developed.

• Fee-burning revenue is too dependent on speculative crypto activity to provide a reliable valuation floor

EIP-1559 stays, but ETH's value shouldn't depend on how much gets burned.

quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
Anthropic 豪掷 34 亿美元抢购燃气发电设备，AI 巨头已经开始直接争夺电力了。

据《金融时报》报道，Anthropic 从美国设备供应商 OnePWR 手中接手 1.7 GW 卡特彼勒重型燃气发电机组采购承诺，交易还包括工程和施工能力，但并未收购 OnePWR。

这不是孤立事件。

过去一年，Oracle、微软、Meta、AIP 等公司都在大规模锁定天然气发电资源：

Oracle：2.3 GW
AIP / Monarch：2 GW
微软：最高 2.5 GW
Meta：366 MW
Anthropic：1.7 GW

中国设备商也开始吃到这轮需求。杰瑞股份今年连续拿下美国数据中心燃气发电设备订单，相关客户累计订单已达 17.2 亿美元。

更有意思的是 SoftBank。

其旗下 SB Energy 正在推进俄亥俄州 9.2 GW 天然气发电项目，但 11 月 6 日，马斯克突然发文称 SoftBank 正在拖欠燃气轮机订单。目前这一说法尚未得到证实。

AI 竞争已经不只是 GPU 的军备竞赛。

当电网接入、变压器和燃气轮机都成为稀缺资源，谁能更早锁定电力，谁才有资格继续扩张算力。

AI 的下一场战争，可能不在芯片，而在电厂。

text:
PLEASE STOP FUCKING WITH ETHEREUM WITHOUT ASKING THE PEOPLE WHO BUILD ON IT: FIVE REASONS I AM TIRED

[feat. Wildcat Labs, a company that is filled with Ethereum die-hards and works exclusively on code that has originated over a billion dollars of economic activity for the chain, but these are my opinions not that of Labs itself etc]

---

REASON ONE: Our entire market deployment flow breaks on day one of Glamsterdam

Wildcat's core product involves a borrower creating a market that they've specified the way that they determine is best for them. That includes the core market itself (interest rate, underlying asset, debt token name), and a separate configuration (through hooks) granting access to the market and its functions (i.e. who can deposit, can debt be transferred, are withdrawal requests subject to a fixed-term tenor and so on).

In our currently deployed, immutable V2 code, what used to be a single transaction bundling those things together goes from 8.6M gas to ~62-71M, which means we can't fit it into a 60M block (don't you dare 'but ackshually' me, I am coming back to this).

Nothing in our contracts changed: the chain reprices bytecode deposits by 7.65x underneath already-audited code. We only have a workaround because our factory happens to expose the two halves separately, so we need to boot out an SDK and frontend release, plus pray folk are using a wallet that will sign a 35M gas field.

Every borrower's first market to date used a call that will no longer fit in a block as-is (I said I'm coming back to it).

The reason I am starting to... express opinions, is that this is the second time in a year that the execution layer has changed what a deployed contract costs to use (EIP-7825's cap in Fusaka, now state gas), and each time the burden of discovering it lands on us, the teams developing applications that drive economic activity on the chain, and we have to do it by replaying our own history on a testnet.

[This is going to be a long post. I am Not Pleased.]

---

REASON TWO: We are relying on social consensus for any hope of relief

The repricing aspect is consensus: at the fork, every validator must enforce it. The gas limit - the thing that would make a ~70M transaction possible post-Glamsterdam - is a validator-set preference with no mainnet schedule.

Sepolia was handed 200M, and things look fine over there. Hoodi had its 200M yeeted out the airlock the day the fork was postponed. So, the testnet that "proves" the fork works runs with over three times the headroom of mainnet, but the fork's own design assumes a headroom that nobody has committed to.

For a protocol that needs to tell institutional borrowers what a market costs to open, Wildcat's honest answer after Glamsterdam has to be "it depends on a social campaign to change validator config files," and that isn't a dependency that a credit product should carry. We are engineers, not lobbyists.

It also means Wildcat's capacity planning is hostage to the same ACD calls that are currently stalled on a security review of the very EIP that created the problem. 

You know what, Ameen, you are a core dev now. Why not.

---

REASON THREE: As-is, Safe App deployments of mainnet Wildcat markets fail after the fork

Safes are the default custody mechanism for exactly the borrowers Wildcat wants, and just over a third of V2 markets (29 of 82) were deployed via one.

Under EIP-8037, the GAS opcode no longer reports the reservoir, so a Safe's execution check (GS010) can never be satisfied for a transaction that needs more than the execution cap.

On either deploy entrypoint: the core market itself or its hooks.

Historical Wildcat Safe deployments set safeTxGas to zero and survive. The Safe App and safe-apps-provider path set it from the estimate... and die. :)

We can patch our own route (send safeTxGas 0, which our testnet branch already does), and we will. What nobody owns is the default: every Safe App on Ethereum that lets the provider fill safeTxGas from an estimate above ~16.4M dies in the same way.

This is not Wildcat's bug, nor is it Safe's in any useful sense.

It is a consensus change that silently invalidates a safety check in the most widely deployed smart-contract wallet on Ethereum, with no deprecation path, and as of today nobody owns fixing it. Building on a platform where our users' wallets can be broken by a gas-accounting EIP is something that every single protocol team should be screaming things that would get us put on trial in The Hague about.

---

REASON FOUR: Every single part of the tooling stack currently assumes tx.gas stops before the reservoir

Fusaka taught Ethereum developers that a transaction cannot exceed 16.78M, and so tooling calcified around that number because... why wouldn't it? It's not even a year old yet!

As it stands, geth's default 50M RPC cap can't estimate the combined deploy of a Wildcat V2 market, and public nodes cap eth_call the same way.

Even our own release ceremony prices contract deployments statically at 200 gas per byte against the 1,530 already live on Sepolia (our simulation gate catches it, the planner doesn't).

Glamsterdam now says the gas field can be 4.29 billion, with the part above 16.78M living in a reservoir that neither GAS nor most estimators nor any wallet UI understands yet.

When our V2.5 audit is done and it's time for us to deploy the necessary factories, the install is sixteen transactions and about six blocks' worth of gas, at most one big creation per block, and every wallet and integrator that Wildcat touches has to re-learn gas at the same time.

With no shared reference implementation.

None of this is Wildcat's code, all of it is Wildcat's outage, and the execution layer will have shipped two contradictory gas models in consecutive forks.

Masterful gambit.

[and this last one's just me being me about my most hated and well-known bugbear]

---

REASON FIVE: Code bytes are now 96 percent of what one of our markets costs to deploy, but the spec is still moving

I have spent coming up ten years - near enough since its introduction - begging for the death of EIP-170, and I genuinely don't know why I dared to believe that anything except a monkey's paw would answer me.

At 1,530 gas per byte, the cost of deploying a V2.5 market (when it launches) is almost entirely the price of copying 23 KB of bytecode into state. A lender’s first deposit to a Wildcat market costs about 3x the gas it would pre-Glamsterdam, because every fresh storage slot went from 22,100 gas to 110,020.

EIP-7954's promised 64 KB contracts are capped in practice at about 38 KB by a 60M block, so the one concession to builders in this fork - the one I have been asking for since my age first started leading with a 3 - is muted on mainnet until the aforementioned social campaign gets the gas limit bumped to 200M. Which we have to take on faith right now.

Meanwhile, the refill and reservoir semantics of EIP-8037 are under review, Hoodi is unscheduled and mainnet has no date, which means that Wildcat Labs just paid six figures to get Wildcat V2.5 into external audit against gas semantics that may change before it ships.

The cost - and the apparent lesson - of being an early, careful team on Ethereum is that you run the risk of needing to audit twice: once against the chain you deploy to, and once against the chain it becomes.

---

WHAT WE ARE DOING ABOUT THIS: Upcoming SDK and frontend releases will, defensively and until we can safely revert to type, split market creation into two transactions and send safeTxGas 0 on the Safe App route. Existing markets will keep running. Lenders will be affected in cost only: first touches (first deposit, opening a withdrawal request, first approval) about 2-3x, everything else 1.1-1.6x. What we cannot do is make a 65M transaction fit in a 60M block.

That part is on you lot, the social layer.

Further to the above, Wildcat Labs will happily send an invoice for an audit rebate to anyone willing to provide it if we end up having to re-check things for V2.5 once semantics are finalised.

Mind you, we'd provide an EOA, as we're a bit wary of anything contract-based right now.

Enjoy your Sundays.

text:
I have read the reaction of @marcusgnt and @ValerioCapraro to @ElliotGlazer astounding announcement. I strongly disagree with them and for practical reasons. 

I’m working on understanding and rewriting the OpenAI H10 paper: very far from done. But bringing Glazer’s work into the mix was actually helpful. It has shed light on some of the rewritings that a collaborator and I are trying to make. I’m still digesting things, and I’m not claiming to have verified his proposed proof, though I definitely hope eventually to understand it as well.

I disagree with the idea that “slop on slop” is somehow additive. The effect need not be cumulative in the negative direction. There can be a nonlinearity here, where an attempt at a harder result can shed light on an earlier undigested argument. That is actually exactly what I’m seeing empirically in this case. Making more raw material available can actually help.

It is the responsibility of the mathematical leadership to design new incentives that promote understanding. Asking people not to produce more raw material seems just not empirically useful and not an adequate response from academic leadership. 

Regarding Capraro's outrage. "The argument looks plausible, and plausibility takes the place of verification." Who said that this is so? The mathematical community will have to digest and verify these arguments of course. However the plausibility here is valuable for this process: this is more raw data that has a strong chance to be correct and be actually profitably used by the humans thinking about the proof. And I am not talking in generalities: this is exactly what is happening here.

关于美国各州数据中心的建设，虽然这两天负面满天飞，但近期这三个事件还是值得关注：
1、北达科他州哈伍德，选民以压倒性多数拒绝了针对数据中心的新的限制措施。这个小镇预计到2028年能获得165万美元的财产税收入，外加200多个永久性就业岗位。哈伍德的镇长：“我个人非常高兴能有这个数据中心。”

2、SpaceX宣布计划在亚利桑那州Cochise县建设超过700英亩的数据中心园区及电池储能系统。地点靠近未合并社区Cochise。SpaceX承诺：约1000个长期岗位，并表示“可能会完全从本地招募永久员工”。采用干冷系统（用空气而非水冷却）不会抽取地下水。并举行了社区见面会，开始多数居民反对，但在工作人员解答相关问题后部分人开始表示支持。

3、阿拉巴马州新当选的州长汤米·塔伯维尔宣布，该州将迎来数据中心，并将向所有小学生教授使用人工智能。

从这里能看出来：
1）数据中心如果能解决社区担心的电费、环境保护、水资源的问题之后、反对的声音就会小很多。

2）虽然很多地方反对建设数据中心的声音很大，但是也有不少地方看到数据中心建设带给本地就业机会和经济拉动作用。最后就变成了各州的争夺战。
