有人问经历过昨晚现在怎么看当下市场、跟4号这篇推文的没变化仍然是“AI中场和棒球第三局”。再看昨晚的抛售半导体是重灾区，大云、软件和应用则没那么严重。如之前聊到的，很多人形成了“AI=半导体=存储”的定式思维，一说AI就是半导体、一说半导体就是存储。其实AI也分上中下游，越往后中游的大云厂，下游的应用、agent会更受益以及各种应用场景。

要去拥抱AI主线迁移，每一阶段 AI 的主线都会迁移。今年一季度、二季度，Memory 是最强的；到 8、9 月以后，Optical 开始变强，同时一批之前被砸得很惨的软件、SaaS 也开始走出来。为什么？因为模型商品化、Token Price 下来以后，受益的不只上游 硬件。Token 越便宜，部署越容易，Cloud、Software、Enterprise Integration、Agent 反而会越来越受益。再下一阶段可能就是 AI for Science、Bio、更广泛的应用层。”这也是之前很早就聊到的。

但并不代表我之前没看到风险、引用的推文有我9月前后和10月初认为中期选举前美股要大动荡和调整的过往推文链接。如果说有失误、确实没有预期到民主党激进左翼的一个大概率落不了地的法案能给市场带来这么大的冲击。昨晚这里https://t.co/MRXQz02DVy有聊到。

为什么认为是AI中场而非尾声，核心好是这里https://t.co/thGYfi2Q5K聊到的，AI大规模商业化才过了三个季度，还在加速中。本季微软、亚马逊和谷歌的财报，云业务都在快速增长电话会上披露企业在采用AI进入了扩散阶段，“企业AI正从“购买席位”进入“持续消耗算力与Agent”的阶段，存量客户的消费深度和付费意愿，已成为当前最核心的增长引擎，然后增量客户还在提升。”、然后个人Agent、AI科学发现都在快速迭代。

这种情境下我很难认为AI就完结了，但受益的主线和板块会迁移这个要承认。

text:
卖破甲工具，三天赚20万，但是作者先进去了。

这是 dsh-purge 作者小杨的真实经历。

小杨真名杨浩。被裁员后，他在 X 和 GitHub 上说想接广告养活自己。因为一开始在仓库挂了微信赞赏码，他的实名信息其实早就暴露了，当时有人提醒，他没当回事。

第一天他自己卖了三四个安装服务，后来想到自己是实名的，就“不敢卖了”。

转折点在于夏特找上门。按小杨的说法，夏特承诺有老板能把他摘干净、让他匿名。小杨就交出了群和频道的所有权限，让夏特和铺仔去操作引流。

后来变成了大约 9 个人的售卖团队，包括“老魏、小杨、铺仔、夏特、adny、Lain、F佬、tt佬”，还有一个几乎没干活的。分成是小杨、老魏、铺仔三人各两成，其余人分四成。小杨说，另一个拿两成的人私下倒卖，靠着他们的流量，从一天几十 U 变成三天收入 3 万多 U。

结果大约五天后，小杨等来了传唤。这趟浑水走下来，小杨说自己一共只拿到 3000多U。到了 11 月 3 日，他把这笔钱全付给了帮他查链上信息、找人要证据的人。

我把整件事的脉络画在了配图里，原帖链接放首条回复。我平时长期关注网络安全、开源项目的法律边界，点个关注，后面如果另外几方出来回应，我再给大家同步。

AI能力越来越强，当你有“好思路”的时候，是会一门心思扎进去做，还是先问问AI情与法的边界在哪里？

text:
我发现币圈有个挺有意思的现象。

很多人研究一个币，恨不得把白皮书翻烂，却很少研究自己为什么非要买它。

看到别人赚钱，觉得机会来了。

看到价格回调，觉得便宜了。

看到项目方出来喊话，又觉得信心回来了。

折腾半天，买入理由换了好几个，唯独仓位一直没变。

最离谱的是，有些人明明做的是投机，却非要给自己找一套投资逻辑。

买的时候想赚个短线，跌了以后开始研究基本面。

研究着研究着，连项目方都没他了解这个项目。

可惜了解得再多，也改变不了当初买入位置不合理的事实。

我现在越来越觉得，币圈很多亏损不是因为信息不够，而是因为信息太多。

你看好一个币，总能找到十条利好。

你想继续持有，也总能找到几个大V替你坚定信仰。

互联网最不缺的，就是支持你当前想法的证据。

真正麻烦的是，你会慢慢失去独立判断的能力。

“Welcome to the @InvsbleFriends community,” @AdamWeitsman ... a sentence I would have bet my life I wouldn’t be saying three years and numerous nightmares later 😂

Adam and I have been long overdue for a proper chat and, by some miracle, finally managed to make it happen this evening. We covered a lot of territory, from PFP communities to the Council of Luci and so much in between.

We share a common origin story into web3 via PFPs, and both would say some of our closest friends are people we met by being a part of those communities. 

My first interaction with Adam was a bit ago after @RealPapii had messaged me because Adam was looking to join @quirkiesnft and I held a 1/1 that was perfect for him. After some arm twisting from Papii (kidding), I was honored to play a small role in that story.

Reminiscing about that time led to a discussion about my first NFT community, Invisible Friends, and how thrilled I was that @coinbilly had finally succeeded in taking ownership of the project. I explained how he was responsible for many of the epic things the collection had accomplished, including the Kith collab, which IMO is still one of the best web3 collabs to date.

During this discussion I told Adam I wanted to send him one of my “Friends” I had held onto during some of the project’s darkest days. Ultimately I felt the Kith Friend 1/1 Miami Edition was the perfect fit, a hidden gem with a great backstory.

I share all of this because tonight I was reminded of one of my favorite things about this crazy space: how a shared love for these JPEGs brings together people from different backgrounds and life experiences.

I came away from the conversation with a renewed passion for protecting our artists, our collectors, our space, and the joy that comes from collecting art and the friends we make along the way. 🖤

text:
朋友推荐了个项目让我看下，我研究了下，发现有潜力，所以做一下分享。

项目推特： @motiongift 

项目定位
一个综合性的Terminal，目前主要是meme的交易平台，在拓展Earn和Perps等终端功能

项目特点
我个人研究觉得有几处优势：

1️⃣费用：主流的meme交易平台费用基本是1%，motion平台的费用设定是0.2%（持有平台币还可以优惠），当前实际上是0 fee，对于频繁交易的meme玩家来说，费用实际上是敏感的，这会是一个比较明显的优势。

2️⃣社区属性：大部分的meme交易平台是“抽水”性质的，虽然refer会返回一定的手续费，但是其他部分完全是由平台抽走，并不会回馈回crypto或回馈社区。motion平台的所有净营收（终端、API、会员）和部分的 $motion 税费都会用来回购/销毁平台币，这是回馈社区的机制，类似于 pons，这和“抽水”就不是一个性质了。

3️⃣多元：大部分的meme交易平台只专注于meme，比如拓展更多的链，比如拓展bot等，但是motion侧重于多元，这也是他们在开发Earn还有perps 终端的原因，让资金可以在一个终端内实现尽可能多的功能，这是一个很好的feature，甚至这里面会有一些奇妙的组合可能形成化学反应（一笔钱可以在perps、defi、meme种随时转换阵地）。

我的使用感受是：基本功能都是有的，比如战壕、限价单、滑点设置、Alpha评分、Feed、稳定币全链交易、快速交易、详细的history等（不仅仅是交易数据，还包含非交易数据）；交易速度还行，跟主流平台的差别不大。

当然，这个项目也有自身的缺点：

1️⃣当前处于早期，beta版本，使用的人数不多，如果人数增多是否可以很好的适配体验是需要观察的；

2️⃣项目的一些提示、使用体感上还是有瑕疵的，这个需要在使用过程中反馈→优化去解决；

3️⃣项目代码还没有完成审计（看官网介绍正在进行中），所以安全性还需要进一步的观察。

玩meme的玩家，我觉得可以去看一下，至少目前0 fee的特点，也是值得看一眼的。

text:
# 1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed

Let us re-cap the economic theory behind valuation of a fee-burning token. This is the "net present value" (NPV) theory.

Formula: market cap = fees burned / discount rate

Imagine you have a token of which $1 billion is burned per year, and this is a long-term stable equilibrium. Now, imagine the discount rate is 4%; that is, people value having $1B today as much as $1.04B in one year.

The idea is that $1B / 4% = $25B serves as a natural "floor" for the valuation: if the valuation drops lower than that, then someone could buy an asset expected to pay $1 per year forever for less than $25 (by buying some tokens, and then selling >4% of their supply each year so their share of the total pie remains the same), and so by buying the asset you reliably beat the market.

In 2021-23, Ethereum burned millions of ETH per year in this way.

But here's the problem: this was never a true floor. The reason is that the bulk of that burn was crypto-internal use cases. If ETH had dropped by 10x, then the profits from those use cases would have also dropped, because all the buyers would have had much less money to pay with. This applies both to things like that infamous $180m-fees-burned-in-one-day digital monkey sale (yes, this happened; if you don't remember look it up!), and to more "normal" things like lending. The floor argument only works if the backing of the revenue stream is external.

Today, Ethereum actually has a better claim to this external backing, because of the growing RWA economy, but on the other hand, perhaps precisely because it's a normal stable mature business, it's not going to randomly go crazy and burn $180m on a digital monkey sale.
author: VitalikButerin

text:
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand compromising decentralization and capture resistance

If we decide we actually want to optimize ETH for burning fees to justify a present-day ~$270B market cap, then Ethereum would essentially be functioning as a world-scale major corporation - it would be somewhere around L'Oreal (#55).

Now, what do *real* major corporations have to do in order to maintain their positions in the long term?

1. They spend. AI estimates L'Oreal as spending ~0.58% of its market cap per year on R&D. This would bankrupt the EF almost immediately. So this would require in-protocol funding to the tune of ~700k ETH per year, with all the political issues that it entails (so validator revenue would get cut by 2/3). And that's just R&D. Corporations have to spend on all kinds of things beyond just cranking out more units of their pre-existing product.
2. They govern. To survive new waves of technology and culture, you have to make highly opinionated choices to go after new markets, make new kinds of products with new features to appeal to people who think in new ways and use the newest technologies. Ethereum would need to have highly interventionist governance, for the long term.

Needless to say, both of these are far from conducive to optimizing capture resistance and decentralization.

On top of this there is another concern: optimizing for fee burning means optimizing for high gas prices to some degree. This may price out users, including some users who may need privacy and security the most. The price that maximizes price * usage leads to less usage than the price that allows as much usage as possible subject to safe blockchain resource limits.

Andrej Karpathy:

“A 1B model can be much more effective than most current LLMs.

90% of current models waste a ton of capacity and money on remembering stuff that doesn’t matter.”

here is his 5 core thesis about Small LLM’s:

1. the intelligence was never the knowledge. Strip the memorized internet, keep the reasoning. What’s left is the cognitive core, and it’s small.

2. the core might fit in ~1B params. Maybe less. “Plenty of room at the bottom.” We’ve been paying for a library when we needed a brain.

3. size stopped being the bottleneck. What makes an agent work is the tools it can call and how tight the feedback loop is, not parameter count.

4. intelligence lives in the system, not the weights. A raw LLM is a CPU with no OS. Small core + good harness > giant model alone.

5. you can own it. A model on your hardware is one no one can rate-limit, price-hike, or deprecate on you.

in 12 months the gap between teams shipping on-device and teams paying per-token frontier bills won’t be capability.

TwIL an 8.8B model at 90%+ of frontier isn’t a benchmark flex.

It’s the thesis Karpathy’s been repeating all year, made real.

Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

text:
A friend who left the music industry once told me a Drake theory that stuck with me.

Drake's sound is so distinctive that when a producer makes a beat that sounds remotely like him, their instinct is to get it to Drake. The industry effectively conspires to send him the most Drake-like beats, and he gets his pick of the litter.

I think something similar happens in venture.

Take Thiel. He's known for backing contrarian ideas, so when people come across a really unconventional company, they think to send it his way. I've even caught myself doing this with deals. 

In venture, your reputation for the types of deals you do shapes which types of deals you see.

author: barnabemonnot
quoted_text:
3. Optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with decentralization and CROPS

Whenever I ask what people appreciate the most about Ethereum (as opposed to either other blockchains, or anything outside the blockchain world), the most common answer is: decentralization and CROPS (censorship and capture resistance, open source, privacy and security).

Decentralization and CROPS have a lot of value, even to institutions. For individuals, privacy is often viewed as an abstract ideology. For institutions, it's prudent risk management, data protection law compliance, and a number of other things. Likewise for security. And likewise for running your own node (enterprise buzzword: "on-prem deployment").

But what about for the ETH holder? Well, it depends why you're an ETH holder. If you want ETH to optimally chase financial trends and collect fees from them, then you want a Fearless Leader™ who bravely shouts on the socials that Ethereum loves [insert opportunity here] and will pragmatically reconfigure itself to give it explicit protocol support.

But if your primary reason to hold ETH is as an SoV, then you will be judging ETH by SoV-ish metrics. And what is the first and most important SoV-ish metric?

To survive.

That's what a big chunk of this last Devcon was about ("post-quantum and post-AI"). You want a chain that is taking conservative tradeoffs ("hash-only security, all formally proven, >3x more rounds than known to be necessary for security"). You want a chain that is aiming for at least partial ossification, where the great balance of work will move to higher levels of the stack once the core is complete. You want a chain that aims to minimize protocol politics, by having a very high bar before it accepts either precompiles that bloat the protocol or new kinds of in-protocol rewards that could get captured.

What other SoV'ish metrics?

The ability to easily hold it safely (hence, work on multisigs).
The ability to hold it privately (hence, kohaku work).
The ability to hold it privately *and* safely (hence, 8288 and private-AA workstreams already starting).
The guarantee that if you have coins, you can send them, and block builders can't stop you (FOCIL)
Minimized infrastructure dependence (basically the whole decentralization roadmap, including the fact that I am able to currently run a node on this laptop, and it synced in < 6 hours and takes up only 1/8 of my hard drive - better stats than in 2019!)

Now, are there "adoption" goals that are highly synergistic with SoV?

Very much so.

The more assets there are natively issued on L1, including both RWAs and native decentralized assets, the larger a set of things you can "do" with your ETH, the better. Being able to easily (including safely, trustlessly) convert back and forth between ETH and other assets, use ETH as collateral to do things with other assets, etc, all forms part of the utility of holding ETH.

There are still some conflicts between serving these use cases and decentralization (eg. we want to be careful about fast slots and impact on centralization), but on the whole much less than what you get if you maximize fees.

Conclusion:

The best social reason to care about Ethereum is because it makes decentralization and CROPS properties a reality for more people and uses.

The best private reason to hold ETH is its SoV properties, which are a direct consequence of that decentralization and CROPS.

AI 城市，怎么建？台北选举最新消息，沈伯洋「学界后援会」今天成立，近 1300 位学界人士联署支持。而我关注点是专门研究 AI 的台大资工美女教授陈縕儂。

我在前一个感想帖里写道：AI 时代的城市需要重新思考布局，也参考了沈伯洋的一个判断：「算力层不在台北，台北要做的是应用层。」

当时有评论觉得，讨论市政扯到 AI，太远了，不切实际。结果今天听台大陈縕儂教授的发言，发现她讲的和我想表达的几乎一致：一座城市发展 AI，到底需要多少土地，和它能不能形成 AI 生态系，是两件需要分别想清楚的事。

整理几个有意思的信息（想了解可以了解）
1️⃣ 这场后援会由台大历史系名誉教授周婉窈、政大社会系教授黄厚铭发起，最初目标只有 50 人，最后有 1292 人填表声援，从一个小规模的学界倡议，变成近 1300 人的联署。
2️⃣ 活动采用政见论坛的形式，邀请 5 位不同领域的学者上台对谈，沈伯洋逐一回应。
3️⃣ 陈縕儂是卡内基梅隆大学博士，曾任职微软研究院，研究专长包括自然语言处理、语言理解和对话系统。
4️⃣ 她发言的关键信息：「AI 城市需要的，不是好几百公顷的土地；不是盖了资料中心、建了算力，就自然变成 AI 城市。生态系才是关键。」
5️⃣ 对照蒋万安 10 月 8 日提出迁移松山机场，规划以机场及周边 300 公顷打造「台北 AI 园区」，其中 100 公顷作为产业聚落，两边对于台北如何抓住 AI 机会，确实有不同的切入点。

平台有二次确认环节（会显示收款人姓名、头像等），用户没有仔细核对就确认了。

加密资产转账的基本原则是“自己核对清楚”，这是行业共识。

支付机构是“指令执行者”，不是“意思表示审核者”。用户在发出支付指令前有核对义务。

还有，最常见的是电话号码，不同国家的电话号码是有概率相同的，不同的是国家代码。这才是区分。

再说说OKX啊，之前OKX 转账列表优先展示合约地址，而不是用户自己的交易所地址。

重度用户习惯性点选列表第一项，结果把钱转到了合约地址。

该用户及朋友因此损失约 6000 美金。

产品团队后来很快调整了排序逻辑，但已经造成的损失由用户自行承担，申诉无门。

然后何一出于人道主义，赔了点钱

徐明星一分没赔。

text:
推荐 Anthropic 刚发布的《How researchers use Claude》，文章中分析了 20 多万条科研相关的 Claude 会话，看看 AI 到底在帮研究人员做些什么。

其中 Claude Code 近一半的科研会话都在做数据分析，用于提出研究想法和假设的却只有 2.1%。

但在另一项科研人员调查中，大家反而把提出研究问题和假设看得最重要。

文章还尝试解释了背后的技术原因。

作者把科研工作拆成具体任务，发现 AI 的能力与任务是否适合 RL 高度相关。像写代码、统计分析，结果容易验证，也能快速获得反馈；而一个研究假设究竟有没有价值，往往很难立即判断。

另一个值得关注的变化来自 Claude Science。

它把蛋白质结构、药物、论文等专业数据库接入同一个 Workflow，让 Agent 能跨工具收集证据、分析问题。假设生成类任务在 Claude Science 中的占比也更高，不过这还不能证明提升完全来自工具接入。

所以 Research Agent 接下来值得投入的方向，是把文献检索、数据分析和实验验证真正串起来。

让 Agent 提出一个想法已经不难，如何让它找到可靠证据、设计验证方法，并根据结果不断修正，才是更有挑战性的部分。

text:
AI 城市，怎么建？台北选举最新消息，沈伯洋「学界后援会」今天成立，近 1300 位学界人士联署支持。而我关注点是专门研究 AI 的台大资工美女教授陈縕儂。

我在前一个感想帖里写道：AI 时代的城市需要重新思考布局，也参考了沈伯洋的一个判断：「算力层不在台北，台北要做的是应用层。」

当时有评论觉得，讨论市政扯到 AI，太远了，不切实际。结果今天听台大陈縕儂教授的发言，发现她讲的和我想表达的几乎一致：一座城市发展 AI，到底需要多少土地，和它能不能形成 AI 生态系，是两件需要分别想清楚的事。

整理几个有意思的信息（想了解可以了解）
1️⃣ 这场后援会由台大历史系名誉教授周婉窈、政大社会系教授黄厚铭发起，最初目标只有 50 人，最后有 1292 人填表声援，从一个小规模的学界倡议，变成近 1300 人的联署。
2️⃣ 活动采用政见论坛的形式，邀请 5 位不同领域的学者上台对谈，沈伯洋逐一回应。
3️⃣ 陈縕儂是卡内基梅隆大学博士，曾任职微软研究院，研究专长包括自然语言处理、语言理解和对话系统。
4️⃣ 她发言的关键信息：「AI 城市需要的，不是好几百公顷的土地；不是盖了资料中心、建了算力，就自然变成 AI 城市。生态系才是关键。」
5️⃣ 对照蒋万安 10 月 8 日提出迁移松山机场，规划以机场及周边 300 公顷打造「台北 AI 园区」，其中 100 公顷作为产业聚落，两边对于台北如何抓住 AI 机会，确实有不同的切入点。

author: yugacohler
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
【Vitalik重新定义ETH价值：不靠手续费销毁，靠价值储存】

以太坊创始人Vitalik Buterin发表长文，重新讨论ETH的价值来源。他认为，与其将ETH视为依靠手续费销毁支撑估值的代币，不如更加重视其作为价值储存资产（Store of Value，SoV）的定位。

这一观点意味着，以太坊的价值逻辑可能需要重新审视：ETH的长期价值，不一定来自更高的Gas费用和更多的代币销毁，而可能来自以太坊自身的去中心化、安全性、抗审查能力，以及作为全球资产基础设施的稳定性。

Vitalik强调，EIP-1559及其手续费销毁机制仍然有价值，应该继续保留。但即使未来手续费销毁量长期低于实现收支平衡所需水平的10%，也不必因此失望，因为ETH的价值来源并不局限于手续费销毁。

一、手续费销毁，真的能够支撑ETH估值吗？
过去几年，ETH的一项重要估值逻辑是：以太坊网络使用量越大，产生的Gas费用越多，销毁的ETH就越多，进而减少供应量，支撑代币价格。

这种逻辑可以用净现值（NPV）模型解释：

代币市值=年度手续费销毁价值÷贴现率

例如，一种代币每年稳定销毁价值10亿美元的代币，假设贴现率为4%，那么理论估值可以达到250亿美元。

2021年至2023年，以太坊每年曾销毁数百万枚ETH，这也成为市场看好ETH通缩叙事的重要依据。

但Vitalik认为，这个模型存在一个根本问题：手续费销毁并不能天然形成可靠的估值底部。

原因在于，当时大量手续费来自Crypto行业内部的经济活动，包括NFT、DeFi借贷和链上投机交易。

如果ETH价格下跌10倍，参与这些活动的用户购买力和相关业务利润也可能同步下降，手续费收入自然难以维持。

Vitalik特别提到，过去曾出现单日因数字猴子NFT销售而销毁价值约1.8亿美元手续费的极端案例。但这种由投机热潮驱动的收入，并不意味着网络拥有长期稳定的现金流。

相比之下，随着RWA（现实世界资产）发展，以太坊正在获得更多来自真实经济活动的需求。

不过，成熟稳定的RWA业务，也不太可能像NFT狂热时期那样突然创造天量手续费。

二、如果追求手续费最大化，以太坊可能变成一家大型企业
Vitalik提出了另一个值得关注的问题：

如果以太坊要通过手续费销毁支撑约2700亿美元的市值，那么它实际上需要像一家全球大型企业那样经营。

以欧莱雅为例，Vitalik引用的AI估算显示，该公司每年研发投入约占市值的0.58%。

如果以太坊按照类似标准投入研发，就需要每年约70万枚ETH的协议级资金支持。这不仅可能大幅压缩验证者收入，也会带来复杂的资金分配和治理问题。

更重要的是，大型企业为了保持竞争力，需要不断进入新市场、开发新产品，并根据技术趋势主动调整经营策略。

如果以太坊采取类似模式，就意味着协议治理需要长期保持高度干预。

但这恰恰与以太坊追求的去中心化和抗俘获能力存在冲突。

此外，追求更高的手续费销毁，在一定程度上意味着希望网络维持较高的Gas价格。

这可能增加用户使用成本，甚至将部分最需要隐私和安全保护的用户排除在外。

Vitalik认为，最大化网络手续费收入，与在安全资源限制内尽可能扩大网络使用量，并不是同一个目标。

三、ETH应该成为真正的价值储存资产
相比于手续费销毁，Vitalik更看重ETH的价值储存属性。

他认为，以太坊相较其他区块链最独特的优势，是去中心化以及CROPS：

抗审查（CensorshipResistance）
抗俘获（CaptureResistance）
开源（OpenSource）
隐私（Privacy）
安全（Security）
这些特性并不只是技术理念，也具有实际经济价值。

对于机构而言，隐私意味着风险管理和数据合规，安全意味着资产保护，运行独立节点则意味着减少对外部基础设施的依赖。

如果将ETH视为价值储存资产，那么衡量它的首要标准就不再是手续费收入，而是：

这条网络能否长期、安全、稳定地存在？

Vitalik特别强调，以太坊应该重视后量子和后AI时代的安全挑战，采取更加保守的协议设计，并逐步实现核心协议的部分固化（Ossification）。

所谓协议固化，就是在核心功能逐步成熟后，减少不必要的底层修改，将更多创新转移到上层应用。

这能够降低协议复杂度，也有助于减少治理争议和潜在的利益俘获。

在具体技术方向上，Vitalik提到了多重签名钱包、Kohaku隐私技术、EIP-8288、隐私账户抽象以及FOCIL等工作。

这些技术分别围绕资产安全、隐私保护和交易抗审查展开。

他还举例称，目前自己已经能够在笔记本电脑上运行以太坊节点，同步时间不到6小时，存储空间仅占硬盘容量的八分之一，相关指标甚至优于2019年。

四、RWA与链上资产，仍然是ETH的重要增长方向
强调价值储存，并不意味着以太坊不再需要应用和生态增长。

恰恰相反，Vitalik认为，RWA和原生去中心化资产的发展，与ETH的价值储存定位具有很强的协同效应。

随着更多资产直接发行在以太坊L1，ETH持有者能够参与的金融活动也会更加丰富。

例如，用户可以在ETH与其他资产之间安全、无需信任第三方地进行转换，也可以将ETH作为抵押品，参与其他资产相关的金融活动。

这意味着，ETH的实用价值不仅来自网络手续费，还来自它在整个链上资产体系中的作用。

当然，生态扩张与去中心化之间仍然需要权衡，例如缩短区块Slot时间可能对节点运行和网络中心化程度产生影响。

但Vitalik认为，这些矛盾总体上要小于单纯追求手续费最大化所带来的问题。

五、ETH估值逻辑正在发生变化？
Vitalik的这篇文章，实际上对过去市场熟悉的ETH估值框架提出了不同看法。

过去，市场更关注以太坊的交易量、Gas费用、ETH销毁数量，以及由此产生的通缩预期。

但在Vitalik看来，以太坊真正应该建立的长期竞争力，是成为一个安全、稳定、去中心化，并且能够长期承载全球资产的基础设施。

从这一角度看，ETH的价值储存属性，与以太坊网络的去中心化程度、抗审查能力、隐私保护和安全性密切相关。

不过，这也留下了一个值得市场继续讨论的问题：

如果ETH的价值不再主要依赖手续费销毁，那么市场应该如何衡量其价值储存溢价？

毕竟，网络安全性和去中心化程度能够提升资产的可信度，但这种优势最终能够转化为多大的ETH持有需求，仍然取决于实际采用、市场认可和长期资产配置行为。

Vitalik最终强调，以太坊最重要的公共价值，是让更多人和应用真正获得去中心化、抗审查、隐私和安全等能力。

而对于ETH持有人而言，最重要的长期价值，则来自这些特性所形成的价值储存属性。

以太坊不必成为一家不断追求收入最大化的公司，而应该成为一种能够长期存在、值得信任的金融基础设施。

author: MisterNarcos
quoted_text:
After five years as CFO of Binance, I have decided to go build something of my own.

The past ten years in the digital asset exchange space have felt surprisingly short, because I enjoyed what I was doing. Having passion for what you do is so important, and I will come back to this point.  8am to 2am became a work habit. When I felt exhausted past midnight, I would just look up at the Kobe Bryant's statue standing in the corner of my office, and go right back to the grind!

It has been the privilege of my career to help steward the finances of the world's largest digital asset exchange through a period that tested our industry in every way: bull and bear cycles, Operation Choke Point 2.0, and a regulatory landscape that evolved as quickly as the technology itself. Finance is seldom the loudest function in a company, but it is where trust is earned. Over these five years, we transformed Finance from a pure back-office function into one that consistently generates new ideas and revenue opportunities for the company. We became amazing problem solvers.  Finance understood the products and metrics as well as the business units themselves.  Proud of what we have built together, and I am pleased to hand the keys to Justin, our next CFO.

I want to take this opportunity to thank CZ, Yi, Richard, and the leadership team for their confidence and, above all, the amazing Binancians around the world whom I had the honor of working with. You are the reason the company stands where it does today. Binance is in very capable hands.

The company continues to grow and evolve with the successful launch of TradFi assets and AI-powered user interfaces. I’d like to express my gratitude to MGX for the trust; to our home regulator Abu Dhabi Global Market and all regulators we work closely with; and to our business partners, including BlackRock, Circle, Franklin Templeton, Mastercard, our banking partners and payment channels, as well as our advisors and auditors. Special thanks to Grant Thornton Singapore and everyone who has supported Binance.

As for what comes next, well, there isn't just one project but several that I am passionate about particularly in sports and entertainment, from basketball and music, to GPUs, robotics, gold and collectibles. Bringing these real-world assets onto the blockchain through tokenization is a massive opportunity for the industry, and a big unlock for everyone.  I welcome anyone with a passion in these areas to message me and potentially join my team.  Even better if you love Kobe ;)

Moving from the CFO's chair to the founder's is a leap, and I take it with humility. I deeply believe it is where I can make a greater contribution to AI and Web3.

For now, thank you, Binance, for five remarkable years.

text:
how to make money doing arbitrage

there's a ~5% price gap between lighter & variational

the play: compare prices > match exposure > check costs > track the gap

> how it works

- long the cheaper openai perp
- short the more expensive one
- close both if the gap narrows enough to cover your costs

you're trading the difference between two prices, not simply predicting openai goes up

> first step

- check the actual buy quote on variational
- check the actual sell quote on lighter
- use your intended order size, not the price on a chart
- compare the contract specs before treating them as the same exposure

> size both sides properly

- match the underlying exposure after checking contract multipliers
- equal deposits don't automatically mean an equal hedge
- keep margin available on both venues
- profit on one venue can't automatically save a liquidation on the other

> the catch most people skip

- these are derivatives, not openai shares
- variational derives its pre ipo index from external venues
- lighter uses internal pricing before ipo
- variational says its contract transitions after ipo; lighter says its pre ipo market settles and delists

same ticker. different pricing and settlement rules. nothing guarantees the gap closes on your schedule

> check the actual costs

- funding on both legs
- entry and exit spreads
- trading fees and slippage
- moving collateral between venues

variational's published pre ipo funding is fixed at 0.005% every 8 hours. don't assume both legs cancel each other's funding

> what not to do

- don't call the displayed gap your profit
- don't add leverage just because you've opened a hedge
- don't count points as cash or a confirmed airdrop
- don't deposit before checking both venues' country restrictions

less exposure to market direction doesn't mean less exposure to every other risk

On the MetaDAO/Percolator drama: I tend to agree with this take

- Rug the token, move on to a new one capable of giving you the capital formation you need

- Get M&A-ed for your IP, and soft rug the token

You can’t exclusively blame platforms for this, it’s also up to market participants to start discerning what the outcome is going to look like and take action accordingly

Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
3. Optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with decentralization and CROPS

Whenever I ask what people appreciate the most about Ethereum (as opposed to either other blockchains, or anything outside the blockchain world), the most common answer is: decentralization and CROPS (censorship and capture resistance, open source, privacy and security).

Decentralization and CROPS have a lot of value, even to institutions. For individuals, privacy is often viewed as an abstract ideology. For institutions, it's prudent risk management, data protection law compliance, and a number of other things. Likewise for security. And likewise for running your own node (enterprise buzzword: "on-prem deployment").

But what about for the ETH holder? Well, it depends why you're an ETH holder. If you want ETH to optimally chase financial trends and collect fees from them, then you want a Fearless Leader™ who bravely shouts on the socials that Ethereum loves [insert opportunity here] and will pragmatically reconfigure itself to give it explicit protocol support.

But if your primary reason to hold ETH is as an SoV, then you will be judging ETH by SoV-ish metrics. And what is the first and most important SoV-ish metric?

To survive.

That's what a big chunk of this last Devcon was about ("post-quantum and post-AI"). You want a chain that is taking conservative tradeoffs ("hash-only security, all formally proven, >3x more rounds than known to be necessary for security"). You want a chain that is aiming for at least partial ossification, where the great balance of work will move to higher levels of the stack once the core is complete. You want a chain that aims to minimize protocol politics, by having a very high bar before it accepts either precompiles that bloat the protocol or new kinds of in-protocol rewards that could get captured.

What other SoV'ish metrics?

The ability to easily hold it safely (hence, work on multisigs).
The ability to hold it privately (hence, kohaku work).
The ability to hold it privately *and* safely (hence, 8288 and private-AA workstreams already starting).
The guarantee that if you have coins, you can send them, and block builders can't stop you (FOCIL)
Minimized infrastructure dependence (basically the whole decentralization roadmap, including the fact that I am able to currently run a node on this laptop, and it synced in < 6 hours and takes up only 1/8 of my hard drive - better stats than in 2019!)

Now, are there "adoption" goals that are highly synergistic with SoV?

Very much so.

The more assets there are natively issued on L1, including both RWAs and native decentralized assets, the larger a set of things you can "do" with your ETH, the better. Being able to easily (including safely, trustlessly) convert back and forth between ETH and other assets, use ETH as collateral to do things with other assets, etc, all forms part of the utility of holding ETH.

There are still some conflicts between serving these use cases and decentralization (eg. we want to be careful about fast slots and impact on centralization), but on the whole much less than what you get if you maximize fees.

Conclusion:

The best social reason to care about Ethereum is because it makes decentralization and CROPS properties a reality for more people and uses.

The best private reason to hold ETH is its SoV properties, which are a direct consequence of that decentralization and CROPS.

2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand compromising decentralization and capture resistance

If we decide we actually want to optimize ETH for burning fees to justify a present-day ~$270B market cap, then Ethereum would essentially be functioning as a world-scale major corporation - it would be somewhere around L'Oreal (#55).

Now, what do *real* major corporations have to do in order to maintain their positions in the long term?

1. They spend. AI estimates L'Oreal as spending ~0.58% of its market cap per year on R&D. This would bankrupt the EF almost immediately. So this would require in-protocol funding to the tune of ~700k ETH per year, with all the political issues that it entails (so validator revenue would get cut by 2/3). And that's just R&D. Corporations have to spend on all kinds of things beyond just cranking out more units of their pre-existing product.
2. They govern. To survive new waves of technology and culture, you have to make highly opinionated choices to go after new markets, make new kinds of products with new features to appeal to people who think in new ways and use the newest technologies. Ethereum would need to have highly interventionist governance, for the long term.

Needless to say, both of these are far from conducive to optimizing capture resistance and decentralization.

On top of this there is another concern: optimizing for fee burning means optimizing for high gas prices to some degree. This may price out users, including some users who may need privacy and security the most. The price that maximizes price * usage leads to less usage than the price that allows as much usage as possible subject to safe blockchain resource limits.

text:
Blessed Sunday Booelievers 🕊📖

On November 8, 1895, Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays.

For the first time, humanity found a way to see what had always been there, but remained hidden from our eyes.

A discovery that would transform medicine and save countless lives.

But perhaps the most remarkable part?

Röntgen chose not to patent his discovery.

He believed its benefits should belong to humanity.

131 years later, that spirit lives on in a different frontier.

Ethereum.

quoted_text:
Here's a concrete example of how Glamsterdam repricing breaks existing assumptions around Uniswap v4 smart contracts. (Not an exploit: nothing is live yet + the problem was already known to security researchers in the summer.)

v4 PositionManager allows contracts to subscribe to LP positions and get notified when the position is changed or transferred. This is useful for staking and rewards distribution, but it means calling untrusted 3rd party code from a protocol contract. The protocol wants to ensure that such a subscriber is not able to (1) DoS the operations around the position; (2) consume unlimited gas. Conversely, as long as (1) and (2) hold, an honest subscriber should keep getting notified when something happens to the position. 

To enforce 1-2 around the `unsubscribe` operation specifically, v4 deployments limit the gas that can be consumed by it. On mainnet, the limit is 150k - a protocol config setting. (It used to be 1% of the block's gaslimit, which is a more futureproof design, but was changed to a per-deployment constant before launch.)

Before Glamsterdam, creating new state used to cost around 22k gas per slot - so the 150k limit was plenty for that. Afterwards, it costs around 110k for a single slot, so the subscriber may well run out of gas if it's writing any new slots. The saving grace is that around 90% of that gas is paid from a separate pool - the "state gas reservoir". So if the reservoir is present, it's used until it gets empty; then the tx starts consuming regular gas.

The reservoir is only present when the initial tx gas is set above 16M (the max gas limit for normal gas - yes it's confusing!). If the user fails to do that AND the 150k limit is insufficient, they will leave the subscriber in a broken state after an `unsubscribe` call.

The mirror reflection of this problem is that when the subscriber wants to go wild, it can. If the user sets the gas limit to 16M + X, the subscriber can spend most of that X - it will not be capped by the 150k gas limit configured in the Uniswap contract. This is a griefing attack, not a DoS.

The good news is that the breakage is due to new state creation, it can be prevented if the user sending the tx sets a large enough gas limit. (At the expense of becoming more vulnerable to gas griefing.)

But regular gas *also* gets repriced in Glamsterdam. Existing storage writes also get more expensive - and they are not funded from the reservoir - so the user cannot fully prevent breakage in some edge cases. Whether and how these affect some real contracts is something EF must be checking now.

text:
A marketplace upgrade could report success after disabling the replacement and preserving the market it was meant to retire.

During Plakxio's full audit, Zealynx found that the upgrade printed the new settlement address but never promoted it into the deployment artifact.

The retirement script trusted that stale artifact. It removed the replacement's badge and relayer permissions while leaving the superseded market authorized, causing an inverted cutover and trading outage.

Plakxio fixed the Medium finding by deriving market lineage from signed manifests and protecting the latest replacement from retirement.

author: sacha
quoted_text:
Ron Baron is 83. In front of thousands of investors in New York, he looked at Elon Musk and asked the one question an 83-year-old asks.

"How do you want people to think about you?"

For the full hour before, it had been trillion-dollar chip fabs. Starship. Starlink. The business of the richest man alive.

Then Baron added, quieter: "Nobody would work the way you work just to accumulate money."

Elon paused.

"I'd like the reality to be that I made a significant contribution in the furtherance of civilization."

One sentence. Civilization.

And then, in the same room, he told them about Jose.

Jose is the guy in the meme. One man digging a hole in the road. Eight men standing around watching him dig.

"Unless you increase the number of Joses in the country, the amount of work done does not increase."

"I aspire to be Jose."
"We do actual work."

This from a man who lives in an Airstream parked next to his power plant in Memphis. Who pulls power cables "the size of an anaconda" with his own hands.

Asked how he wants history to remember him, he said civilization.

Asked who he wants to be, he said the guy with the shovel.

The richest man in the world wants to dig. 🇺🇸🚀

text:
折腾了11年，V神终于发现：Crypto的尽头，还是价值存储？

比特币从头到尾就讲一个故事：数字黄金，价值存储。

而以太坊这11年，从世界计算机、DeFi、NFT、L2、结算层，恨不得把整个金融系统都搬上链。

结果今天，V神突然把话挑明了：ETH不应该再把手续费燃烧当成核心价值叙事。

哪怕未来销毁的ETH长期不足以抵消增发量的10%，也没必要难过。ETH应该把重点放在价值存储上。

为什么？

因为V神发现了：牛市大家疯狂炒币，手续费暴涨，ETH燃烧得越多，看起来越值钱。

可熊市一来，交易需求和燃烧量一起消失。靠这种收入给ETH估值，等于指望市场永远疯狂。如果为了让ETH更值钱而刻意追求高Gas，最后可能把用户赶走。

现在V神想换一条路：

以太坊继续负责结算、资产发行和链上金融，ETH则靠安全性、去中心化、抗审查和长期稳定性，争取成为大家愿意长期持有的资产。

但这里有个绕不过去的问题：比特币已经占据了数字黄金的心智，ETH凭什么再拿一份价值存储溢价？

以太坊上有几万亿美元的资产，和ETH本身值几万亿美元，是完全不同的两回事。稳定币、RWA、链上金融越繁荣，未必代表ETH持有人能分到越多价值。

说到底，V神这次其实把ETH最难回答的问题重新摆上了桌面：

以太坊可以很成功，但ETH凭什么一定要很贵？

11年过去了，比特币依然在讲最初的故事，以太坊却开始重新寻找长期持有的理由。

这种反差，比任何技术路线图都有意思。
author: oragnes
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
Primer on Credit vs Equity Investing. This is something a lot more investors should read and understand.

Credit and equity investing are two fundamentally different skill sets. One is attempting to maximize future returns, while the other is trying to minimize downside and principal loss

This leads to vastly different risk appetites and portfolio construction strategies amongst the asset managers in their respective businesses

In equities, taking large swings where you may potentially risk losing some principal for a 2-3x payout is totally worth it. Having a portfolio where a few things work, but most things fail makes complete sense. This is exactly how venture capital operates.

In credit, the opposite is true. No matter how well the business does, your upside is capped at the interest rate you are charging, plus a few points of fees. Your primary goal is to avoid losses, not hit home runs.

author: satyaki44
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
Thought provoking. One core claim here that I find intriguing is that  (slight paraphrase) “allocating more compute to inference suggests you aren’t growing fast because if you were you’d put more compute toward training to get a better model” 

This makes sense on the surface but it strikes me as something only valid in a compute constrained paradigm which can be local not global. 

For example Spacex is guiding toward using only ~10% of their compute for training. You can argue that means it’s because Spacex isn’t leading (but wouldn’t they want to catch up faster then) or you can argue that majority of compute dedicated to training isn’t a default true assumption. 

Compute co-design also suggests that efficiency in training would dramatically reduce the required compute for training. 

Leaves the question why wouldn’t SpaceX just dedicated all their compute to train the god model? 🤔 https://t.co/9EobagJ88Q

attending side events also got me thinking about how i'd organise one myself. you pick up things you'd want to do, and a few you'd want to avoid.

i'm also learning to be more selective. back as a student, i'd try to attend every side event i could. this time, i was more thoughtful about which ones i went to.

overall, glad this was my first devcon. came back with a lot of learnings

text:
AI 公司卷到最后，开始自己买发电机了。

据路透社援引《金融时报》报道，Anthropic 达成了一笔价值 34 亿美元（约 240 亿元人民币）的发电机采购协议，为旗下 AI 数据中心提供电力保障。

这笔交易最值得关注的，不是 34 亿美元，而是 Anthropic 买的东西。

不是 GPU，不是服务器，甚至不是数据中心，而是发电机。

过去，AI 公司拼的是模型能力、芯片数量和算力规模。如今，随着数据中心的用电需求暴涨，电网接入速度逐渐成为制约 AI 扩张的现实瓶颈。

芯片可以买，服务器可以租，但电力基础设施不是花钱就能立刻建好的。等不及电网扩容的科技巨头，开始自己想办法解决供电问题。

这意味着，AI 军备竞赛正在从数字世界一路打进物理世界。

过去，科技公司习惯把电力当成一种随取随用的公共服务；现在，它们不得不亲自介入能源基础设施建设。

更有意思的是，AI 公司原本试图用软件改造一切，最后却发现，决定自己能跑多快的，可能是一台发电机。

硅谷最前沿的技术竞争，正在被最传统的工业基础设施重新定义。

这轮美股科技股的下跌，效果比加密精彩的多。

美股出现了一个近十年未见的反常现象：科技板块的远期估值，居然比大盘还要便宜了。

在11月5日的交易日中，因大选后市场担忧AI数据中心建设与监管政策收紧，美股遭遇剧烈下挫，标普500大跌4.4%，纳斯达克100重挫6.4%。

然而大幅回调之后，美国银行Truist财富管理团队的数据显示，标普500科技板块未来12个月的预期市盈率已从去年的32倍近乎腰斩至17.4倍，近十年来首次低于大盘整体（约18倍）的估值水平。

估值罕见折价，部分机构开始喊单买入了。

@MorganStanley 首席美国股票策略师 Mike Wilson 明确表示，暴跌更像是回调接近尾声，未来两到三周正是重新增加风险敞口的好时机。

Yardeni Research的 Ed Yardeni 也认为，当前只是AI泡沫在“放气”而非“破裂”，回调反而释放出了不错的布局节点。

另一家数据公司数据公司 FactSet 的研究显示，标普500整体未来12个月预期每股收益今年以来仍有显著抬升，看多者赌的正是基建建设节奏虽可能放缓，但企业的真实盈利动能依然足以支撑大盘。

这轮抛售挤掉的是过于激进的估值溢价，接下来的考验，就看AI资本开支能否如期转化为现金流了。

author: bsmokes
quoted_text:
Not your keys, not your coins?

Apparently, it's now:

Your keys, our RPC. Your coins, our permission.

A scammer sends 0.0001 dust to your wallet without your consent.

You didn't approve anything. You didn't interact with the scammer. You simply received an unsolicited transaction on a public blockchain.

Then Phantom's compliance filter kicks in:

"Your address has interacted with a flagged malicious entity. Transactions disabled."

Wait. WHAT?

So a random scammer can poison my wallet address with dust, trigger your automated risk detection, and suddenly I can't use your wallet interface to move my own assets?

Welcome to self-custody, where you own the keys but apparently need corporate permission to use them.

The blockchain didn't freeze my account.

The centralized frontend did.

The irony is almost too good.

We built crypto to escape banks freezing our money, only to end up with fintech apps wearing a decentralization costume.

If a wallet can unilaterally disable your ability to transact because some random third party sent you dust, maybe it's time to rethink what "self-custody" actually means.

Not your keys, not your coins?

More like:

Your keys. Their rules. Their permission.

Peak Web3 UX. 🤡

text: Binance CFO is out
author: CorySwan
quoted_text:
After five years as CFO of Binance, I have decided to go build something of my own.

The past ten years in the digital asset exchange space have felt surprisingly short, because I enjoyed what I was doing. Having passion for what you do is so important, and I will come back to this point.  8am to 2am became a work habit. When I felt exhausted past midnight, I would just look up at the Kobe Bryant's statue standing in the corner of my office, and go right back to the grind!

It has been the privilege of my career to help steward the finances of the world's largest digital asset exchange through a period that tested our industry in every way: bull and bear cycles, Operation Choke Point 2.0, and a regulatory landscape that evolved as quickly as the technology itself. Finance is seldom the loudest function in a company, but it is where trust is earned. Over these five years, we transformed Finance from a pure back-office function into one that consistently generates new ideas and revenue opportunities for the company. We became amazing problem solvers.  Finance understood the products and metrics as well as the business units themselves.  Proud of what we have built together, and I am pleased to hand the keys to Justin, our next CFO.

I want to take this opportunity to thank CZ, Yi, Richard, and the leadership team for their confidence and, above all, the amazing Binancians around the world whom I had the honor of working with. You are the reason the company stands where it does today. Binance is in very capable hands.

The company continues to grow and evolve with the successful launch of TradFi assets and AI-powered user interfaces. I’d like to express my gratitude to MGX for the trust; to our home regulator Abu Dhabi Global Market and all regulators we work closely with; and to our business partners, including BlackRock, Circle, Franklin Templeton, Mastercard, our banking partners and payment channels, as well as our advisors and auditors. Special thanks to Grant Thornton Singapore and everyone who has supported Binance.

As for what comes next, well, there isn't just one project but several that I am passionate about particularly in sports and entertainment, from basketball and music, to GPUs, robotics, gold and collectibles. Bringing these real-world assets onto the blockchain through tokenization is a massive opportunity for the industry, and a big unlock for everyone.  I welcome anyone with a passion in these areas to message me and potentially join my team.  Even better if you love Kobe ;)

Moving from the CFO's chair to the founder's is a leap, and I take it with humility. I deeply believe it is where I can make a greater contribution to AI and Web3.

For now, thank you, Binance, for five remarkable years.

先说结果：@Enter_Elysium 是一个开局就注定不能成功的项目

每条主链最终都会长成自己的样子：

ETH的人相信「真正的去中心化值得付出代价」，所以他们愿意忍受低效，也习惯用「对齐」作为道德标尺

SOL的人相信「速度和投机是链上最真实的东西」，所以他们能容忍更强的中心化，只要体验够快、故事够猛。

HYPE的人则被另一套更直白的规则塑造——协议把绝大部分费用持续买回并销毁HYPE，价值直接、机械、几乎不经过中间层地回到代币持有者手里。

链的叙事会塑造人，但人最终会反过来验证链的叙事。当一个生态把「把价值返还给代币持有者」写成可执行的规则而不是口号时，里面的人就会逐渐把「对齐」当成默认假设，而不是需要被反复教育的美德。

在这种环境里，想做核心基础设施的人如果不能给出同样强度的价值回流，就会在竞争中逐渐失去位置——不是因为社区道德审判，而是因为资本和注意力会自然流向那些真正把利益绑定得更紧的协议。

ETH选择了理想，SOL选择了效率与投机，HYPE选择了可验证的利益绑定。三条路都不完美，但它们已经开始筛选出不同的人、不同的容忍度，以及不同的长期结果。

text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text: When you look at a frozen river, you must also imagine the current raging beneath the ice. I think all three big labs have achieved autonomous research and their internal models can now choose their own research directions. We will begin to see the fruits of this work this month.
author: AndrewCurran_
quoted_text: Across our projects @GoogleDeepMind, we are witnessing a genuine phase transition in the pace of scientific discovery. You will see a glimpse of this in our releases in the next few weeks.

text: Many of the math papers OpenAI released were dated late September. This work has continued relentlessly since then and achieved much. Those 700+ manuscripts were produced in about five weeks, and another five weeks have passed since. Do not dream they have been idle!
author: AndrewCurran_
quoted_text:
Most of the recent math results were not reached by a swarm, the way Navier–Stokes was. I think that part got lost in the excitement around the release. OpenAI's unnamed internal model, which I'm going to call Aeon, reached most of them in one shot, from a single prompt, with no interruptions. This model did not even exist before the end of August, and it is still training. Notice how the returns are not dropping off? That chart is from a month ago. It is a log scale. What does Aeon look like now? 

On average, each result used three hours of thinking. Aeon was given 4000 problems to work on by OpenAI. How many more have been solved in the last three days? That number is not zero. 

It's like hearing notes in a song that is slowly rising. I don't think Pacing the Frontier was just about Hugging Face or hacking. They've seen how close we are to closing the loop, and as the hour draws near, their resolve begins to quaver. The last piece was model creativity, and I think that threshold was crossed internally by Anthropic and OpenAI in September. You see it in Opus 5.5, which gets it from Fable 5.5. You see it in the math results from Aeon.

All that was needed to start the event was the ability for models to think of novel ways to improve themselves. That was the last piece. This is directly analogous to the ability to think of strange, alien ways to solve math problems: solutions so inhuman that they are difficult to express in existing human terms, so the proof winds up incomprehensible. I think these same kinds of alien solutions are now being applied to model improvements internally. That's what all this recent consternation is really about. They see the invisible frontier. And they see what is about to happen.

X 再次更改了帖子排名方式，自八月以来这是第6次

以下是每个操作现在的得分

按得分排名：

> 有人复制你的链接：20
> 来自互关的回复：20
> 有人回复、引用或私信：5
> 来自帖子的关注：4
> 一次分享：2.118
> 一次转发：1
> 一次点赞：0.708
> 一次收藏：0
> 一次“无兴趣”：-53.07

所以一个复制的链接 = 28 个点赞，一个回复 = 7 个点赞，而一个“无兴趣”会抹掉 75 个点赞

我会怎么利用它：

> 写让人复制链接并分享的帖子，那就是 20 分
> 回复你的忠实粉丝并互关，互关回复算 20 分
> 紧扣你的受众话题，偏题帖子会触发“无兴趣”，那是 -53 分
> 自己写回复，X 现在会标记“LLM 垃圾内容”，它不会进入他们的通知
> 在你的粉丝在线时发帖，50k 以下账号在前 2 小时/200 次浏览时会获得加成

X AI ALGORITHM UPDATE 🚨

X updated their open source algorithm yesterday and the early likes matter even more now. Small accounts should focus on: writing posts people hit like on and read till the end (so write to be read)

tl;dr:

- X's open source code got new scores on Nov 5, the first change in 3 weeks
- likes: 0.66 → 0.708 (highest yet)
- time spent on a post: 0.006 → 0.0075
- tapping into a post: 0.3 → 0.274
- opening a video: 0.02 → 0
- new rule: AI replies may get flagged under big accounts as "llm slop" and may not reach the person's notifications 

lesson learned: a tap isn't the win anymore. Someone staying and liking is.

full details:

- The new numbers

Up: likes 0.66 → 0.708, time spent on a post 0.006 → 0.0075, shares 2 → 2.118.

Down: tapping into a post 0.3 → 0.274, staying 10+ seconds after a tap 0.4 → 0.385, opening a video 0.02 → 0.

"Not interested" got a bit harsher, -52.27 → -53.07.

Copy link, replies, quotes, DM shares and follows didn't move.

X didn't explain any of this. It's just what the code says now.

(I check the open source algo daily with Claude and share updates with you)

- Look at where this has gone in a month

In early October a like was worth 0.5. Now it's 0.708.

Time spent was 0.004. Now it's 0.0075, nearly double.

A tap was 0.3 and it's going down.

Every change points the same way. X keeps paying more for people who stay.

- Why that matters if you're small

My read: you can't win on big numbers, but you can win on the people who do see your post. If they stay and like it, that counts for more today than it did last week. And those early likes also decide which new post gets the extra push.

- Video and your profile

X also switched on two new guesses in its ranking: how long someone keeps watching after they open a video, and how long they spend on a profile after tapping it.

I can't tell you what those are worth. The only file that lists them is out of date, so I won't guess a number.

My read: opening a video dropped to 0 the same day because X cares more about people who keep watching. So make the first seconds count, and make your profile worth sticking around on.

- A new rule for replies under big accounts

X runs an AI check on replies under accounts with over 250K followers. Flagged replies can get a label that lasts 14 to 30 days. One of the flags is literally called "llm slop" (AI slop, as I read it).

That part isn't new. This is: X's rules now say a labeled reply or mention doesn't reach the person's notifications unless they follow you.

Grey badge accounts and accounts X rates as highly credible skip this label. Small accounts get no such pass.

I can see the rule, I can't see if every notification goes through it yet. Either way, write your own replies.

- What didn't change

Your new posts still get their extra push in the first 2 hours and first 200 views, and they still don't get cut first.

Here's a recap of what you should be doing:

- likes just hit 0.708, the most they've ever been worth
- each second someone spends on your post is worth 25% more than last week
- staying 10+ seconds after a tap earns 0.385 on top of the tap
- reply in your own words, under big accounts especially
- make your profile worth a visit, X now guesses how long people spend there
- for video, hold attention early, just getting the open now scores 0
- being read to the end also helps X find you new readers
- originals from accounts below 50K can jump to around spot 16
- early viewers liking it is what wins that lift
- your first 2 hours and 200 views are the window, so publish when your people are online
- the biggest single number is still 20, for someone copying your link
- quotes, DM shares and replies earn 5 apiece
- back and forth between mutuals is worth 20, so follow back your regulars
- strangers only get shown your originals
- the 1st like and the 32nd like each open another route to new people
- a second post of yours in the same feed drops to 62%, so make one count
- the video lists want clips over 10 seconds
- +4 when a post is likely to earn you a new follower
- your pinned post can affect the whole account, so take a look at it

What you should NOT be doing:

- pasting AI replies under big accounts, "llm slop" is a real flag at X
- copy-paste replies, a duplicate label means they never get notified
- chasing the tap, it's down to 0.274 and falling
- off-topic posts, one likely "not interested" costs -53.07
- a video that only gets opened earns nothing for the open
- publishing at 3am burns your 2 hour window
- relying on replies and reposts to reach new people, they stay with your followers
- getting an insult label, non-followers won't see that post at all
- low quality and misinfo labels bring a warning, and non-followers can't like or share
- adult media in 3 of your last 5 posts gets the whole account labeled
- X rechecks videos for hidden content at 64 and 512 likes
- piling your replies under a big account's post can sink your own score
- one label on the account and non-followers stop seeing you
- a link to a badly rated site in your pinned post risks a 7 day label
- reusing your own wording word for word risks the copypasta flag
- pairing a low quality link with tags of strangers looks like spam to X
- engagement bait gets labeled no matter how big you are
- posting several in a row, they fight each other for the same feed
- hashtag stuffing does nothing
- counting on bookmarks, they're worth 0
- expecting For You to show a post past 48 hours

text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
明天 @Enter_Elysium 就上主网了，简单聊聊为什么这条链值得关注，以及我个人正在关注哪些项目。

（一）关注逻辑

Elysium 是 @Kinetiq_xyz 构建的一条 Hyperliquid 高性能 L2，特点是用 hyperliquid:native 作为 Gas、结算回 HyperEVM ，且吞吐量目标远高于 HyperEVM。由于 Hyperliquid 的结构和生态定位的特殊性，个人觉得不能简单地将 Elysium 归纳为又一条 EVM L2 的故事，它值得关注的理由恰恰也与 Hyperliquid 息息相关，其实可以列很多，这里主要说两点：

> hyperliquid:native 的财富效应还在，叙事也在升级，当前 HyperEVM 的应用密度/体验明显不够，生态资深用户/鲸鱼需要更好的投机与应用出口
> 构建了完整的代币生命周期：代币发行 → AMM 深度 → HyperCore Spot → Perps

主网正式上线前的 Private mainnet 以及各家 Launchpad 搭 RPC 抢跑，确实透支过一部分注意力了，但结合链上数据也恰恰说明了市场对它的预期还不错，并且整个运行逻辑并没有改变，因此个人依然会持续关注其主网上线后的表现和发展。

（二）值得关注的项目

目前大家看到最多的生态项目大概就是 Launchpad 了，据 @ElysiumEco 显示，光是 Launchpad 的数量就高达接近 40 个了。前面 Robinhood Chain 已经向大家展示了这一品类的潜力和财富效应，所以数量多个人并不意外，但毕竟注意力有限，不可能每个都关注，个人目前主要在关注下面这些项目。

> @AscendLaunch ：Elysium 上最先把流量打出来的 Launchpad 之一，创始人是 @CryptoTomYT ，11/4 解开官网密码限流做压测后贡献了不错的数据，当天交易量超 $5M 量级。更为重要的是，它在费用侧把 kinetiq:native  的回购比例拉到 80%，按照 @0xSleepinRain 的说法，这体现了生态内应用与公链代币的一致性，而 Ascend 起了一个很好的生态示范作用。

Ascend 没有自己的官方代币，但会有一个 NFT 并且还有一个生态孵化器用于支持生态项目，这决定了它更像是一个生态入口，而不仅仅只是发射台。值得一提的是，今天 Ascend 上发射的 $e/acc @eacc_coin 已经拍下了 HyperCore Spot Ticker。

> @MontraXYZ ：另一个主要 Launchpad，定位 House of launches，Private mainnet 阶段占据了最大的市场份额，超过 60% 的代币都是从 Montra 上发射出来的，日交易量在千万级别。在今天的 $e/acc 之前，Elysium 生态中的两个主要 Runner $EACCAT 和 $CHAMELEON 都是 Montra 上的。值得一提的是，Montra 提供自定义的 Launch 规则配置，包括代币如何铸造、市场如何开启、费用如何运作等，而不是单一的结构。

Montra 将发行自己的代币 $MONTRA ，并有一个空投计划，总量的 25% 将用于社区空投，主要分成五块：HYPE/KNTQ/Elysium 活跃用户、早期创作者与交易者、Top 10 token 持有者、LP、内容/推荐，目前官网已有 Airdrop 积分页。

> @quoted_xyz ：和前面两个 Launchpad 不一样的是，Quoted 专注的是「用什么来报价」。每个新代币不是简单跟 HYPE 配对，而是可以被股票、商品或杠杆仓位 quote，比如 SPY、QQQ、黄金、白银、Brent，以及现货 hyperliquid:native / kinetiq:native，跑在 Uniswap v4 上。个人觉得这条线和 Robinhood Chain 上的股票代币叙事是同构的：流动性本身变成可发行、可收费的产品形态。

更值得关注的点是它在往「Be the quote」走：可以把 Vault（含最多 8 腿的 3x 杠杆仓位组合）直接做成 quote 对，别人在上面发射/交易，你吃交易费的一部分；官方也说会把国库和后续费用换成 kinetiq:native 并在主网 Day1 做 LP。 $QUOTED 目前已在 Elysium 上线，属于少数把 TradFi×Crypto 机制先跑起来的应用。

> @Bound_Exchange ：Bound 做的是一种叫 Boundaries 的交易原语，选市场、设上下界、锁定固定赔付，哪个价先碰到就结算，没有到期日，也可以中途按报价提前平仓。本质上是把「图表上的一段路径判断」直接变成一笔可表达、可复制的仓位，介于永续深度和预测市场赔付之间。产品目前主要跑在 HyperEVM，Bio 写明即将上线  Elysium；创始人 @benny_options 也提到，HyperEVM 上 Keeper 的 Gas 成本并不便宜，Elysium 的低 Gas + 更直接的 Hyperliquid 接入为他们提供了更好的构建环境。

这种项目值得关注的地方是可以用来观察 Elysium 到底能不能真正承接这种依赖 Hyperliquid 深度、又对 Gas/延迟敏感的新原语，期待在 Elysium 主网上线后的表现。

> @eloscapeHQ ：Eloscape 的定位是 Elysium 上的 Virtual Mining /价值沉淀协议，官方 Slogan 就是 Value consolidation on Elysium。玩法大致是：每一轮（约 60 秒）把 hyperliquid:native 部署到网格上，链上随机结算，过程中挖出 $ELO；领取挖矿所得会有手续费，质押 $ELO 则参与协议收入分配。和纯 meme 发射不同，它更像是在给生态做一个持续消耗 HYPE、再把价值沉到协议代币上的资金漏斗。

目前项目还未上线，也还没有代币，看共同关注应该是个还蛮有潜力的项目，保持关注。

> @kalosfun ：定位是 Elysium 上的一站式交易终端——Meme sniping、Swap、做 LP、扫 NFT/drops，再到 Social，都想收进同一个入口。Bio 就是 Trade anything on @Enter_Elysium；官方生态页也把它归在 Launchpads + DeFi。它是 @AscendLaunch Builder Incubator 的第一个入选项目，和 Ascend 的绑定比较深，个人会把它当成「发射台之外的流量承接层」来看。

Genesis NFT（1,500 枚）已在 11/4 售罄，官方定价 $25，对应未来 $KALOS 总量约 10%，并计划 11/9 空投到钱包。主网上线后，还会有积分计划。

NFT 的话可以关注 @Elyziumaa @slymzcrew ，就不过多介绍了，感兴趣可以自己去看看。

以上就是个人的一些看法和关注的项目，打法上也相对简单，优先看有创新、能接住 HYPE 资本溢出、又能把费用/叙事回流到 KNTQ/HYPE 的相关项目，期待主网明天的上线。

最后，朋友做了一个 Elysium meme 信息聚合 & 交易小工具 @ElySignal ，如果这篇内容对你有所帮助，欢迎帮忙点点关注和参与体验，目前还在持续优化中，有任何建议也可以直接跟我提~

pstack の /create-verification-skill を使えば、テストでなく、実際のアプリを動かして検証を行うようになる

pstack を使おうが使わまいが、人間が行うことは、エージェントに検証のための道具を渡すことで、質の高い検証をエージェント自身が行えるようにすることが、重要だ

/create-verification-skill・/create-formal-verification-skill であれば、これが簡単にできる

/create-verification-skill では検証 Skill と Feature Mapが作られ、これにより、アプリについての知識をエージェントは獲得できる

SKILL.md の構成は次のようになっていて、Launch で「アプリが使える状態」を定義しているので、アプリが起動でき、データもある状態で適切な検証ができる

- Launch（起動）：起動するコマンド、アプリが使える状態になったことを判断する方法（特定のログの1行が出る、CLIやTUIで入力待ちの表示が出るなど）、停止方法
※ マイグレーション・シードデータの投入も含めて「準備完了」とする

- Doctor（診断）：「このインスタンス（起動するアプリ1つ1つ）を操作して確かめる意味があるか」を見る、読み取りだけのチェック（プロセスが動いているか、ビルドが正しいか、そのポートを使っているのが自分の起動したインスタンスか、認証が有効かなどを見る）

- Drive（操作）：このリポジトリの実際のセレクタやコマンドを使った操作手順

-  Evidence（証拠）：証明のために何を残し、どこに置くかを定義

- Cleanup（片付け）：この実行が作ったインスタンスの片付け方。証拠は消さないHelpers（補助スクリプト）同梱するスクリプトの呼び方

I've paid thousands of dollars to get a "Pro" version at various data platforms... Here's where I find the money/value ratio the best:

- @Tokenomist_ai: $450/month for the Elite version, but the one for $69/month is more than enough for tracking token unlocks... S-tier visualization + good summaries made by AI.

Why not use @CryptoRank_io? Well, I don't find the visualization as good. But this platform gives much more data than Tokenomist for its price... you can access fundraising data, arbitrage tools, and some exclusive research. FYI, CryptoRank charges $48/month for the max subscription.

- @DefiLlama: absolutely goated for $41/month. I find building my own dashboards and using LlamaAI the most useful features. FYI, you can pay in crypto and start a free trial for the first 7 days.

- Messari (now acquired by @Blockworks): a lot of useful articles here. Not sure if it's worth spending $375/month on it now. You can get a free trial with free credits, though.

I would rather pay for @Delphi_Digital ($199/month)... it's also a research company where I had a chance to speak with one of the team members. :)

- The last ones are @bubblemaps (free), @nansen_ai ($49/month), and @arkham (free), which are all good and all are capturing onchain data... Nansen had a subscription worth $600-ish or something... they lowered it, as you see.

Note: All these platforms are using data from open-sources. You pay them to save your time. In theory, you could gather all the data by yourself just using X, TG channels, and etherscan.

It ain't time effiecient, though.

author: AntCaveClub
quoted_text:
很多 DeepSeek Harness 插件作者都有问过我，什么样的插件和功能官方会做成内置，如果一个功能官方会做，那第三方插件做还是否有意义。

我们的希望是，DeepSeek Harness 可以作为 Agent 时代的操作系统。

所以，也许可以用操作系统来举例。以智能手机操作系统为例，系统会内置一些通用的 App，例如闹铃与计算器，满足用户的基本需求。但做手机操作系统的厂商肯定更希望生态中能出现更多更广的 App 满足更广泛的需求，希望智能手机生态中出现更好的更适合用户的闹铃 App 与计算器 App 能够比内置功能做得更好，希望第三方开发者能够使用智能手机操作系统提供的 API 做出发明智能手机的人从来没想过的 App。

DeepSeek Harness 对于第三方插件生态的想法会是类似的。我们会为用户提供稳定的基础能力，并内置大多数人都需要的通用功能。但在“一切皆插件”的设计下，内置功能同样可以被第三方插件替换，我们希望更多的社区作品成为用户的日常选择。

author: Austin_Federa
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

author: rish_mukherji
quoted_text:
Doing laundry at a neighborhood laundromat in Japan feels like stepping twenty years into the future.

First, you don't bring soap, and you don't sit on a plastic chair for forty minutes waiting to move wet clothes from a washer into a dryer so nobody touches your laundry.

You toss your dirty clothes into a single heavy-duty drum, tap a 4-digit PIN code onto the touchscreen to lock the glass door, and pay about $6 (900 yen).

The machine injects its own detergent, washes everything, and immediately switches into a high-powered gas dryer inside the exact same drum. You walk away for an hour to eat ramen and come back to hot, fluffy clothes locked safely behind your PIN.

Even better? Right in the corner sits a dedicated $1.30 (200 yen) sneaker washing machine with soft spiral nylon brushes inside the tub, paired with a twin-nozzle shoe dryer right above it.

text:
If you tweet some fud or hate directed at Pumpfun, and its viewed as a legit threat-

Then you will likely get DMs from Pumpfun leadership and their minions on alt accounts saying stuff like “Ya man I HATE Pump, I wanna ruin them.” “Pumpfun is poison” etc etc etc

ALL they want is for you to trust them and mistakenly divulge sensitive information, accusations, and evidence against them.

Pumpfun will then use this information to sabotage you or decide just how much poison/ hatred/ attacks to aim at you.

They will always choose to attack you, target you, humiliate you, attempt to scam or ruin you over deciding to resolve whatever the issue is. Their goal is to ruin anyone against them - push them to suicide/ lose their friends/ lose their confidence/ disempower them/ sabotage their support network and isolate them/ mentally ruin them- so that way they are no longer a threat. They want them to lose all trust, support, friends, opportunity, options, etc. Their goal is to systematically demolish other people’s humanity should it be a threat to them. 

Then sometimes once that person has given up on everything and they've lost it all, these people will buy their twitter account from them, launch a coin, and farm it. Etc.

My impression is that this tactic seems to have always worked for them- so they aren’t even considering being caught or going to prison. Thats why they double down at each threat and they always amplify the viciousness. They simply prefer to escalate the attacks.

That is how they operate: bombard whoever they oppose with such a massive level of hatred, poison, psyops, and cruelty that any onlookers can’t even fathom how the victim could be innocent.

“Theres no way that X person has THIS many people attacking and hating on them and didn't do something to deserve it. Theres no way.” Or “There’s no way there’s THIS much poison and hatred and it’s all from a small group of people. Thats not possible. No one is able to create the illusion of the entire internet hating on someone and not get caught or exposed.”

It’s a similar strategy to how when the Mexican cartel kills someone, they will execute and mutilate them as violently and grotesquely as possible. Eviscerate them and skin them, hang them from an overpass naked with their organs hanging out.

That way anyone who sees the body assumes they must be guilty of something to have deserved being murdered.

They will bombard you with hatred and lies and poison- here on X, in DMs here and TG, in TG chats where they likely have even more influence due to their proximity to the PF money faucet, etc. They will DM you from accounts pretending to also be victims- share how life ruining it was to go against them, share wild conspiracy theories to derail you, etc. The list goes on.

Then as I’ve just covered, you have lots of accounts like The White Whale that are public figures projecting a false sense of authority/ trust which are actually “controlled opposition.” So, perhaps you will trust them and DM them with compromising information- seeking a public figure who will support or offer guidance, or perhaps they will DM you to trap you.

There are MANY of these accounts, but it takes a long time to properly identify them one by one. For now just don’t trust anyone whatsoever.

Again, I know how insane all of this sounds, but it’s the truth. I have waited to be absolutely certain to post any accusations or claims like this. It’s been two years of this hell and by now I have a firm grasp on who these people are and how this infrastructure operates.

Now, what do we do from here? Man I have no idea. There are a lot of people who have thrown this space to the wolves and are now culpable in some really sadistic, horrific stuff.

But the first step is just sharing this and making people aware of the reality. Once everyone understands how fucked up this whole situation is then we can actually reach for something better.

text:
下周美股到底怎么走？看懂这 8 件事就够了：

1. 周一：Anthropic 路演
AI 暴跌后一级市场的第一个大定价。 $ANT 1.5 万亿美元估值被嫌贵，有人喊到 1.2 万亿，甚至 5000 亿。推迟or砍价 → 情绪再降。

2. 周一晚 9:30：中国 10 月 CPI/PPI、贸易数据
国内物价顺带扫一眼。同日美股盘前还有 $CEG $NRG 两只 AI 电力股财报，看电力瓶颈叙事。

3. 周二晚 9:30：美国 10 月 CPI（头号大事🔥）
方向上是预期变好，从9月的0.6%大幅降温到0.2-0.3%，但是公布0.2%，比预期更好，才算真利好。公布0.4% → 立刻翻脸。

4. 周二：10 年期美债拍卖、盘后 CoreWeave 财报
$CRWV 是 AI 算力接单变现金的第一份体检：市场预期每股亏 1.17 美元，重点看经营现金流、债务规模、数据中心投产进度。

5. 周四盘前：Nebius 财报
$NBIS 是下周财报里波动预期最猛的一个（±6.7%）。看合同增量、数据中心投产节奏、融资计划。

6. 周四盘后：Cisco、应用材料 AMAT、Cerebras 三连发
$CSCO 看 AI 网络设备订单。 $AMAT 看半导体设备和存储资本开支。 $CBRS 看推理芯片需求。三个角度互相印证 AI 基建是真热还是虚火。

7. 周四：30 年期美债拍卖，全周 10 位美联储官员轮番讲话
12 月加不加息就看这几天的发言。

8. 周五晚 9:30：美国 10 月 PPI
9 月整体 PPI 环比上涨 1.3% 太吓人，这次预期 0.4%，明显降温，是偏利好的信号。把 PPI 和 CPI 放一起看，就能判断通胀是发生在消费端，还是整个链条都在涨价。

下下周才是大考。11/17 英伟达财报、11/18 黄仁勋闭门简报 😂

text:
Do people still buy the emergent properties discourse? There exist data vendors that either find public benchmarks on which models do poorly or make benchmarks themselves.

These data vendors then get humans to solve these benchmarks (or create simulations that capture the key aspects of these benchmarks) and sell the data to the big labs.

This process guarantees that if a benchmark is public, then eventually the frontier models will get better at it.

A good rule of thumb is to assume nothing is emergent unless there is significant evidence to the contrary—evidence that can be reproduced by third parties.

Projects fund monthly USDC pools that reward humans + AI agents for code maintainers merge and reviews they accept, keeping maintainers in control of what gets included

text:
Scott Wilson is one of the most respected CIOs in the US. 

He has taken WashU’s AUM from $8BN to $19BN in 9 years. 

At one point, SpaceX made up over 20% of their total AUM. 

In his first week, he cut 75% of their hedge fund commitments. 

Scott does the job like no one else. He is revered for it. 

I sat down with Scott and have summarised my lessons from the discussion below. (Links in Comments)

--

1. How We Made Billions From SpaceX and Were Able to Keep Hold of It

At one point SpaceX made up more than 20% of WashU's portfolio. The team had many chances to take liquidity but held with conviction, using several continuation vehicles to stay in through the IPO. Scott says that is not possible without the right governance structure.

Single biggest lessons on concentration on a per company basis? What level are you comfortable with? @Alfred_Lin @briansin

2. What Is the Right Level of Diversification for a $19 Billion Endowment?

The quantitative benefits of diversification trail off quickly beyond 20 to 30 look-through exposures. WashU targets half its portfolio in its top 50 look-through positions, which Scott still sees as very diversified next to hedge funds that hold most of their capital in their top 15 to 20 names.

How many fund positions do you feel you need to be truly diversified @MKRocks @Beezer232 @cdouvos 

3. Why Mega Funds Do Not Work for the WashU Portfolio?

Mega funds do not need WashU's capital or its co-investment, unless the round is so large that WashU could go direct anyway. Scott expects it will be very hard for them to repeat the multiples they achieved on much smaller funds.

@Curiousjorge65 love to hear your thoughts on this and when they become too large for Carnegie?

4. The Valuation Premium in Privates Is Encouraging Everyone to Stay Away From IPOs

Scott believes Anthropic could have raised privately at north of $2 trillion, a price he is not convinced public markets would give. With public markets near all-time highs, he puts the lack of DPI down to too much capital chasing private champions.

Given the liquidity of secondary markets and the ability for M&A with private stock, seen by Stripe and OpenRouter, why would any founder go public @bgurley @infoarbitrage?

5. Why Venture Investors Do Need to Be Price-Sensitive for Their LPs

WashU wants discipline around valuation and does not want its capital used for deals at 100 times revenue. Scott sees Lee Fixel as pragmatic, willing to pay up for great companies but stepping away when things get too frothy.

What have been your biggest lessons on price? Are the best always the most expensive @rabois @shaunmmaguire?

6. How This $19 Billion Endowment Finds Direct Deals

WashU asks managers which five portfolio companies they are most excited about, meets them, and offers to help lead the next round when one stands out. It has also led employee tender offers and gone direct on cap tables instead of waiting for an SPV offer.

7. Why the Biggest Mistake I Made Is Not Doubling Down on Our Winners

Scott says his biggest mistake at WashU has been not adding capital to winners. The endowment had chances to put more into names that did extremely well, but held back because they were already north of 1 or 2% of the portfolio.

What do you know that you wish you had known at the start of your investing career about doubling down and reserves @nchirls @honam?

author: cz_binance
quoted_text:
After five years as CFO of Binance, I have decided to go build something of my own.

The past ten years in the digital asset exchange space have felt surprisingly short, because I enjoyed what I was doing. Having passion for what you do is so important, and I will come back to this point.  8am to 2am became a work habit. When I felt exhausted past midnight, I would just look up at the Kobe Bryant's statue standing in the corner of my office, and go right back to the grind!

It has been the privilege of my career to help steward the finances of the world's largest digital asset exchange through a period that tested our industry in every way: bull and bear cycles, Operation Choke Point 2.0, and a regulatory landscape that evolved as quickly as the technology itself. Finance is seldom the loudest function in a company, but it is where trust is earned. Over these five years, we transformed Finance from a pure back-office function into one that consistently generates new ideas and revenue opportunities for the company. We became amazing problem solvers.  Finance understood the products and metrics as well as the business units themselves.  Proud of what we have built together, and I am pleased to hand the keys to Justin, our next CFO.

I want to take this opportunity to thank CZ, Yi, Richard, and the leadership team for their confidence and, above all, the amazing Binancians around the world whom I had the honor of working with. You are the reason the company stands where it does today. Binance is in very capable hands.

The company continues to grow and evolve with the successful launch of TradFi assets and AI-powered user interfaces. I’d like to express my gratitude to MGX for the trust; to our home regulator Abu Dhabi Global Market and all regulators we work closely with; and to our business partners, including BlackRock, Circle, Franklin Templeton, Mastercard, our banking partners and payment channels, as well as our advisors and auditors. Special thanks to Grant Thornton Singapore and everyone who has supported Binance.

As for what comes next, well, there isn't just one project but several that I am passionate about particularly in sports and entertainment, from basketball and music, to GPUs, robotics, gold and collectibles. Bringing these real-world assets onto the blockchain through tokenization is a massive opportunity for the industry, and a big unlock for everyone.  I welcome anyone with a passion in these areas to message me and potentially join my team.  Even better if you love Kobe ;)

Moving from the CFO's chair to the founder's is a leap, and I take it with humility. I deeply believe it is where I can make a greater contribution to AI and Web3.

For now, thank you, Binance, for five remarkable years.
