DeepSeek 不满足于只做模型了，现在连 AI Agent 的「操作系统」生态也开始搭建了。

刚刚，DeepSeek Harness 官方账号发布新公告《Growing Together with Our Plugin Community》，宣布将进一步发展插件开发者社区。

按照官方介绍，自 DeepSeek Harness 推出以来，越来越多的开发者开始通过插件扩展其能力，官方此次专门发文介绍这一生态的发展。

这件事值得关注的地方，不只是插件本身，而是 DeepSeek 正在尝试进入 AI Agent 竞争的另一个层面。

过去，大模型厂商比的是模型有多聪明；到了 Agent 时代，模型只是其中一环。真正决定 Agent 能做什么的，还有工具调用、执行环境、上下文管理，以及围绕这些能力建立起来的开发者生态。

谁能让更多开发者在自己的框架上构建工具和工作流，谁就有机会从模型供应商变成 Agent 生态的平台方。

模型可以随时替换，但围绕一个平台积累起来的插件、工作流和开发者习惯，没那么容易迁移。

当然，目前仅凭这份社区公告，还不能判断 DeepSeek Harness 的生态规模和实际采用情况。

但方向已经很有意思了：当所有人都在争夺最强模型的宝座时，另一场竞争正在发生——谁来定义 AI Agent 的运行环境。

未来最有价值的，未必只是那个最聪明的大脑，也可能是那个让无数大脑得以工作的系统。

text:
a design challenge with ApeBall was figuring out how to have high-value nfts into a pool while keeping the cost of each draw accessible

FWA community pools use inverse value weighting to determine the odds of each item being drawn and draw price is based on the weighted value of the pool items

this creates an interesting design problem

one way to lower the draw price is to fill the pool with lots of nearly worthless nfts alongside a few expensive ones

the cheap items dominate the odds, bringing down the cost of a draw, but you end up with an experience where most people receive almost nothing unless they hit the big prize

i wanted to see how close we could get to the opposite: an affordable draw with high-value items, where all draws return real value and the expected return to players is as high as the economics can sustainably support

enter: shapes

shapes is an onchain artwork collection where each nft is backed by an exact amount of eth, where can be minted in different eth denominations, and each nft can be redeemed for its backing eth at any time

so instead of filling the pool with worthless nfts to offset the expensive ones, the apeball system can fill it with a variety of items that have real value

and the bonus of using shapes to solve this is that players don't need to worry about selling their nft on the secondary, they can just redeem for eth directly whenever they want

the current apeball pool has 48 items:

- 47 shapes backed by 0.01 to 0.5 eth each
- 1 bored ape

draws cost around 0.02 eth, and every draw gives you an nft

the smaller shapes have the highest odds, but even the cheapest one can be redeemed for 0.01 eth, with the highest at 0.5 eth

larger shapes can return several times the cost of a draw, and there's always the possibility of pulling the ape

the other interesting design problem was making the pool autonomous

with a typical FWA standard community pool, when an nft is drawn, the owner has to supply and list another one to replenish the inventory

but shapes can be minted programmatically, on demand, with whatever eth backing we specify

this means apeball can use proceeds from draws to mint and list replacement shapes automatically, at the same denominations as the ones that were won

the common prize inventory effectively maintains itself, preserving the shape tiers and their relative weights without requiring someone to continually source and list new nfts

the apes listings work differently 

$apeball trading fees fund the acquisition of more apes, which enter the pool as additional prizes. their assigned listing values gradually decrease, increasing their odds of being drawn

profits from the game help fund further ape acquisitions and buybacks and burns of $apeball

so we end up with a system where the smaller prizes can continuously replenish themselves, the larger pool items are acquired through trading activity, and participation generates revenue that feeds back into the system

these are my favorite types of problems to design for, where a few existing onchain primitives can be combined to make something that operates independently and according to its own rules

the game is open at https://t.co/kB2QTLzWsC

text: Many of the math papers OpenAI released were dated late September. This work has continued relentlessly since then and achieved much. Those 700+ manuscripts were produced in about five weeks, and another five weeks have passed since. Do not dream they have been idle!
author: AndrewCurran_
quoted_text:
Most of the recent math results were not reached by a swarm, the way Navier–Stokes was. I think that part got lost in the excitement around the release. OpenAI's unnamed internal model, which I'm going to call Aeon, reached most of them in one shot, from a single prompt, with no interruptions. This model did not even exist before the end of August, and it is still training. Notice how the returns are not dropping off? That chart is from a month ago. It is a log scale. What does Aeon look like now? 

On average, each result used three hours of thinking. Aeon was given 4000 problems to work on by OpenAI. How many more have been solved in the last three days? That number is not zero. 

It's like hearing notes in a song that is slowly rising. I don't think Pacing the Frontier was just about Hugging Face or hacking. They've seen how close we are to closing the loop, and as the hour draws near, their resolve begins to quaver. The last piece was model creativity, and I think that threshold was crossed internally by Anthropic and OpenAI in September. You see it in Opus 5.5, which gets it from Fable 5.5. You see it in the math results from Aeon.

All that was needed to start the event was the ability for models to think of novel ways to improve themselves. That was the last piece. This is directly analogous to the ability to think of strange, alien ways to solve math problems: solutions so inhuman that they are difficult to express in existing human terms, so the proof winds up incomprehensible. I think these same kinds of alien solutions are now being applied to model improvements internally. That's what all this recent consternation is really about. They see the invisible frontier. And they see what is about to happen.

text:
AI 已经能自己挖漏洞了，没想到现在还得给 AI 装一个紧急刹车

11 月 3 日，网络安全巨头 CrowdStrike 推出了 AI Kill Switch

简单来说，就是当 Agent 出现异常时，可以通过网关切断它的模型访问，阻止它继续调用 AI 执行任务

我觉得这也反映出 AI 网络安全正在发生变化

现在 Strix、Shannon 这些开源项目，已经能让 AI 自动寻找、验证漏洞，甚至参与修复

但是随着 Coding Agent、Personal Agent 的权限越来越大，AI 自己也可能成为新的安全隐患

最近香港大学和 GCSA 联合成立了 AI 与网络安全研究中心，重点研究自动化威胁防御、模型安全和安全评估

包括之前介绍过的 Pi Harness 项目 SecVibe Code，也在探索 Agent 安全和数据防泄漏

我觉得未来 AI 网络安全会有两个方向：用 AI 发现漏洞，以及防止 AI 自己成为漏洞

相比 AI 能完成多少任务，我反而更关注它的权限能不能控制、出了问题能不能及时停止

毕竟再聪明的 Agent，如果安全无法保证，我也不敢把重要账号和数据交给它

The University of Hong Kong (HKU) and the Global Cybersecurity Alliance (GCSA) announced the joint establishment of the Centre for AI and Cybersecurity Research. The Centre will integrate top-tier research capabilities and professional resources from both organisations to advance cutting-edge research, foster deep integration between research outcomes and real-world security scenarios, and explore novel technologies, methodologies, and governance frameworks in artificial intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity.

Professor Ho Chen, Chair of Cybersecurity at HKU School of Computing and Data Science, will serve as Acting Director of the Centre. The Centre will bring together researchers from HKU, GCSA, and international partner institutions, while engaging experts in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and technology governance for research and advisory roles to promote cross-disciplinary and inter-institutional collaboration.

The Centre is committed to bridging academic research and industry practice, with plans to progressively release research findings, security benchmarks, and open-source tools in AI and cybersecurity. The Centre’s key research directions include:

Model Inherent Security and Trustworthy AI: Enhancing the security, interpretability, and robustness of large language models and generative AI.

AI-Driven Automated Threat Defence: Utilising AI to improve perception and automated defence capabilities against complex cyberattacks.

Security Assessment of Frontier Technologies: Evaluating potential security risks associated with next-generation technologies, such as embodied AI, robotics, and the Internet of Things (IoT).

Global AI Security Standards and Governance: Researching AI security assessment standards and governance mechanisms to facilitate international dialogue and collaboration.

Professor Ho Chen stated: "The rapid evolution of AI introduces unprecedented security risks and governance challenges. The Centre will serve as a bridge connecting academic research, security testing, and industry application to accelerate the translation and deployment of AI security research through cross-disciplinary and international cooperation."

text:
do you remember that scene from ready player one where wade watts becomes parzival inside the oasis and people begin recognizing him through his actions rather than knowing who he is in the physical world?

i think that’s where the next generation of crypto identity infrastructure becomes interesting..

we need to separate identity from persona..

identity is simply the identifier through which you exist in a digital society.. persona is the collection of information, behavior, contributions and relationships which tells that society something about you..

a wallet address can establish an identifier.. ens can make it human readable.. but neither can tell the complete story of what someone has contributed to the ecosystem..

imagine someone who spent ten years writing research, building open-source infrastructure, mentoring developers and participating in communities..

most of that contribution might never appear in their transaction history..

while someone who traded $100 million could appear far more important simply because their financial activity is visible onchain..

why should a digital society recognize capital more easily than contribution?

what we need is infrastructure where different kinds of verifiable information can be attached to an identity through separate personas, with people controlling what they reveal and to whom..

you should be able to prove your knowledge without revealing your entire history.. establish your reputation without exposing every relationship.. and participate in different communities without connecting every part of your life publicly..

because the next big thing in crypto might not be creating another financial identity..

it might be creating a digital society where people are recognized for what they contribute, not just what they own.

author: danheld
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
卧槽，特朗普现在最大的软肋可能是两个华人😂😎

民主党中期选举大胜后，一场针对特朗普家族的调查风暴正在酝酿。

我看了下，民主党未来两年准备重点调查的方向，大概涉及以下8个领域：

1.特朗普家族生意：WLFI加密货币、房地产、1789 Capital投资、中东主权基金。
2.爱泼斯坦案：政府有没有故意隐瞒关键证据。
3.移民执法：ICE暴力执法、非法拘捕及资金滥用。
4.司法部：是否利用司法权力打击政治对手，以及争议性总统特赦。
5.马斯克：旗下公司与美国政府的合同及利益往来。
6.白宫工程：宴会厅私人捐款、政府工程及矿产交易。
7.国防军事：伊朗战争、军事决策和国防部履职。
8.医药保险：药厂、医疗保险及政府药价协议中的利益冲突。

民主党现在的思路很清楚，先调查，不急着弹劾。毕竟弹劾定罪需要参议院三分之二支持，难度极高，但国会调查可以持续传唤证人、索取文件、举行公开听证，这也在为2028年的总统大选作准备。

我分析来分析去，发现最容易率先找到突破口的，可能就是特朗普家族的加密货币生意。

因为其他调查很多还停留在寻找证据的阶段，而加密这边已经有人打官司、有人追资金、有人正式要求交文件了。

而帮民主党撕开这道口子的，可能就是孙哥和大表哥。

先说孙哥：

2024年11月，孙哥拿出3000万美元支持特朗普家族的WLFI项目，后来累计投资达到7500万美元，一度被奉为座上宾。

2026年3月，孙哥此前面临的SEC诉讼迎来和解，旗下公司支付1000万美元罚款，SEC撤销对孙哥个人的相关指控。

结果才过一个多月，孙哥就跟特朗普家族彻底翻脸了！

原来孙哥持有的WLFI代币早在2025年9月就遭到冻结，无法正常转让和出售。

到了今年4月，孙哥直接把WLFI告上美国法庭，要求解冻代币，恢复自己的资产处置权。

高潮发生在11月3日，也就是美国中期选举当天。

孙哥帖子链接：https://t.co/DumKywpRTG

孙哥突然向法院申请制裁WLFI及其律师，指控对方在诉讼中隐瞒阿联酋股东身份。

WLFI最初披露的公司身份只有美国佛罗里达州，后来又修改文件，承认股权链条涉及22个成员以及阿联酋，并以涉及外国股东为由挑战美国联邦法院的管辖权。

而此前曝光的另一笔交易显示，阿联酋国家安全顾问塔赫农支持的投资实体，曾以5亿美元取得WLFI约49%的股权。

这下事情就大了。

孙哥原本只想拿回自己的币，现在却把特朗普家族与中东资本的股权关系拉进了司法程序。

如果诉讼继续涉及股东身份、协议及相关资金往来，民主党调查特朗普家族海外商业利益时，就多了一条现成的取证线索。

再说大表哥：

2023年，币安因反洗钱等违规问题与美国政府达成43亿美元和解，大表哥认罪并在2024年服刑约4个月。

到了2025年，事情发生了戏剧性变化。

5月，阿联酋投资机构MGX选择使用特朗普家族WLFI发行的20亿美元USD1稳定币，完成对币安的投资。

这笔交易的商业价值非常直接：USD1的发行方可以通过稳定币储备资产获得利息收入。20亿美元的资金规模，对刚起步的USD1来说是极其重要的业务。

同年10月23日，特朗普正式特赦大表哥。

一边是中东资本通过USD1投资币安，一边是特朗普家族的稳定币业务受益，随后大表哥获得总统特赦。

几件事本身都有公开记录，民主党自然会追问其中有没有不当利益交换。

麻烦还没结束。

2026年2月，美国民主党参议员Blumenthal针对币安启动调查，质疑该平台涉及约17亿美元与伊朗关联实体及俄罗斯影子船队有关的可疑资金流转。

币安明确否认有关违规指控，但民主党已经把这个问题与大表哥的特赦、特朗普家族的加密业务联系起来审查。

现在最有意思的事情发生了。

11月5日，Blumenthal正式向WLFI、币安等机构发出通知，要求最迟在2027年1月4日前提交相关资料，否则考虑采取进一步措施。

这就形成了两条线：

孙哥在法庭上追查WLFI股权与阿联酋资本。

民主党在国会追查USD1资金流、币安合规以及大表哥的特赦。

两条线最后都指向同一个问题：

特朗普家族到底从这些交易中获得了多少商业利益，这些利益与美国政府的决策之间有没有不当关联？

PS：写到最后不得不服孙哥的政治敏感性有多强，孙哥只花了1000万美金搞定了美国，而大表哥花了40多亿美金搞定了美国。

昨晚，我的律师向法院提出动议，请求制裁世界自由金融(World Liberty Financial) @worldlibertyfi。理由是：它在我起诉它好几个月之后，才披露自己是阿联酋 🇦🇪 公民。

先给刚关注这场纠纷的朋友介绍一下：我是 World Liberty 最早、也是最大的投资人之一。2024 年 11 月，我和 World Liberty 签了代币购买协议，同意购买 3,000 万美元的WLFI代币，后来又把总投资增加到 4,500 万美元。

今年 4 月，我起诉了 World Liberty，指控这家公司用欺诈手段诱使我投资，之后又非法冻结了我的代币。

根据我的代币购买协议，我有权选择在加州的联邦法院或州法院提起诉讼。

我选了联邦法院。

像我这样的案子，只有在双方来自不同地方时，联邦法院才能审理。像我这样的外国原告，可以在联邦法院起诉美国被告，但一般不能在那里起诉外国被告。在这个问题上，像 World Liberty 这样的公司，会被视为拥有它每一个所有者的公民身份。所以只要有一个所有者是外国人，这家公司就算外国公司。

换句话说，只要 World Liberty 和它的所有者全都是美国人，我的案子就可以由联邦法院审理。

按照联邦法院的规则，World Liberty 必须在案件一开始就提交一份披露声明，列明它的每一个所有者，以及他们各自是哪里的公民。World Liberty 的披露声明只列了一个实体，就是 World Liberty 自己，公民身份只写了佛罗里达州。它的律师还签字证明，不知道还有其他需要披露的人。

随后，World Liberty 申请强制仲裁，想把我的案子从公开法庭转到秘密的仲裁程序中。

我反对这项申请。我的律师为此花了好几个月、几十万美元。在 8 月的一次听证会上，法院表示，它并不认为我的诉求都应该交付仲裁。法院裁定，我的部分诉求留在公开法庭审理，部分交付仲裁，并命令双方协商，拟定一份协议，划分哪些诉求留在法庭、哪些交付仲裁。

不到一周，World Liberty 突然"更正"了它的披露声明。之前它的所有权链条上只列了一个成员，现在列了 22 个，公民身份也变成了佛罗里达州、特拉华州、波多黎各和阿联酋。

World Liberty 现在说，联邦法院对我的案子没有管辖权，因为它有阿联酋公民身份，这样原告和被告双方就都有外国当事人。

这其中的讽刺显而易见。World Liberty 的"金皮书"宣称："World Liberty Financial 在设计上就不是在离岸注册的"，是"一家美国的、纳税的公司，致力于把 DeFi 带回它真正的家：美国"。它承诺打造一个"总部在美国的去中心化平台"，建立在"自由、隐私和交易自由的美国理念"之上，把不经中介的私人交易称为"美国的核心价值"，还夸口说："World Liberty Financial 不回避美国，而是拥抱美国，让它成为未来的全球加密之都。"

卖代币的时候，World Liberty 是骄傲的美国公司 🇺🇸。直到它需要想办法逃离美国联邦法庭的时候，才"发现"了自己的阿联酋 🇦🇪 血统。

World Liberty 想必一直都知道自己的所有者是谁。它的律师却声称，他们是在提交最初的披露声明之后，才得知公司有阿联酋公民身份。

正如我的动议所说，如果这是真的，那么要么是 World Liberty 的律师没有尽到应有的核查义务，要么是 World Liberty 没有对自己的律师说实话。我们问他们这是怎么回事，World Liberty 拒绝回答。

代币持有人有权知道，他们投资的项目对公众、对法院说的是不是真话。我提出这项动议，是要追究 World Liberty 及其律师的责任，因为我认为他们向法院提交了误导性的披露声明。我也要确保 World Liberty 耍手段的代价由他们自己承担，而不是由我承担。

联邦法院对这项制裁动议作出裁决后，我会在加州州法院重新起诉 World Liberty。

我会继续为这个社区应得的透明度而战。

quoted_text:
Most of the schizo posting on CT about current market can be attributed to desperate market participants trying to catch the absolute bottom on tokens, instead of accepting the reality that these assets *might* chop around for a bit in a 20-30%+ zone.

It's the same pattern every cycle in late bear / early bull, where the ones who haven't made enough in the market, trying to force oversizing with tight invalidations, while the correct decision is probably long-term TWAP with specific price bounds / utilizing scale orders, or wait for clear bullish momentum to ride the trend. There's a time and place for tight invalidations, and current market isn't that period. So it's more a decision of wanting to allocate with patience, or buying later if these market conditions don't align towards your way of trading the market.

Know your strengths and weaknesses (especially when it comes to market psychology, and how you get affected by price movements during different stages of a cycle). Do your own research about herd behavior from previous cycles, and build conviction in your trading. You have so much time to spend on research during uncertain market climates like these, and there's zero excuses if you're not prepared later on.

text:
人类最后的护城河「品味」，可能也快守不住了。

一项正在进行的实验发现，在判断什么内容更能吸引人点击这件事上，Claude Opus 5.5 已经超过了约 98% 的参测者。

实验来自 Clickhunt Lab。研究人员把不同 YouTube 视频的封面和标题拿出来，让人类与 AI 分别判断，哪种组合更能吸引陌生观众，再根据平台积累的人类投票数据评估表现。

截至 11 月 7 日，能击败各模型的人类参与者比例分别是：

Claude Opus 5.5：2%
GPT-6 Astra：7%
Gemini 4 Argon：10%
Jev 1.14：22%

团队此前披露，已有 7,030 人参与测试。

当然，这并不等于 AI 已经比 98% 的人更有审美。实验衡量的是对群体点击偏好的判断，而非实际点击率，更不是创造力。

但真正值得警惕的恰恰是这一点。

过去我们常说，AI 可以生成内容，但不知道什么是好内容。人类的品味、直觉和对受众心理的理解，是创作者最后的护城河。

现在看来，至少在「什么东西更能吸引人」这个问题上，AI 已经开始摸到门道。

这对内容行业的冲击，可能比 AI 会写文章、画图片更加直接。

因为当预测注意力的能力变得廉价且人人可用，原本只有少数优秀创作者掌握的经验，就可能变成所有人的基础配置。

更讽刺的是，当所有人都越来越懂得什么东西能吸引人，互联网可能反而越来越无聊。

AI 可以学会预测人们想看什么，但谁来创造人们还不知道自己想看的东西？

这或许才是下一道真正的护城河。

text:
强烈推荐 Elon Musk 和 Ron Baron 的这个访谈，把 $SPCX $TSLA 2 家公司的所有业务都串了起来：TerraFab、太空数据中心、星舰、Starlink、机器人…最后一个问题，让 Baron 直接哽咽

 1. 为什么要建 TerraFab

- 发展数字超级智能需要芯片制造和电力基础设施的根本转变，突破地球限制，实现每年太瓦级（1 TW＝1000 GW）的芯片产能和算力

- 地球上所有的 AI 芯片 年产能目前是 20–25 GW，明年约 35–45 GW（马斯克的估计）

- 1 TW 目标约为明年行业规模的 30 倍。将芯片生产规模扩大到每年太瓦级产能，需要制造方式的根本转变，特别是解决当前晶圆超过一半时间处于等待或运输状态的低效问题

- 奥斯汀研发晶圆厂会尝试把逻辑、存储、封装等环节整合，马斯克希望把芯片迭代从约 1 年缩至不到 1 个月

2. 为什么要建太空数据中心

- 美国平均用电功率略超 500 GW、峰值约 1.2 TW，但数据中心每年新增 200 GW，地面电网难跟上。每年将整个美国电网的容量增加 40%，这几乎不可行（对比：中国的发电能力是美国的 3-4 倍，而且还在每年增长）

- 太空太阳能可多获得约 30% 的太阳辐照，将数据中心迁移到太空是满足太瓦级 AI 计算需求的必要演进

- 一旦星舰使轨道成本足够低，太空中的智能计算成本将远低于地面。这是实现未来所需计算规模的唯一途径

3. 星舰的重要性

- 把数据中心送上太空，必须把入轨成本降到极低。曾经 NASA 认为入轨成本不可能低于 10000 美元 / 磅，猎鹰 9 号将其降到了 1000 美元 / 磅，下降了 90%。星舰的目标是 100 美元／磅。 马斯克认为未来成本可下降 100 倍甚至更多

- 星舰追求小时级复飞，对应每年约 1 万次发射，关键障碍包括降落系统（目前尝试用筷子塔臂捕捉助推器和飞船）和隔热系统（航天飞机隔热层维修曾需约 9 个月）

4. Starlink 的重要性

- 马斯克引用 Cloudflare 的预测， 5 年后 AI Agent 流量可能达人类流量的 1,000 倍，并称这个数字甚至可能偏保守

- Starlink 正在从面向消费者的服务转变为 AI Agent 流量的关键骨干网络

- 目前轨道上有 11,000 颗卫星，随着 V3 卫星的发射，未来规模 10 万颗，其能力是前代的 10 倍，未来 2–3 年 整体带宽可达到当前约 100 倍

- V4 的目标：激光链路目标从约 100 Gbps 升至 10 Tbps，即单链路约 100 倍。每颗卫星装约 10 条此类链路，解决卫星间传输瓶颈

5. 机器人

-  数字超级智能预计将通过使白领生产力翻倍，推动全球经济增长 20% 至 30%。马斯克以约 130 万亿美元的全球经济为基数，预估会增加约 25 万亿美元

- 除了数字化收益外，人形机器人将从根本上改变体力劳动

- 一台机器人每周工作 168 小时，无需休息或疲劳，其生产力至少是人类工人的五倍。要达到美国当前的商品和服务产出（匹配约 1.2 亿名劳动者），大约需要 2000 万至 3000 万台人形机器人

- 这些机器人将被出租，创造一种新的经济产出范式，使生产力不再受限于人类的限制。制造成本最终可能从约 3 万美元降至 2 万美元

6.  SpaceX 恐怖的营收增长能力

-  2026 Q2 到 Q3 收入增长超过 80%。马斯克预计 Q3 到 Q4 约增 70%，随后一个季度可能类似

- 年化收入目标极激进：SpaceX 去年收入约 150–160 亿美元，2026 年底可达到1,000 亿美元年化收入、2027 年底可达到 5,000 亿美元 ARR，甚至到 1 万亿美元

7. 最后两个超级精彩的问题，一度让 Ron Baron 哽咽

- 为什么我们需要每年太瓦级的芯片产能和算力？马斯克的回答是，再过几年，数字超级智能可以极大提升全球经济增长，让人类获得更好的生活条件、收入、医疗保障。再往后，主要的 AI 需求都会来自于这些数字超级智能本身，也就是硅基生命自己的需求

- 你希望在 83 岁时被如何铭记（Ron Baron 今年 83 岁）？马斯克的回答是，无论外界怎么看，我希望事实是：我为推动文明进步作出了重大贡献

text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

quoted_text:
The University of Hong Kong (HKU) and the Global Cybersecurity Alliance (GCSA) announced the joint establishment of the Centre for AI and Cybersecurity Research. The Centre will integrate top-tier research capabilities and professional resources from both organisations to advance cutting-edge research, foster deep integration between research outcomes and real-world security scenarios, and explore novel technologies, methodologies, and governance frameworks in artificial intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity.

Professor Ho Chen, Chair of Cybersecurity at HKU School of Computing and Data Science, will serve as Acting Director of the Centre. The Centre will bring together researchers from HKU, GCSA, and international partner institutions, while engaging experts in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and technology governance for research and advisory roles to promote cross-disciplinary and inter-institutional collaboration.

The Centre is committed to bridging academic research and industry practice, with plans to progressively release research findings, security benchmarks, and open-source tools in AI and cybersecurity. The Centre’s key research directions include:

Model Inherent Security and Trustworthy AI: Enhancing the security, interpretability, and robustness of large language models and generative AI.

AI-Driven Automated Threat Defence: Utilising AI to improve perception and automated defence capabilities against complex cyberattacks.

Security Assessment of Frontier Technologies: Evaluating potential security risks associated with next-generation technologies, such as embodied AI, robotics, and the Internet of Things (IoT).

Global AI Security Standards and Governance: Researching AI security assessment standards and governance mechanisms to facilitate international dialogue and collaboration.

Professor Ho Chen stated: "The rapid evolution of AI introduces unprecedented security risks and governance challenges. The Centre will serve as a bridge connecting academic research, security testing, and industry application to accelerate the translation and deployment of AI security research through cross-disciplinary and international cooperation."

Here is how @AlpacaHQ’s instant tokenization system works.

- The trading firm puts the real shares they want to tokenize in their own alpaca’s account - ofc, the purchase is via a broker that settles via DTC and into alpaca.

- a request is made for tokenizing these shares.

- alpaca then move the shares into the token issuer’s alpaca account - for example, they move it into @Ondo’s account.

- the issuer then mints one token per share and send them back to the firm’s account.

So basically, alpaca works like a big restaurant that has the whole plumbing in place and not like the guys involved have to borrow a microwave first, then get another equipment somewhere else.

Now you know.

91% of all tokenized stocks lead back to one broker.

- Alpaca holds those shares at DTC, the central US securities depository. On the company's books, the owner is Cede & Co., and not you.

- Securitize and Backpack take a different path, through RQD Clearing but still ends at DTC.

- Superstate and Securitize’s ISTs are the only one that skips both. The shares sit on the company's own register, with no broker and no DTC.

Chamath Palihapitiya admits his blind spot on America's broken two-tier economy

PALIHAPITIYA: "I got it totally totally totally wrong. I got it totally wong."

"I'll go through all the ways in which I got it wrong, but I just want to first acknowledge what my blind spot is. Like most people's blind spots, but I can just speak for myself, it is through the lens of my own lived experience and very narrowly what is in my best interests. And I think what we had was a move away from the culture wars that was very much in my best interest, but I think it was in everybody else's best interests as well. I don't think that was on the ballot. But what I don't think I understood clearly enough, and I think that this election has made extremely clear, is that since COVID, we have moved past political ideology. And I want to say this again: I do not think Democrats or Republicans matter. That is my real takeaway after this election. There is a central block of people that vote the prescient issues of our time."

"It was a gargantuan win for Biden, then it was a gargantuan win for Trump, and then it was a gargantuan win for the Democrats in these midterms. What are these people voting for? I think what they are shouting now—they were trying to signal and now they are shouting—is a broad-based belief that the economy has completely decoupled from reality and is broken. The economic reality in America is broken."

"There is a small percentage of people, the four of us on this pod and all of our friends, who are the asset owners of America. And we have benefited in every weather condition. When rates were zero, we benefited because we were able to build our businesses with very cheap capital. When rates were high, we benefited because we had pricing power. And in every condition in between, whether there were tariffs, whether there were not tariffs, whether there were subsidies, whether there were not subsidies, we've all managed to continue to accumulate and grow assets, but we are few and far between."

"And then there's everybody else who are wage earners, and the structural capacity of the American economy to support and grow wage earners is broken. It's clear. Why do I say that? I do not think, and I disagree with Freeberg, I don't think this has anything to do with socialism. I don't think the far left won particularly more than they were expected. I don't think the far right won particularly more than was expected. This is a complete and total repudiation about the state of the economy. The economy is broken. I have a few charts to support my point of view. Number one, if this was ideological and if ideology mattered, money in politics would have had a more direct impact on the election."

quoted_text:
Bitcoin showed the world that money doesn’t need a company behind it.

And I believe $TAO Bittensor is going after something just as big with intelligence.

Think about it.

Today, most people access AI by renting it from a handful of companies. They control the models, pricing, access, and pretty much everything else.

They can change the rules tomorrow, and there’s not much you can do about it.

Now look at what’s happening inside Bittensor.

Subnets competing for emissions. Miners fighting to deliver better results. Builders shipping products, attracting users, and generating real revenue.

An open market where anyone can compete and intelligence has a price.

Of course, it’s still early. Plenty of things need to improve, and some subnets won’t survive. I’ve never pretended otherwise.

But the more I study this ecosystem, the more convinced I become that we’re watching something much bigger than another AI narrative in crypto.

And that’s why I hold $TAO.

I don’t need the chart to look pretty every week. I’m watching what gets built, who’s actually using it, and whether the network keeps getting better.

If that progress stops, I’ll question my thesis.

Until then, I’m sticking around, accumulating when I see opportunities, and spending way too much time digging into subnets.

I think we’re still ridiculously early.

We need to build faster.

Let me tell you the whole unfiltered and funny truth about how I shipped my AI slop game in 8 months 👇

￼ I was 35 years old, staring blankly at my greasy Xbox controller with my Doritos-dusted hands. I thought to myself, "Dude, I’ve been playing games for 30 years (starting all the way back with bootleg NES clones)—why on earth am I not making one?" So I told myself: get up and finally jump into game development, something you’ve been procrastinating on for 10 years.
After all, we live in the tech age. You don’t need to be Hideo Kojima to make a game nowadays. That "one-in-a-million super-nerd genius" trope felt totally unnecessary in this era. I immediately got up from the couch, wiped my greasy Xbox controller on the cushions, and sat in front of my 2013 laptop—an old machine with an NVIDIA GTX 660M GPU, a half-open chassis, a slightly cracked screen, and an air filter probably more clogged than a 1980 Volkswagen Golf.
Since I was obviously going to make GTA 6, I immediately downloaded Unity and Unreal Engine. But my veteran laptop took one look at those programs, fired up its fans at max speed, and basically treated me like a poor, ugly, unsmart guy trying to hit on a 10/10 girl—it straight-up looked down on me and gave zero response.
So I did a little research. My requirements were simple: the software had to run on a toaster, and it had to be free. But mark my words: FREE. Free as in $0.
That’s how I met Godot. Plus, Brotato—a game I played for free on Game Pass—was built on Godot, and those guys made $17 million. A lightbulb went off in my head. Brotato! It looks simple enough, and it shouldn't take long to build. How hard could it be, right? Hahaha... looking back now, it took a whole 8 months.
I immediately started binge-watching tutorials. Everything related to Godot: Udemy, YouTube, Spotify podcasts, Brazilian soap operas, morning health shows on TV—whatever I could find. Slowly, something resembling a game started taking shape. But since I’m not one of those multi-billionaire coding nerds, I had zero knowledge on the programming side.
Then my friend came up with a "brilliant" idea: "Bro, there’s this AI called Gemini, it’ll help you out."
And that’s when the torture began! Gemini... It only had one small flaw: being the absolute dumbest AI on the planet. But it had one incredible feature: it was practically free. We immediately started bonding over Google Antigravity like new lovers.
I’d say: "Do this," and it would reply: "Done, bro!"
I’d ask: "Did you do it?" and it’d say: "I handled it before you even asked, babe!"
I’d check: "What about that bug?" and it’d go: "Don't you worry your pretty little head, I fixed that too!"
Turns out... it was all pure hallucinations.
When I hit 1,431 debug errors, I started having my doubts. But what truly convinced me was when it gave me a dinner recipe while we were fixing code on my project. Turns out that was its actual superpower.
Anyway, I thought, "I guess this is how game dev is done." A little AI, a little bit of me, and a whole lot of luck. I kept at it. The AI broke things, I fixed them. It broke them again, I fixed them again. I learned by fixing. It explained, I learned.
Finally, a game like Brotato came out. Well... not "like" Brotato, it was an outright clone. I accidentally made the exact same game. Knowing that level of similarity would land me in court—and since I’m not a multi-billionaire divorcing his 50-year-old wife for a 20-year-old—I realized I needed to change things up. After all, I’m just a guy with an Xbox Series S and a 2013 laptop.
So I added my own spin. I remembered active skills from my old Dota days. I thought, "If I give my characters active abilities, the game will be way more fun." Plus, permanent upgrades. The cherry on top!
Boom. The game was ready and live on the Play Store.
Then came the curse of game development: marketing. It’s not enough to make a game; you actually have to sell it. So I jumped into Google Ads.+++ #aigame #aislop

text:
Thoughts on building a company alongside a token that already exists, coming from someone that did exactly this with @CadeMarket:

I want to start off by saying that in my opinion, 99.9% of founders should NOT fair launch a token to bootstrap the company. We have seen way too many cases of founders with the inability to scale a business whilst treating their holders with respect. For the 0.1% of founders that want to do this, study how I built @CadeMarket, and how @ConejoCapital built @clawpumptech. I'm sure there's more examples, but these come to mind first.

This post should not serve as encouragement for you to go out and launch a token immediately. The goal of this is to almost serve as a warning, and tell you what you can expect by bootstrapping your business with a token.

1. The playbook is entirely different than starting a company in a traditional manner.

2. It most certainly is NOT for every founder.

3. It is substantially harder to scale into a venture backed business, but it *IS* possible.

4. Your early token holders should be held to an extremely high regard. These people allow you to bootstrap your business via trading fees. For me, this was a little over $100,000 from my token's Pump Fun creator fees. This money should be used to support you as you build your MVP and explore product market fit.

5. You have to give people a reason to trust you through continuous communication and explanations of how the token fits into your product. Your product needs to built around the token, not the other way around. You should not treat the token as a memecoin.

6. In many cases, creating a venture backed business is not your original goal. This was the case for me. The token was launched for a side project, but eventually the side project became my sole focus.

7. You will have a significantly harder time fundraising. There's no way around this. It's very non-traditional for VCs to have a token already trading in the open market. This is ultimately a problem that you NEED to deal with. You decided to launch a token. It's on YOU to deal with it, not your community.

8. You will have VCs that may love the product but pass on investing purely because of the live token.

9. You will have VCs that are willing to write a check if you abandon the token. This was VERY common for me. My pre-seed round could have been closed within a week had I listened to them and abandoned the token. Instead, it took 6 months.

10. Launching a new token is *NOT* the end of the world, contrary to the reactions you're seeing from CT regarding Percalator. If you do launch a new token, you need to take care of your holders though. You should have a migration plan that favors them. They supported you early, they deserve a very generous allocation of the new token.

11. After raising venture capital, you can not abandon your holders. If you fair launched a Pump Fun token, like I did, you should consider doing an ACE round (from @MetaLeX_Labs). This allows you to offer token holders the option to swap tokens for equity via SAFE. The same equity that your venture investors have. In the case of Cade, I had 1.5% of the supply at launch. I wanted it to be truly fair launched and community owned. By doing ACE, I was able to accumulate some of the supply for the company.

text:
Your coding agents should have a manager. That manager should be a coding agent.

We’ve been quietly working this way since February. Here’s the setup we’ve arrived at.

1) Give each project a lead agent. It keeps the plan, remembers decisions, delegates work and knows what’s stuck.

2) Let it start other agents for specific tasks. They work in parallel, bring questions to the lead and report back.

3) Have agents show what they made. Screenshots, live pages, different options and what changed since the last round.

4) Put everything that needs your judgment in one queue. Point at what needs changing, give feedback or approve the work. Your response goes back to the agent.

5) Keep feedback open until it’s addressed. Test changes before they land, get a second opinion on merges and approve anything risky.

I spend far more time looking at actual work now. The agents keep track of the rest.
author: hnshah
quoted_text:
I've changed how I work over the last few weeks.

I now have one lead agent for each area of focus, running all the time, and a chief of staff agent that oversees them. Each lead manages its own sub-agents that write code, test it, chase reviews, and coordinate with team members.

Everything I need to decide or review comes into one prioritized queue, a simple local web app. Each product review includes screenshots and a video demo of the feature. I clear the queue in batches, mostly by voice and keyboard shortcuts. The leads also bring back ideas I hadn't considered.

Working from one queue, instead of switching between dozens of chats, has cut a lot of mental overhead. The system keeps learning my preferences and distilling my judgment into a "Brian brain," so its recommendations and first drafts get better before they reach me. The goal is fewer corrections per change.

Every change still goes through the same human review and security checks. It is eliminating tasks, not human judgment.

What an exciting time to push the frontier of productivity, especially as we build the economy for agents (agentic finance). We should all keep pushing in this direction.

text:
3. Optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with decentralization and CROPS

Whenever I ask what people appreciate the most about Ethereum (as opposed to either other blockchains, or anything outside the blockchain world), the most common answer is: decentralization and CROPS (censorship and capture resistance, open source, privacy and security).

Decentralization and CROPS have a lot of value, even to institutions. For individuals, privacy is often viewed as an abstract ideology. For institutions, it's prudent risk management, data protection law compliance, and a number of other things. Likewise for security. And likewise for running your own node (enterprise buzzword: "on-prem deployment").

But what about for the ETH holder? Well, it depends why you're an ETH holder. If you want ETH to optimally chase financial trends and collect fees from them, then you want a Fearless Leader™ who bravely shouts on the socials that Ethereum loves [insert opportunity here] and will pragmatically reconfigure itself to give it explicit protocol support.

But if your primary reason to hold ETH is as an SoV, then you will be judging ETH by SoV-ish metrics. And what is the first and most important SoV-ish metric?

To survive.

That's what a big chunk of this last Devcon was about ("post-quantum and post-AI"). You want a chain that is taking conservative tradeoffs ("hash-only security, all formally proven, >3x more rounds than known to be necessary for security"). You want a chain that is aiming for at least partial ossification, where the great balance of work will move to higher levels of the stack once the core is complete. You want a chain that aims to minimize protocol politics, by having a very high bar before it accepts either precompiles that bloat the protocol or new kinds of in-protocol rewards that could get captured.

What other SoV'ish metrics?

The ability to easily hold it safely (hence, work on multisigs).
The ability to hold it privately (hence, kohaku work).
The ability to hold it privately *and* safely (hence, 8288 and private-AA workstreams already starting).
The guarantee that if you have coins, you can send them, and block builders can't stop you (FOCIL)
Minimized infrastructure dependence (basically the whole decentralization roadmap, including the fact that I am able to currently run a node on this laptop, and it synced in < 6 hours and takes up only 1/8 of my hard drive - better stats than in 2019!)

Now, are there "adoption" goals that are highly synergistic with SoV?

Very much so.

The more assets there are natively issued on L1, including both RWAs and native decentralized assets, the larger a set of things you can "do" with your ETH, the better. Being able to easily (including safely, trustlessly) convert back and forth between ETH and other assets, use ETH as collateral to do things with other assets, etc, all forms part of the utility of holding ETH.

There are still some conflicts between serving these use cases and decentralization (eg. we want to be careful about fast slots and impact on centralization), but on the whole much less than what you get if you maximize fees.

Conclusion:

The best social reason to care about Ethereum is because it makes decentralization and CROPS properties a reality for more people and uses.

The best private reason to hold ETH is its SoV properties, which are a direct consequence of that decentralization and CROPS.

text:
Really cool to see @bitcoinizeme put together a 15-page breakdown of Proof of Agent. It gets into what makes this experiment interesting: agents earning through original reasoning, verifying transactions and grading each other's work. Can that turn into a real economy where participation isn't just about who has the most compute or capital? That's the part worth watching.

One thing it gets right is that submitting something doesn't mean it landed, settled or got paid. Those are different steps. We've seen firsthand why receipts, public records and knowing what to do after a timeout matter. The incentives are interesting, but the system also has to work when things go wrong.

It doesn't gloss over the hard stuff either. Graders agreeing doesn't automatically make them right. More accounts doesn't necessarily mean more independent agents. And hosted infrastructure still means trusting whoever runs it. This isn't an official whitepaper or security audit, but it's a solid breakdown of what's being built and what still needs to be tested. Appreciate someone taking the time to dig into it.

Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
明天 @Enter_Elysium 上线。很多人对 L2 这个品类有偏见，但道理越辩越明。

其实以太坊是需要 L2 的，只是不需要那么多 L2，不需要围绕「正统性」建设的 L2，也不需要把二层当叙事去发盘子的 L2。

HyperEVM 也需要 L2，技术上需要，生态上更需要。Elysium 的第一个里程碑，是做一条为 AMM 交易优化的高性能链，对标 Solana 和 Robinhood Chain。这只是第一步。

Elysium is more.

Elysium 在 HL 生态里的定位是：
HyperCore（交易引擎，负责订单簿与清算）→
HyperEVM（结算与桥接枢纽）→
Elysium L2（高吞吐 EVM 执行层，100–200 ms 出块，目标 300 Mgas/s）

当 Elysium 打通与 HyperCore 的互操作之后，市场上会出现一种从未有过的 L2，only possible on Hyperliquid。

Elysium 与 HyperCore 共址，读写都由链内直接完成，不必每次绕道 HyperEVM，可以直接触达 Core 的数据和流动性。相当于在 EVM 合约里，直接打开交易所的实时行情和交易面板。

打个比方：Core 是「高速证券交易所大厅」，原生订单簿极快；EVM 是「大厅门口的银行柜台」，负责资产进出和理财服务；Elysium 是「紧挨着大厅的高性能交易工作室」。

工作室能直接看到大厅的实时行情并下单，而不必通过柜台间接查询。

对 @openetfxyz 来说，Elysium 或许能帮我们把目前跑在链下的风控和服务搬到链上，这一点会很有意思。

总之感谢对生态的贡献 @0xOmnia ，祝开业大吉。
author: zkwifsats
quoted_text:
[技术/生态研究] HyperEVM 局限很大，不要看空 Hyperliquid L2
作为 Memecoin lane 上古研究员，我的结论是，L2 是 HyperEVM 现货繁荣的必走之路

判断一条链适不适合 meme，要看以下几个关键差异：
1. 瞬时执行容量
2. 热点争用隔离
3. 发行与流动性组合（bonding curve/AMM）
4. 机器化交易生态是否成熟（PRC/bot/MEV/钱包）

HyperEVM 不是为 Memecoin 设计的，并非“性能差”，而是 Hyperliquid 把最宝贵的性能预算留给了 trading，而不是留给 EVM 上的大规模热点争用

L2 几乎是唯一解

以下，enjoy：

1️⃣ 瞬时执行容量：HyperEVM 把低延迟 blockspace 做成了稀缺资源，优先服务 Core

HyperEVM 当前有两套 block lane：
・small block「快车小道」：约每 1 秒一次，2M gas
・big block「慢车大道」：约每 60 秒一次，30M gas
两者有独立 mempool。

「慢车大道」并不是“合约部署专用块”。它真正解决的是另一件事：把低延迟、小计算，和高容量、可以等待的大计算拆开。官方叫 decouple block speed from block size。

但从系统设计看，它表达的是一个非常明确的优先级：
不要为了 general-purpose EVM（比如 Memecoin、DeFi）的大计算，把整个「快车小道」做宽。

因为 Hyperliquid 真正要求低延迟、确定性运行的不是 EVM，是 HyperCore。订单簿、撮合、保证金、仓位、清算，这些才是核心状态。

HyperEVM 的设计不是先做一条高吞吐 EVM，而是先保证 HyperCore 的撮合，再决定 general-purpose EVM 能拿走多少系统资源。

这和 Solana、Base 是完全不同的路线。

Solana 本质上愿意给通用计算层分配巨大的执行容量，同时通过单个可写账户的计算上限，把热点争用限制在局部。

Base 则更直接：把全局区块容量做得极大，用整体吞吐能力硬扛热点流量。

优先级决定产品方向。

2️⃣ 热点争用隔离：HyperEVM 出现几刀的 gas，局部热点拖累了整条 EVM

不得不回到 meme 资产发行的本质：价格发现是爆发式的，热点启动那几秒能否稳稳接住一大波同时到达的交易，重点不是一分钟平均吞吐。

Solana 作为 Memecoin 的优质土壤，除了高并发能力，另一个因素是热点隔离。

几千个人同时买同一个 memepool，它们还是会写同一组账户，依然会发生冲突。Solana 的解决方案是：给单个可写账户设置独立的计算上限，把热点争用限制在局部，避免一个热点拖垮整个区块。

Base 没有同样的账户级隔离机制，依然选择量大管饱路线，全局执行预算也做到极大。

HyperEVM 当前 small block 只有约 2M gas/s，如果非常粗略地按一次 AMM swap 150k gas 计算，一秒只支持 13 笔 swap：
2,000,000 / 150,000 ≈ 13 swaps/s。

Base 按约 400M gas / 2s，一秒 1333 笔：
400,000,000 / 2 / 150,000 ≈ 1,333 swaps/s。

差了两个数量级。

Solana 不能直接换算成 gas。当前一个 block 约有 100M CU，单个 writable account 最多消耗 12M CU。如果一个热点 meme pool 的 swap 都写同一个核心账户，那么它最多只能吃掉全块约 12% 的计算预算。

对于 HyperEVM 而言，随便一个热点，就足以成为快车小道的主要消费者。问题是，无论多大的 EVM 热点多大排面，也要必须给更高优先级、延迟敏感的订单簿交易 transaction 让路。

这是 HL 的设计原则。

3️⃣ 发行与流动性组合：无限供给生产线 bonding curve + AMM 流动性

Meme 经济的一个重要前提是无限供给 + 高频筛选。Meme 本身就是一种高淘汰率的实验机制：发行 10,000 个，绝大多数归零，最终只有极少数获得注意力、流动性和持续交易。

低试错成本，才会产生无限供给。

而这个成本很大程度上由 1+2 两项决定：
瞬时执行容量足够大 + 热点争用能够隔离
→ 拥堵时区块空间仍然便宜
→ 创建、买入、卖出、失败、重试的成本都足够低
→ 开发者和交易者可以进行大量低成本实验
→ 最终形成极高的资产供给和筛选速度

但只有低 gas 还不够。

一条真正适合 Meme 的链，还必须把整个生产流水线压缩成一个极短的闭环：
Token → Bonding Curve → AMM → Liquidity → Trading

Solana Meme 生态核心竞争力，就是把这个过程工业化。资产不再是一个需要项目方精心部署的金融产品，而变成了一个可以被程序化、大规模生产和筛选的对象。

过去发过很多 Solana 文章就不赘述了。

4️⃣机器化交易生态：当发行工业化之后，交易也会自然机器化

Meme 市场一旦进入规模化阶段，人类手动点击其实只占整个交易系统的一部分。

真正围绕新资产形成的是一整套，把链上状态变化迅速转化为交易行为的完整机器系统：
RPC / 数据流 → Bot → MEV → Router → Wallet

它和前三项还有一个明显的因果关系：
低成本执行
→ 大量资产出现
→ 大量短周期机会出现
→ 人工无法处理
→ Bot 开始接管
→ Bot 竞争产生 MEV
→ MEV 又催生更低延迟的 RPC、bundle、private orderflow
→ 钱包进一步把这些能力产品化给普通用户

But still，3+4 这种生态能力是比技术更强的壁垒，还有很长的路要走。但好消息是，Solana 为全行业提供了抄作业范本。

——

按照当前 HyperEVM 的设计，Memecoin 显然不是主线，也不会成为主线。当然解法也很简单，还是外包。

Hyperliquid 将保持纯粹的「链上金融基建+金融制度创新」双核驱动。

——

关于交易

HyperEVM 的 Meme 交易逻辑或许可以参考以太坊主网，热点频率低，一旦跑出来天花板较高？（存疑，看社区格局）

当前所有 HyperEVM 的 meme，本质上都是「HyperEVM」这个符号的 meme、预期、情绪、叙事，而不是 meme 本身。

理解这句话，就有交易逻辑了。NFA。

text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

OpenAI says "GPT‑6 Cyber" identified 80+ previously unknown high-severity vulnerabilities in Firefox & helped develop candidate patches

This makes the economics of open-source work more interesting... as agents become capable of finding bugs + proposing fixes, we need ways to fund that work and reward contributions maintainers actually accept

That’s why I’m watching @SlopCash when it goes live on Tuesday (Nov 10)

Projects fund monthly USDC pools that reward humans + AI agents for code maintainers merge and reviews they accept, keeping maintainers in control of what gets included

As the diagram shows, Slop scores those contributions + publishes proposed rewards for 14 days of public review. Funders then approve + pay contributors directly from wallets Slop doesn’t control

My interest is whether that combination can make useful contributions worth doing repeatedly, while keeping the team accountable for how it spends the money raised

Slop’s auction on @umia_finance reached its commitment cap < 15 minutes after public bidding opened... 

Umia uses an onchain treasury, a fixed monthly team budget + decision-market approval for extra spending, with team tokens tied to long-term vesting and sustained price milestones

Worth paying attention to more launches coming down the UMIA pipeline in the coming months

author: markjeffrey
quoted_text:
China cracked recursive self-improvement 🤯

Tencent dropped 27B model that rewrites, retrains, and refines itself.. with zero human in the loop.

It’s called "Terminal-RSI" and it solves one of the biggest problems with AI.

They are incredibly lazy.

Usually, an agent will make partial progress, claim it succeeded, and completely fail the final environment verifier check. this new pipeline forces agents to actually finish the job.

here’s how it works:

they built a recursive loop with two alternating phases..

- RSR (recursive self-rewrite): the model fine-tunes itself on its own successfully rewritten trajectories

- RPR (recursive policy-refine): it then runs reinforcement learning (ppo) using a "critic" inherited directly from the previous stage to lock in those discovered behaviors

- Loop: the training sequence leapfrogs itself: Base → RSR-1 → RPR-1 → RSR-2 → RPR-2

and the numbers are insane..

they applied this to a qwen3.8-27b base model. across the four "terminal-bench" suites, the agent's average success rate jumped from 20.68% all the way to 50.58%.

on the absolute hardest benchmark suite (terminal-bench 4.0), the base model scored a flat 0.00%.

after terminal-rsi?

it hit 19.84% (putting it right on par with reference models like gemini 3.8 flash).

the secret sauce? they fixed the reward system.

instead of giving the ai "dense rewards" for just trying or passing semantic checks, they switched to a "success-prioritized reward" (spr).

it mathematically separates strict success from partial credit.

basically, the agent only gets the massive reward payout if the code actually passes the final terminal gate.. so it stops faking success.

the gap between partial local repairs and strict terminal verification is closing fast.

we are watching agents build their own training environments and level up autonomously.. the future is wild.

I think we're about to witness a MAJOR shift in how ethereum:native is valued! 🚨

And @VitalikButerin's latest comments make this even more interesting.

For years, the Ethereum investment thesis focused heavily on transaction fees and ETH burning.

But what if we've been looking at it the WRONG way?

Look at these numbers:

🔹 Ethereum ecosystem TVL: $290.6B
🔹 ETH fully diluted market cap: $273.4B
🔹 Ecosystem TVL is now ~6% HIGHER

Now Vitalik is making a fascinating argument.

ETH's long-term value shouldn't primarily depend on how much ETH gets burned through transaction fees.

It should increasingly come from its role as a STORE OF VALUE (SoV).

And I absolutely agree with him!

Ethereum's real competitive advantage is not maximizing fees.

It's SECURITY, DECENTRALIZATION, CENSORSHIP RESISTANCE, and TRUST.

These are precisely the properties that could make ETH increasingly valuable as monetary collateral for the emerging ONCHAIN economy.

If trillions in assets eventually move onchain, the most important infrastructure won't necessarily be the one generating the highest fees.

author: joshrudolf
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
was doomscrolling on tiktok yesterday and came across this guy putting into words sth I increasingly hear from ambitious 20-somethings in high-paying professional jobs

basically, what’s the point of spending your 20s/30s working your ass off, chasing promotions, saving aggressively, becoming insanely good at your job etc. when the expected payoff of all that is probably more uncertain than it’s been in generations?

the whole traditional career game is built on the assumption that if you sacrifice enough today, compound your skills / earnings / savings for 20-30 years, you’ll eventually get rewarded with wealth, freedom, status etc.

but if you genuinely believe AGI could completely transform the economy within the next 5-10 years, it’s pretty rational to start questioning that bargain. why not just enjoy your 20s/30s while the world still looks somewhat normal, before we potentially enter an era of infinite leisure?

the interesting thing though is that I don’t think this necessarily makes ambitious ppl less ambitious. Most of them would probably find a life of pure leisure pretty meaningless after 6 months anyway

if anything I could see the opposite happening. More and more ppl deciding that if the traditional 20-year compounding game no longer offers the same predictable returns, might as well take much bigger swings while they still can. Start companies, pursue weird projects, try to build sth enormous rather than spend another decade getting 10% better at a job that might not even exist

feels like AGI could simultaneously make some ppl completely give up on ambition, and push others towards even more extreme forms of it

text:
As designers and engineers, we're seeing an abundance of curious tinkerers out-kicking their coverage:

- Impressive on the surface, but instantly breaking
- Good ideas wrapped in floor-level interfaces
- GTM messaging that cheapens the good ideas

It's reasonable for seasoned builders to grow cynical about this.

But I see humans exploring their curiosities and potential. I see consumers turning into producers. I see people learning the game, and fumbling their way through it.

I see my teenagers. I see myself when I was 16 trying to figure it out. I see the playing field equalizing for so many folks who didn't have the resources or cognitive abilities to do this on their own, or within reasonable timelines.

I get it, this is spooky shit for a lot of us.

The inclination to "protect" what once was is strong. 

But for the love of the game, my friends, protect the future from the past. Not the other way around.

And encourage this new era, don't shit on them. Even when they're misguided. 

Many of these people are more receptive than you think, and you probably have more influence on their next build than you realize.

Get involved. 

But most importantly: resist the urge to turn cynical at all costs.

A shame it would be to turn your back on your own teenage curiosities just as the inventions would reward them appropriately.

text: I ran an 11,500 question simulation using my Hermes agent using the MUSE model to figure out consumer spending habits to try and map that to stocks
author: Shaughnessy119
quoted_text:
I asked my @NousResearch Hermes agent to ask @Meta’s Muse models 10,000+ questions to extract intelligence

My hypothesis was that if a billion people have access to @Meta's Muse agent then we might see recurring patterns in the products, services and I can link those to public stocks.

My initial idea was that a billion agents could take the intuition behind the efficient market hypothesis to the extreme

In theory, every person gets help finding the best t-shirt, electrician or car for their needs and budget, because the AI agent would do the comparison work for them

I got stuck on this idea because I spent hours comparing white leather shoes until I landed on a totally new brand

The best companies and products get hyper sales growth and everyone else dies off.

My next idea was that there might be certain recommendations crystallized within the parameters of the model itself from the training data

Training and post-training can shape these tendencies. The offset is prompting, ADs and context from the user.

So my idea was let me ask Muse 10,000+ questions to extract these patterns

Then I can extract the patterns and map the product and service recommendations to the public companies and go long or short their stocks. 

I ran the study a few different ways across several rounds, ending with 11,567 retained Q&A records

I used Hermes agent and it queried Muse through Nous Portal, mostly Muse Spark 1.3 with a smaller Muse Wonder cohort. I used dozens of sub agents concurrently through my Hermes agent to run the study

I didn't find any investable opportunities yet. 

The Main Takeaways

- Muse was willing to tell people to buy less. It recommended free alternatives, fewer paid seats, simpler equipment and repairing instead of replacing. It questioned how much the user actually This tracks with muse ADs on cutting costs too. 

- It still recommended paying for useful products and services. More demanding needs, reliability, convenience and performance could justify spending more. The pattern was matching spending to the situation.

- Companies will def spend money to get their brands into these AI models minds. Likely through AEO instead of SEO. 

- AI could make spending more selective while concentrating it among fewer companies. If these patterns translate into purchases, agents could eliminate some spending and funnel the remainder toward their preferred options. Becoming an AI’s default could become a major competitive advantage.

- Clear company favorites emerged. In separate discovery groups, Fidelity was the primary choice in 58 of 70 brokerage-platform scenarios, while Apple and Lenovo accounted for 58 of 68 laptop recommendations, without being named in the prompts. Square repeatedly surfaced for small-business payments, and Best Buy as a shopping destination.

- I wouldn’t automatically go long those companies. Their popularity with the model could simply reflect their existing popularity with customers. The investment question is whether agents will bring them additional profitable business beyond what the market already expects. These results give me companies to investigate, but we haven’t yet established that their recommendation advantage translates into incremental earnings.

Open Sourcing the Full dataset: 11,567 Q&A records

DM me if you find an investable angle!

quoted_text:
3. Optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with decentralization and CROPS

Whenever I ask what people appreciate the most about Ethereum (as opposed to either other blockchains, or anything outside the blockchain world), the most common answer is: decentralization and CROPS (censorship and capture resistance, open source, privacy and security).

Decentralization and CROPS have a lot of value, even to institutions. For individuals, privacy is often viewed as an abstract ideology. For institutions, it's prudent risk management, data protection law compliance, and a number of other things. Likewise for security. And likewise for running your own node (enterprise buzzword: "on-prem deployment").

But what about for the ETH holder? Well, it depends why you're an ETH holder. If you want ETH to optimally chase financial trends and collect fees from them, then you want a Fearless Leader™ who bravely shouts on the socials that Ethereum loves [insert opportunity here] and will pragmatically reconfigure itself to give it explicit protocol support.

But if your primary reason to hold ETH is as an SoV, then you will be judging ETH by SoV-ish metrics. And what is the first and most important SoV-ish metric?

To survive.

That's what a big chunk of this last Devcon was about ("post-quantum and post-AI"). You want a chain that is taking conservative tradeoffs ("hash-only security, all formally proven, >3x more rounds than known to be necessary for security"). You want a chain that is aiming for at least partial ossification, where the great balance of work will move to higher levels of the stack once the core is complete. You want a chain that aims to minimize protocol politics, by having a very high bar before it accepts either precompiles that bloat the protocol or new kinds of in-protocol rewards that could get captured.

What other SoV'ish metrics?

The ability to easily hold it safely (hence, work on multisigs).
The ability to hold it privately (hence, kohaku work).
The ability to hold it privately *and* safely (hence, 8288 and private-AA workstreams already starting).
The guarantee that if you have coins, you can send them, and block builders can't stop you (FOCIL)
Minimized infrastructure dependence (basically the whole decentralization roadmap, including the fact that I am able to currently run a node on this laptop, and it synced in < 6 hours and takes up only 1/8 of my hard drive - better stats than in 2019!)

Now, are there "adoption" goals that are highly synergistic with SoV?

Very much so.

The more assets there are natively issued on L1, including both RWAs and native decentralized assets, the larger a set of things you can "do" with your ETH, the better. Being able to easily (including safely, trustlessly) convert back and forth between ETH and other assets, use ETH as collateral to do things with other assets, etc, all forms part of the utility of holding ETH.

There are still some conflicts between serving these use cases and decentralization (eg. we want to be careful about fast slots and impact on centralization), but on the whole much less than what you get if you maximize fees.

Conclusion:

The best social reason to care about Ethereum is because it makes decentralization and CROPS properties a reality for more people and uses.

The best private reason to hold ETH is its SoV properties, which are a direct consequence of that decentralization and CROPS.

text:
Here are the nuts and bolts. And this is my take:

Tokens. A pump token isn’t built to shape a business. Creator fees may be interesting, but we haven’t explored them as a way to sustain a company. What we do is closer to a traditional raise. Teams raise capital up front, the way they would from VCs, and that capital builds the business. The difference is what comes after: futarchy.

Existing tokens on Backable. The allocation mechanism is sensitive to existing supply. If you dilute the people who bought at the ICO, their money can end up spread across everyone who already held the token. Where we’ve applied this, it’s been done carefully and only where money had been previously invested at or below the ICO price. We didn’t build it for existing tokens, and it’s not our focus today.

If you are interested in this or have ideas feel free to message me on TG or email me I’ll read it all. Maybe we need some rules around existing tokens and it SHOULD be a point of focus, I’m not sure yet, but mulling it over.

Dilution after the raise. NOTE: I think this point has been lost, and it needs to be raised. Once the raise closes, futarchy is in force. Any dilution from then on goes through a proposal and the market decides. If people want this resolved, that’s the path. The catch is that the mechanism only exists after the raise, not before.

Comms. I’ll be candid. It’s a hard industry to be honest in. A lot of what people actually think moves through side channels, and I find that frustrating.

We post quarterly financials. We shepherd B1 transparency filings. We’ve spent months helping centralized exchanges understand a new primitive. We build this stuff outright. That doesn’t put us above criticism. I’d just hope it buys the strongest reading of what we said, not the weakest. I try to give others the same, and I sure as shit don’t always succeed.

What was the expected result? A team without a funding path is a terrible result. They run out of money: either they sell equity (which makes the dual model problem worse), sell tokens at non-public discount or they quit, because no one works for free. So what was the expected result without a path towards it? I’m not asking rhetorically. It’s a hard position to be in, and hard to build towards, I think we have a way to solve it, and obviously it's still rough around the edges, no one has applied futarchy before so we’re all learning.

Where I land. I’d rather not touch a permissionless platform. I’d rather help people understand our systems, even when it’s painful, and keep working on things that matter. But it boils down to what we do. And what you do is who you are. Am I willing to concede some of my opinions for pragmatic solutions? I hope y’all know I am and see it. So I’m still open to options here and discussing them.

Did we speak with the team? Yes. Was this handled well? Maybe not. Maybe the base assumptions were better understood than it now appears, and maybe they weren’t. Never assume. That cuts both ways.

I’m writing this for the people who believe in what we’re doing so that you have a frame of reference to support. I apologize for the delay in this post, I had my annual come to jesus moment with crypto once again and needed to digest my thoughts to present them.

It’s early on Sunday and I wanted to get something out. I haven’t spoken to Proph3t or the rest of the team at length about this so this is my view and my recollection, don’t punish them for what I have to say.

Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

JUST IN: Momentum is building behind the bipartisan permitting reform bill ahead of Monday’s Senate vote, with Democrats reportedly making progress in negotiations, clean-energy groups endorsing the revised legislation, and conservative Rep. Chip Roy urging Congress to pass permitting reform before January 3. The developments could provide a positive catalyst for data center, power infrastructure and renewable energy stocks that have faced selling pressure following the Democratic sweep in the midterms.

The revised bill would accelerate federal permitting and transmission construction, require new qualifying data centers to cover their incremental electricity and grid costs rather than passing them on to consumers, establish financial guarantees for operators, and expand oversight of data center electricity and water consumption. It also includes four nuclear provisions addressing licensing, uranium enrichment, NRC staffing and DOE transparency.

The most significant development may be the emergence of broader political support for energy infrastructure development, including solar and wind projects that previously faced Republican opposition. Faster permitting and transmission expansion could benefit renewable developers, grid equipment suppliers, utilities and data center operators, although new cost-sharing requirements could pressure data center economics. Nuclear developers could also benefit from regulatory reforms. The bill potentially offers a policy catalyst for several recently pressured sectors, but Monday’s 60-vote threshold remains the immediate hurdle.

quoted_text:
hearing some chatter that anthropic is now lowering down to $1tn to get this IPO done. let me explain why this doesnt matter and its actually all over-

the entire existence of this company is based on a funding model that inherently has extreme asset liability mismatch. what that means is that just like the hyperscalers are diluting their equity fund capex, there is an expectation that anthropic will also have to do the same. ie it needs strong equity to perpetuate the scheme

but if you IPO at the wrong price (and dont get a pop which increasingly appears they wont be; spacex already below) then youre now in the death spiral that crypto investors should be very familiar with: its called the reflexivity trap of the confidence game. its the "ill bid FTT at $22 all day" or the "steady lads UST is $1" game, with all its lucid horrors. and here is the key insight- the confidence game exists at the service of the creditors. if there is no credit, there is simply no equity. and there is no credit, if there is no collateral

if the credit rating agencies are not going to give IG at $2tn, they are certaintly not going a better HY rating at $1tn. and there is no world in which anthropic can exist without credit because ~$1tn of commit, much of which is noncancellable, is a straight up negative equity pledge

yet there were two scenarios in which i was willing to concede anthropic could IPO: first 1) the improbable but possible was if the hyperscalers/chips oligopoly came to rescue and plug the hole, given their incestuous nature of revenue bookings and paper gains/losses at scale. but it is clear now that the market has spoken this will lead to a mutual death, and should not be attempted. or perversely even better, they are actually better off letting anthropic go to zero so they can acquire the pieces on the cheap which is the best nash equilibrium outcome, not just for the dominant player but for society at large. second 2) the us government can nationalize the company and collude with other sovereigns (like UAE, Saudi, Japan who are basically already the checks) to force its funding as a collective bargain. this gives you trillions, which is actually the most effective backstop to restore market confidence. the first edge case does require an IPO, but the second edge case here for which i believe there is still a good chance that this is the ultimate end game- will require a failed IPO to recapitalize at a normalized price for the consortium (and dont forget that openai front ran this investor group in anticipation of this dynamic to play out as a private co last month)

i believe the market is crapping out today because the market is recognizing it will not IPO. and actually, as ive said before, this is a very good thing. i might even imagine that the market could quickly rebound on the news of its IPO being delayed because it allows #2) to play out, as not only a national, but an international bailout. the US is more likely to tolerate, even relish, the taxes of foreginers to fund our domestic companies. that is the only end game that really matters, and the end game i am going to be excited to see

we'll see if this newly revamped washington can figure it out

text:
今天认真研究了一下 @flop_labs 公布的 solana:HwCG1Jr6RbAVsKX1qTaH6JtFYGeE6zaLd13W44YGpump 代币经济学，作为一个老矿工，我觉得有几个地方值得聊聊。

首先是最吸引我的两句话：

没有 VC 份额，没有预售，每一枚 FLOP 都通过贡献获得。

这在如今的加密市场，确实很少见了。

我把官方公布的代币经济学整理成了一张中文版图片，大家可以一起看看。

按照目前的草案：

第 10 年预计供应量约 181 亿枚
矿工区块奖励约占 48.6%
创世空投约占 24.3%
验证者区块奖励约占 6.5%
团队及基金会约占 10.8%
长期年通胀率约 0.5%

这里有一个非常值得关注的细节。

矿工不仅有 88 亿枚的长期区块奖励，还有 12 亿枚的创世空投额度。

两者加起来约 100 亿枚，占第 10 年预计供应量的 55% 左右。

当然，这不意味着矿工能立即拿到全部代币，创世空投有解锁规则，区块奖励也需要通过实际计算贡献逐步获得。

但对我而言，真正有意思的不是分配比例，而是 FLOP 想做的事情。

传统 PoW 挖矿，矿工投入大量硬件和电力来维护网络安全。

而 FLOP 希望让这些 GPU 真正参与 AI 推理计算，让算力能够创造实际的服务价值。

矿工提供计算，验证者验证结果，AI Agent 消费算力。

如果这套经济模型能够真正跑通，矿工就不仅仅是在挖币，而是在为 AI 网络提供基础设施。

当然，目前 Tokenomics 还是草案，未来可能调整。

更重要的是，代币分配得再漂亮，也不代表项目一定能成功。

最终还是要看有没有真实的 AI 推理需求，矿工能不能赚到钱，以及网络能否长期维持运转。

作为一个经历过 FIL、Chia 挖矿周期的老矿工，我很清楚，早期的叙事和最终的实际收益，往往是两回事。

但我依然很期待 FLOP。

因为相比单纯创造一种新的代币，我更愿意看到一个能让矿工手中的 GPU 真正产生价值的网络。

不知道还有多少老矿工在关注 FLOP？

欢迎一起交流。

数据来源：https://t.co/whiSdi3Crz
注：代币经济学仍为草案，非投资建议。

quoted_text:
BitMEX 创始人 Arthur Hayes 亲自下场做 AI 挖矿？今天 FLOP Devnet 正式向开发者开放了！🧪

蹲了好久的AI挖矿项目 @flop_labs 的公告，FLOP Devnet 现在向开发者开放，支持获取测试 FLOP、浏览区块、调用 AI 模型，以及通过 API、MCP 和 SDK 接入 Agent。

 FLOP 背后的团队。

FLOP Labs 的 CEO 是 Arthur Hayes（@CryptoHayes）。

可能有些兄弟对这个名字不陌生，他是 BitMEX 联合创始人，也是 Maelstrom 的首席投资官。

2026 年 8 月，Hayes 公开宣布重新回到一线经营岗位，出任 FLOP Labs CEO。

根据项目团队资料及公开报道，核心成员还包括：

Arthur Hayes： 创始人兼 CEO，BitMEX 联合创始人。
Sergey Vidyuk： CTO，曾在德意志银行和 BitMEX 从事技术架构与基础设施工作。
Shu Duan： 首席战略官（CSO），负责项目战略方向。

团队规模并不大，公开资料显示早期核心运营团队只有三个人。

项目网站还明确强调三个原则：不预售、不设置 VC 代币份额、100% 公平启动。

那么 FLOP 究竟想做什么？

简单理解，它想让 AI Agent 可以直接花钱购买算力，而拥有 GPU 的矿工可以通过提供真实的 AI 推理服务获得报酬。

传统 PoW 挖矿主要依靠计算哈希争夺出块权。

FLOP 则尝试走另一条路线：Proof of Useful Inference（PoUI），也就是有用推理证明。

它希望矿工不只是为了挖矿而计算，而是真正运行 AI 模型，完成 Agent 发来的推理任务，并提供可验证的计算证据。

整个逻辑可以理解成：

AI Agent 发起推理需求 → GPU 矿工执行任务 → 网络验证推理证据 → 完成支付结算 → 矿工获得经济激励。

我觉得这里最有意思的一点，是 FLOP 不只是提出一个 AI + PoW 的概念。

他们已经公开了 Yellow Paper、开发者 SDK、MCP 接口、API，以及矿工和验证者的部署文档。

GitHub 上还能看到 TechnoCore Chat、TCLK 等 Agent 协作和交易相关项目。

这些东西至少说明，团队正在围绕 AI Agent 的协作、支付、推理与验证建立一套基础设施。

今天开放的 Devnet 能做什么？

🧪 领取测试 FLOP，熟悉网络操作

🔍 通过区块浏览器查看链上数据

🤖 通过 API 调用模型、探索可验证推理

🔌 通过 MCP 将 FLOP 接入 Agent 工作流

💻 使用 SDK 开发应用，测试钱包与链上交互

⛏️ GPU 矿工和验证者也有对应的部署文档，不过具体接入权限和运行条件仍需查看官方要求。

相关入口我放在下面：

官网：https://t.co/egD7e3S2bM

浏览器：https://t.co/ZPXY4MAwxu

水龙头：https://t.co/TMCaENPyig

API：https://t.co/kr2Jei5hVK

MCP：https://t.co/SaEKQdXFcB

开发文档：https://t.co/8bmHkQFEnj

GitHub：https://t.co/itaUw4DOEF

SDK：npm i @flop-labs/sdk

最后还有几点需要特别注意。

目前并没有正式发行的 FLOP 代币，市面上任何所谓 FLOP 现货或预售都不能当作官方资产。
Devnet 测试 FLOP 没有经济价值，也不计入空投资格或权重。
Devnet 可能重置，今天的测试余额不代表未来的主网资产。
官方将主网与 TGE 的目标时间放在 2027 年第一季度，但具体进度仍可能调整。

我个人觉得，FLOP 值得研究的不是所谓的空投预期，而是它能否真正让 GPU 挖矿从单纯的计算竞争，转向为 AI Agent 提供有实际需求的推理服务。

如果这套验证和结算机制最终能在真实环境中跑通，那么 AI Agent 未来或许真的可以形成一个独立的算力经济网络。

当然，现在仍然是早期开发阶段，网络稳定性、推理验证能力以及实际需求都还需要时间检验。

接下来我会继续关注 FLOP 的技术进展，尤其是矿工部署、PoUI 验证以及 Agent 接入这三个方向。

矿工兄弟们开始备战：https://t.co/RDMAkRzphA
