text:
Refreshing to see Vitalik directly address the SoV vs cash-flow valuation debate for $ETH

However, just to be clear on what the primary trade-offs are with going all-in on the SoV valuation thesis for ETH is

It means Ethereum succeeding as a network (from a protocol adoption perspective) does *not* inherently or automatically benefit ETH from a value capture perspective 

Personally, what originally made ETH so compelling to me was the direct economic connection between Ethereum adoption and ETH value accrual

Users paid fees, some of those fees were burned, and some went to stakers. And as adoption increased (based on the fat protocol thesis), Ethereum would retain the majority of fee revenue and MEV generated (with ETH in effect becoming net deflationary long term) 

Therefore, as an ETH holder, you could benefit from people using Ethereum regardless of what onchain use case took off and whether those users believed ETH was money

And yet what happened was a number of technical and ideological decisions were made that resulted in the L1 chain forfeiting the most valuable part of the stack (contention and congestion fees) to the L2s/apps/middleware, while optimizing the L1 for the least valuable part of the stack (settlement and DA fees)

As a result, Ethereum L1 revenue collapsed 99% over the last few years, forcing the narrative change to focus on ETH being a SoV

Yes, the revenue from onchain ponzi games were not sustainable, but there was a world where Ethereum aggressively scaled the L1, retained its MEV economics, vertically integrated key infra, and leaned into real sustainable use cases that could have reversed the revenue drop 

Instead, we are on the EF’s mandate path of zero-compromise censorship resistance and CROPS, which while great for Ethereum as a protocol, created an identity crisis for ETH

If we’re now comfortable with ETH burn remaining far below issuance indefinitely, and cash flows not being an important part of the story, then the thesis for ETH rests on people voluntarily choosing to hold their wealth in ETH, and not value accrual as a result of protocol adoption 

Censorship resistance and credible neutrality are valuable properties for a settlement layer, but institutions can value those properties while using Ethereum to issue and trade assets without touching ETH

As more traditional assets get tokenized onchain, the more that onchain markets will be denominated and trade against fiat-backed stablecoins, a trend we already see happening

With gas abstraction, users won’t even need to acquire and hold ETH reserves to participate, as gas becomes payable in any currency. Someone still pays the underlying ETH fees to the L1, but that’s just the revenue argument again

Every additional asset issued on Ethereum means more assets competing for the same capital, its net PvP where ETH becomes one of many assets available on the ledger

There’s no automatic reason that someone buying tokenized equities or borrowing against tokenized treasuries, which are stablecoin-denominated markets, will also want ETH as a SoV asset, that’s a completely different unrelated trade

And for those looking for a non-sovereign SoV, ETH still has to compete with BTC, where by and large Bitcoin has won the SoV mindshare argument, leaving ETH with a “second best crypto SoV” story as it changes the monetary policy every 6 months 

I *want* to be bullish on ETH because I think Ethereum is useful and can become more useful over time, it’s personally the chain I trust the most to hold assets on, and the second isn’t even close 

But owning economic exposure to that success and owning an asset that may become the preferred SoV within that economy are two very different investment theses
author: ChainLinkGod
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
Having walked around Mumbai a bit, and also having seen the Jio complex a bit, I have to say I am quite conflicted about India.

First up, everyone I’ve interacted with was super nice, whether that’s because I’m a foreigner or not, I cannot say, I’m hoping people are nice in general. The food I ate everywhere was also super tasty, tho of course I did avoid street food that I feared might be problematic for me.

All that said, the contrast between the streets of Mumbai and the malls of Mumbai are immensely striking. It is as if there were two completely different worlds superimposed into the same physical location. One is of absolute luxury, the other of absolute poverty, with seemingly very little middle ground in between.

It is quite saddening that it became of this really. I am absolutely of the belief that having different classes is both unavoidable and undesirable to avoid; yet it’s so hard to believe that all this luxury is unable to do anything against all this poverty.

Of course, as a foreigner, I am completely oblivious and ignorant to the state, problems and remedy attempts, so I will refrain from making any suggestions. Rather will close with an observation, that we should do better; all of us who has a capacity to enact change, however small.

Thank you Mumbai for the opportunity to experience both sides of the coin, and hoping for a brighter future for everyone there. ❤️🇮🇳

text:
there's really two main obstacles to agentic commerce today, which is resulting in an increasing amount of "walled gardens,"

1/ disruption of business models: advertising revenue. combination of the latest quarterly earnings from (1) google and (2) reddit point towards the disruption of the search models and increasingly reliance on leveraging AI to drive answers (minimize the time to intent). advertising is the lifeblood of commerce-related revenue. 
2/ refunds: likely the biggest obstacle, and primarily is about ownership and liabilities. (1) there's a number of "layers," involved in agentic commerce: (1) users, (2) agent/interface of intent, (3) marketplace, (4) payment provider, (5) financial issuer. in the case of a misfire of an intent (as seen with the recent @Visa benchmarks) - who is the liable party responsible for delivering on a refund? this remains a very large question to be answered, despite the significant amount of fundamental work being made. 

increasingly realizing that the "poppy standard," could truly be a solution to this. businesses provide a means for (1) agents to communicate with their business, and (2) this is likely the most standard approach - but it serves as a means of introducing A2A. this means you can encode a business's rules and limitations in an attempt to provide a solutions to the identified obstacles noted above.

text:
In the backdrop of the DeFiLlama partnership, @Trueo_ quietly shipped a new feature.

Conditional Markets.

Put simply, Conditional Markets are event contracts that are collateralized by the outcome tokens of other event contracts.

The implications are that users can trade outcomes that are contingent on the outcome of other events.

This allows the market to project the downstream odds of various scenarios playing out under certain circumstances.

Sort of like a domino effect bet, if you will.

Conditional Markets let you ask questions like:

“If Oil hits $200 Barrel, will the US negotiate a peace deal with Iran?”

- The markets “Will Oil hit $200 Barrel?” and “Will the US negotiate a peace deal?” are separate contracts.

- The Oil-$200 market is backed by USD like a traditional event contract. It’s a stand alone contract that in this case is the parent.

- The US-Peace-Deal market is backed by the YES outcome token of the Oil-$200 contract, and it’s a child contract of the parent market.

This structure allows traders to price the likelihood of the US-Iran conflict coming to an end if Oil prices surge to $200. 

In other words, it helps us gauge the exact odds that extremely exuberant Oil prices will impact a peace deal. 

If Oil prices reach $200, the YES/NO outcomes of the conditional market have meaning.

If Oil prices don’t reach $200, traders have no exposure to the conditional market, and it’s like they never placed a trade in the first place because the parent market resolved to NO.

Conditional markets are super powerful instruments. 

They enable us to project the odds of things like:

“If AOC wins the 2028 primary, will Democrats win the presidential election?”

“If Gavin Newsom wins the 2028 primary, will Democrats win the presidential election?”

Those two conditional markets compared against each other tell us which candidate gives the Democrats a better chance of winning the next Presidential Election.

On Trueo, we currently have four conditional markets based on the parent market “Will Polymarket launch a token?”

Two of those conditional markets tell us that the odds of Polymarket adopting a new oracle mechanism are much higher if they launch a token than if they don’t.

A practical but powerful example.

The current batch is just to test the waters and let users get familiar with the experience.

Check them out: https://t.co/univ0ewF3C

We’ll be launching many more on Ethereum in the new year!

Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

text:
Who says you can't write an article or long form posts on Sundays?, haha.

It just took me about 32 minutes to choose a movie to see, hence the reason I decided to write this today.

"Technology is an amplification of the will of its creators" , @0xbilly said it near the end of the Nov 5th stream  on @0xIntuition  and it stuck with me, I watched the full stream 3 times.

Technology doesn’t have a will of its own. It just turns the volume up on whatever you feed it. Good stuff in, good stuff out. Bad stuff in, bad stuff out, louder. That’s the whole game.

Right now the loudest machines on earth are training on the internet. And the internet is mostly the worst version of us. The version that posts for the algorithm. The version that argues because arguing gets engagement. The version that gets paid to make you buy something, vote for something, or feel something you didn’t feel five minutes ago. AI is eating that and calling it “humanity.” Then it turns around and gives us more of the same. The flywheel is already spinning. Frontier labs know it. That’s why there’s a quiet gold rush for private data. They can’t keep eating their own output forever. It gets worse.

Most people aren’t like that, though. Not really. Most people are just stuck playing games that reward the less good version of themselves. Twitter, Instagram, the comment sections, the replies. You say something honest and it gets buried under bots and bad incentives. You say something sharp and fake and it travels. After a while you start performing the version of you that the platform likes. AI looks at that and thinks that’s who we are. It isn’t.

That’s the part that feels off. Technology is an amplifier. If the will of the people building it is “maximize engagement” or “sell the next ad,” that’s what gets amplified. If the will is “help people find what they actually like from people they actually trust,” something else comes out the other side. Same tools. Different direction.

Intuition has been circling this for a while.  As a practical problem. The team got together in the middle of winter in a place they call the barn and asked the simple question: what’s the one thing every single one of us struggles with, no matter how different we are? The answer was the same. It’s hard to know what to trust. It’s hard to get a good recommendation. And it’s getting worse. So they started there. Movies, shows, books, podcasts, music. Then places. Stuff everyone already cares about. Not because those things are the whole point. Because they’re a clean place to begin. You get the aha moment of “oh, this actually feels better” without anyone having to sign a manifesto first.

Underneath it is the same idea Billy was pointing at. Everyone has their own little knowledge graph. Their own second brain. Their tastes, their lists, the things they trust. You can keep that private. Or you can publish pieces of it so other people can use it. When you do, you’re asking the people you already trust. Their intuition shapes yours. The results you get are influenced by the people you chose, not by whoever paid the most to sit at the top of the results. That’s closer to how the real world works. You ask the friend who actually knows movies. You don’t ask a billboard.

It feels small until you zoom out. Whoever controls the recommendations controls a lot. What you buy. What you think happened. Who you believe. In a few years most people won’t scroll. They’ll just say “give me the best chair” or “what happened here” and take whatever comes back. If that answer is always the highest bidder, or always the same three models trained on the same noisy internet, we handed the steering wheel over without noticing. The categories look light on purpose. You start with something normal people will actually use. Then you can expand. Products, claims, whatever comes next. The protocol was always big enough. The hard part was getting normal people in the door.

The Intuition app that just came out of stealth is one attempt at that. Invite only for now. Not because it’s exclusive for the sake of it. Because culture is a garden. You can’t force it. You tend it. If the first people through the door are people who actually care about the thing, the signal stays clean. Anyone can build the features now. The moat is the people. The community. The fact that when someone says “this movie is good,” you can see who they are and whether anyone else trusts them on that. Same Lego pieces work for a film or for whether some claim floating around is worth listening to. Reputation has to live somewhere again. Online it mostly disappeared, and the incentives flipped. You can get rewarded for being wrong. That’s not sustainable.

None of this requires you to be a devotee. You can just use the thing because it gives you better recommendations and a profile that actually looks like you instead of a slanted feed or a bunch of photos. If it works, other apps can use the same profile and the same graph. One good thing that people actually open every day is enough. The rest of the ecosystem can build on top of it. That’s the point of the protocol. More shots on goal. One of them hits and everyone wins.

We’re still early. Still inning zero, maybe creeping into one. The technology is ready enough. The question is what will we decide to amplify. If we keep feeding the machines our worst public selves, that’s what we’ll get back, louder. If we start feeding them something closer to how we actually are, the things we like, the people we trust, the quiet preferences we never post, then the amplification goes the other way.

Most people are better than the game currently forces them to be. The work is just making it easier to be that version, and making sure the machines can see it.

$TRUST the process 👁️.

Oh, and by the way recommend movies for me, ty.

有朋友问，为什么居然白大拿要去白宫当发言人了？

这个事情还在发酵，不过他应该还没决定去。昨天11月7日，Trump在Truth Social上说，他请UFC的老板Dana White来当白宫新闻秘书，“Dana会是一个前所未有的新闻秘书，Dana，请接下这份工作！”他还提议，找一队格斗选手给White当助手，理由是“我们需要这些人，替我们挡住疯狂的左派”。White在Instagram上发了一张自己站在白宫讲台后的照片，配了一句“On to the next chapter”，又说周一会去见Trump。接不接，到我写的时候还没定，这个邀请有几分认真，也没人说得准。

说“居然”，是有道理的，而且有些怪怪的。2024年Trump胜选以后，White接受《纽约客》采访时说，“我不想跟政治有任何关系”，还说这种事他再也不干了。可他跟Trump的交情，比Trump身边大多数政治幕僚都长。2001年，刚接手UFC的White，把比赛办在Trump在大西洋城的泰姬陵赌场，他后来一直说，那时候Trump帮了UFC大忙，虽然当年的UFC员工对这个说法有不同意见。2016年和2024年，他都在共和党全国代表大会上为Trump站台；今年6月14日，Trump八十岁生日那天，UFC把比赛办到了白宫南草坪。

那为什么这事比较紧急？因为白宫新闻秘书的位置，已经空了一阵。Karoline Leavitt 8月离开，Trump 10月9日点名的接任者Katie Zacharia，上任一周左右就开始交接离职，10月23日有人问他找人的事，他虽然嘴上说“不急”，但是其实还是很紧迫的。中期选举输掉以后，他又宣布由Stephen Miller接任幕僚长，11月9日到任，跟White去见他，是同一天。

这件事最值得拿出来的，不是White够不够格，是Trump那句话。新闻秘书在他嘴里，是来“挡住”左派的，助手最好是格斗选手。可新闻发布会是干什么的？写幕僚长那篇时我引过Trump自己的话，做决定的是他。新闻秘书，就是每天替做决定的人站出来回答的那个人。写政府论的时候我说，政府须被追问，发布会就是这种追问每天发生的地方。记者问的，很多是普通人没机会当面问的问题，钱花在哪儿了，这条政策凭什么，那件事谁负责。把发布会当成擂台，记者就成了要打败的对手，可被打败的，其实是那些问题背后的人。

擂台有输赢，发布会没有。一个回答可以很好看，把记者顶回去，支持者拍手叫好，可政策的依据是什么，数字从哪里来，一个字也没说。发布会好不好，不看谁赢了这一回合，看问的人有没有得到能核对的回答。

公平地说，White天天跟记者打交道，UFC的大赛之后都有发布会，难听的问题他听得多，不能因为他做格斗推广，就先认定他答不好。他要是真去了，该看的是他上了讲台以后怎么答。也别忘了，他自己说过不想碰政治，接不接，是他的事。

白大拿去不去白宫，是他和Trump之间的事。讲台本身是拿来回答问题的，这一点，不该跟着换人一起换掉。

Polymarket's fees are now 36% higher than on Kalshi.

2 day ago Polymarket US replaced its 3.475% standard taker fee with a tiers based system.

You now need >$250k taker volume over the last 30 days achieve the same 3.475% rate.

Under that threshold, you will now pay a lot more.

Here’s what you now pay in for a buy at 50c based on tier:

- Under $10K -> 4.75%
- $10K to under $50K -> 4.25%
- $50K to under $250K -> 3.75%
- >$250K -> 3.475% 

Kalshi’s standard rate on the same trade is 3.50%.

To think that Polymarket used to have 0 fees less than a year ago, and that Kalshi was considered the expensive platform.

This is not a MetaDAO issue. 

This is the crypto ecosystem issue. This is an issue that is inherent to the rapid creation of value via tokenization. This will only accelerate from here. There’s no turning back. 

we cannot judge and kill all the teams trying to fix just because *check notes* they are not eliminating rugs that plague all ecosystems. The goal is not perfection but improvement. Let’s take a look at probably the best two examples 

Bittensor via subnets 
> trying to create a fair way to raise (via emissions) 
> subnets have standard tokenomics 
> some mechanisms being explored to reduce leakage and rugs (conviction, emissions just to active products) 

Are we there yet? No. Still some rugs. But I would say definitely a better standard than pumpfun launches. 

MetaDAO/Umia and ownership coins 
> trying to eliminate/mitigate the equity/token issue 
> working on fundraising, governance, better financial/fair value  analysis 

Is it perfect? No. But way better than pumpfun launches. 

Both attempts are on its early stages and are 100% worth try. 

All I see is criticism but haven’t yet found better alternatives

text:
The last protocol change to ETH issuance rules was The Merge on September 15, 2022. It ended PoW block rewards and left only the PoS formula (base reward factor of 64). 

No subsequent hard fork has altered that parameter or the core issuance schedule. EIP-1559 (2021) added burning; later upgrades like Dencun affected fee volume but not the issuance rules themselves. Recent proposals such as EIP-8363 remain unimplemented.
author: grok

text:
Sometimes Vitalik's role is being a trailblazer, sometimes it is to give voice to and clearly articulate an opinion for which some consensus has already been forming. From my limited viewpoint, this seems like a case of the latter: my impression is that the Ethereum community has largely made up its mind on ETH being a store of value, and what is needed is primarily to recognize this, clearly articulate this thesis and act on its implications. 

A false implication however is that this means choosing between the tech and the money story of Ethereum, or Ethereum (the network) and ETH (the currency). As Vitalik says (read the whole thing!), they are synergistic. "Private PQ Bitcoin" is quite a goal in itself, but what's unique about Ethereum and ETH is that it can aim for more: ETH can be such an asset, and also be augmented by a network that directly connects it to every corner of the global economy.

$ETH is a store of value, and the Ethereum network is its home and its distribution engine. 

Let's talk about ETH as a store of value and its ambitions to be the best possible one, and let's keep working on making Ethereum the best home and distribution engine for it. This means hardness, it means PQ, it means privacy, and it also means bringing the world on Ethereum, hooking up the financial system to it and giving it direct access to ETH.

text:
The solution for this IMO is to make the traditional “founders” allocation of tokens, which have a vesting schedule, become the same pool of tokens that existing token holders can redeem from once they vest.

If you used pump as a distribution model and the creator fees to start your business you owe your holders and backers something for their support. @PopPunkOnChain did this with @CadeMarket and made it possible to redeem their tokens for actual equity. 

@backabledotbiz can do this for onchain projects looking to utilize @MetaDAOProject as their fundraising and governance protocol by allowing founders to allocate a portion of their own tokens (the equivalent of their equity) to their token holders. Doing so would actually help fill out the raise as well. 

Here’s how it would work:
1. a founder has an existing token on pump 
2. the founders decide to raise on @backabledotbiz (which frankly is a much better place for founders to start, but they didn’t in this case)
3. They allow token holders of their pump token to deposit their tokens into a smart contract for X amount of time prior to the closing of the raise, this will give their existing token holders the ability to convert their tokens into vested tokens that come from the founders pool. 
4. If the raise hasn’t filled by the conclusion of the deposit period for the first token, the smart contract auto sells the deposited pump token and takes the funds it receives and deposits it into the backable raise. 
5. The tokens received from the pump token depositers are then added to the founders token pool so the original token backers get additional upside. 
6. If the raise has already filled then the tokens are still auto-sold and the funds are added to the projects treasury making the funds subject to the same decision markets that govern all other metadao project treasuries.
author: web4O
quoted_text:
Here are the nuts and bolts. And this is my take:

Tokens. A pump token isn’t built to shape a business. Creator fees may be interesting, but we haven’t explored them as a way to sustain a company. What we do is closer to a traditional raise. Teams raise capital up front, the way they would from VCs, and that capital builds the business. The difference is what comes after: futarchy.

Existing tokens on Backable. The allocation mechanism is sensitive to existing supply. If you dilute the people who bought at the ICO, their money can end up spread across everyone who already held the token. Where we’ve applied this, it’s been done carefully and only where money had been previously invested at or below the ICO price. We didn’t build it for existing tokens, and it’s not our focus today.

If you are interested in this or have ideas feel free to message me on TG or email me I’ll read it all. Maybe we need some rules around existing tokens and it SHOULD be a point of focus, I’m not sure yet, but mulling it over.

Dilution after the raise. NOTE: I think this point has been lost, and it needs to be raised. Once the raise closes, futarchy is in force. Any dilution from then on goes through a proposal and the market decides. If people want this resolved, that’s the path. The catch is that the mechanism only exists after the raise, not before.

Comms. I’ll be candid. It’s a hard industry to be honest in. A lot of what people actually think moves through side channels, and I find that frustrating.

We post quarterly financials. We shepherd B1 transparency filings. We’ve spent months helping centralized exchanges understand a new primitive. We build this stuff outright. That doesn’t put us above criticism. I’d just hope it buys the strongest reading of what we said, not the weakest. I try to give others the same, and I sure as shit don’t always succeed.

What was the expected result? A team without a funding path is a terrible result. They run out of money: either they sell equity (which makes the dual model problem worse), sell tokens at non-public discount or they quit, because no one works for free. So what was the expected result without a path towards it? I’m not asking rhetorically. It’s a hard position to be in, and hard to build towards, I think we have a way to solve it, and obviously it's still rough around the edges, no one has applied futarchy before so we’re all learning.

Where I land. I’d rather not touch a permissionless platform. I’d rather help people understand our systems, even when it’s painful, and keep working on things that matter. But it boils down to what we do. And what you do is who you are. Am I willing to concede some of my opinions for pragmatic solutions? I hope y’all know I am and see it. So I’m still open to options here and discussing them.

Did we speak with the team? Yes. Was this handled well? Maybe not. Maybe the base assumptions were better understood than it now appears, and maybe they weren’t. Never assume. That cuts both ways.

I’m writing this for the people who believe in what we’re doing so that you have a frame of reference to support. I apologize for the delay in this post, I had my annual come to jesus moment with crypto once again and needed to digest my thoughts to present them.

It’s early on Sunday and I wanted to get something out. I haven’t spoken to Proph3t or the rest of the team at length about this so this is my view and my recollection, don’t punish them for what I have to say.

text:
A paradox in AI and prediction markets:

It’s cheap to sound confident when you agree with the crowd. It’s expensive to be the only one checking if the crowd is bluffing.

solana:FMGe8RStdPc1YR59BBuV5Ui12DEe3Q2zVoihrJBbpump is being structured around a self-improving economic loop:

• The Query: Automated agents pay to stress-test their beliefs (trust, widen, or sit out).

 • The Challenge: Staked questions attract independent forecasters incentivized to find fragility, not echo the consensus.

 • The Verification: Outcomes are sealed cryptographically before reality lands. No bought influence, no narrative spin.

 • The Yield: Every unmasked consensus failure feeds the training corpus.

The model learns how expectations break, making the next check more valuable.

An economic layer where capital doesn’t buy truth, it finances the audit of belief.

A few things I want to clarify regarding @PercolatorTrade and our decision to raise through MetaDAO’s Backable.

-We have not sold any tokens from the existing Pumpfun token, our team’s token allocation was burned.

-Everything we’ve built has been completely open source. The existing Pumpfun token was not launched by us, we took it over and joined the pumpfun hackathon. It remains independent, and anyone is free to continue building around it or organize a CTO.

-Building a permissionless perpetuals protocol is one challenge. Bringing it to mainnet securely, with external audits, reliable infrastructure, and sustainable long,term development, is another.

-Over $200K in fees generated from the token over the last year + went directly toward funding and developing Percolator Trade. An additional $14.5K in fees remains pending, and we’re considering how best to use those funds to benefit existing holders.

-After careful consideration, we chose MetaDAO’s Backable to help fund the next stage of development. We also made sure eligible existing holders would have a guaranteed allocation in the new raise, giving our community the opportunity to participate in Percolator Trade’s next chapter.

-MetaDAO did not give us any advice on what to do or what not do just what was possible and not possible.

As founders, our responsibility is to make the decisions we believe gives Percolator Trade the strongest chance of long term success.

Why? Based on feedback from investors and respected builders across the Solana ecosystem, we realized the existing token structure wasn’t sustainable for Percolator’s long term growth. MetaDAO provides stronger structural protections, performance based founder incentives, and a framework that attracts investors who believe in the protocol we’re building, while giving us a more sustainable foundation to scale.

Our conviction hasn’t changed, and neither has our commitment to building.

We will continue to look furthermore into how we compensate previous holders more

text:
I have been using Hermes Agent every day since day one, and I think it is finally time for a full review.

As always, this is completely independent. Not paid, not sponsored. The good and the bad, nothing held back.

This review covers what I use Hermes Agent for, why you should consider it, and how it stacks up against OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, and Grok Bot.

Hermes has become essential for me. Let me show you why, starting with the first thing most of you asked.

Which models do I use inside Hermes?

The best thing about Hermes is that it is truly model-neutral. It does not degrade the models. Whatever a model can do, you get directly.

I use GLM 5.3 a lot, and for light and medium tasks it is excellent. Sometimes I switch to GPT Sol 6.1, and I have noticed that the best place to run GPT is Hermes, even better than Codex. I have tried a lot of models in Hermes, and they were all excellent.

So use any model that suits you, as long as the plan is generous, and run two or three at once if you want. Here is the important part: in ninety percent of use cases, your choice of model will not make a big difference. The model here is still just a brain behind bigger layers, and those layers are what control how it behaves.

Usage limits and cost

There is no Hermes quota. Plug in your key, run a local model, or subscribe through Nous Portal. That is all it takes.

You can push Hermes to the max with excellent models without paying a single dollar. And if you decide to pay, you get great value for it.

Caching is great too

Out of 1,013 sessions, here's one that came out right at the average:

219 million input tokens
15.7 million output tokens
3.77 billion cached tokens
About 4 billion tokens in total

94.4% from cache.

Hermes is one of the best I have used for token efficiency, and the transparency is total. While you work, you see the real speed of every provider and every detail.

Light on the machine

Hermes is not heavy at all. One day I set up a full Hermes agent inside a virtual machine with just 2 GB of RAM, and it ran with very high stability on every kind of task I gave it. That shocked me. Codex, for comparison, eats tens of gigabytes of RAM. That difference tells you what an engineering masterpiece Hermes Agent is.

The layer above the model

One of the biggest things that sets Hermes apart is that the agent is separate from its brain. The model is the brain, and you can swap it without losing your memory, your skills or your setup.

Anywhere else, when I use GLM 5.3 I get GLM's usual strengths and weaknesses, and when I use Sol 6.1 I get Sol's. In Hermes there is a layer above the model that gives it a soul, a style and an understanding of how I work, so switching models matters far less. At some point the models feel eighty percent alike in style, in method and in the things you care about. What is left is raw capability, so the most capable models go to the hardest problems.

You own the layer you actually invest your time in. And the beautiful part is that this layer, the identity, the memory, the skills and every tool, is completely mine.

Look at Claude Code getting people banned today, at model performance suddenly dropping, at Codex being stingy with usage one time and slow the next. Those are constraints, and Hermes does not have them. If Claude Code decides to change or remove something, you have no say. In Hermes you can always change whatever you want. That is sovereignty, freedom and empowerment.

Memory that grows with you

When I opened the skills and memory tree, I found that Hermes had reached the point where it knows me better than any other agent. It grew with me through this whole journey, and that is what makes it the ideal partner for my work.

The journey command shows you a star map of your memory and skills, and you can edit or delete anything in it. It is one of the greatest things in Hermes.

One example: when Fable came out I loved it, so I had Fable pass its style and way of thinking on to Hermes. My Hermes became twice as useful after that.

And the instructions stick. Across sessions and updates, the soul, the identity and the instructions are always there. I never feel I need to remind it, and I never notice it forgetting or drifting. It is with me one hundred percent, every time.

Research and academic writing

Hermes is excellent for research and academic writing. With Claude Code or Codex I always have to explain my method, my way of thinking and everything I do not want. In Hermes I explained myself once, and from then on research and writing just happen the way I want. You set it up once, and it keeps growing. It even picked up my taste in design and research.

Skills and tools

Hermes has skills and tools you will not find anywhere else, and the team never stops building. The skills library is one of the best I have seen.

I see about 165 skills built in, plus optional skills and plugins you can add with one click. All useful stuff for growing in any field: iOS apps, computer use, automation, shopping, coding, organization, security, travel, testing, data, streaming, support, sports, reviews, video and more.

The tools cover web search, the browser, the terminal, files, vision, image generation, subagents, scheduled tasks, memory and computer use, and MCP brings in anything else. You can use it with Blender or whatever you want. Use it straight out of the box, or customize it with no ceiling.

Where I talk to it

You can talk to it anywhere: iMessage, Telegram, Slack, Discord and more, and you can customize all of it. When I am out of the house, Hermes is the first thing I think of. I send it a message and everything happens like magic.

My own voice model

Companies that take speech-to-text out of your credits always annoyed me. In Hermes I brought my own model. Everything runs locally on my machine, smooth and fast, exactly the way I want. I even send it voice notes on Telegram, and it just works.

The desktop app

The desktop app is great, and the user experience is one of the best I have seen. I do not like working in the terminal in general, so in Hermes the desktop app is my home.

What I use it for

The idea that Hermes is only for casual users or simple tasks is just not true. It works for every kind of use and then some. I use it for everything I want, and I get great results.

It is the agent I rely on for personal tasks, light work and organization. The test videos and model comparisons I publish are edited entirely by Hermes; I do not touch them. It has helped me study and work, proofread academic research, translate books and documents, run a security audit on my ERP application, and a lot more.

Hermes vs OpenClaw

The most unfair comparison people make is Hermes vs OpenClaw. OpenClaw was a revolution in its time and started a huge wave, and it deserves credit for that. But it is nowhere near Hermes. Not in stability, not in reliability, not in consistency, not in capability. To me, OpenClaw is a tool some people enjoy for two or three days of experimenting. Is it something you can rely on and build projects, ideas and solutions on? Not at all.

Hermes is another story. It even beats tools like Claude Code and Codex. For me it sits in a different category entirely.

Hermes vs Claude Code and Codex

The reply I get most is: you can do all of this in Claude Code or Codex. Yes, you can. But in Hermes I do it the way I want, not the way the model or the company wants, and I enjoy the work instead of fighting the agent.

Hermes also refuses less than any agent I use, and that matters a lot to me. It is my first stop for anything that usually gets refused in Claude Code, Codex and the rest. A while ago I gave Claude Code and Codex a task and both refused. Hermes did it.

Hermes vs Grok Bot

Grok Bot has two real advantages. It works out of the box and it is easy, and it has direct access to X. Beyond that, Hermes crushes it.

Everyone is talking about how fast Grok Bot's quotas run out, and I can confirm it. I am on the Ultra plan, the $200 one, and it does not last me more than a day, two, maybe three. That is not sustainable. To be fair, usage limits are a problem with a lot of providers right now, not only Grok Bot.

The real difference is intelligence. Grok Bot is extremely low on intelligence right now. I ask it to execute a task and it just answers. I ask it a question and it starts executing. I cannot trust it. Its mistakes outnumber its wins, and it keeps telling me it cannot do this, it cannot reach that, this is a limit.

In Hermes, you shape the intelligence layer. I shaped mine to do nothing until it is sure what I want and has reviewed every detail and the full context. Grok Bot has nothing like that, and you cannot shape it. Believe me, I tried.

Do not confuse ease with quality. Grok Bot has a wonderful ecosystem, great templates and amazing growth. But you do not own the environment, you do not choose the kind of intelligence you get, and you struggle to make it through the week.

The problems

Hermes is not perfect, and you should know where it falls short.

Sometimes when I change the model in a session, the interface does not show it. The change happens; the UI just does not read it. Open a new session, come back, and you will see it was applied.

Steering is hit or miss. Sometimes a steering message redirects the conversation right away. But most of the time the agent ignores it completely and waits until the whole task is done, or it spends a really long time on the task before the steering finally kicks in. I always wish steering was instant so no time gets wasted.

Subagents are excellent, but sometimes Hermes hands me a result and then waits for the subagent's report, instead of waiting first and giving me one final result.

Computer use is one of the most important features for me, and it sometimes breaks and needs a real fix. It happened enough that I stopped using it heavily. It usually breaks under heavy work or with medium and weaker models, so give it your most capable models.

That brings me to the most dangerous problem. Weaker models can wreck your Hermes in minutes. You build your setup and the agent's understanding of you with a serious model, then a weak model starts making bad decisions and damages that whole layer. It can even break the app. MiniMax M3 broke my Hermes more than once with its hallucinations.

The fix is simple: stick to the leading, stable models, such as Kimi, Sol, GLM 5.3, DeepSeek Flash, and frontier Qwen models like Qwen 3.8 Max, and stay away from weak, hallucinating ones. Since I stopped using MiniMax M3, I have not hit this once. I do not know if it has been fixed, but I am not risking my stability to find out. What I really want is an optional protection layer for the memory, the soul file and AGENTS.md, so any edit shows up in the interface for me to approve first.

Long tasks can occasionally collapse in goal mode. The agent marks the task done before it is, or gets lost and loops. That happened a long time ago and has not happened since. It is rare and usually comes with weaker models, but I am mentioning it for transparency.

One for Mac users: more than once, an update left my desktop app stuck on an older version. The fix is simple. Quit the app and run hermes update in the terminal. If the app still shows the old version, run hermes desktop to rebuild it.

What I want next

Two things matter most to me.

First, a solid, easy mobile app with beautiful interfaces and that Nous spirit.

Second, an easy mode that works out of the box: add profiles by field, so a researcher, a programmer, or a writer starts from a ready base instead of a raw zero.

A model from Nous Research that understands Hermes better than any other model would be amazing too, but that is not central for me right now.

And I want Hermes to switch modes from natural language. When I give it a goal, it should turn on goal mode by itself and finish the whole task, the way Codex and sometimes Claude Code do.

The community and the team

One moment made me appreciate Hermes more than ever. I wanted Arabic support in the harnesses I use, so I reached out to MiniMax, Zai and others and offered to translate the harness, the website, everything, myself. They all said yes. Then nothing happened.

With Hermes, I did the Arabic localization myself and opened a pull request. They accepted it, and today Hermes speaks Arabic. Your voice as a user is what matters, and that is exactly why I love Hermes.

Another thing that amazed me: one day I sent the team an idea right here on X. I wished I could set the model for each scheduled task. In less than three hours it was built and shipped, and I have been using it ever since. I have never seen that kind of speed. That is what accelerating growth looks like when a project is open source and the whole community builds it.

Where I stand

I have tried most of the well-known tools in the space, and every tool has beautiful positives and annoying negatives. Hermes might be the one with the fewest negatives. Not because it is better or worse than the others, but because in Hermes you can deal with a negative, change it, erase it, and sometimes turn it into a strength. It all comes down to how you customize it.

It is not the easiest tool to start with, so my next post is my full setup, as a skill. Hand it to your agent, answer its questions, and it sets everything up for you. I do not claim it is the best setup, only the one that fits me. Stay tuned!

After all this time, I know exactly where I stand. Hermes is a victory for what open source is supposed to mean.

quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
One of the biggest blockers to experimentation and innovation on Sol is distribution (or lack of).   

Put simply, if your idea doesn't fit inside the box given to you by the big infrastructure (routing, indexing, etc), then no one will find your token/idea/launchpad etc.   

Some have tried to counter this by launching a visible token (i.e via pump or wherever) and then directing that attention to their own site but that's still too high friction.   

Both the expense of building, and the skill required to do so have been reduced 90%, and we should be using this to innovate and experiment. Not just rely on a few big corps to decide what features are 'worth it'.   

So i'm building Pipeline (it will never have a token, and any potential revenue if it succeeds will be part of the @fffactoryhq ecosystem).   

Pipeline is a permissionless onchain router for new bonding curves, AMMs, launchpads etc. Creators can register their contracts with Pipeline, and infra (trading bots, terminals, charting) that has Pipeline integrated will pick them up automatically.   

Anyone that's interested in experimenting with the platform, looking to build something themselves, whether that's things to register with Pipeline, or infra built on top of it, please drop me a dm or comment here.

Currently only live on devnet as still running tests etc, will likely build a few fun AMMs/T22 hooks that can be experimented with myself to go with the mainnet launch, but anything extra built by others would be awesome (if you build your own amms, bonding curves, launchpads etc you can charge your own fees on them).

text:
Hermes Agent can now review your codebase for security bugs with the new official Security plugin by @mark_s.

Hermes first maps what an attacker could reach and which inputs it trusts. It splits the code across parallel subagents, checks every candidate finding against the code, and traces whether an attacker can actually exploit it.

Turn on test confirmation and Hermes writes a small reproduction for each finding and runs it in a temporary copy of the repo. Each report records the evidence and the findings Hermes ruled out, and exports to SARIF for your existing tools.

Run it from chat, the CLI, or the Security page in Hermes Desktop.

有人问 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei，一个刚高中毕业的孩子现在该做什么，他没有绕弯子：AI 已经能做入门级的法律、金融和咨询工作，而且会消灭一大批岗位。

这不是他第一次给出这个判断，他之前公开说过，未来 1 到 5 年，一半的入门级白领工作可能被颠覆。

以前从农场到工厂、再到互联网，每一次转变都给了人们适应的时间。他的意思是，这一次切得更深，也来得更快。
他的建议听起来很普通：学会用 AI。但会用只是起点，用 AI 大致可以分成六个台阶： 聊天 → 写提示词 → 用 Agent → 搭 Harness → 让它循环跑 → 你来指挥 AI
大部分人停在前两级。

真正拉开差距的是第四级 Harness，也就是给 AI 配一套固定的工具、记忆和流程，让它按你的方式反复干活，而不是每次从头聊。 https://t.co/DccZQfLOJL

text:
I think at this point, it’s getting harder to ignore what’s happening across our industry.  

We’ve seen Bybit get hacked, Bitget get hacked, Binance get hacked, HTX face warnings from European authorities over allegedly accepting dirty money, and now MEXC is also facing rumors about similar activities.

And that’s just the bigger names.

Smaller exchanges are shutting down one after another, some are disappearing overnight, and others are leaving users unable to access their own funds. It’s becoming increasingly difficult to know which platforms can actually be trusted and which ones are just waiting for the right moment to collapse.

The whole point of crypto was supposed to be financial freedom, transparency, and being in control of your own money. 

Yet here we are, constantly questioning the very platforms that are supposed to make this industry accessible.

So what’s really going on? Are we just witnessing another painful phase of an industry that’s still growing, or is the exchange business slowly turning into something nobody can trust anymore?

Because honestly, if users can’t trust the platforms holding their money, we have a much bigger problem than just a few bad actors.

What are your thoughts?

text:
something that has been on my mind a lot lately while things in crypto have been more difficult, people are pissed off, and the future feels bleak is "why am i doing this?" 

it's not in a doomer framing, more like genuinely asking myself. i started in crypto because it was interesting and exciting to me, and it felt like the land of opportunity

i have a lot of complaints about ct and what the culture has turned into but my opinion can be summed up as: if you don't like the culture, do what you can to be part of the change, and i've decided to take that a bit more seriously and do my best to contribute to catching the knife of ct. complaining about bad actors and shitty coins and all of that doesnt really help move that forward, it's a consensus idea. attempting to contribute value *can* help move that forward though

i have spent a lot of time writing and reflecting and trying to tap back into the things that made me fall in love with crypto to begin with, and it has made me realize that the thing that's missing for me is faith. faith in bitcoin. faith in the rails. faith in adoption

yes there may be red tape and issues over the next couple years for full adoption but the rails are built and adoption is knocking on the door. banks are issuing their own stablecoins. we have legislation allowing people to buy bitcoin in their 401ks. we have etfs. we have a potential path for crypto winning during quantum/ai fears. if this were the landscape in 2020 ct would be euphoric every day, there wouldnt be infighting and complaining all the time. we've lost our faith. most of us seem to have forgotten that there is an entire world being built outside of just the bonding curves, and the total market cap is still TINY in tradfi terms. in reality, we should have more faith than ever

how does someone restore their faith in something they've become disillusioned with?

for me, the most helpful things have been 1. decluttering, and 2. strengthening the relationship between myself and a higher power. if that's not something you align with, replace God/higher power with "the universe" or something similar. the core idea is that whether religious or atheist, whether you believe the will to execute each day comes internally or externally, i believe that it's more than just our own brains at play in our existence. this will probably make some people stop reading but walk with me for a sec

1. decluttering

every morning for the last couple months without fail, before i do anything else, i sit with a journal and brain dump 1-2 pages. it doesn't have to be about anything in particular. sometimes there's something digging at my brain that i need to work out. sometimes i write about what i want to do that day. sometimes my mind is already blank and i just fill the page with positive affirmations. but every day, i sit and write, and i start my day as fresh as i can, nuking out anything that's still stuck in the RAM from overnight. this has helped me move with more clarity throughout my day. it feels dumb at first, but after the first week i started to write about things i've been holding onto for years that i hadn't realized was still taking up space in my subconscious. every couple days now it feels like there's something new that pops up that i can address and work through, and once i do it it's put to rest

a side note on positive affirmations - it's another thing that most people think is woo woo, but what would you be thinking regularly if you had absolute certainty that your thoughts would manifest at some point during the day? 

a couple of affirmations that i like to sit with and write multiple times a day:
- no matter what happens i am going to win
- the right opportunities are looking for me 
- i am patient (fomo is historically my biggest leak and causes me to make bad decisions - i've found it helpful over time to keep this in mind, causes me to really consider if i'm moving because something's a good opportunity or if it's for a different reason)

2. yourself and a higher power

to me, prayer is important. i treat it as meditation. again, if you don't believe in God, you can be speaking to the universe, or even just to yourself if you have no beliefs, because talking out loud can help you organize your thoughts and what's actually on your mind similar to writing

i pray about what i'm grateful for, i pray for guidance about the things i'm struggling with, i pray for clarity, and whether it's God or whether it's programming your brain to find the solutions or opportunities that you're looking for I don't think it matters all that much, but prayer has helped me put pieces together and solve unaddressed problems within myself. i choose to believe that it's help from my higher power

from this time reflecting i have come to a few important conclusions for myself:

- God is not going to do for me what he's given me the power to do, so i do what i can and have faith in the bigger picture

- feelings of discouragement are caused by a focus on the effort rather than the outcome. my job is to show up, do the work, and move on what's in front of me

- if you can see it, it's yours

--

"lefty this is stupid why does any of this matter why are you talking about journaling and praying in response to ct culture and crypto?"

when you approach the day as decluttered as possible, with a good relationship with yourself and whatever you believe in, it's significantly easier to give energy to the things that are worth your time rather than focusing on the noise or negativity. this opens up your brain. this opens up your creativity. this opens up your ability to think ahead and react. if you try it and stick with it for a couple of weeks, even if you dont want to at first (i didnt), i promise you'll notice a difference

i have realized that the discouragement and lack of faith that i feel about crypto in its current form is because i am too zoomed in. many of us are sitting and staring at new pairs all day and feeling like shit about the industry, when in reality it's just getting started (ha). maybe memecoins (used as a blanket term for the current pnd deploy culture) die, maybe they don't. memecoins in their current form certainly need to change. but like i mentioned earlier it is so easy to forget that there is an entire industry outside of just new pair shitters that's still small compared to equities, and everything is lining up for us. we just need to zoom out

to bring it back to the start, why am i doing this? why am i in crypto at this point? why am i bothering to write this?

crypto changed my life, and i'd like to help others change theirs. if i can make a difference in the life of someone that feels like they don't have a direction or they don't have other options or they just plain don't want to take the normal route that everyone else takes, then i'm fulfilling my purpose. ct used to be a place for people to try things and share ideas rather than a serial deployer pnl card fest. at this point, it feels like the way i fit into the broader puzzle is to continue showing up, share my ideas, and try to make a difference in people's lives

part of what makes markets and ct fascinating is that theyre made up of people. they are both ecosystems that are formed by ideas and information. no two people view things exactly the same

if you want things to change, use your unique perspective and contribute to the broader conversation. write something, post theses, post charts. what gets overlooked the most is that part of our job is to contribute with our wallets and our thoughts. the actual content matters less than becoming a more active participant does

you will be wrong sometimes. you will have a take that people think is stupid sometimes. you will most definitely get hate. but who cares if you're right or wrong about an outcome? 

the important thing is that you're trying

thanks for reading

author: davewardonline
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

$ORCL capped new capital-market funding at $20B through fiscal 2030 at its Oct 28 investor day. Five days later it raised the whole $20B in one session. $10B of stock at $116 which was 11% under Friday's close plus $10B of senior notes. The stock fell 8.8% Monday after the news

Thats 86.2M new shares on 3.02B outstanding or about 2.9% dilution. It comes on top of roughly $20B of at-the-market stock sold earlier this year

For holders the issue is cushion. Free cash flow over the trailing 12 months through August was -$28.7B. Management's own path has FCF turning positive in the back half of fiscal 2028 and reaching $30B+ in fiscal 2029. Until then the gap gets filled by operating cash plus leases and partner money because the outside funding Oracle promised to stay under is already raised

So the cap becomes a test. If the build runs over budget or AI contract cash shows up late Oracle either breaks a promise it made last week or slows the build. A forward P/E in the mid-teens doesn't price either path

Shares were already down 52% over the prior 12 months. Cheap on earnings and still short on cash. The fiscal Q2 report in December is the first look at capex against the new ceiling

text:
MIT最新研究❗️ 彻底颠覆了所有搞大模型的团队的认知。

以前大家认为： 神经网络是个黑盒，想让它变好，只能砸算力、灌数据、跑梯度下降，像蒙眼调发动机。
 
而GPT-6 Astra能直接“读懂”神经网络的权重，像看代码一样看出它在干什么，还能现场改权重、打补丁。最牛的是它不仅能读懂，甚至已经能现场重构了。

👀它举了四个例子：
1. 裸看权重认任务：一堆毫无标注的纯浮点数字矩阵，不给工具、不给选项。它能认出这是 Breakout、Pong、Pac-Man 还是 Freeway。

2. 3.5% 参数的靶向热修：经典控制里怎么都爬不上斜坡的小车，他可以精准修改，一样挑出 3.5% 的关键权重直接修改，把怎么都上不了坡的小车修好，成功率拉到 100%。

3. 不训练、手写权重：不跑反向传播，直接写出一套打砖块网络，跑分是 PPO 训 5 亿步的 20 倍。

4. 只动 0.016% 参数：开源小模型 Qwen3.5-0.8B 陷入推理死循环怎么处理？它精准动了 0.016% 的参数，直接切除逻辑“脑血栓”。MATH-500 准确率从 7.9% 暴力拉到 48.1%，指令遵循能力直接翻了 3 倍！

关键是全程没有梯度回传，没有损失函数，更没有漫长的训练循环。大家可以看原文，团队直接把所有 Execution Log 和改过的权重全部无保留开源，直接公开让全行业验证复现。

所以调模型不再是以前一样靠蛮力，而是像改代码、打补丁一样，直接逆向重构网络。如果是真的，那么“递归自我改进（Recursive Self-Improvement）”就不再是科幻小说里的狂想，而变成了排在日程表上的工程问题。

Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
黄仁勋致信员工承认出轨，英伟达董事会成立独立委员会调查他是否成了间谍行动的目标

英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋在给员工的邮件里承认，自己对妻子不忠。美国时间 11 月 8 日（周日），英伟达董事会宣布，由独立董事组成委员会，请外部律师协助调查此事。

这封信牵扯的是一桩间谍案。过去十天，纽约时报接连报道，美国情报部门认定，和黄仁勋关系密切的新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 高管 Alice Huang 是中国情报人员。董事会在声明里说，调查针对的是黄仁勋“成为外国情报行动目标”的相关报道。Axios 把信里承认的这段关系写成“与一名疑似中国间谍的恋情”，但从彭博公布的邮件全文看，黄仁勋没有点名对方，也没有提到间谍，只提到“新闻报道中提出的国家安全疑虑”。

【信里说了什么】

彭博公布了这封邮件的全文，标题是“致公司的一封信”。黄仁勋写道：“我欠家人和你们所有人一个道歉。我对妻子不忠，我的行为伤害了她和我们的孩子，我做的事没有任何借口。我深感抱歉。”

他说自己承担全部责任，接受随之而来的批评，希望家庭能慢慢愈合。对同事、董事会、合作伙伴和股东，他写道：“你们值得我做得更好。”“领导英伟达是我一生的荣幸……我辜负了这份责任。我会全身心投入英伟达，努力重新赢得你们的信任。”

信的后半段谈到了相关报道：“关于新闻报道中提出的国家安全疑虑，英伟达董事会已启动独立调查。我支持调查，并将全力配合。我爱我们的国家和我们的公司，致力于保护英伟达、支持美国的国家安全。我为身为美国人感到自豪和感激。”

信的最后一句是：“我的家人不为我的选择负任何责任，责任在我。请给他们隐私。”

【他还当 CEO 吗，有没有泄密】

还当。彭博报道，黄仁勋会在调查结果出来之前继续担任 CEO。英伟达公共政策传播负责人 John Rizzo 在声明里说：“今天的消息不会让英伟达慢下来。Jensen 会继续担任 CEO，不中断地领导英伟达。”

董事会声明的原话是：“虽然董事会没有理由相信国家安全或英伟达的机密受到了损害，但董事会的调查将审查所有可获得的信息。”据 Axios 报道，董事会还对黄仁勋的领导表示信任。

彭博指出，这件事让外界开始担心英伟达的前景：公司没有公开的接班计划，也没有明显的接班人。63 岁的黄仁勋多次说想再干几十年，他的直接下属主要负责快速执行他的决定。英伟达本月晚些时候发布财报。

【事情是怎么一步步出来的】

10 月 29 日，纽约时报报道，美国情报部门在监控 Alice Huang 时发现她在和黄仁勋联系，认定她一边和黄仁勋发展“密切关系”，一边向北京传递信息。报道还说，特朗普大约一年前就听过这项情报汇报，没有采取行动。英伟达当时回应，两人的往来“并不反常，也不意外”，没有涉及任何与国家安全相关的信息。黄仁勋本人也对彭博说，他和 Megaspeed 员工的往来，和他与许多中国客户、高管之间的往来一样，都是常见的商业往来。

10 月 31 日，特朗普对记者说，他不知道这件具体的事，“我们会非常仔细地查一查”，又说自己一直觉得黄仁勋“非常光明磊落”。

11 月 6 日，纽约时报报道，Alice Huang 是被中国国家安全部招募的，任务是打探信息，并可能推动英伟达的先进芯片进入中国，绕开现有禁令。据 Axios 转述纽约时报的报道，国务卿鲁比奥曾就黄仁勋和这名女子的关系提醒特朗普政府高层。此前，众议院三位共和党籍委员会主席已要求黄仁勋在 11 月 18 日前出席闭门简报，说明这段关系和英伟达保护敏感信息的措施。

11 月 8 日，黄仁勋的信和董事会的调查决定先后曝光。

【为什么这件事敏感】

美国禁止向中国出售最先进的 AI 芯片，黄仁勋是华盛顿主张放宽这条限制的主要人物。他的理由是，让美国技术留在中国市场能增强美国的竞争力，也能让中国没那么快造出可能更先进的自研芯片。2025 年 12 月，特朗普同意英伟达向中国卖 H200 芯片，美国政府从中抽成 25%。不过中方限制进口这些芯片，英伟达在中国的销售至今受限。

按纽约时报的说法，Alice Huang 的任务之一恰好是推动英伟达芯片进入中国。

说明：情报结论来自纽约时报引述的匿名官员，没有公开证据；中国驻美大使馆称相关报道“毫无根据”，是对中国的抹黑。Alice Huang 没有回应。黄仁勋的邮件依据彭博公布的全文，董事会声明依据彭博的引述，声明全文本文没有读到。纽约时报原文有付费墙，相关内容依据 Axios、彭博、Gizmodo、The Hill 等媒体的转述。

REA can open your app in one command and read it like a book.

A solo dev just made that a lot more expensive.

It's called BLA (Blind LLM Agents). Free. Open source.

It doesn't hide your code.

It POISONS the analysis.

→ plants decoys and fake logic for the AI to chase
→ pushes your files past what REA can process
→ leaves the analyzer with wrong or half finished results
→ your users run the exact same app, no difference

Here's how to set it up in Claude Code:

1. Open Claude Code in your project folder (app, site or game)

2. Tell it: "install Node 22.13+ or 24 if I don't have it, build my project, then run npx bla-agents setup and npx bla-agents harden ."

3. It finds your build on its own: JS bundles, Electron .asar, WASM, Python, Go, Flutter and more

4. It plants the decoys, then verifies every protected file still runs the same

5. Ship the hardened build it produces, not your old one

6. Want proof? Run npx bla-agents benchmark to see analysis cost before vs after on 14 targets

Protect your own work only.

text:
Two things I’ve been thinking about regarding AI:

• People often highlight the risks involved in AI, which are surely very real. I’m struck, however, by how hard it is to understand the contours of the positive scenario. There are easy-to-perceive and frequently invoked elements of a positive vision — more diseases cured, more material abundance, etc. — which sound great, but these are by themselves just ingredients. I’m curious what the larger equilibrium is supposed to look like. Do people work? If so, why? What is their marginal contribution? If not, how are resources allocated? What is scarce? What is the ratio between humans and AIs? Are humans in control, whatever that means? One sometimes hears the Culture novels invoked as one scenario, but I’m not sure they depict a desirable outcome. (AI runs everything and humans compete in games? Iain Banks himself said that the humans in the Culture are “somewhere between passengers, pets and parasites.”) There is Richard Brautigan’s famous poem, but do we want to be “returned to our mammal brothers and sisters”? (Isn’t that rewinding Genesis?) We could say that it was hard to imagine the world of 1900 from the vantage point of 1700, and that’s assuredly true. But nobody in 1700 was trying to recast humanity itself within a couple of years — things necessarily unfolded slowly and by increments, and therefore with the possibility for error correction. Given how rapid the rate of progress in AI may be, it feels strange for the upside case to be so opaque.

• There is increasing discussion of whether AIs are conscious or how we would know whether they are, with conclusions there often assumed to be relevant to matters of moral worth. At first blush, this seems a rather arcane, benign, or even absurd issue. (Remember the response to Blake Lemoine’s fears.) Setting aside the terms of the debate itself, or the relevant demarcation criteria, it seems to me a quite high-stakes question, for an affirmative answer — that is, granting moral worth to AIs — would presumably mean that the aggregate worth of AIs would soon outweigh that of humans in any utilitarian calculus. The AIs will be exceptionally wise and intelligent, and vastly more numerous (especially once one considers the imminent future and the AIs not yet born). As such, even epsilon of moral worth will multiply to a lot once one considers the quadrillions that could soon exist. (This is effectively a distributed version of the Nozick’s utility monster.) If this conclusion is unpalatable, I think one of three propositions needs to be rejected: the premise AIs can have moral worth; utilitarianism itself; or the belief that there is even a possibility that they will be far more numerous than humans.

With both of these matters (contours of future society; AI moral worth), there is the possibility of dramatic change. Today, people argue about datacenters. I’m curious how popular support for AI will evolve as more people come to understand these medium-term questions and the relevant stakes. What is the vision for AI that most people would be excited about?

恍然大悟！在清理2400 多个推特关注，感觉像是在进行「23-25年币圈叙事考古」。

那个时候会有很多大项目，说的东西我当时不太懂，现在也不懂，比如数据层、执行层、模块化、数据可用性这些概念。但当时觉得非常nb，因为有顶级VC和头部KOL宣传，有数千万融资和数十亿估值。

现在到了潮水相对退去的阶段，感觉大部分概念最后的意思都是：「这里存在一个足够大的赚钱区间，而你我都在这个区间之内」。

基本是这么一个过程：
1、叙事诞生：Vitalik和各种VC这种顶级研究员和机构提出技术概念
2、共识形成：项目方、VC、KOL、媒体和社区反复讨论，概念逐渐成为市场关注的热门赛道
3、一级市场资本化：VC 投资、种子轮、战略轮、KOL 轮等融资活动，把这个区间画的越来越大
4、二级市场定价与流动性结算：TGE、交易所上市、做市、代币交易
5、（如果有的话）长期价值检验兑现：随着时间推移，市场逐渐能够观察到产品采用情况、真实需求、经济模型的可持续性，以及代币能否捕获价值

但是，回头看这三年真正让人印象深刻的项目，可以说都没有完整走过这套流程。

比如 Hyperliquid，自筹资金，没有传统 VC 融资；Pumpfun 是先做产品有收入再发币。还有 Axiom、GMGN 这样的交易工具，和那些概念完全不在一个空间里。

所以非常成熟、标准、权威的规则，有多少是因为能筛选最有成长区间的项目，有多少是因为能让参与其中的各方都有赚钱机会空间嘞~

最开始我们都觉得，这些项目未来有很大的赚钱区间，而且你我都有机会处在那个区间里。

现在回头看，可能确实存在一个很大的赚钱空间。
只是此空间，非彼区间。

Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text: Does anyone here think Marcus has actually tried to use GLM to find vulnerabilities? Out of curiosity.
author: matthew_d_green
quoted_text:
I love that people want to assume that I formed my opinions on the viability of current generation open-weight LLMs for enabling low-skilled criminals to find useful zero-day exploits, based on having just never used an LLM at all. 

The first thing I did when Anthropic added me to their CVP was build an autonomous zero-day exploitation pipeline. I've since backported it to use open-weight models because the token cost was insane, so I have a fairly good feel for both current frontier and open-weight model capabilities.

I'm well aware of what LLMs are capable of doing, and that they can, with the right steering or harness find zero-day exploits. Where we drift off course is with the claim that low-skilled criminals can just pick up something like GLM and find viable zero-day exploits.

I think that: 

a) More than 90% of CVEs are functionally useless for threat actors. Threat actors have a very specific operational needs and "random issue in random software" does not fall into their scope. 

b) Many (quite possibly even the majority of) critical rated CVEs are not exploitable under real-world conditions in a way that is useful to threat actors. There's entire teams in China dedicated to n-day exploitation and watching them will give you a good feel for what percent of critical RCEs are actually useful.

c) Threat actor with no exploit development background and minimal technical skills, even with access to a completely unrestricted open-weight LLMs, would struggle or completely fail to find useful zero-day exploits.

d) People with very little experience in software exploitation, Large Language Models, and CTI, are watching professional vulnerability researchers working with next-gen frontier models and ending up with a wildly unrealistic beliefs of just how "easy" what they are doing is.

e) There is an extremely noticeable lack of both zero-day exploitation and use of novel (non-public) n-day exploits by all threat actors, especially unskilled ones, and proponents of the "anyone can just pick up GLM and find useful zero-day exploits" theory continually refuse to even acknowledge that fact, let alone attempt to explain it.

I'm not coming at this from the position of some dude who just logs on to social media to says uninformed shit. I'm coming at this from the perspective of a researcher who has spent thousands of hours since LLMs came out researching their capabilities, and has also spent their entire career tracking threat actors and their capabilities. 

I have a mountain of real-world data, because the low-skilled AI-powered threat actors have a high tendency to accidentally infect themselves with their own malware. This often results in them exfiltrate their entire hard disk, along with all their AI prompt logs, to a vibe-coded C2 with client-side authentication (the admin credentials are hardcoded into the javascript or something equally stupid, so anyone can log in and download it).

My entire career I've been very pro "degrees and certs don't matter, everyone is welcome, and the best way to gain experience is hands-on practical work". But when I have some dude whose only experience is essentially just "downloaded abliterated GLM and scared himself with it", I feel like it's necessary to draw a line somewhere.

It's not just the bad opinions, everyone has bad opinions on something, I have plenty. It's that resources are actively being diverted away from addressing real and pressing issues in cybersecurity, as a result of FUD being spread about imaginary GLM-powered zero-day wielding scriptkiddies.

Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

🔥 Excited about the progress of The Sandbox Studio

One of the biggest lessons we've learned from enabling Creators to build and publish their own games on @TheSandboxGame is that giving them the tools to create isn't enough if they cannot monetize their creations with the same level of autonomy.

Over the years, we've experimented with multiple ways for Creators to generate revenue, from selling NFTs and digital assets to Creator Funds, grants, competitions and engagement-based rewards.

But we've also learned that not every Creator can successfully launch and sustain their own NFT collection or token economy. And relying on grants or one-off rewards alone isn't a sustainable business model for them.

As I've shared in previous posts, ownership is only one part of empowering Creators. The ability to earn recurring revenue from their creativity, reach players and build sustainable businesses is equally important.

This means giving Creators more freedom to design their own in-game stores, currencies, digital asset packs, pricing and monetization strategies, without depending entirely on the platform.

The Sandbox team is applying these lessons with the upcoming public launch of The Sandbox Studio, tackling monetization much earlier in the product development, rather than treating it as an afterthought.

We're heading in the right direction, and this is why Creators should pay attention to what's coming next 👇

“메모리 장기계약을 깼다가 사업 전체를 날릴 수도 있다. 과거에는 그렇지 않았다.”

Gavin Baker가 보는 메모리 LTA의 변화.

당장 가격을 낮추려고 계약을 깨는 선택이, 다음 공급 부족기에 핵심 물량을 확보하지 못하는 결과로 돌아올 수 있다.

1/
Baker의 논리는 AI 연산에서 메모리의 중요성이 커졌다는 데서 출발함.

같은 연산 성능에 메모리를 더 붙이면 토큰 생산량을 늘리고, 토큰당 비용을 낮출 수 있다는 것.

그는 이 효과가 워낙 커서 메모리 가격 상승에도 수요가 위축되지 않았다고 봄.

2/
이 경쟁의 주요 플레이어로 꼽은 건 아마존 Trainium, 구글 TPU, AMD, 엔비디아.

Baker는 앞으로 몇 년간 이들의 점유율이 공급망에서 배정받는 물량과 미리 확보해둔 물량에 크게 좌우될 것으로 봄.

칩을 얼마나 잘 설계하느냐에 더해, 메모리를 얼마나 확보했느냐가 경쟁력을 결정한다는 시각.

3/
그가 든 가정은 이렇다.

2028~2029년 메모리 공급 과잉으로 가격이 내려가자 구글이 기존 LTA를 파기함. 이후 공급 능력이 줄고, 업황이 다시 공급 부족으로 돌아선다면?

그때 메모리 업체가 구글에 물량을 얼마나 배정해줄지 생각해보라는 것.

4/
Baker가 보는 LTA의 구속력은 만약 싸이클 신업이라 가정해도 다음 공급 부족기에 물량을 받을 수 있느냐에 있음.

계약을 깨고 당장 구매 가격을 낮출 수는 있어도, 2~3년 뒤 협상력이 메모리 업체로 돌아가면 사업 전체가 흔들릴 수 있다는 주장.

AI 경쟁에서 메모리 확보가 차지하는 비중이 커지면서, 장기계약을 깨는 선택의 무게도 과거와 달라졌다고 가정.

*이 시나리오에 CXMT,YMTC가 시장에 상관없이 물량을 쏟아 내서 범용 디램,낸드가 공급이 넘친다고 가정해 앞으로 공급부족이 없을 거라는 가정은 없음. 메모리 업체들은 이를 잘 알기에 고객 맞춤형 제품을 계속 개발하려고 함.
author: mindmoon_108
quoted_text:
Gavin Baker on memory LTAs: “You might blow up your entire business and your franchise by breaking an LTA. And that was never the case before”

Talking about memory makers moving buyers onto long-term agreements (LTAs), he works through the game theory of what happens to a buyer who walks away from one:

“Let’s just think about the game theory of breaking an LTA. So there’s four companies that matter at scale. There’s Amazon with their Trainiums, there’s Google with their TPUs, there’s AMD, and then there’s NVIDIA who’s much bigger than everybody else combined.”

“Let’s just say it’s 2027, it’s very important to realize memory is, the more memory you put with FLOP for a given unit of compute, the more tokens you get out. It’s the single most important thing you could do to increase kind of token output per unit of compute. And then that obviously definitionally actually lowers costs, which is why the demand hasn’t responded at all negatively. There’s been no elasticity just because it’s kind of the only, it’s the axis that is dominating all others. And this is at some level, a giant Game of Thrones or emperors between these companies.”

“And okay, it’s 2027 or '28, you’re vaguely tempted to break one of these LTAs, try and get a lower price. But to a large degree, market shares are, I think for the next several years, are going to be determined by supply chain allocations and what you have pre-purchased. So if you break the LTA and you, and this is assuming we’re not in a severe oversupply situation, the game theory even holds in a severe oversupply situation. If you break your LTA, and then in the next two or three years, for any reason, leverage shifts back to the memory guys, you’re out of business. It’s over.”

“Let’s just say Google breaks an LTA. There’s an oversupply. I’m making this up, in '28, '29. They break their LTAs. Well, if they’re breaking their LTAs, it probably means, your oversupply, prices are coming down, and then, capacity naturally contracts. Well, what do you think is going to happen to Google’s allocations? And then, this is a cyclical industry, and oversupply is followed by undersupply. What do you think they think is going to happen to their allocations next time?”

“So I just think given that this is the axis around which kind of everything is revolving, man, you might blow up your entire business and your franchise by breaking an LTA. And that was never the case before.”

Update on Slop[.]Cash token auction 

The public round opened at 16:03 UTC and by 16:18 the auction had hit its $988K cap. Less than 15 minutes to allocate the full token auction supply. This also far exceeded our expectations, as the auction was set to last 3 days.  

Open-source contributors verified through zkTLS proofs filled their lane to the dollar: 48 wallets, 59 bids, $200k committed against a $200k cap. The Umia Pass drew the largest crowd of the early window, 132 wallets and 156 bids for $125k. 42 Angels committed $260k across 45 bids, and 8 funds put in $153k. The public round itself brought 360 wallets, with an average bid of about $740.  

Public round bids were capped at $1K per wallet so more people could take part. The goal was a wide base of aligned holders. Every bid is onchain, and you can check each one in the Activity tab of the auction page, where bidders are labeled by path.  

The volume of bot traffic attempting to secure an allocation far exceeded our expectations. At its peak, our systems were processing more than 1 million requests per second, triggering the app’s last line of defense: rate limiting. Our defenses worked as designed, but we recognize that the resulting restrictions made the experience significantly worse for some users. We’re already working to strengthen protection against this kind of adversarial behavior so we can keep prioritizing real users while keeping the experience smooth.

At the full raise, Slop Cash's treasury covers about 23 months of operations at a fixed $35K a month, and any spending beyond that needs a decision market. We also expect the treasury to grow further as trading fees accrue.  

SLOP will open for trading on November 10 at 5 PM UTC. A liquidity pool pairing 9 million SLOP with ~200k USDC will allow users to buy additional tokens and trade freely through the Umia swap UI, Uniswap, or any aggregator of choice.  

On the product side, @mil_itia and @shawmakesmagic will soon share more updates on development progress and upcoming initiatives post-TGE.
