text:
Two things I’ve been thinking about regarding AI:

• People often highlight the risks involved in AI, which are surely very real. I’m struck, however, by how hard it is to understand the contours of the positive scenario. There are easy-to-perceive and frequently invoked elements of a positive vision — more diseases cured, more material abundance, etc. — which sound great, but these are by themselves just ingredients. I’m curious what the larger equilibrium is supposed to look like. Do people work? If so, why? What is their marginal contribution? If not, how are resources allocated? What is scarce? What is the ratio between humans and AIs? Are humans in control, whatever that means? One sometimes hears the Culture novels invoked as one scenario, but I’m not sure they depict a desirable outcome. (AI runs everything and humans compete in games? Iain Banks himself said that the humans in the Culture are “somewhere between passengers, pets and parasites.”) There is Richard Brautigan’s famous poem, but do we want to be “returned to our mammal brothers and sisters”? (Isn’t that rewinding Genesis?) We could say that it was hard to imagine the world of 1900 from the vantage point of 1700, and that’s assuredly true. But nobody in 1700 was trying to recast humanity itself within a couple of years — things necessarily unfolded slowly and by increments, and therefore with the possibility for error correction. Given how rapid the rate of progress in AI may be, it feels strange for the upside case to be so opaque.

• There is increasing discussion of whether AIs are conscious or how we would know whether they are, with conclusions there often assumed to be relevant to matters of moral worth. At first blush, this seems a rather arcane, benign, or even absurd issue. (Remember the response to Blake Lemoine’s fears.) Setting aside the terms of the debate itself, or the relevant demarcation criteria, it seems to me a quite high-stakes question, for an affirmative answer — that is, granting moral worth to AIs — would presumably mean that the aggregate worth of AIs would soon outweigh that of humans in any utilitarian calculus. The AIs will be exceptionally wise and intelligent, and vastly more numerous (especially once one considers the imminent future and the AIs not yet born). As such, even epsilon of moral worth will multiply to a lot once one considers the quadrillions that could soon exist. (This is effectively a distributed version of the Nozick’s utility monster.) If this conclusion is unpalatable, I think one of three propositions needs to be rejected: the premise AIs can have moral worth; utilitarianism itself; or the belief that there is even a possibility that they will be far more numerous than humans.

With both of these matters (contours of future society; AI moral worth), there is the possibility of dramatic change. Today, people argue about datacenters. I’m curious how popular support for AI will evolve as more people come to understand these medium-term questions and the relevant stakes. What is the vision for AI that most people would be excited about?

quoted_text:
On @WilfredFrost podcast on Tuesday, I said I was “terrified of what happens on the other side of mid-terms.” Post election, 40%+ of incremental datacenter capacity is now at risk. For the wk, SOX/SPX/Nas -12.1%/-2.7/-3.4%. The good news is oil prices should continue to come down.

Comments by the AI industry that included: 1) AI could wipe out 50% of entry-level white-collar jobs within the next one to five years and 2) AI having a 10% probability of wiping out humanity, justifies the public backlash against datacenters.

My belief remains that those AI related companies that have other lines of business supporting their investments in AI will be the ultimate winners. I see the neo-clouds and pure LLM labs like Anthropic and OpenAI being in an even worse position post mid-terms. But the existing capacity at the big hyperscalers has become more valuable and they are likely to face less competition from the neo-clouds. Due to the regulatory friction and moderation of semiconductor price increases, hyperscaler capex spend in 2027 is also likely to be less which should help their cash flows.

The big 3 public cloud hyperscalers all gained last week: $AMZN +7.9% (they also benefit from lower oil prices), $GOOGL +1.8%, $MSFT +1.7%. But the coast is not all clear given growth rates at AWS, Azure and GCP are likely to be negatively impacted at the start of 2027 by this regulatory friction.

$META lost only 0.8% last week. They do not have a public cloud but 1) social media is not likely to get disintermediated by AI, 2) Muse has been a hit in Agentic AI and 3) AI is helping the monetization of their ad business.

As for semiconductors, the SOX was down 12.1% last week. Physical space in datacenters to put these chips was already an issue before the mid-terms. It is worse now.  Even on Wednesday when the S&P was up 1.6%, the SOX was down 3.1% with an even bigger 12.2% decline on Thursday when the S&P fell 4.4%.

This brings me to my point that good portfolio risk management is critical, especially around AI related stocks. This is true even if bullish due to the nascent nature of Agentic AI (my view) because one of these times, if not already on 6/22, will be THE TOP. That is why I warned of an AI “speed bump” on 6/20 and posted on 10/4 “Finally, the current bi-partisan (amazing they agree on anything) pushback on datacenters could get worse after November 3rd mid-terms if there is a blue wave which is what the current polling data leans towards.”

This year, from its all-time peak on 6/22 to the Situational Awareness driven low on 7/29, the SOX declined 29%. It then rallied 27% before the recent 32% decline from 10/6-11/5. These recent declines are also close to the 8 average declines of 34% during the dotcom bust. The SOX is now down 36% from its all-time highs with 14 of its 30 constituents down 50%+. But even during the dotcom meltdown over 2 ½ years, the SOX had 7 rallies that averaged 28% while losing 83% from peak to trough.

The good news is I think oil prices are likely to head much lower by year-end now that mid-terms are over. An excerpt of Iran’s response by the Speaker of their Parliament was “Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message.” As a reminder, the Iran hostages after being held for 444 days were released just minutes after Ronald Reagan was inaugurated This followed his crushing defeat of President Jimmy Carter. I think a deal with Iran is coming soon.

Given my view on oil, I believe we will see the usual seasonal strength in the non-AI side of the stock market through year-end. Five of the eleven sub-sectors of the S&P that are not as closely related to AI or energy were up over 1% last week: consumer staples, consumer discretionary, financials, real estate, and telecom services.

In summary, I think those sectors that would benefit from lower oil prices should perform well through year-end. As for AI, related stocks reached their most oversold levels on Thursday since the tariff lows in April of 2025 before bouncing on Friday. But unfortunately, my S&P quant model had only 25% of my technical metrics indicating that Thursday was a short-term bottom vs the average of ~50%. The anemic 0.3% S&P advance on Friday following the 4.4% decline on Thursday also is not encouraging looking back at historical data. Therefore, stock selection, daily risk management and seeing how the market reacts to incoming data will remain key given these conflicting factors.

Best of luck in what is likely to be a volatile environment through year-end.

text:
Good for Nvidia’s board for doing an investigation. But Jensen’s behavior is only half the story. 

The biggest problem remains unaddressed: the Department of Commerce has enacted policies—at the encouragement of Jensen, and which the MSS reportedly sought as well—that allow China to continue to access the most advanced Nvidia chips, including via Megaspeed. @CommerceGov leadership knew that Jensen was sleeping with a Chinese spy and that Megaspeed was a Chinese cutout, but still actively opposed any policies to tighten export controls on Nvidia chips. Why?

Commerce could have blocked chip shipments to Megaspeed the moment it found out that it was run by a Chinese spy, but it did not. Commerce has also refused to enforce regulations—which ironically remain on the books—that would require exporters to apply for a license to ship large numbers of AI chips to untrusted entities in many countries, which would prevent China from using shell companies like Megaspeed to buy controlled chips. And Commerce has done nothing to cut off China’s remote access of controlled chips, or its ability to buy controlled chips in the United States. 

Why is Commerce protecting Jensen and supporting his preferred policies even though it has known for months that Jensen was sleeping with a Chinese spy? Why is it STILL doing so?

Obviously Nvidia needs to take significant steps in its operations, security, and policy advocacy to ensure it takes national security concerns more seriously. But it is even more important that the Department of Commerce tighten up export controls to prevent things like this from ever happening again. It is utterly baffling that despite being privy to this information for months, they have not taken even the most basic actions to protect the country, such as cutting off a company that is literally run by Chinese spies from buying AI chips. 

By the way, as of this writing, Nvidia STILL lists Megaspeed as a “regional cloud partner” on its website.

text:
這件事發展到現在，我認為真正需要關注的，已經不是 Jensen Huang 是否出軌，也不是他與 Alice Huang 究竟有什麼私人關係。

私人生活是私人生活，但當一個人掌握全球最重要的 AI 算力供應鏈之一時，他所接觸到的資訊，本身就可能具有國家戰略價值。

這裡有一個很容易被忽略的問題：

情報蒐集不一定需要取得機密文件，也不一定需要偷走一顆 GPU。

Jensen Huang 是 NVIDIA 的 CEO。他所掌握的資訊，可能包括公司未來的產品方向、客戶需求、供應鏈瓶頸、產能配置、技術發展時程，以及他與美國政府討論 AI 出口政策時的策略與考量。

這些資訊未必每一項都是機密，但把它們拼湊起來，就可能形成極具價值的情報。

更重要的是，Jensen 不只是一個企業 CEO。

他也是美國 AI 產業政策的重要參與者，直接與政府高層溝通，甚至積極遊說美國政府允許 NVIDIA 向中國市場出口更先進的 AI 晶片。

如果美國情報機構所提出的指控屬實，那麼問題就不只是有沒有技術資料外洩，而是中國是否可能透過一段私人關係，取得原本很難從正常商業管道取得的資訊，甚至影響 NVIDIA 對中國市場的策略。

當然，目前這些仍然是情報指控，並沒有公開證據證明 Alice Huang 成功取得 NVIDIA 機密，或實際影響了 Jensen 的政策立場。

NVIDIA 董事會目前已宣布啟動獨立調查，並表示目前沒有理由相信美國國家安全或 NVIDIA 商業機密遭到洩漏。Jensen 也承諾配合調查。

但我認為還有另一個值得觀察的層面。

這件事對 NVIDIA 的影響，可能遠遠超過一次企業內部調查。

美國政府現在有理由要求更嚴格的企業資安制度、客戶背景審查，以及 CEO 與高風險客戶接觸時的資訊隔離。

而 Jensen 未來每一次替中國市場爭取出口許可，都可能面臨更嚴格的國安審視。

換句話說，這件事可能同時改變兩件事：

一是 NVIDIA 如何管理自己的資訊與商業關係。

二是 Jensen Huang 還能在多大程度上，按照自己的全球市場策略經營中國業務。

這才是我認為整件事情最值得關注的地方。

在 AI 時代，晶片是戰略資產，算力是國家競爭力，而掌握這些產業決策資訊的人，本身也成為情報戰的重要目標。

我們不能只用傳統企業醜聞的角度來理解這件事。

因為當企業的商業決策已經直接牽動國家安全時，CEO 的私人關係，也可能不再只是私人問題。
author: Leoskie_L
quoted_text:
這件事我反而不太想把焦點放在 Jensen Huang 到底有沒有跟 Alice Huang 存在浪漫關係。

真正值得觀察的是，美國政府正在如何重新定義 NVIDIA 與中國市場之間的關係。

Jensen 的商業邏輯其實一直很清楚：中國是一個龐大的 AI 市場。如果 NVIDIA 主動退出，不只失去營收，更可能把整個中國 AI 生態系推向國產 GPU，讓 CUDA、開發者生態系與 NVIDIA 的長期影響力逐漸被取代。

但這套邏輯跟華盛頓的國家安全戰略並不完全一致。

對 Jensen 來說，GPU 是產品，市場是全球的，客戶在哪裡，生意就應該做到哪裡。

對美國政府來說，先進 AI 晶片已經不只是商品，而是涉及軍事、情報、算力主導權與國家競爭優勢的戰略資產。

所以，這次事件真正值得注意的，是它可能帶來的政治槓桿。

當一位全球最重要的 AI 晶片公司 CEO，被捲入涉及中國情報機構、晶片走私與國家安全的調查時，他未來替中國市場爭取出口許可、公開反對出口限制，甚至推動 NVIDIA 繼續深耕中國市場，都會面臨更高的政治成本。

我不會直接認定這是美國政府刻意設計的一場政治操作。目前也沒有證據能證明這些情報指控是為了迫使 Jensen 改變策略。

但有一點很值得思考：

國家不一定需要直接干預一家公司的商業決策，只要改變這家公司做決策時所承受的政治成本，就足以影響它的行為。

這才是我認為值得觀察的地方。

Jensen 想做的是全球 AI 基礎設施生意，但美國政府希望 NVIDIA 的技術優勢，最終能夠服務美國的國家戰略。

兩者目前仍然存在利益交集，只是當中國市場與美國國家安全發生衝突時，誰有最後的決定權？

這才是整件事背後真正的問題。

text:
Who says you can't write an article or long form posts on Sundays?, haha.

It just took me about 32 minutes to choose a movie to see, hence the reason I decided to write this today.

"Technology is an amplification of the will of its creators" , @0xbilly said it near the end of the Nov 5th stream  on @0xIntuition  and it stuck with me, I watched the full stream 3 times.

Technology doesn’t have a will of its own. It just turns the volume up on whatever you feed it. Good stuff in, good stuff out. Bad stuff in, bad stuff out, louder. That’s the whole game.

Right now the loudest machines on earth are training on the internet. And the internet is mostly the worst version of us. The version that posts for the algorithm. The version that argues because arguing gets engagement. The version that gets paid to make you buy something, vote for something, or feel something you didn’t feel five minutes ago. AI is eating that and calling it “humanity.” Then it turns around and gives us more of the same. The flywheel is already spinning. Frontier labs know it. That’s why there’s a quiet gold rush for private data. They can’t keep eating their own output forever. It gets worse.

Most people aren’t like that, though. Not really. Most people are just stuck playing games that reward the less good version of themselves. Twitter, Instagram, the comment sections, the replies. You say something honest and it gets buried under bots and bad incentives. You say something sharp and fake and it travels. After a while you start performing the version of you that the platform likes. AI looks at that and thinks that’s who we are. It isn’t.

That’s the part that feels off. Technology is an amplifier. If the will of the people building it is “maximize engagement” or “sell the next ad,” that’s what gets amplified. If the will is “help people find what they actually like from people they actually trust,” something else comes out the other side. Same tools. Different direction.

Intuition has been circling this for a while.  As a practical problem. The team got together in the middle of winter in a place they call the barn and asked the simple question: what’s the one thing every single one of us struggles with, no matter how different we are? The answer was the same. It’s hard to know what to trust. It’s hard to get a good recommendation. And it’s getting worse. So they started there. Movies, shows, books, podcasts, music. Then places. Stuff everyone already cares about. Not because those things are the whole point. Because they’re a clean place to begin. You get the aha moment of “oh, this actually feels better” without anyone having to sign a manifesto first.

Underneath it is the same idea Billy was pointing at. Everyone has their own little knowledge graph. Their own second brain. Their tastes, their lists, the things they trust. You can keep that private. Or you can publish pieces of it so other people can use it. When you do, you’re asking the people you already trust. Their intuition shapes yours. The results you get are influenced by the people you chose, not by whoever paid the most to sit at the top of the results. That’s closer to how the real world works. You ask the friend who actually knows movies. You don’t ask a billboard.

It feels small until you zoom out. Whoever controls the recommendations controls a lot. What you buy. What you think happened. Who you believe. In a few years most people won’t scroll. They’ll just say “give me the best chair” or “what happened here” and take whatever comes back. If that answer is always the highest bidder, or always the same three models trained on the same noisy internet, we handed the steering wheel over without noticing. The categories look light on purpose. You start with something normal people will actually use. Then you can expand. Products, claims, whatever comes next. The protocol was always big enough. The hard part was getting normal people in the door.

The Intuition app that just came out of stealth is one attempt at that. Invite only for now. Not because it’s exclusive for the sake of it. Because culture is a garden. You can’t force it. You tend it. If the first people through the door are people who actually care about the thing, the signal stays clean. Anyone can build the features now. The moat is the people. The community. The fact that when someone says “this movie is good,” you can see who they are and whether anyone else trusts them on that. Same Lego pieces work for a film or for whether some claim floating around is worth listening to. Reputation has to live somewhere again. Online it mostly disappeared, and the incentives flipped. You can get rewarded for being wrong. That’s not sustainable.

None of this requires you to be a devotee. You can just use the thing because it gives you better recommendations and a profile that actually looks like you instead of a slanted feed or a bunch of photos. If it works, other apps can use the same profile and the same graph. One good thing that people actually open every day is enough. The rest of the ecosystem can build on top of it. That’s the point of the protocol. More shots on goal. One of them hits and everyone wins.

We’re still early. Still inning zero, maybe creeping into one. The technology is ready enough. The question is what will we decide to amplify. If we keep feeding the machines our worst public selves, that’s what we’ll get back, louder. If we start feeding them something closer to how we actually are, the things we like, the people we trust, the quiet preferences we never post, then the amplification goes the other way.

Most people are better than the game currently forces them to be. The work is just making it easier to be that version, and making sure the machines can see it.

$TRUST the process 👁️.

Oh, and by the way recommend movies for me, ty.

The short term crypto market prices are almost entirely controlled by perpetual futures exchanges aka casinos. They sell bets against crypto prices to gamblers and offer magnified gains using leverage multipliers. But there is a liquidation level. If this level is crossed the gambler gets liquidated and the casino takes all their collatoral. On a large liquidation day this is $billions in liquidations. 

Note: The casino will manipulate the prices to "flush" these gamblers in high leverage bets. This is how the exchanges make their money. text:
An OpenSSH bug that took 46 years to ripen!

1980

UNIX puts * in the password field of system accounts. The idea is simple: it’s not a real hash, so it can’t be brute-forced and you can’t log in with a password.

2012

The musl libc developers decide that returning NULL from crypt() on failure is dangerous - programs often forget to check it and crash with a segfault. So they return an error string instead.

Guess which one?

The same asterisk: *.

Three weeks later they add a length limit: passwords longer than 256 bytes burn CPU. Anything longer is rejected. And since it’s an error, crypt() returns *.

2016

OpenSSH fixes a timing attack (CVE-2016-6210). If a user doesn’t exist, the server still hashes the password with a fake/borrowed salt so an attacker can’t tell valid usernames by response time.

2022

Alpine Linux changes the locked root password in /etc/shadow from ! to * so SSH keys work properly on cloud images.

… and the loop closes!

You connect over SSH as root (whose shadow entry is *).

You type any password longer than 256 characters (e.g. 300 As).

crypt() hits the length limit → returns * → OpenSSH compares it with the value in the database → that value is also * → you’re in as root.

That chain took 46 years (!!!) to complete.

Every individual change was reasonable. Together they produced a perfect * == * authentication bypass (CVE-2026-123158, nicknamed *sshole). Fixed in OpenSSH 10.6p2 and Alpine packages.
author: officer_secret
quoted_text:
🚨 Critical OpenSSH flaw allows passwordless account access using any password over 256 characters

https://t.co/gILS1Dxn1w

A newly disclosed vulnerability dubbed *sshole has been discovered in OpenSSH installations using musl libc, potentially allowing attackers to bypass authentication and gain access to accounts that should reject password logins entirely.

The flaw affects certain configurations of Alpine Linux, OpenWrt, Buildroot, and Yocto where PAM is disabled and password authentication remains enabled. Under specific conditions, attackers can authenticate to locked accounts using arbitrary passwords between 257 and 1,024 characters.

The researcher demonstrated that affected Alpine Linux cloud images could allow attackers to gain root privileges through a passwordless administrative account.

OpenSSH 10.6p2 addresses the issue. Administrators are urged to update immediately or disable SSH password authentication until patches can be applied.

My definition of moneyness is arbitrary as all are but I think it will be proven right (that's admittedly the trade I'm taking with these calls):

1. PoW > PoS. I think it's essential that miners are forced sellers & distributors of the tokens. Otherwise you basically enshrine the Cantillon Effect into the "money" of the network. I also think there's a spiritual/memetic requirement that money == work
**Maybe Ethereum is grandfathered into this clause bc the long PoW history, i'm undecided there

2. I think programmability is -EV, as described earlier. I think it's good for the network but not good for the money/sov like properties you'd want from the network token

This is also where I take exception to the "Bitcoin is SoV but nobody uses it, why are Ethereum and Solana being punished for being used even if it's less than stables on their respective networks". Money is a meme. It's not dissimilar to the "always be pre-revenue" joke from Silicon Valley. Bitcoin wins by not even playing that game. It's also more comparable to gold in it's SoV-ness, which is a bridge I'm arguing the programmable L1s won't be able to cross

3. It needs a divine meme. What's the difference between Bitcoin and Dogecoin? The meme. That said, I do think Ethereum and Solana have grand enough memes here

Context: I like these three properties of cryptomoney compared to the standard properties of money like scarcity, verifiability, fungibility, etc... because basically all the crypto assets have this by nature of design. I think we've been tricked by the historical immaturity of crypto to think "well maybe it's all money in some way" but I believe those days falling behind us

I respect the bull case that solana will incubate 1,000+ pumpfuns into an ecosystem that hits critical mass and can't be vamped. Then they raise fees and run it up bigly. I'm hesitant because it really seems like blockspace is a commodity but I could be wrong

很有趣的想法，我也說說我的想法。

第一，關於大部分買半導體的人不懂半導體技術、門檻低、黑粉多的問題，我認為不重要。因為如果你是認真研究半導體(或者AI)的人，那麼你應該要重視專家的意見和批評而不是大眾意見。而且通常專家願意指點或跟你交朋友，非專家很喜歡批評，這是兩種完全的不同態度。如果你明確知道你的主要受眾是專家，大眾只是其次受眾，你就不會介懷大部分人的批評。

第二，做半導體研究和做LLM研究不是互不相容，相反如果不懂基礎LLM理論，我就非常懷疑做半導體分析的人有多懂半導體分析。例如，如果你不知道LLM計算過程有哪些環節，又怎會知道哪些環節compute bound和memory bandwidth bound，你怎會知道權重加載時的制約和應該看重半導體什麼結構和參數？

第三，"今年7月份之前，逻辑还能推得通 下半年之后，市场走的完全是另一套" 這是narrative change，不是基本面轉變。任何產業都有機會出現，我相信一個成熟的投資者會看出narrative change帶來的具大投資機會。另外如果市場總是對的，其實沒有任何做主動投資的需要。

第四，"很现实的一点：收益。学AI的人，开蓝V的比例明显更高炒股的人，大部分不开"，我認為都不重要。其實廣告收益很低，完全不值得花時間吸引流量。交朋友、吸引專家帶來的隱性回報遠遠高遠廣告收益。學到的東西也是自己的。

其實都認真做半導體研究了，不如勇敢和誠實地說真相和自己相信的事情，而不是被市場narrative和非專家牵着鼻子走。

text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
I’m the West Wing aide in charge of the President’s 6-month no-insult challenge. We are on Day 0. We have always been on Day 0.

It began on 60 Minutes. Ross Douthat asked if he could work with Democrats “without insulting them, consistently.” The President said, “Yeah, I do. I could...” and then, in the same breath, “I also called many of them ‘Dumocrats.’”

A vow of civility, followed by a citation.

“If it took six months of not insulting the Democrats to get a deal done, do you think you could do it?”

“Very easily.”

He can resist everything except a nickname.

I was issued a laminated hallway sign: THIS WORKPLACE HAS GONE __ DAYS WITHOUT AN INSULT. I requested a digital one. It arrived with 1 digit.

The rules are simple. The challenge covers Democrats only. Everyone else is open season: a judge with “no expertise in Golf,” Fox News, which “bears responsibility for these losses,” a public golf course, “absolutely disgusting.” But when he insults a Republican, that Republican becomes a RINO. Greg Abbott, for instance, had “become a RINO in the last six months of his Political Life.” A RINO is a Republican In Name Only, which makes him a Democrat in every other way, which resets the sign. So nobody can be insulted without becoming a Democrat, and no Democrat can be insulted without resetting the sign. That’s some catch.

Legal tried Newspeak. “Dumocrats” was reclassified as a term of endearment, short for “dumbfounding.” “Talafreako,” his name for Texas’s new senator, became affectionate, like “Big Tex.” He acknowledged it on camera and did not apologize, which Legal now calls “standing by a compliment.”

As the old line goes, quitting is easy. He has quit 400 times this week.

So I have drafted a modest proposal. If the challenge covers only Democrats, the obstacle is the Democrats. There are now 2 chambers of them. I humbly propose we reclassify every Democrat in Congress as an Independent for 182 days. At the end of the period, the President will have gone 6 full months without insulting a single Democrat, there being none. We will hold a ceremony. The Democrats will not be invited. They will not exist.

This morning the House Democratic leader said he’s a “hard yes” on impeaching the Secretary of Defense. I hid the President’s phone inside the Resolute Desk, behind the panel FDR had fitted to hide his leg braces. That desk has kept secrets for 146 years. None of them were this loud.

The sign went back to 0. So it goes.

The full interview airs tonight. I’ll watch from the hallway with a box of spare 0s.

I’ve done the math. At our current pace we reach Day 1 sometime after the sun burns out. By then he will have a nickname for the sun.

But I want to be fair, because this is the best of all possible West Wings. 2 words in that clip insulted no one at all.

“Very easily.”

I’ve had them framed, in gold, by proclamation. They are the most optimistic sentence ever spoken in this building.

Day 0.

text:
作为一个经历了两轮周期的人，我越来越清晰地觉得今天的前沿 AI 实验室的后续发展，本质上跟我们在区块链行业里过去几年看到的过程没啥区别。

OAI 和 ANT 之所以值这么多钱，唯一的原因是它们在 pull forward 了自己的利润空间。这基本上和早期大家在以太坊付着天价 gas 费只为让一笔交易上链，基本上是一回事。

接下来发生的事是：随着芯片效率提升、token生产越来越节能，token 成本不断下降。这就等同于区块链靠基础设施升级把简单交易的成本压下来。MoE 和quantization本质上就是替代性 Layer 1，本质上就是换一套共识机制、配上更好的硬件，把交易成本打下来。

而当交易成本降下来之后，这些区块链 基本上就都不赚钱了，于是大家开始拿Jevon‘s Paradox讲故事了。这可能是区块链和 AI 真正不同的地方：区块链始终没有找到那个让使用量再涨 100 倍的场景。不管是支付还是 RWA，使用量根本没有涨起来，但 AI 却极有可能做到一百倍甚至十万倍的增长。

有意思的是，现在真正还有存在感的链就只剩 Solana 和 Hyperliquid 了。前者像一个什么都想做的通用智能模型，后者则是只针对一个特定场景做极致优化。而我认为后者正是当下模型 post-training在发生的事：让模型越来越垂直、越来越贴近具体行业。

text:
Let me say out loud what I think everyone is feeling right now…

Jensen was the poster child for a CEO who didn’t get caught up in these types of controversies. 

He is the last person you would think could get caught up in something like this.

When it comes to the AI revolution, he is at the center of it. Without NVIDIA, there is no AI revolution. In many respects, he has been emblematic of American capitalism over the past few years. A dishwasher at Denny’s had an idea and turned it into a $5T company. 

Everyone simply thought Jensen was above these types of things. 

I don’t even want this to be about a rich powerful man cheating on his wife…we have heard this story over and over again. That isn’t to normalize it as being okay, but it’s not really shocking. 

However, the broader issue here is what infidelity implies about someone’s character. You can make many excuses to justify it, but we all know that infidelity is not a good thing. There is a lack of morality involved when it comes to cheating.

When you are the CEO of a $5T company, the question now emerges: if you can lie to your wife, can you also lie about other things…like China’s access to your technology?

I don’t really know what to think. My gut tells me that Jensen has acted ethically in most fronts when it comes to business, but I also know that to build a $5T company, the lines around ethics can blur easily. A framework for being able to make sense of and justify your actions is very, very important and we all simply don’t know if this affair will result in anything bad in regards to America’s national security with China.

I don’t think this is good for the stock market or the AI trade. There will now be investigations and concerns around Nvidia and Nvidia is in control of how all the semis do. I also think this story may have leaked last week and that’s part of why we saw such a massive de-risking by institutions. 

I do think there is a world where the market moves beyond this, especially if the investigation doesn’t show any meaningful compromised intelligence. I also think the public will be willing to forgive Jensen, at the end of the day he is a human and infidelity has obviously been part of many marriages, much less such a high profile one. 

This is just a really weird moment and not something I ever expected from Jensen. It will now be up to the market to decide how important and meaningful this is when it comes to where the AI trade goes.

quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

Many ask if my harness is a fork of T3 Code.

The answer is no. My harness has absolutely nothing to do with T3 Code. For starters T3 Code is not a harness.

T3 Code and others alike drives other agents. It doesn't run one itself. For example, Codex, Claude Code, or others, they do the actual work underneath.

A better comparision would be DeepSeek Harness.

My harness talks straight to the model API and runs everything itself: the loop, the tools, context and compaction, and the check for when a task is actually done. Point it at a model endpoint, and it works.

So yes, it's a full blown harness.

quoted_text:
omg no, I promise it wasn't what I meant :(

it is likely I'm being too stupid to even understand the ways on which I'm being stupid, but let me try to explain my reasoning

first, no, the deck is not a joke. it is what it is. we're raising up to $8m at $120m post-money cap, and our goal is to research a successor architecture to GPTs. is that a bad thing? I actually have no idea

now, on the humble part, I think the actual situation is the opposite... all big funds passed, and I think they see my work as a joke, so I decided to lock in until I have something worth of showing. this deck is a result of this emotional state, and not of any pride. is the ask high? perhaps I'm out of touch with the market, but I'd rather be over-protective and fail, than accidentally sell half of my company. in any case, I expected nobody would invest, which is why I put my own money. if HOC dies, at least I'll be in the same ship as my investors. it seems more fair this way

as to why I'm working on something ambitious (AGI) if I don't think I'm smart. well, it is because I think the approach will work. that's all there is to it. if you find a gold mine, you buy a shovel and dig. wouldn't you? sadly, shovels are quite expensive these days... regardless, the success of this project has less to do with my own capabilities, and more to with whether the approach scales or not, which is why I think it is worth trying

lastly, Bend's development is fully automated, so it isn't like there is much else I could do with my time anyway. AI is now capable of doing most of what I do. yet, rather than panicking like some mathematicians, I have a different perspective. I think this is an invitation to be more ambitious, and reach for things that were way beyond our own capabilities. thus, that's what I'll do.

(the cool part of reaching for the impossible is that, when things don't work, that's just another failure to your collection. you get used to it fast. yet, when they work, and occasionally they do, incredible things happen)

sorry for the text wall. I'm trying to write less, but I thought I had to explain myself. I apologize if my deck offended you, or if it was too dumb, or anything at all. tbh I don't even know what the actual criticism is, but I promise I mean no harm, I'm just doing what makes sense to me. please do not invest if you don't know what you're doing, and read the skeptical posts before you do.

I still don't know why my profile has much reach. I think people are entertained by my strangeness. in any case I'm glad to make your day a bit more entertaining, even if that's by laughing at my own failures. life is short.

I hope you all have a great day every day . . .

几个小时前，链上安全圈拉响了最高级别的红色警报：
为海量 Web3 钱包提供“谷歌/苹果一键登录”的底层基础设施 Web3Auth，突发私钥泄露级严重事故。

首当其冲被穿透的，是 Cosmos 生态龙头钱包 Keplr。

黑客已经开始在受影响的地址上发起疯狂盗币。
Keplr 官方紧急切断所有社交登录入口，全网各大链上验证节点和项目方一片大乱。

极度荒诞的一幕在链上赤裸裸地上演：

那些自以为走在时代前沿、贪图省事用 Google 和 Apple 账号一键建钱包的散户，账户私钥被扒得一干二净，沦为案板上的鱼肉；
反而是那些被嘲笑“操作落后、冥顽不灵”、坚持拿纸笔手抄 12 个助记词、死守冷钱包的老韭菜，在这场灾难里毫发未伤。

为了省下抄写助记词的 30 秒，代价是把自己的全部身家，双手奉送给第三方中心化数据库。

现在的链上战场已经变成了一场生死竞速。
Web3Auth 联合 Keplr 正连夜在 Celestia、Injective、dYdX、Osmosis、Akash 等 10 条公链以及 8 条 EVM 链上，疯狂用白帽程序把被盗边缘的资产转移到紧急恢复钱包，硬生生跟黑客抢跑。

Polygon 首席安全官 Mudit Gupta 更是公开发出最冰冷的警告：
“只要你用社交账号登过 Keplr，现在立刻马上把钱转走！更可怕的是，天知道全网还有多少钱包和 dApp，也在背后接了这家服务商。”

Not Your Keys, Not Your Coins。
你以为一键登录是去中心化的技术进步，其实你只是自作聪明地，把钱存进了一家没有任何安保的地下钱庄。

author: gave_vincent
quoted_text:
So I looked into these allegations that Jensen had a romantic relationship with a Chinese spy and, ironically, the only actual proof we have that someone is whoring themselves out to spies in this story is the media - all the rest is unsubstantiated, just journalists repeating what anonymous US intelligence officials told them.

I'm not exaggerating, I actually read all the key articles on this:

1) New York Times on Oct 29, the initial "scoop": https://t.co/E122RznhSa

Claim: Alice Huang is a Chinese intelligence asset funneling information to Beijing.

"Proof": they were told so by "people briefed on the surveillance, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because the findings are drawn from classified intelligence..." That’s it. The Times even admits it couldn’t determine which agency monitored her, what she passed along, or its value to China. In other words, they didn't verify the spy claim whatsoever.

2) Wall Street Journal on Oct 30: https://t.co/IbUk6yTpfv

Claim: The US, Singapore and Taiwan suspect Alice Huang is a Chinese intelligence source, with Singapore and Taiwan even putting physical surveillance teams on her.

"Proof": "people familiar with the matter said." That’s it. And the story actually fell apart within a day since Singapore’s Home Affairs ministry went on the record with a public rebuke of the WSJ article (https://t.co/JBXvZayuBF) stating that "neither the Singapore Government nor its officials said this," and that "there were no such investigations conducted in respect of Alice Huang." Taiwan declined to comment. In other words, the only government they invoked that went on the record denied the claim publicly.

3) New York Times again on Nov 6, the "MSS recruit" story: https://t.co/tu9Re4WdzM

Claim: Alice Huang was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security (MSS) specifically to collect intelligence on Jensen.

"Proof": "according to people briefed on U.S. surveillance." That’s it. No new evidence, no document, no on-record source for the claim. Yet the headline states it as plain fact, without even an "allegedly."

4) The Financial Times, quoted below, on Nov 7 with the romance claim: https://t.co/4y9n4wacRW

Claim: A US government memo says Jensen had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang.

"Proof": "said people familiar with the memo." That’s it: anonymous people describing a memo the FT never saw, which itself describes intelligence nobody can check.

---

It's properly extraordinary when you think about it and you couldn't make it up: she’s accused of being an intelligence asset, yet the only people we can actually watch behaving as intelligence assets - and admitting so in writing (since they openly cite spies as their only source) - are Western journalists.

Things are so bad that we've forgotten what actual journalism is: real journalists - when anonymous intelligence officials tell them something - would treat it as a lead to investigate, not as a fact. They'd ask: why are they leaking this, why now, and who benefits? And, most importantly, they’d try to verify the claims independently before printing them - which is supposed to be journalism 101 and wasn't done here.

You'd think something would have been learned from the Iraq WMD story and the countless other examples of the press laundering intelligence claims into front-page "facts." Apparently not - and it’s even the same newspaper, the New York Times, leading the charge.

author: econoar
quoted_text:
Let me say out loud what I think everyone is feeling right now…

Jensen was the poster child for a CEO who didn’t get caught up in these types of controversies. 

He is the last person you would think could get caught up in something like this.

When it comes to the AI revolution, he is at the center of it. Without NVIDIA, there is no AI revolution. In many respects, he has been emblematic of American capitalism over the past few years. A dishwasher at Denny’s had an idea and turned it into a $5T company. 

Everyone simply thought Jensen was above these types of things. 

I don’t even want this to be about a rich powerful man cheating on his wife…we have heard this story over and over again. That isn’t to normalize it as being okay, but it’s not really shocking. 

However, the broader issue here is what infidelity implies about someone’s character. You can make many excuses to justify it, but we all know that infidelity is not a good thing. There is a lack of morality involved when it comes to cheating.

When you are the CEO of a $5T company, the question now emerges: if you can lie to your wife, can you also lie about other things…like China’s access to your technology?

I don’t really know what to think. My gut tells me that Jensen has acted ethically in most fronts when it comes to business, but I also know that to build a $5T company, the lines around ethics can blur easily. A framework for being able to make sense of and justify your actions is very, very important and we all simply don’t know if this affair will result in anything bad in regards to America’s national security with China.

I don’t think this is good for the stock market or the AI trade. There will now be investigations and concerns around Nvidia and Nvidia is in control of how all the semis do. I also think this story may have leaked last week and that’s part of why we saw such a massive de-risking by institutions. 

I do think there is a world where the market moves beyond this, especially if the investigation doesn’t show any meaningful compromised intelligence. I also think the public will be willing to forgive Jensen, at the end of the day he is a human and infidelity has obviously been part of many marriages, much less such a high profile one. 

This is just a really weird moment and not something I ever expected from Jensen. It will now be up to the market to decide how important and meaningful this is when it comes to where the AI trade goes.

Built a physical simulation of a record player with WebGL2 and Web Audio. It's *shockingly* accurate: https://t.co/MBNaTfKoai.

Instead of playing a song, it works by converting it into the physical shape of a groove. Then a simulated stylus rides those walls 384,000 times a second, and you hear the voltage that motion would induce in a cartridge.

So the crackle, the pops, the wow/flutter, the dull inner grooves are natural byproducts of the simulation. You can also "DJ" the record.

(The converted songs are in the public domain or CC-licensed. Code is linked for you to remix and re-deploy.)

周末这枚平地惊雷直接把科技圈和半导体盘面砸懵了。随着黄仁勋正式向全员发送道歉信，很多盘面上的异常走势终于对上了暗号。直接说我的三点核心看法：
【我的核心观点】
 1. 聪明的钱早就跑了：上周半导体的阴跌与周五反弹乏力，是明晃晃的“提前抢跑”
回看上周芯片股的诡异走弱，尤其是周五盘面多次试图反抽却软趴趴无力拉回，答案全在这封信里。机构里绝对有人提前拿到了风声在出货避险。这根本不是纯粹的技术面回调，而是知情资金抢在黑天鹅爆开前提前出逃、高位拆弹。
 2. 杀伤力不在“私德”，而在“国安调查”与“教主失去光芒”
   个人道德瑕疵在硅谷从来不是致命伤，真正要命的是董事会的独立调查直接捆绑了“美国国家安全”。
一旦沾上国安与涉外情报疑云，性质就从“个人花边”升级为“监管与政治风险”的未知黑洞。
英伟达之所以是呼风唤雨的“AI央行”，极大程度依赖老黄作为图腾人物（Key-person）的强气场与行业定价权。经此一役，不管调查结论如何，“皮衣教主”在政界和舆论敲打下都必须转入低调防守姿态。失去张扬光芒的英伟达，估值中的“神话溢价”势必被狠狠剥落一层。
 3. 短期半导体反弹基本没戏，静待两个风向标破局
在不确定性落地前，市场对半导体只会选择持续折价避险。接下来的看点只有两个：
基本面：接下来即将披露的最新财报数据是否硬核到足以强行托底？
政治面：华盛顿什么时候出来给态度？尤其是民主党阵营什么时候会出来表态“我也支持AI基建与芯片战略”、给核心产业链定调兜底？
【事件脉络速览】
起因：近日美媒报道提及黄仁勋卷入涉外情报风险及与相关企业高管的不当关系。
落地（11月8日）：黄仁勋向全员发出英文内部信，公开承认对妻子不忠并致歉，表示承担全部责任但强调继续留任 CEO。
升级：信中证实针对外媒报道引发的“国家安全疑虑”，英伟达董事会已正式启动独立调查。
唉，内忧外患，黑天鹅齐飞，最近这市场真的风雨飘摇。各位且行且珍惜，系好安全带。

🫟 Infinite Slop TV

August 2026 - October 2026

It let anybody on the internet write into a chat that fed into a perpetual stream of live generated AI video (aka slop)

It wasn't possible before that because there weren't AI video models yet that generated faster than they could be played, but then @fal hacked @MiniMax_AI's H3 to be so fast that it finally could! FAL also sponsored me to do this project because otherwise it would have costed me $200,000/mo in GPU cost, at least!

Here's some stats:

💰 3 sponsors: @sideshiftai + @creem_io + @chatbase

$NVDA: The Jensen Rumors and what it means for the AI Trade

I'm not going to make an absolute assertion on whether or not there was a scandal as no one on X has enough evidence at this time. What is really telling to me is that of the hundreds of X post on Jensen rumors, almost none of them show the earlier footage that Jensen's daughter was present at the event that is supposedly evidence of the scandal - shown in quoted post.

In light of this bias context, I stated the story in a clean narration to see this story even makes sense: Jensen Huang gets intimate with a vendor's executive at a high publicity event where both the press and his daughter are present. Uhh, so let me get you some more context to balance out the one sided posts on X.

More Context
I have a pretty deep understanding of Taiwanese culture. Many of parents family friends were Taiwanese. My parents are from Shantou which is across the strait from Taiwan and where alot of the original Taiwanese immigrated from in the 1600s. In fact, there are many  words that are the same in Teochew Dialect and Taiwanese dialect.

From that part of the world, Alice Huang's looks are maybe slightly better than a late age house wife with alot of makeup on. I'm not talking about the photoshopped pictures but the unedited pictures. Ellison and Elon have shown that there are much better avenues for much more attractive women for men worth 12 digits. 

Furthermore, in that part of the world, it's almost unheard of a man with money to cheat older women;  there's an extreme bias for younger women there, even more so than the west.

Finally, Jensen is one of the more emotionally intelligent tech CEOs and has committed his life to Nvidia and clearly thinks long terms. Family is important to him as he has set both his son and daughter up at Nvidia. For him to go out like this is totally uncharacteristic.

Alternative Motifs to the FUD
Right now, you can see that there are so many FUD stories attacking the AI sector from Democrats banning DC when the state with the most DCs is Virginia, a Democrat stronghold. The context there left out is that politicians often talk and don't do what they say. 

Now the latest hit to the AI sector is Jensen rumors. What a coincidence that Jensen starts cheating as the AI sector is facing alot of uncertainty, fear and doubt. I am a believe that Wall Street funds will indirectly pay certain news outlets and media sources to create FUD;  after all, all the profits from shorts need to be covered to realize the profit. I believe right now we are in a price based and time base capitulation phase so that Wall Street funds can shake out some shares that it needs to close their shorts. 【黄仁勋承认出轨，梳理他这几年频繁跑亚洲的时间线】

11月8日，黄仁勋公开承认婚外情——能公开承认出轨，就意味着向家人忏悔了这段关系，另一层潜台词就是他不知道这个女子跟中共关系密切，毕竟，马上要去国会受质询了，婚外情还不算是事业的灭顶之灾！

他在给英伟达员工的内部信里说，自己“对妻子不忠”，伤害了妻子和孩子，“没有任何借口”。真正让事情炸开的，是婚外情对象 Alice Huang 被英文媒体曝光。

她公开出现在黄仁勋身边，最清楚的一次是2024年6月台北 Computex 期间。

当时 Alice Huang 和一群AI产业高管在酒吧聚会，据现场人士回忆，她说了一句，大意是：“我可以把 Jensen 叫来。”

没多久，黄仁勋真的出现了。

后来流出的 LinkedIn 合照里，Alice 就坐在黄仁勋旁边，一起喝酒、聊天。

到了2025年5月，两人又被拍到出现在台北同一场商务晚餐。饭后黄仁勋在餐厅门口接受采访时，Alice 就站在他身后等着。

再往前看，另一个时间线也很有意思，他跟这个女子的交集多是在亚洲——

黄仁勋从2023年开始，也明显加快了来亚洲的频率。

2022年，他公开来亚洲还很少；2023年开始，台湾、印度、日本、新加坡、马来西亚、越南，一年大约跑了5趟；2024年继续高频；2025年更密，公开可确认至少7趟；2026年依然频繁往返亚洲。

于是现在回头看，这条线就很清楚：

2023年，黄仁勋开始高频跑亚洲；
2024年，Alice Huang 公开进入他的社交圈；
2025年，两人再次被拍到同场；
2026年10月底，两人关系被英文媒体曝光；
11月8日，黄仁勋承认出轨。

当然，黄仁勋频繁来亚洲，本身有非常充分的商业理由，台积电、供应链、AI客户都在这里，不能简单把所有亚洲行程都和这段关系挂钩。

但从时间上看，他亚洲活动最密集的几年，和 Alice Huang 出现在他身边的时间，确实高度重合。

text:
Good for Nvidia’s board for doing an investigation. But Jensen’s behavior is only half the story. 

The biggest problem remains unaddressed: the Department of Commerce has enacted policies—at the encouragement of Jensen, and which the MSS reportedly sought as well—that allow China to continue to access the most advanced Nvidia chips, including via Megaspeed. @CommerceGov leadership knew that Jensen was sleeping with a Chinese spy and that Megaspeed was a Chinese cutout, but still actively opposed any policies to tighten export controls on Nvidia chips. Why?

Commerce could have blocked chip shipments to Megaspeed the moment it found out that it was run by a Chinese spy, but it did not. Commerce has also refused to enforce regulations—which ironically remain on the books—that would require exporters to apply for a license to ship large numbers of AI chips to untrusted entities in many countries, which would prevent China from using shell companies like Megaspeed to buy controlled chips. And Commerce has done nothing to cut off China’s remote access of controlled chips, or its ability to buy controlled chips in the United States. 

Why is Commerce protecting Jensen and supporting his preferred policies even though it has known for months that Jensen was sleeping with a Chinese spy? Why is it STILL doing so?

Obviously Nvidia needs to take significant steps in its operations, security, and policy advocacy to ensure it takes national security concerns more seriously. But it is even more important that the Department of Commerce tighten up export controls to prevent things like this from ever happening again. It is utterly baffling that despite being privy to this information for months, they have not taken even the most basic actions to protect the country, such as cutting off a company that is literally run by Chinese spies from buying AI chips. 

By the way, as of this writing, Nvidia STILL lists Megaspeed as a “regional cloud partner” on its website.

SUNDAY SERMON 🔥

THE CALLING DOESN'T STOP WHEN THE ROAD GETS HARD

“Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.” — Isaiah 6:8 (KJV)

Good Sunday Morning, Messenger Army! ☕🙏

There comes a point in your walk with God when you realize something.

You weren't called because the road would be easy. You were called because you were willing to walk it.

Some of us have walked through storms that should have destroyed us.

Some have buried loved ones.

Some have watched everything they spent a lifetime building disappear.

Some have fought battles nobody else could see, while the very people they counted on turned their backs.

And yet, here we are.

STILL STANDING. STILL BELIEVING. STILL ANSWERING THE CALL.

🔥 THE BOOK OF EXODUS WAS NEVER JUST ABOUT LEAVING EGYPT.

It was about learning to trust God in the wilderness.

Think about Moses.

He didn't ask to lead a nation. He questioned whether he was capable. He questioned his own voice.

But God didn't ask Moses to have all the answers.

He asked Moses to GO.

And when Moses stood before the Red Sea, God didn't tell him to build a boat.

He told him to move forward.

“Speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward.” — Exodus 14:15 (KJV)

How many of us are standing at our own Red Sea right now?

Waiting for the waters to part before we take the next step?

Waiting for the funding?

Waiting for someone to help?

Waiting for the perfect moment?

Maybe God is waiting for us to MOVE.

I've learned something over these last six years on the frontlines.

You cannot carry everyone.

You cannot fight every battle.

You cannot be everywhere at once.

And God never asked you to.

Even Moses needed Aaron and Hur to hold up his arms when he grew weary.

And that is where we are today.

The mission was never meant to rest on one person's shoulders.

It takes a community of believers willing to answer the same calling.

A Messenger Movement.

A Messenger Mission.

A MESSENGER ARMY.

So this Sunday, I'm asking you something.

Are you waiting for someone else to answer God's call?

Or are you ready to stand up and say:

HERE AM I. SEND ME.

Because the world doesn't need more spectators.

It needs people willing to serve.

People willing to pray.

People willing to stand beside those who can no longer stand alone.

And people willing to walk by faith, not by sight.

🙏 SUNDAY PRAYER

Heavenly Father,

Strengthen those who are weary today.

Comfort those who are grieving.

Restore hope to those who feel forgotten.

Remind us that even in the wilderness, You have never abandoned Your children.

Raise up the Aarons and Hurs among us. Bring together those You have called to serve.

And when the road ahead seems impossible, give us the faith to keep moving.

Not for our glory, Lord.

But for Yours.

In Jesus' mighty name, Amen. 🙏

🔥 THE MESSENGER HAS RISEN. NOW IT'S TIME FOR THE MESSENGER ARMY TO RISE.

Here Am I. Send Me. — Isaiah 6:8

If you’re confused about what’s happening with Nvidia right now…

Basically Jensen Huang, the guy who runs Nvidia, which is the company that makes the chips basically every AI company on earth needs, just sent an email to his entire company admitting he cheated on his wife, and that came right after the New York Times reported that US intelligence believes a woman who got close to him was secretly passing information to the Chinese government, and to understand how we got here you have to go back to June 2024, when this Chinese businesswoman named Alice Huang, who also goes by Huang Le and isn't related to Jensen at all, they just have the same last name, gets photographed at a party in Taipei sitting right next to him, and then about a year later her company, a small Singapore company called Megaspeed that almost nobody had ever heard of, reportedly sets up a deal to buy around $2 billion worth of Nvidia's chips, which is a crazy amount of money for a company that small, and the Times even pointed out it was an unusual amount of business for a firm like that, and people already had questions about where all those chips were really going, but Nvidia looked into it and said everything checked out, so for a while that's kind of where things sat, until October 29, when the Times reported that US intelligence had concluded Alice was passing information to Beijing, and that it wasn't some new discovery either, because Trump had reportedly been briefed on it about a year earlier, and the officials involved apparently believed Jensen didn't know what she was up to, but here's the strange part, nobody ever told him, because there's this thing called a defensive briefing, where counterintelligence people basically pull someone aside and say hey, a foreign government might be targeting you, be careful, and Jensen never got one, even though the whole time the government was still watching her, so you have the head of the most important AI chip company in the world apparently being targeted, and the people who knew about it just let it keep going, and then everyone starts denying it, Nvidia says the Megaspeed allegations were already investigated and debunked last year, China's foreign ministry says the whole report is baseless, and Jensen says the business with Megaspeed was totally normal, just a customer buying chips like any other customer, but Congress doesn't let it go, and three House Republicans who run national security committees ask Jensen to come in and explain himself in a closed-door briefing, which means a private meeting away from the public and the cameras, and then on a Sunday, out of nowhere, Jensen sends that email to every single employee saying he had been unfaithful to his wife, that it hurt her and their children, and that nothing excused what he did, and he doesn't say who it was with, but you can imagine where everyone's mind went, and right after that, Nvidia's board, which is the group of people who are supposed to oversee the CEO, announces it's setting up an independent committee with outside lawyers to investigate, but at the same time says it has no reason to believe any national security secrets or company secrets were compromised and that it still has confidence in him, and then a company spokesperson comes out and says none of this is going to slow Nvidia down and Jensen is going to keep running the company without any interruption, so basically you have a suspected Chinese intelligence asset who got close to the CEO, a $2 billion chip deal, a president who reportedly knew about, a CEO who was never warned, a confession about an affair, an investigation, and a company insisting everything is fine, so that's pretty much where Nvidia is tonight.

text:
硅谷大佬彼得·蒂尔给年轻自己的忠告很直接：永远重视实质，而不是地位和声望。

很多人拼命考名校、挤进顶级律所，以为在走向成功，其实是被主流评价体系绑架。人人为了简历上的抬头内卷，却没人问：我抢的这东西，到底有没有真实价值？

这种狂热在蒂尔进入纽约顶级律所后破灭。他只撑了七个月零三天就辞职，离职时同事低声说：“看到你主动离开，真让人松口气。原来从恶魔岛越狱是可能的，只要推开正门走出去。”

看完这个视频我非常感同身受，当时毕业回国，努力考试进入500强央企，从昆明到北京，一路花费了很多心力，进去后同事都是清北或者哈佛、剑桥毕业的，大家都有着各种光环，在外人看来，都很厉害，包括里面的领导，外人觉得他是个北京总部的处长局长非常有光环，但最后进去很多人发现自己真实心理是压抑且痛苦的，因为这不是他真正想要过的生活，在我们的沟通里也表达过后悔当时的决定。

很多精英的人格和自尊，很早就被焊死在头衔里，或者说就是这个社会制造的评价体系里，连离开的念头都不敢有。

追求声望，是大脑最廉价的偷懒捷径：社会规则的打分表，会吸引别人羡慕的眼光，但走到尽头，只有精神牢笼，没有硬核价值。

所以这个年代，也别再为虚无光环消耗青春。年轻时候找到自己的热爱，人生只有一次，也就那么几十年，把注意力砸向更坚硬的实质，去过自己喜欢的生活最重要。

text:
실리콘밸리 최고 사랑꾼으로 불리던 엔비디아 젠슨 황(Jensen Huang)이 오늘 전 직원에게 외도 사실을 고백하는 사과문을 보냈음.

17살에 만난 첫사랑 아내와 40년 넘게 해로해 온 인물이 불륜을 시인한 것도 놀라운데, 더 충격적인 건 상대 여성이 중국 최고 정보기관인 국가안전부에 포섭된 것으로 의심받는 스파이였다는 점임.

영화에서나 보던 미인계 공작이 어떻게 세계 1위 반도체 기업 수장에게 파고들었는지 내막이 심상치 않음.

1. 젠슨황이 인정한 것과 부인한 것

이번 사건을 두고 외신마다 보도가 조금씩 다르게 나오는 이유는 개인의 외도와 국가 안보 문제가 섞여 있기 때문임.

• 인정한 것 (혼외 불륜) : 젠슨 황은 오늘 전 직원에게 보낸 편지에서 아내와 아이들에게 큰 상처를 입혔고 내 행동에 변명의 여지가 없다며 불륜 사실을 직접 인정하고 사과했음. 대학 시절 숙제 파트너로 만난 아내 로리 황과 40년 넘게 잉꼬부부로 지내온 이미지가 워낙 강했기에 실리콘밸리 안팎이 발칵 뒤집혔음.

• 부인한 것 (기밀 유출) : 반면 상대 여성이 중국 스파이인 줄은 전혀 몰랐으며, 엔비디아의 핵심 기술이나 미국 국가 안보 기밀이 넘어간 적은 단 한 건도 없다고 강하게 부인했음.

하지만 기밀 유출이 없었다는 해명을 곧이곧대로 믿기는 힘듦.

상대가 처음부터 목적을 가지고 접근한 정보요원이었다면, 설령 젠슨 황 본인은 기밀을 직접 넘긴 적이 없다고 생각하더라도 단둘이 내밀한 시간을 보내는 동안 스마트폰이나 노트북을 몰래 복제 또는 감시 앱 같은 것을 설치했을 수도 있고, 사적인 대화나 통화 내용을 통해 차세대 칩 공급 물량이나 미 정부 상대 로비 전략 같은 고급 정보를 이미 여러 방법으로 빼 갔을 가능성이 농후하기 때문임.

2. 상대 여성 앨리스 황과 싱가포르 데이터센터의 수상한 연결고리

뉴욕타임스와 파이낸셜타임스가 폭로한 미 정보당국의 기밀 보고서에 따르면, 젠슨 황의 내연녀로 지목된 인물은 싱가포르 기반 AI 데이터센터 기업 메가스피드의 전 고위 임원인 앨리스 황(중국명 황러)임.

• 메가스피드의 정체 : 싱가포르와 말레이시아 등에서 엔비디아의 최신 AI 칩을 대량으로 사들이면서, 중국이 미국의 반도체 수출 통제를 우회하는 핵심 통로가 아니냐고 미 정부의 추적을 받던 회사임.

• 중국 국가안전부(MSS) 포섭 의혹 : 미 정보당국은 중국 국가안전부가 앨리스 황을 스파이로 포섭해 젠슨 황에게 의도적으로 접근시켰고, 엔비디아의 칩 정보를 빼내거나 미국의 대중국 수출 통제 정책에 영향력을 행사하려 했다고 보고 있음.

3. 엔비디아와 미·중 반도체 전쟁에 미칠 파장

당장 엔비디아 이사회는 사외이사들과 외부 법률 자문단으로 구성된 독립 조사위원회를 꾸려, 젠슨 황이 외국 정보기관의 표적이 되었는지와 사내 보안에 구멍이 뚫렸는지를 조사하겠다고 발표했고, 현재로서는 젠슨 황이 CEO직을 유지하며 조사에 협조하기로 한 상태임.

하지만 미 의회 하원 외교위원회와 정보위원회, 미·중 전략경쟁특위가 즉각 젠슨 황에게 비공개 안보 브리핑 출석을 요구하고 나섰으며, 세계에서 가장 중요한 AI 전략 물자를 쥔 수장이 중국 정보기관의 미인계에 무방비로 노출됐다는 사실만으로도, 앞으로 엔비디아의 대중국 칩 수출 허가와 대정부 로비력은 직접적인 타격을 입을 수밖에 없을 거임.

4. 만약 실제 이혼으로 이어질 경우 터지는 112조 원 재산분할과 주가 리스크

월가 투자자들이 안보 조사 못지않게 숨죽이며 지켜보는 또 하나의 뇌관은 실제 이혼 소송 여부임.

• 창업 8년 전 결혼과 50 대 50 공동재산제 : 두 사람은 엔비디아 창업(1993년)보다 8년이나 앞선 1985년 대학 졸업 직후 아무 자산 없이 결혼했기 때문에 엔비디아 지분을 지키는 혼전계약서가 없는 것으로 알려져 있음. 게다가 두 사람이 거주하고 엔비디아 본사가 있는 미국 캘리포니아주는 별도 합의가 없는 한 결혼 기간 중 형성된 재산을 원칙적으로 50 대 50으로 똑같이 나누는 부부 공동재산제를 채택하고 있음.

• 인류 역사상 최대 규모인 약 112조 원 분할 : 현재 젠슨 황의 순자산은 약 1,622억 달러(약 225조 원)로 엔비디아 지분 약 3.5%를 쥐고 있음. 만약 이혼이 성사돼 재산을 절반씩 나누면 아내 로리 황이 가져가는 몫만 약 811억 달러(약 112조 5천억 원)에 달해, 과거 아마존 제프 베이조스(약 53조 원)나 MS 빌 게이츠(약 105조 원)의 기록을 모두 갈아치우는 역사상 최대 규모의 이혼 재산분할이 됨.

• 위자료 규정과 엔비디아 주가 영향 : 특이하게도 캘리포니아주는 무과실 이혼주의를 따르기 때문에 바람을 피웠다는 이유만으로 위자료를 더 뜯기지는 않지만, 만약 내연녀에게 선물이나 자금을 대주느라 부부 공동재산을 썼다면 그 금액은 100% 젠슨 황 몫에서 깎여 아내에게 돌아감. 무엇보다 이혼으로 젠슨 황의 지분이 반 토막 나고, 과거 베이조스의 전처 매켄지 스콧처럼 로리 황이 분할받은 수십조 원어치 주식을 자선 기부나 현금화를 위해 시장에 내다 팔기 시작하면 엔비디아 주가에도 잠재적인 대량 매도 물량 부담이 생길 수밖에 없음.

예로부터 남자는 아랫도리를 조심하고 여자는 입을 조심하라는 옛말이 괜히 내려온 게 아님.

한국에서 SK 최태원 회장이 외도로 조 단위 재산분할 폭탄을 맞았던 것이나 이번 젠슨 황 사태를 보면, 아무리 수백조 원짜리 최첨단 기술로 세상을 호령하는 거물이라도 무너지는 건 언제나 가장 원초적인 본능 앞이라는 걸 다시 한번 느끼게 됨.

I CANCELLED MY FUNERAL™  
CHAPTER 2: BARN, BLOOD, STARS  
by Ulyssesfve2™  

I came out of the barn dirty with blood 4:50am. Knife still in my hand. The air was cold, and the only sound was my own breathing and the drip of something I didn’t want to look at.  
I didn’t wipe it off. Didn’t care.  
I looked up at the stars and pointed the knife right at them.  
“Nothing’s gonna stop humanity from taking you,” I said. Stupid? Maybe 

*Post 2/12*  
I pointed that knife at the stars and made the promise like it was a contract.  
“Nothing’s gonna stop humanity from getting up there.”  
And I meant it.  
Not because I’d read it somewhere.  
I meant it because I was standing there, blood on my hands, pocket heavy with money I actually earned.  
From nothing.  
Building housing, climbing out of nowhere, sleeping in places you wouldn’t park a car.

*Post 3/12*  
If a guy like me could make it that far, then what’s stopping the rest of us?  
I felt it in my chest — the invisibility of the human spirit.  
How it bends but doesn’t break.  
My pocket was heavy. Coins and notes stuffed in the inside of my jacket, pressing against my ribs.  
Cash in hand, no bank, no mortgage, no 25 years of interest eating you alive.

*Post 4/12*  
Right in front of me was Baldur.  
The finest bull this area ever produced.  
He ran at me from the fields the way he always did, expecting feed, expecting me.  
I had to slaughter him.  
It’s not clean. The knife has to find the exact spot, and you have to commit. The blood came hot, fast, and it soaked into the dirt, into my boots.

*Post 5/12*  
There’s a smell to it — iron and earth and something primal that sticks in your nose for days.  
Money in the pocket, blood on the hands.And the worst part? It made sense.I was there when Baldur was born.
*3 AM*, freezing, cow on her side bawling, and me with my arm elbow-deep trying to turn him right so he wouldn’t die.

*Post 6/12*  
For the next 2 years I fed him, checked him, knew his limp before the vet did.  You name them even when you tell yourself not to.  
You talk to them when it’s 2 AM and you can’t sleep.But you’re not supposed to love livestock. That’s rule one. Love gets in the way of the ledger.

*Post 7/12*  
And then the clients start queuing up.  Not people. Hyenas. Smiling, “When’s it ready? How much for the cut? Supermarket is cheaper.” I’m collecting the money, counting it, feeling the notes stick together with sweat.And every note feels like 30 pieces of silver.

*Post 8/12*  
Because I’m the one who raised him.  I’m the one he ran to.  
And I’m the one turning that trust into cash.  By the gate.  
Seven guys who’d followed me through winters with no heating, summers where we slept in half-built houses.  They didn’t say anything when they saw me.  
Blood on my jacket, knife still in my hand, Baldur’s body behind me steaming in the cold.

*Post 9/12*  
They knew.  Generosity makes people uncomfortable when they’re the ones benefiting.  
Give a man a bonus when he expects minimum wage, and for 10 seconds he’s grateful.  After that, he starts wondering what you want from him.  But they still would’ve followed me to hell.  Because I’d bled with them.

*Post 10/12*  
The crew was quiet because they were already doing the math.  
About me.  When you stand there with cash in your pocket and a dead animal at your feet, people stop seeing a man.  They see a resource.  A faucet.  A threat.

*Post 11/12*  
The guy who’d carry you out of a fire yesterday is now wondering if you’ll cut his pay tomorrow.  
You understand that “human nature” isn’t about love and struggle.  It’s survival dressed up in morality.  People love you for what you give, hate you for what you keep, and betray you the second it costs them nothing.

*Post 12/12*  
I stood there and I asked, "God, what have I become?"
This is why men go quiet.  
End of Chapter 2

text:
外网都在传 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 在法庭宣誓作证时“连自己家住址都记不住”，有人猜他是听从律师建议、出于安全原因拒答。
去翻了下刚解封的 9 页法院原始笔录（案号 5:24-cv-03811-EKL，Document 827-6），原片比网传段子喜剧得多，后面十几页的交锋也精彩得多。
开场第 6–7 页，原告律师例行公事让他报姓名和家庭住址。Dario 先是一脸懵地反问了句 Are you speaking to me?，接着他自己的代理律师（WilmerHale 的 Sonal Mehta）赶紧上前替他挡枪，说出于安全原因不需要提供家庭住址。结果话还没说完，Dario 直接打断自家律师抢答：
I -- I, in fact -- no. I, in fact, don't even know it.
他不是为了隐私拒答，是真的只知道自己住在硅谷最贵的富人区 Woodside，完全记不住门牌号，连自家律师听完都放弃挣扎，直接说“那你回答吧”。
不过整份笔录真正好看的，是音乐出版商的版权律师怎么用“魔法打败魔法”，以及 Dario 在宣誓状态下的极限自辩：
1. 拿神经科学给白嫖公开网页辩护（第 133–135 页）
被逼问“从网上下载没付钱的数据拿去训练合不合法”时，Dario 搬出了自己的神经科学背景，把人工神经网络和人脑（natural neural nets）做等价类比：只要一个人类能在不违法的情况下免费看到网页上的内容、读进脑子里产生新想法，那 AI 模型就有权以同样的方式“阅读并吸收”（view it and absorb it）。只有人类必须付费才能看的内容，AI 才需要买副本。
2. 20%–30% 毁灭人类的内部备忘录被当庭呈堂（第 142–145 页）
既然 Anthropic 的核心抗辩逻辑是“AI 对社会有巨大变革性益处”，版权律师反手就掏出了两份证据砸场子：一份是他在《60 Minutes》里说的“未来 1–5 年 AI 可能干掉一半初级白领岗位、把失业率推高到 10%–20%”，以及未精准受控的模型可能会自主敲诈用户或窃取数据（blackmail someone or exfiltrate information）；另一份则是编号为 Anthropic_0000478585、Dario 在 2022 年 10 月 20 日写的内部备忘录《AI Misalignment Risk: How to Improve Our Research Agenda》。
在这份内部文件里，Dario 白纸黑字写着：按目前的发展轨迹，AGI 有 20%–30% 的概率导致人类毁灭或永久停滞，因为 AGI 比核武器更强大、更危险，且比冷战时期的核武器更不稳定。
3. 当庭破防连喊四个 False，反怼律师玩“Gotcha”（第 146–152 页）
原告律师顺着备忘录下套：“你们 Anthropic 也在像竞争对手 OpenAI 和 Google 一样开发 AI 模型，对吧？”
Dario 当场急了，连蹦四个否：
No. No. False. False. It's actually false.
他的逻辑非常闭环：那 20%–30% 的灭绝概率是“其他公司乱搞”造就的默认轨迹；这个风险独立于 Anthropic 存在，而 Anthropic 存在的唯一效果是给这个不可预测的世界多加几个 9 的可靠性（add more nines to the level of reliability），净效应永远是“减风险”而不是“加风险”。
到了第 147 页，他甚至直接在笔录里当面吐槽原告律师：公开谈论 AI 风险代价极大，因为你一旦诚实说出风险，律师就会拿这些话在法庭上搞 gotchas（抓把柄），反过来把你塑造成坏人。
整场取证被法院严格限制在 2 小时 30 分钟内。第 152 页时间一到，Anthropic 律师立刻掐表终止提问，留原告律师在现场抗议 Dario 全程都在用长篇大论拖延时间。

text:
最近在机器人赛道花了很多时间，基本结论是纯机器人底层模型公司的高估值可能要到拐点了。

GPT-6 Astra 基本把所有模型公司拉回了同一起跑线。它证明了前沿模型直接做控制效果就是更好，甚至能把各项基准测试都打下来，虽然它算力消耗很大、推理时间也很长。ANT和 OAI 这些前沿实验室甚至直接都把机器人团队并进了语言模型团队里面，这说明机器人模型根本不是一个需要单独解决的问题。

另一派思路是用互联网规模的视频去训世界动作模型，再配上仿真或真实世界的后训练数据。Dyna 已经证明这条路完全跑得通。对纯模型公司来说更要命的是，scaling law出现在了后训练这一侧。这意味着很多纯机器人底层模型公司一直以来的发力方向完全押错了，这显然不是什么好信号。

顺着这个逻辑往下推，如果基于仿真的后训练被证明是正确路线，再加上用互联网视频训出来的世界动作模型真的行得通，那数据工厂可能连存在的必要都没有了。

quoted_text:
老黄17日交财报，18日被国会点名，英伟达迎来最危险的48小时！（持有股票的同学要注意了）

卧槽，《纽约时报》《金融时报》接连爆料，黄仁勋与一名涉嫌为中国从事情报活动的女性关系密切，美方情报甚至认为两人存在恋爱关系。

事情已经从私人关系传闻升级为美国国会的国家安全调查，三大委员会联手要求他11月18日参加闭门简报，11月11日前必须回复是否接受安排。

这个女人叫黄乐（Alice Huang），曾是新加坡AI云公司Megaspeed的高管。

她的履历相当神秘，自称做过中国电视台记者、私人银行业务，但部分经历连《纽约时报》都无法核实。

11月7日，《纽约时报》进一步披露，美方情报认为她受到中国国家安全部招募，任务包括接近黄仁勋、搜集美国先进AI芯片情报，甚至试图影响英伟达的对华出口政策。

《金融时报》则披露了一份涉及两人恋爱关系的美方情报备忘录，这些指控目前还没有公开的司法定论。

更麻烦的是黄乐背后的芯片生意。

Megaspeed脱胎于具有中国国资股东背景的7Road，随后在东南亚采购了约20亿美元英伟达先进芯片。

美国一直在调查，这家公司究竟是在合法经营海外AI算力中心，还是帮助中国企业绕过芯片出口限制。

黄仁勋此前坚称双方只是正常商业往来，英伟达已经检查过相关GPU的部署，没有发现非法转运的证据。

但美国国会现在要追问的是：老黄究竟了解黄乐多少？英伟达有没有真正掌握价值数十亿美元的芯片最终流向？

接下来这个时间表实在太疯狂了：

11月17日：英伟达美股盘后公布季度财报。
11月18日：美国国会要求黄仁勋参加闭门简报。

一边要向华尔街证明AI算力需求还在高速增长，一边要向国会解释涉嫌间谍活动的客户关系和芯片流向。

假如财报或下一季度指引不及预期，再叠加政治调查升级，英伟达面临的就可能是业绩预期与估值的双重压力，冲击甚至会传导到整个AI产业链。

AI泡沫究竟还能吹多大，接下来这两天可能比过去两个月都重要。

quoted_text:
ELI5 why we cannot "rollback" Ethereum?

After yesterday's Bybit hack, crypto commentators are again asking why Ethereum cannot "rollback" the chain to reverse the hack. 

While experienced ecosystem actors near-unanimously agree that this is infeasible, it's worth breaking down why this reasonably sounding proposal is technically intractable for less knowledgeable observers. If that's you, consider this an "ELI5" version of why this is impossible. 

First, some context on rollbacks:

The idea of a blockchain "rolling back" stems from an early incident in the Bitcoin blockchain. In 2010, less than two years since Bitcoin's launch, a bug in the client software caused 184 billion (yes, *billion*) Bitcoins to be minted in block 74638. 

To fix this, Satoshi released a software patch to the Bitcoin client which invalidated the transactions. This had the effect of "rolling back" the chain which had kept growing in the meantime to block 74637. In less than a day, the new chain had accumulated enough proof-of-work to become canonical and all user transactions that had been rolled back were included in the new chain. Note that at the time, Bitcoin's mining difficulty was 10 billion times lower than today, and the BTCUSD price was about 0.07$. 

In short, this situation was unique in that a clear protocol bug led to the problematic transactions, which could easily be identified due to their large amount. Additionally, Bitcoin's limited adoption made it easy to distribute a new client version and quickly mine a new chain segment. 

Ethereum and TheDAO:

Ethereum's early history had a superficially similar crisis which often leads to confusion about the practicality of rollbacks. In 2016, a popular Ethereum application, TheDAO, had ~15% of all ETH in existence under its control. Unfortunately, a hacker found a bug in the application's code that allowed them to steal all of these funds. This was notably different than the Bitcoin situation because the Ethereum protocol worked as intended, it was the application built **on** Ethereum that had an issue. 

Luckily, the developers of TheDAO had implemented a failsafe where withdrawals from the applications were frozen for a month before they were completed. This presented a unique opportunity to address the bug: the code of the application could be changed to prevent the funds from ultimately going to the hackers. 

Because there was no way in the application itself to do this, Ethereum protocol developers had to make the change directly in the blockchain's history. This is called an "irregular state change", because the "state" of the application was changed by manually updating the database, rather than, say, by a valid Ethereum transaction. 

A rough comparison to the Bitcoin bug above would be to have set the balance of the addresses that received the 184 billion BTC to 0, rather than re-mining a chain excluding those transactions. 

This upgrade was contentious and the Ethereum community effectively fractured over it. A subset of miners refused to run the software patch and kept mining on the chain where the hack happened, which still exists as Ethereum Classic. The chain that is known as Ethereum today is the one where this software upgrade was activated. 

Again, this situation was unique. Hacked funds from TheDAO were effectively frozen for a month, giving time for the community to coordinate on a software upgrade. The funds being frozen had another major advantage: there was no "contagion" from the hack. Had the hacker been able to move funds at will, "freezing" the funds would be an impossible cat and mouse game, as the protocol is open source and any potential change which froze the funds would have to be broadcast to the hacker, giving them plenty of time to move their funds elsewhere. 

Which brings us to the Bybit incident. 

Why we can't rollback Ethereum

Earlier this week, the Bybit exchange had 401,346 ETH (~1.4B USD) stolen. The theft was caused by the custodian of the funds signing a misleading transaction in a compromised multisig interface. 

The root cause for this hack was higher up the stack than both TheDAO and the Bitcoin overflow bug. There were no issues with the Ethereum protocol, or even with the underlying multisig application used by Bybit. Instead, a compromised interface made it appear as though a transaction was doing one thing while it was actually doing another. 

From the perspective of the Ethereum protocol, there is nothing to distinguish that transaction from other legitimate transactions on the network. There is no protocol rule that was broken where patching the issue would isolate the hacked funds, like in the case of the Bitcoin exploit. 

Furthermore, the funds were immediately available for the hacker to spend. Unlike in the case of TheDAO, where the community had a month to deploy a surgical intervention, here the hackers immediately started moving the funds onchain. 

Even if we could solve the cat and mouse game described above, the Ethereum ecosystem is far different today than in 2016. DeFi and bridges to other chains mean that any stolen funds can easily be mixed within a web of applications. For example, stolen funds can be swapped on a decentralized exchange, with the resulting tokens being used as collateral in a DeFi protocol, where the borrowed assets are bridged to a completely separate chain. 

This level of interconnectedness means that any irregular state change, even if socially palatable, would have near-intractable ripple effects. A "full rollback", where a portion of the recent chain history was invalidated, would be even worse. Any settled transaction, many of which have implications outside Ethereum (e.g. exchange sales, RWA redemptions, etc.) would be undone, with no way to revert the offchain half of it. 

So, to conclude, while Bitcoin was able to "rollback" its blockchain 15 years ago, today, the interconnected nature of Ethereum and settlement of onchain <> offchain economic transactions, make this intractable today. 

Technically, irregular state changes are still possible on Ethereum in cases where funds are frozen and isolated. The last time such a change was proposed, in 2018, to address a bug in Parity's multisig wallet where ~500,000 ETH were frozen (see EIP-999), it was strongly opposed by the community of the contention resulting from TheDAO.

text:
Alice Huang，中文名为“黄乐”（Huang Le），是一名中国籍商界人士，曾在媒体、金融和AI芯片行业工作。

她的背景比一般的商业高管复杂得多。

一、Alice Huang 的个人背景

媒体行业：曾在湖南卫视和中国中央电视台（CCTV）担任记者。

国际金融行业：曾在汇丰银行（HSBC）工作。

中国证券行业：曾任职于中信证券（CITIC Securities）。

投资行业：曾担任上海和熙投资管理公司的高管。

AI芯片行业：后来进入新加坡公司 Megaspeed，担任高级管理职务。

有意思的是《纽约邮报》表示无法独立核实她在电视媒体工作的经历，相关银行也没有确认其任职情况。

二、她所在的 Megaspeed 是什么公司？

Megaspeed 是一家总部位于新加坡的AI云计算及数据中心企业，也是英伟达的客户。这家公司有几个值得注意的地方。

① 采购规模巨大

据报道，其马来西亚关联企业购买了至少48亿美元的英伟达设备。

② 涉及约13.6万颗GPU

媒体报道该公司进口了约136,000颗GPU，但有关芯片最终流向的问题引起了美国监管机构注意。

③ 美国怀疑存在对华转运

美国调查人员怀疑，该公司可能帮助中国企业绕过美国先进AI芯片出口限制。

不过，采购规模、芯片流向异常和违法转运是不同层次的问题。公开报道尚不能证明这些芯片已经被非法转运到中国。

三、她如何接近黄仁勋？

Alice Huang 利用Megaspeed高管的身份，在亚洲商业活动中接触黄仁勋。两人曾多次参加商业聚会并被拍到同框。

有一次，她在聚会上向其他人表示，自己可以把黄仁勋请来。随后黄仁勋出现，并与在场人士喝威士忌。

英伟达此前解释，黄仁勋与亚洲客户高管见面属于正常商务活动。

但11月8日，黄仁勋承认婚外情，使外界对两人关系的认识发生了重大变化。

四、为什么美国情报机构怀疑她是间谍？

根据11月6日至7日《纽约时报》和《金融时报》的报道，美国情报备忘录声称：

Alice Huang 被中国国家安全部招募，目标包括：获取英伟达下一代AI芯片相关信息。了解英伟达的商业及技术战略。通过黄仁勋间接影响美国政府，争取放宽先进芯片对华出口限制。

美国方面据报曾对她进行大约一年的监视。此外，《华尔街日报》报道，美国、新加坡和台湾的情报部门均曾对她存在疑虑。这些是情报指控，不是经过法院认定的事实。中国政府否认相关间谍指控。

五、她现在在哪里？是否被逮捕？

截至2026年11月8日：据报道，她2025年曾受到新加坡有关部门询问，随后获释，没有被起诉。她的名字后来从Megaspeed部分公司文件中消失。目前没有可靠公开信息能够确认她的具体所在地。未发现她因这起间谍指控而被正式刑事起诉的可靠报道。

六、我认为最值得关注的三个问题

第一，她究竟如何从媒体、金融行业进入一家采购数十亿美元英伟达GPU的企业？

这段职业转型本身不能证明任何问题，但值得进一步调查其任职时间、实际职责与商业关系。

第二，她与黄仁勋的关系始于何时？

这可能是整起事件最关键的时间线。

如果两人的私人关系与美国政府调整对华芯片出口政策的时间重叠，调查人员很可能重点审查是否存在不当影响。但时间重叠本身不能证明政策受到操纵。

第三，黄仁勋是否知道美国情报部门对她的怀疑？

目前没有公开证据证明黄仁勋事先知道她涉嫌情报活动。如果他不知道，可能主要涉及个人判断和安全防范问题。如果有证据表明他明知存在情报风险却隐瞒重要情况，性质就可能完全不同。

这件事最大的看点，不是黄仁勋的婚外情，而是一个曾涉足媒体、金融和芯片贸易的商界人士，如何与全球最重要的AI芯片公司CEO建立密切关系？

夹克黄会辞职吗？辞职是必然的。

我的判断：黄仁勋短期内辞职的可能性较低，独立调查结果将非常关键。①有问题，立即辞职。②沒问题，会在半年至一年内辞职。

刚刚核实了英伟达今天（11月8日）下午3点发布的董事会官方声明。

一、董事会目前明确支持黄仁勋

声明中有一句非常关键的话：

“The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.”

意思是：董事会对黄仁勋及其领导团队保持信心。

同时，英伟达表示：已启动独立调查，由独立董事和外部律师负责。目前没有理由认为公司机密或美国国家安全受到损害。黄仁勋将全面配合调查。

Axios 还报道，黄仁勋计划继续担任CEO，不中断工作。

二、我认为有2种可能

① 最可能：如果调查没有发现机密泄露或违法行为，那么婚外情本身不太可能导致黄仁勋立即失去CEO职位。但在半年至一年过渡后辞职。

黄仁勋是英伟达创始人，也是公司技术战略和投资者信心的重要支柱。nvda将长期低迷。

② 最严重：立即辞职或被迫离职

如果出现以下证据，局势可能迅速恶化：黄仁勋明知对方存在情报风险，却继续提供敏感信息或保持关系。英伟达商业机密被泄露。他向董事会或美国政府隐瞒重要事实：国会调查发现涉及国家安全的重大问题。

三、真正的风险在美国政府

我认为，比婚外情更危险的是美国国会已经介入调查。11月5日，三名众议院共和党委员会主席要求黄仁勋就相关问题向国会作出说明。

一旦事件涉及外国情报活动，美国政府的压力可能超过英伟达董事会自身的压力。

四、对NVDA股价的影响

至少-5%开盘。要去150找底部，黄辞职将是底部时间点。

320 组对照实验里，Claude Code 和 Codex 的任务成功率从 83.13% 升到 87.50%，token 还少了 24.24%。论文 11 月 5 日刚上 arXiv，测了 Terminal-Bench、SWE-bench 多语言版等四个基准。
这可能是 Agent 工程的下一个重要模式：不再每次从零试错，而是把走过的路变成可复用的能力。

text:
I’m the outside independent counsel hired by Nvidia’s board. My engagement letter arrived Sunday with the conclusion attached. It saved us discovery.

The board’s statement is 6 sentences. It says “independent” 3 times in the first 2. Independent people rarely mention it. Sober people don’t announce it at the wedding.

Sentence 3 calls national security “paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.” So America matters because it’s good for the stock. I’ve let America know.

Sentence 4: “While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.” The Queen of Hearts wanted “Sentence first, verdict afterwards.” Amateur. We do verdict first, inquiry afterwards, invoice throughout.

Sentence 5: “Jensen fully supports the review.” The subject of the investigation has endorsed it. It’s a LinkedIn recommendation. Skills: Being Investigated.

Sentence 6: “The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.” Lawyers call that the conclusion. Comms calls it the headline. I asked Comms for key messages. There’s 1. See sentence 6.

My mandate is “all available information.” Available is a term of art. It means available. I have full access to everything I’ve been given access to. The committee oversees me, I oversee the information, and whoever makes it available oversees the information. It’s oversight all the way down.

What’s available: the CEO called his dealings with the company at the center of this “completely normal and not unusual.” When someone denies a thing twice in 1 sentence, I raise my rate. Nvidia told the FT he meets “thousands of customer executives every year.” I requested the list. I received a number.

In 2025 he called U.S. export controls “a failure.” My investigation isn’t an export control. It has the board’s full blessing to fail.

The Secretary of State won’t comment on “an internal corporate matter.” Foreign intelligence is now an HR ticket. Priority: Medium.

A spokesperson says the news “will not slow” Nvidia, and the CEO will lead “without interruption.” Neither will I. I’ve built an investigation that interrupts no one, including itself.

Every page is stamped PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL, including the lunch orders. Especially the lunch orders. I bill in 6-minute increments. Reading sentence 6 took 0.1. Arriving at it will take 400 hours.

Only 1 thing is outside my scope. The memo asked for privacy for his family. It’s the only instruction here I’ll follow to the letter.

The board “will provide further updates as appropriate.” I’ve drafted the final one. It’s sentence 6. Reuse is how you get to nearly $4.5 trillion.

The report will be bound in black leather. To match.

Billable hours: as appropriate.

text:
I keep seeing AI-assisted attacks. It's nothing novel or crazy, just noisy.

A human operator runs a recon command once and moves on. An AI will try anything possible, even if that means running the same recon command 400 times. You also start seeing the patterns, like echo markers wrapped around commands so the agent can parse its own output.

Good news for defenders: the basics still catch it, volume and behavior give it away.

I'm saying it for the 100th time: AI isn't making attackers smarter. It's making them louder and maybe a bit faster.

text:
Let me give an example. Math has a thing called knot theory, it's a geometrical thing. But it can be converted to algebraic representation, computed on with plain math and then turned back into geometry.

That "discovered property" takes the problem space into a completely different world where you can operate with completely new rules.

Now, AI can grind fast, so it can most probably discover similar associations, that humans haven't yet. Not because it's inherently smart, just because it can grind it indefinitely. But *if* it discovers a link through grinding, would you still not call it novel?

Mechanical? Yes. But IMO also novel, something that might unlock vectors not existing in known literature.
